entries.lat: Octáva Nativitátis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
entries.eng: The Octave of the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.lat: Circumcísio ejúsdem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
entries.eng: The Circumcision of the same our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctæ Martínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, divérsis tormentórum genéribus cruciáta, tandem, gládio percússa, martýrii palmam adépta est. Ipsíus vero festum tértio Kaléndas Februárii recólitur.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy virgin Martina, who was put to diverse torments, under the Emperor Alexander, and at length gained the crown of martyrdom by the sword, whose feast we keep upon the 30th day of the month of January.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, deposítio sancti Basilíi, cognoménto Magni, Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, témpore Valéntis Imperatóris, doctrína et sapiéntia insignítus omnibúsque virtútibus exornátus, mirabíliter effúlsit, et Ecclésiam advérsus Ariános et Macedoniános inexpugnábili constántia deféndit. Ejus autem festívitas potíssimum ágitur décimo octávo Kaléndas Júlii, quo die Epíscopus ordinátus est.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Magnus.

entries.lat: Apud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Bonfílii Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, quam cum idem impénse coluísset, ab ipsa in cælum repénte evocátus est. Illíus porro ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Monte Senario, in Tuscany, the blessed confessor Bonfiglio, one of the seven founders of the order of servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, to whom he was devoted and by whom he was suddenly called away to heaven.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Almáchii Mártyris, qui, cum díceret: «Hodie Octavæ Domínici diéi sunt, cessáte a superstitiónibus idolórum et a sacrifíciis pollútis,» proptérea, jubénte Præfécto Urbis Alípio, a gladiatóribus occísus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Almachius, who was slain by gladiators at the command of Alpius, prefect of the city, because he said: "This is the Octave of the Lord's Birth, cease from your idolatrous superstitions, and your unclean sacrifices." Likewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, thirty holy soldiers who were crowned with martyrdom, under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Appia, corónæ sanctórum mílitum trigínta Mártyrum, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, on the Appian Way, the crowning of thirty holy soldiers, Martyrs, under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Apud Spolétum sancti Concórdii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, tempóribus Antoníni Imperatóris, primo cæsus fústibus, dehinc equúleo suspénsus, ac póstea macerátus in cárcere, ibíque Angélica visitatióne confortátus, demum gládio vitam finívit.
entries.eng: At Spoleto, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, the holy martyr, the priest Concordius. He was first cudgelled, then racked, and afterwards suffered imprisonment wherein he was comforted by a visit of angels, and at length was delivered from this life by the sword.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Magni Mártyris.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Magnus.

entries.lat: In Africa beáti Fulgéntii, Ruspénsis Ecclésiæ Epíscopi, qui, témpore Wandálicæ persecutiónis, ob cathólicam fidem eximiámque doctrínam, ab Ariánis multa perpéssus et in Sardíniam relegátus est; atque tandem, ad própriam Ecclésiam redíre permíssus, vita et verbo clarus, sancto fine quiévit.
entries.eng: In Africa, blessed Fulgentius, bishop of the Church of Ruspa, who at the time of the persecution under the Vandals, suffered much at the hands of the Arians because of his Catholic faith, and his eminent teaching. He was exiled to Sardinia; but was at length allowed to return to his own church, where he died a holy death, famous for his life and his words.

entries.lat: Teáte, in Aprútio citerióre, natális sancti Justíni, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, sanctitáte vitæ ac miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Chieti, in Abruzzo Citeriore, holy Justin, bishop of that city, famous for the holiness of his life, and for the miracles worked through him.

entries.lat: In território Lugdunénsi, monastério Jurénsium, sancti Eugéndi Abbátis, cujus vita virtútibus et miráculis plena refúlsit.
entries.eng: At the monastery of St. Claude, upon the Jura Mountains, in the country of Lyon, holy (4th) Eugendus, Abbot (of Condat), whose life was illustrious for his graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Silviníacum, in Gállia, sancti Odilónis, Abbátis Cluniacénsis, qui primus Commemoratiónem ómnium Fidélium Defunctórum, prima die post festum ómnium Sanctórum, in suis monastériis fíeri præcépit; quem ritum póstea universális Ecclésia recípiens comprobávit.
entries.eng: At Souvigny, in France, the holy Odilo, Abbot of Cluny, who was the first to order that the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed should be made in his monasteries on the day after the feast of All Saints; which rite the universal Church afterwards received and approved.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Vincéntii Maríæ Strambi, Epíscopi Maceraténsis et Tolentíni, Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Jesu sodális, pastoráli zelo præclári, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus inter Sanctos rétulit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the birthday of St. Vincent Mary Strambi, Bishop of Macerata and Tolentino, of the Congregation of the Cross and Passion of Jesus, renowned for his pastoral zeal, whom Pope Pius XII enrolled among the Saints.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ deposítio sanctæ Euphrósynæ Vírginis, quæ in monastério virtúte abstinéntiæ ac miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the burial of the holy virgin Euphrosyne, who shone in her nunnery as a great light by the power of her self-denial and her miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, spreto Diocletiáni Imperatóris edícto quo tradi sacri Códices jubebántur, pótius córpora carnifícibus quam sancta dare cánibus maluérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the commemoration of many holy Martyrs, who, despising the edict of the Emperor Diocletian whereby the sacred Books were ordered to be given up, chose rather to deliver their bodies to the executioners than to give holy things to dogs.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ pássio beáti Isidóri Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Antioch, blessed Isidore, Bishop.

entries.lat: Tomis, in Ponto, sanctórum fratrum Argéi, Narcíssi et Marcellíni púeri. Hic, sub Licínio Príncipe, cum inter tirónes esset comprehénsus et nollet militáre, hinc, cæsus ad mortem ac diu macerátus in cárcere, demum, in mare demérsus, martýrium consummávit; ejus autem fratres gládio perémpti sunt.
entries.eng: Argeus and Narcissus were slain with the sword. Marcellinus was a boy, he was taken among the recruits, and for as much as he would not be a soldier he was grievously flogged, and after suffering long in prison was drowned in the sea.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Martiniáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Milan (after the year 431), holy Martinian (17th) bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Nítriæ, in Ægýpto, beáti Isidóri, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Nitria, in Egypt, the blessed confessor Isidore (Bishop of Hermopolis in the fourth century).

entries.lat: Ipso die sancti Siridiónis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: Upon the same day the holy Bishop Siridion.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Macárii Alexandríni, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid the holy Abbot Macarius of Alexandria.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, natális sancti Anthéri, Papæ et Mártyris; qui sub Júlio Maximíno passus est, et in cœmetério Callísti sepúltus.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, holy Pope Anterus, who suffered under the Emperor Julius Maximian, and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus. (He reigned one month and 12 days in the year 236.).

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Floréntii Epíscopi, qui, témpore Galliéni Imperatóris, in exsílium relegátus, illic martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Vienne, in Gaul, holy Florence, (8th) bishop of that see (successor to St. Paracodius), who was exiled in the time of the Emperor Gallienus, and there finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Apud civitátem Aulánam, in Palæstína, pássio sancti Petri, qui crucis supplício interémptus est.
entries.eng: In the city of Aulana, in Palestine, the passion of holy Peter, who was put to death by the punishment of the cross.

entries.lat: In Hellespónto sanctórum Mártyrum Cyríni, Primi et Theogénis.
entries.eng: On the Hellespont, the holy martyrs Cyrinus, Primus, and Theogenes At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy centurion Gordius, in whose praise Basil the Great delivered a noble discourse upon his feast day.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Górdii Centuriónis, Mártyris; de cujus láudibus exstat præclára Basílii Magni orátio, in ejus die festo hábita.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy Centurion Gordius, Martyr; in whose praise there is extant a famous oration of Basil the Great, delivered on his feast day.

entries.lat: In Cilícia sanctórum Mártyrum Zósimi, et Athanásii Commentariénsis.
entries.eng: In Cilicia, the holy Martyrs Zosimus, and Athanasius, keeper of the prison records.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Theopémpti et Theónæ, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, illústre martýrium obiérunt.
entries.eng: In Cilicia, the holy martyrs Zozimus and Athanasius the Notary, also the holy martyrs Theopemptus and Theona, who suffered an illustrious martyrdom in the persecution under Diocletian.

entries.lat: Patávii sancti Daniélis Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Padua, the holy martyr Daniel.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sanctæ Genovéfæ Vírginis, quæ, a beáto Germáno, Antisiodorénsi Epíscopo, Christo dicáta, admirándis virtútibus et miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy virgin (and Patron of Paris) Genevieve, who was dedicated to Christ by blessed Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre, and was famous for her wondrous graces and miracles.

entries.lat: In Creta natális sancti Titi, qui, ab Apóstolo Paulo Epíscopus Creténsium ordinátus, et, post prædicatiónis offícium fidelíssime consummátum, finem beátum adéptus, in ea sepúltus est Ecclésia, ubi a beáto Apóstolo dignus miníster fúerat constitútus. Ipsíus tamen festívitas octávo Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: In Crete, holy Titus, whom the Apostle Paul ordained Bishop for the Cretans. When he had faithfully brought to an end, his work of preaching, he obtained a blessed death, and was buried in that church whereof the blessed Apostle had appointed him a worthy minister. His feast is kept upon the 6th day of the month of February.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Prisci Presbýteri, et Priscilliáni Clérici, ac Benedíctæ, religiósæ féminæ; qui, témpore impiíssimi Juliáni, gládio martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs the priest Priscus, the clerk Priscillian, and the devout woman Benedicta, who won martyrdom by the sword in the time of the wicked Emperor Julian (the Apostate).

entries.lat: Item Romæ beátæ Dafrósæ, uxóris sancti Flaviáni Mártyris, ac matris sanctárum Bibiánæ et Demétriæ, Vírginum et Mártyrum; quæ, post interfectiónem viri sui, primum exsílio relegáta, deínde, sub præfáto Príncipe, cápite plexa est.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the blessed martyr Dafrosa, wife of the holy martyr Flavian (mother of St Bibiana). After the execution of her husband she was first sentenced to exile, and then put to death under the aforesaid Emperor Julian.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sanctórum Hermétis, Aggæi et Caji Mártyrum, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy martyrs Hermes, Aggaeus, and Caius, who suffered under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: Adruméti, in Africa, commemorátio sancti Mávili Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Sevéri Imperatóris, a sævíssimo Prǽside Scápula damnátus ad béstias, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Adrumetum, in Africa, the holy martyr Mavillus, whom the cruel President Scapula condemned to the wild beasts in the persecution under the Emperor Severus, and who thus received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Item in Africa præclarissimórum Mártyrum Aquilíni, Gémini, Eugénii, Marciáni, Quincti, Theodóti et Tryphónis.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the illustrious martyrs Aquilinus, Geminus, Eugenius, Marcian, Quintus, Theodotus, and Tryphon (about end of fifth century).

entries.lat: Apud Língonas, in Gállia, sancti Gregórii Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Langres, holy Gregory, bishop of that see, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, sancti Rigobérti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Reims, in Gaul, the holy confessor Rigobert, bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Telésphori, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, sub Antoníno Pio, post multos labóres, pro Christi confessióne, illústre martýrium duxit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Telesphorus, who toiled much for Christ, and under the Emperor Antoninus Pius obtained by his testimony a glorious martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Anglia natális sancti Eduárdi, Regis Anglórum et Confessóris; qui virtúte castitátis et grátia miraculórum fuit insígnis. Ejus autem festívitas, ex decréto Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi, tértio Idus Octóbris, quo die sacrum ejus corpus translátum fuit, potíssimum celebrátur.
entries.eng: In England, the holy King Edward, famous for his gift of chastity and of the power of working miracles. By command of Pope Innocent XI his feast is kept upon the 13th day of October, which is the day of the translation of his sacred body.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui in Thebáide, sub persecutióne Diocletiáni, divérso tormentórum génere cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Egypt are commemorated many holy martyrs who were slain in the Thebaid in diverse ways, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Simeónis Mónachi, qui, multos annos in colúmna stans vixit, unde et Stylítæ cognómen accépit; cujus vita et conversátio éxstitit admirábilis.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy monk Simeon, who lived for many years standing upon a pillar, whence he is called Stylitis (from the Greek style, which is being interpreted a pillar), whose life and conversation was wonderful.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Æmiliánæ Vírginis, amitæ sancti Gregórii Papæ; quæ, vocánte Tharsílla soróre, quæ ad Deum præcésserat, hac ipsa die migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy virgin Emiliana, father's sister to holy Gregory the Great. Her sister Tharsilla, who had gone to God before her, came and called her, and upon the same day she passed hence to be for ever with the Lord (sixth century).

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctæ Syncléticæ Vírginis, cujus res præcláre gestas sanctus Athanásius monuméntis litterárum commendávit.
entries.eng: At Alexandria (in the fourth century), holy Syncletica, whose noble acts holy Athanasius hath set before us in his writing.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sanctæ Apollináris Vírginis.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy virgin Apollinaris.

entries.lat: Epiphánia Dómini.
entries.eng: The Epiphany of the Lord.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ejus autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.
entries.eng: At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles, and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, in Spain, likewise the birthday of holy Raymund of Peñafort, of the Order of Preachers, Confessor, famous for learning and holiness. His feast, however, is kept on the 23rd day of January.

entries.lat: In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.
entries.eng: On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

entries.lat: In território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, jubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: Rhédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, júgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.
entries.eng: At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed.

entries.lat: Geris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).

entries.lat: Relátio púeri Jesu de Ægýpto.
entries.eng: The return of the Child Jesus out of Egypt.

entries.lat: Nicomédiæ natális beáti Luciáni, Ecclésiæ Antiochénæ Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, satis clarus doctrína et eloquéntia, passus est, ob Christi confessiónem, in persecutióne Galérii Maximiáni, sepultúsque est Helenópoli, in Bithýnia. Ipsíus autem laudes sanctus Joánnes Chrysóstomus celebrávit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, for confessing Christ, in the persecution under the Emperor Galerius Maximian, the blessed martyr Lucian, priest of the Church of Antioch, distinguished for his learning and eloquence, whose praise hath been recorded by holy John Chrysostom. He is buried at Helenopolis in Bithynia.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Cleri Diáconi, qui pro confessiónis glória, sépties tortus ac diu macerátus in cárcere, ad últimum, gládio decollátus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyr the deacon Cleri, who on account of his glorious confession was seven times put to the torture, suffered long in prison, and at length was beheaded.

entries.lat: In civitáte Heracléa sanctórum Mártyrum Felícis et Januárii.
entries.eng: In the city of Heraclea, the holy martyrs Felix and Januarius.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Juliáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Julian.

entries.lat: In Dánia sancti Canúti, Regis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Denmark, the holy martyr King Canute (IV.), whose feast is kept on January 19 (although not in England).

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Crispíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy confessor Crispin (I.), bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Dácia sancti Nicetæ Epíscopi, qui feras et bárbaras gentes, Evangélii prædicatióne, mites réddidit ac mansuétas.
entries.eng: In Dacia, the holy bishop Nicetas, who by his preaching of the Gospel caused savage and barbarous tribes to become mild and gentle. (Fifth century.).

entries.lat: In Ægýpto beáti Theodóri Mónachi, qui, témpore Constantíni Magni, flóruit sanctitáte; cujus méminit sanctus Athanásius in vita sancti Antónii.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the blessed monk Theodore, who flourished in holiness in the time of the Emperor Constantine the Great, and of whom mention is made by holy Athanasius in the life of holy Anthony.

entries.lat: Venétiis deposítio sancti Lauréntii Justiniáni, primi Patriárchæ urbis ejúsdem et Confessóris; quem, doctrína et supérnis divínæ sapiéntiæ charismátibus copiosíssime replétum, Alexánder Octávus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ipsíus autem festívitas Nonis Septémbris, quo die Cáthedram pontificálem ascéndit, potíssimum celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Venice, the blessed Confessor Lawrence de' Giustiniani, the first Patriarch of that city he was filled very abundantly with learning and gifts of divine wisdom from on high, and Alexander VIII. enrolled his name among those of the saints. We keep his festival upon the fifth day of September.

entries.lat: Bellováci, in Gálliis, sanctórum Mártyrum Luciáni Presbýteri, Maximiáni et Juliáni. Horum duo últimi a persecutóribus gládio perémpti sunt; beátus autem Luciánus, qui, una cum sancto Dionýsio, in Gálliam vénerat, et ipse, post nímiam cædem, cum Christi nomen viva voce confitéri non timuísset, priórum senténtiam excépit.
entries.eng: At Beauvais, in Gaul, the holy martyrs Lucian the Priest (first Bishop of that see,) Maximian, and Julian. Maximian and Julian were slain by the persecutors with the sword, but the blessed Lucian, who had come into Gaul with holy Denis, did not receive the like treatment until after great suffering, the which notwithstanding, he feared not to confess aloud the name of Christ. (He died in the year 312.).

entries.lat: In Líbya sanctórum Mártyrum Theóphili Diáconi, et Helládii, qui, primo laniáti ac téstulis peracútis compúncti, demum, in ignem conjécti, ánimas Deo reddidérunt.
entries.eng: In Libya, the holy martyrs Theophilus the Deacon, and Helladius, who were first torn and mangled with sharp potsherds, and then cast into the fire, and so gave up their souls to God.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Eugeniáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyr Eugenian (Bishop of Autun.).

entries.lat: Hierápoli, in Asia, sancti Apollináris Epíscopi, qui, sub Marco Antoníno Vero, sanctitáte atque doctrína flóruit.
entries.eng: At Hierapolis, in Asia, holy Apollinaris, Bishop (of that see,) who was eminent for holiness and learning, in the time of the Emperor Marcus Antoninus Verus.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, natális sancti Severíni Epíscopi, qui fuit frater beáti Victoríni Mártyris; et, post multárum virtútum perpetratiónem, plenus sanctitáte quiévit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Severinus, Bishop (of that see,) brother of the blessed martyr Victorinus he wrought many good works, and fell asleep full of holiness,.

entries.lat: Metis, in Gállia, sancti Patiéntis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Metz, holy Patient, Bishop (of that see, in the second century.).

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Máximi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Confessor Maximus, Bishop (of that see, successor to St Epiphanius. He took part in the 4th and 6th Councils of Rome, held by Pope Symmachus against the Antipope Lawrence at the beginning of the sixth century.).

entries.lat: Ratisbónæ, in Bavária, sancti Erhárdi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Regensburg in Bavaria, holy Bishop Erhard.

entries.lat: Apud Nóricos sancti Severíni Abbátis, qui apud eam gentem Evangélium propagávit, et Noricórum dictus est Apóstolus. Ejus corpus ad Lucullánum prope Neápolim, in Campánia, divínitus delátum, inde póstea ad monastérium sancti Severíni translátum est.
entries.eng: Among the Noricans, the holy Abbot Severinus, who spread the Gospel among that people, and was called the Apostle of Noricum. His body was carried by divine guidance to Lucullanum near Naples, in Campania, and thence afterwards translated to the monastery of St. Severinus.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno, natális sanctórum Juliáni Mártyris, et Basilíssæ Vírginis, ipsíus Juliáni uxóris. Hæc, virginitáte cum viro suo serváta, in pace vitam finívit; Juliánus vero (postquam multitúdo Sacerdótum et Ministrórum Ecclésiæ Christi, quæ, propter immanitátem persecutiónis, ad eos confúgerat, igne cremáta est), Marciáni Prǽsidis jussu, plúrimis torméntis cruciátus, capitálem senténtiam accépit. Cum ipso étiam Antónius Présbyter, et Anastásius, quem idem Juliánus, a morte suscitátum, grátiæ Christi partícipem fécerat, et Celsus puer cum hujus matre Marcionílla, ac septem fratres, aliíque plúrimi passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy martyr Julian, along with whom is commemorated the holy Virgin Basilissa, his wife, who kept her virginity with her husband and ended her life in peace. A multitude of priests and ministers of the Church of Christ had taken refuge with them because of the fury of the persecution. They were burnt with fire, and Julian, by command of the President Marcian, was thereafter made to suffer many torments and was then beheaded.

entries.lat: Smyrnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Vitális, Revocáti et Fortunáti.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, the holy martyrs Vitalis (probably a Bishop, and the others were most likely Deacons), Revocatus, and Fortunatus.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Epictéti, Jucúndi, Secúndi, Vitális, Felícis et aliórum septem.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Epictetus, Jucundus, Secundus, Vitalis, Felix, and seven others,.

entries.lat: In Mauritánia Cæsariénsi sanctæ Marciánæ Vírginis, quæ, béstiis trádita, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: In Morocco, (in the fourth century,) the holy Virgin and martyr Marciana, who was thrown to wild beasts and so finished her testimony.

entries.lat: Sebáste, in Arménia, sancti Petri Epíscopi, fílii sanctórum Basilíi et Emméliæ, atque fratris item sanctórum Basilíi Magni et Gregórii Nysséni Episcopórum, ac Macrinæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, in Armenia, holy Peter, Bishop (of that see,) brother of holy Basil the Great (also of St. Gregory of Nyssa. His father was St. Basil the Elder, his mother St. Emmelia, and his grandmother St. Macrina. He was made head of his convent in the year 362, when St. Basil was made bishop, St. Basil having before been Abbot thereof.).

entries.lat: Anconæ sancti Marcellíni Epíscopi, qui urbem illam (ut sanctus Gregórius Papa scribit) divína virtúte ab incéndio liberávit.
entries.eng: At Ancona, holy Marcellinus, Bishop of that city, the which, as holy Gregory writeth, he did through the power of God deliver from burning. (He succeeded St. Traso in the Bishopric about the year 550, and was followed by St. Thomas about the year 569. He is secondary Patron of Ancona.).

entries.lat: In Thebáide natális beáti Pauli, primi Eremítæ, Confessóris, qui, a sextodécimo ætátis suæ anno usque ad centésimum décimum tértium, solus in erémo permánsit; cujus ánimam, inter Apostolórum et Prophetárum choros, ad cælum ferri ab Angelis sanctus Antónius vidit. Ejus autem festívitas décimo octávo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, blessed Paul, the first Hermit, who from the sixteenth even unto the hundred and thirteenth year of his age dwelt alone in the desert, holy Anthony saw his soul borne heavenward by angels between the choirs of the Apostles and of the Prophets. We keep his feast upon the 15th day of this present month of January.

entries.lat: In Cypro beáti Nicánoris, qui fuit unus de septem primis Diáconis; atque, grátia fídei et virtúte admirándus, gloriosíssime coronátus est.
entries.eng: In Cyprus, the blessed Nicanor, one of the seven first Deacons, who was wondrous for the grace of faith and power, and received a most glorious crown,.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Agathónis Papæ, qui, sanctitáte et doctrína conspícuus, quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Agatho, who, famous for holiness and learning, rested in peace.

entries.lat: Bitúricis, in Aquitánia, sancti Willhélmi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, signis et virtútibus clari; quem Honórius Papa Tértius in Sanctórum cánonem adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Bourges, in Aquitaine, the holy Confessor William, Archbishop (of that see,) famous for signs and works of power, whose name Honorius III enrolled with those of the saints.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Joánnis Boni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy John the Good, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Marciáni Presbýteri.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Priest Marcian,.

entries.lat: In monastério Cuxanénsi, in Gállia, natális sancti Petri Urséoli Confessóris, qui, ántea Venetiárum Dux et deínde Monáchus ex Ordine sancti Benedícti, pietáte et virtútibus cláruit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Cusan, (in the diocese of Perpignan,) the holy Confessor Peter Urseoli, who was sometime Doge of Venice, and then became a monk of the Order of St. Benedict, and was famous for godliness and works of power,.

entries.lat: Arétii, in Túscia, Beáti Gregórii Décimi, civis Placentíni, qui, ex Archidiácono Leodiénsi Summus Póntifex renuntiátus, Concílium Lugdunénse secúndum celebrávit, Græcísque ad unitátem fídei recéptis, compósitis Christianórum dissídiis, Terræ Sanctæ recuperatióne institúta, de universáli Ecclésia, quam sanctíssime gubernávit, óptime méritus est.
entries.eng: At Arezzo, in Tuscany, blessed Gregory X, a citizen of Piacenza, who, from being Archdeacon of Liège, was proclaimed Sovereign Pontiff, and celebrated the second Council of Lyons; and, having received the Greeks into the unity of the faith, composed the dissensions of Christians, and set on foot the recovery of the Holy Land, he deserved exceedingly well of the universal Church, which he governed most holily.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Hygíni, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, in persecutióne Antoníni, glorióse martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Hyginus, who achieved martyrdom gloriously in the persecution under the Emperor Antonine.

entries.lat: Item Romæ natális sancti Melchíadis, Papæ et Mártyris; qui multa, in persecutióne Maximiáni, passus est, atque, réddita Ecclésiæ pace, quiévit in Dómino. Ipsíus autem festívitas quarto Idus Decémbris celebrátur.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the birthday of holy Melchiades, Pope and Martyr; who suffered much in the persecution of Maximian, and, when peace had been restored to the Church, rested in the Lord. His feast, however, is kept on the 10th day of December.

entries.lat: Firmi, in Picéno, sancti Alexandrí, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Fermo, in Picenum, the holy martyr Alexander, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Ambiáni, in Gállia, sancti Sálvii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Amiens, in France, holy Salvius, Bishop and Martyr.

entries.lat: In Africa beáti Sálvii Mártyris, in cujus natáli sanctus Augustínus sermónem hábuit ad pópulum Carthaginénsem.
entries.eng: In Africa, the blessed martyr Salvius, upon whose feast-day holy Augustine preached to the people of Carthage.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Petri, Sevéri et Leúcii.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Peter, Severus, and Leucius.

entries.lat: Brundúsii sancti Leúcii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Brindisi, holy Leucius, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sancti Theodósii Cœnobiárchæ, in vico Cappadóciæ Magariásso nati; qui, multa passus pro fide cathólica, in pace tandem quiévit in eo monastério, quod ille super solitárium Hierosolymitánæ diœcésis montem exstrúxerat.
entries.eng: At Marissa, in Cappadocia, the holy Abbot Theodosius, (head of all the monasteries of Palestine,) who suffered many things for the Catholic faith, but at length fell asleep in peace,.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Palamónis Abbátis, qui fuit mágister sancti Pachómii.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, the holy Abbot Palaemon, the teacher of holy Pachom.

entries.lat: Suppentóniæ, apud montem Soráctem, sancti Anastásii Mónachi, et Sociórum; qui, divínitus vocáti, felíciter migravérunt ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Castel-Saint-Elie, hard by Mount Soracte, the holy monk Anastasius and his Companions, whom the Lord called to pass away unto Him.

entries.lat: Papíæ sanctæ Honorátæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy virgin Honorata,.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Tatiánæ Mártyris, quæ, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, uncis atque pectínibus laniáta, béstiis expósita et in ignem missa, sed nil læsa, demum, gládio percússa, migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Tatiana, in the persecution under the Emperor Alexander. She was lacerated with hooks and combs, thrown to wild beasts, and cast into the fire, but as she remained unhurt, was at length beheaded, and so passed away to heaven.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Tígrii Presbýteri, et Eutrópii Lectóris; qui, Arcádii Imperatóris témpore, cum de incéndio quo Ecclésia princeps et Senátus cúria conflagráverant, tamquam per eos ad exsílium sancti Joánnis Chrysóstomi ulciscéndum excitáto, per calúmniam accusáti essent, sub Præfécto urbis Optáto, inánium deórum superstitióne implícito et Christiánæ religiónis osóre, passi sunt.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, (in Morocco, in the year 259) the holy martyr Arcadius, eminent for his rank and his miracles.

entries.lat: In Acháia sancti Sátyri Mártyris, qui cum ante quoddam idólum tránsiret, in illud exsufflávit, signans sibi frontem, atque statim idólum córruit; ob quam causam decollátus est.
entries.eng: In the Peloponnesos, the holy martyr Satyrus. As he was passing before a certain idol he breathed upon it, and signed himself with the sign of the cross upon his own forehead, whereupon the idol straightway fell down, and for this cause Satyrus was beheaded,.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Arcádii Mártyris, génere et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyrs Tigrius the Priest and Eutropius the Reader, who suffered in the time of the Emperor Arcadius.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Zótici, Rogáti, Modésti, Cástuli, et corónæ Mílitum quadragínta.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Zoticus, Rogatus, Modestus, Castulus, and a crown of forty soldiers.

entries.lat: Tíbure sancti Zótici Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Tivoli, the holy martyr Zoticus.

entries.lat: Ephési pássio sanctórum quadragínta duórum Monachórum, qui ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum, sub Constantíno Coprónymo, sævíssime cruciáti, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: At Ephesus, forty-two holy monks, who were most cruelly tortured and suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus for the honouring of holy images.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Joánnis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor John, Archbishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Probi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, holy Probus, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Benedícti, Abbátis et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In England, the holy Confessor Benedict Biscop, founder, and Abbot of the monastery of Jarrow-upon-Tyne, whose feast we keep upon the 12th day of February.

entries.lat: Commemorátio Baptismátis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
entries.eng: The Commemoration of the Baptism of our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.lat: Pictávis, in Gállia, natális sancti Hilárii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, ob cathólicam fidem, quam strénue propugnávit, quadriénnio apud Phrýgiam relegátus, ibi, inter ália mirácula, mortúum suscitávit. Eum Pius Nonus, Póntifex Máximus, universális Ecclésiæ Doctórem declarávit et confirmávit. Ipsíus autem festum sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: He was a stalwart champion of the Catholic faith, for the which cause he was banished for four years into Phrygia. Among other miracles which he wrought he raised a dead man to life, The Supreme Pontiff Pius IX confirmed and published his title of Doctor of the Universal Church. We keep his feast upon the morrow.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, item natális sancti Remígii, Epíscopi et Confessóris. Hic gentem Francórum convértit ad Christum, Clodóveo, ipsórum Rege, sacris baptismátis undis et fídei sacraméntis initiáto; et, cum annos plúrimos in Episcopátu explésset, sanctitáte et miraculórum glória conspícuus, decéssit e vita. Ejus vero festívitas Kaléndis Octóbris potíssimum recólitur, quo die sacrum ipsíus corpus translátum fuit.
entries.eng: At Rheims, in France, likewise the birthday of holy Remigius, Bishop and Confessor. He converted the nation of the Franks to Christ, when Clovis, their King, had been initiated in the sacred waters of baptism and the sacraments of the faith; and, having fulfilled very many years in the Episcopate, famous for holiness and the glory of his miracles, he departed this life. His feast, however, is chiefly kept on the 1st day of October, on which day his sacred body was translated.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Lavicána, corónæ sanctórum Mílitum quadragínta, quas ipsi, sub Galliéno Imperatóre, pro veræ fídei confessióne percípere meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, forty holy soldiers who earned crowns of martyrdom for confessing the true faith under the Emperor Gallienus.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Gumesíndi Presbýteri, et Servidéi Mónachi.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy martyrs Gumesindus the Priest and Servant-of-God the monk.

entries.lat: In Sardínia sancti Potíti Mártyris, qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre et Gelásio Prǽside, multa passus, demum gládio martýrium consecútus est.
entries.eng: In Sardinia, the holy martyr Potitus, who suffered many things under the Emperor Antoninus and the President Gelasius, and at last was martyred with the sword.

entries.lat: Singidóni, in Mýsia superióre, sanctórum Mártyrum Hérmyli et Stratoníci, qui, post sæva torménta, sub Licínio Imperatóre, in Istrum flumen demérsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Semenden, in Upper Mysia, the holy martyrs Hermylus and Stratonicus, who were cruelly tortured under the Emperor Licinius, and then drowned in the Danube.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Leóntii Epíscopi, qui, sub Licínio, advérsus Gentíles, et, sub Constantíno, advérsus Ariános plúrimum decertávit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, holy Leontius, Bishop of that see, who contended manfully against the Gentiles under the Emperor Licinius, and against the Arians under the Emperor Constantine.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Agrítii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Agritius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Versíaco monastério, in Gállia, sancti Vivéntii Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Vergy, the holy Confessor Viventius,.

entries.lat: Amaséæ, in Ponto, sanctæ Gláphyræ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Amasea, in Pontus, the holy Virgin Glaphyra.

entries.lat: Medioláni, in cœnóbio sanctæ Marthæ, Beátæ Verónicæ de Binásco Vírginis, ex Ordine sancti Augustíni.
entries.eng: At Milan, in the monastery of St. Martha, the blessed Virgin Veronica of Binasco, of the Order of St. Augustine.

entries.lat: Sancti Hilárii, Epíscopi Pictaviénsis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui prídie hujus diéi evolávit in cælum.
entries.eng: Holy Hilary, Bishop of Poitiers, Confessor and Doctor of the Church; who on the day before this took his flight to heaven.

entries.lat: Nolæ, in Campánia, natális sancti Felícis Presbýteri, qui (ut sanctus Paulínus Epíscopus scribit), cum a persecutóribus post torménta in cárcerem missus esset, et cóchleis ac téstulis vinctus superpósitus jacéret, nocte ab Angelo solútus atque edúctus fuit; póstmodum vero, cessánte persecutióne, ibídem, cum multos ad Christi fidem exémplo vitæ ac doctrína convertísset, clarus miráculis quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Nola, in Campania, the holy Priest Felix. Holy Paulinus, Bishop of the same city, writeth that after the persecutors had put Felix to the torture they committed him to prison, where they laid him in chains, upon shells and potsherds, but in the night an angel loosed him and led him forth. In after-times, when the persecution was over and he had turned many to Christ by his example and teaching, he fell asleep, famous for miracles,.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sancti Malachíæ Prophétæ.
entries.eng: In Judea, the holy Prophet Malachi, (415 B.C.).

entries.lat: In monte Sina sanctórum trigínta octo Monachórum, a Saracénis ob Christi fidem interfectórum.
entries.eng: Upon Mount Sinai, thirty-eight holy monks, who were massacred by the Saracens for Christ's faith's sake,.

entries.lat: In Rhaíthi regióne, in Ægýpto, sanctórum quadragínta trium Monachórum, qui, pro Christiána religióne, a Blémmiis occísi sunt.
entries.eng: In the country of Rhaithia, in Egypt, forty-three holy monks who were massacred by the Blemmyes for the Christian religion's sake,.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Dátii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Datius, Bishop of that see, of whom blessed Pope Gregory maketh mention.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Euphrásii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy Bishop Euphrasius,.

entries.lat: Neocæsaréæ, in Ponto, sanctæ Macrínæ, discípulæ beáti Gregórii Thaumatúrgi, et áviæ sancti Basilíi, quæ eúndem Basilíum educávit.
entries.eng: At Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, (in the fourth century,) holy Macrina, a disciple of blessed Gregory the wonder-worker, and grandmother of holy Basil, whom she trained up in the faith.

entries.lat: Sancti Pauli, primi Eremítæ, Confessóris, qui quarto Idus Januárii inter beátorum ágmina translátus fuit.
entries.eng: Holy Paul, the first Hermit, Confessor, who on the 10th day of January was translated among the hosts of the blessed.

entries.lat: In território Andegavénsi beáti Mauri Abbátis, qui fuit discípulus sancti Benedícti; et, hujus disciplínis usque ab infántia erudítus, quantum in eis profécerit, inter ália quæ apud eum pósitus gessit (res nova et post Petrum fere inusitáta), pédibus super aquas incédens patefécit. In Gállias inde ab ipso Benedícto diréctus, ibi, constrúcto célebri monastério, cui quadragínta annis prǽfuit, miraculórum glória clarus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: In the country of Angers, the blessed Maurus, (founder and) Abbot (of Glanfeuil,) a disciple of St. Benedict, by whom he was trained from his childhood, and made such headway that in obedience to him he walked upon water, a thing new and almost unheard of since the time of the Apostle Peter. Benedict sent him into Gaul, where he built a famous monastery, whereof he was Abbot for forty years, and fell asleep in peace, illustrious for miracles,.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sanctórum Hábacuc et Michǽæ Prophetárum, quorum córpora, sub Theodósio senióre, divína revelatióne sunt repérta.
entries.eng: In Judea, the holy Prophets Habacuc and Micheas, whose bodies were found by divine revelation under Theodosius the elder.

entries.lat: Cárali, in Sardínia, sancti Ephísii Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Flaviáno Júdice, plúrimis torméntis divína virtúte superátis, demum, abscíssis cervícibus, victor migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Cagliari, in Sardinia, the holy martyr Ephisius, who under the judge Flavian, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, was strengthened by God to overcome many torments, but in the end was beheaded, and so rose to heaven a conqueror.

entries.lat: Anágniæ sanctæ Secundínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ sub Décio Imperatóre passa est.
entries.eng: At Anagni, the holy Virgin and martyr Secundina, who suffered under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: Nolæ, in Campánia, sancti Máximi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Nola, in Campania, holy Maximus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Boníti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Auvergne, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Bonitus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Macárii Abbátis, qui fuit discípulus beáti Antónii, ac vita et miráculis celebérrimus éxstitit.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy Macarius, Abbot (of Scittir,) a disciple of blessed Anthony, and very famous for his life and miracles.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ beáti Isidóri, sanctitáte vitæ, fide et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: Likewise (in Egypt, in the year 391,) blessed Isidore, famous for the holiness of his life, his faith, and his miracles.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Joánnis Calybítæ, qui aliquándiu in ángulo domus patérnæ, deínde in tugúrio, ignótus paréntibus, habitávit; a quibus in morte agnítus, miráculis cláruit. Ipsíus corpus póstea Romam translátum, et in Ínsulæ Tiberínæ Ecclésia, in ejus honórem erécta, collocátum est.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy John, called the hidden, who lived unknown to his kinsfolk for a while in a corner of his father's house, and then in a hut upon an island in the Tiber, where he was recognised at the time of his death, and famous for miracles, was buried in the same place, where afterward a church was built in his name,.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Salária, natális sancti Marcélli Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, ob cathólicæ fídei confessiónem, jubénte Maxéntio tyránno, primo cæsus est fústibus, deínde ad servítium animálium cum custódia pública deputátus, et ibídem, serviéndo indútus amíctu cilícino, defúnctus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, the holy martyr Pope Marcellus I, who for his confession of the Catholic faith was first cudgelled by order of the tyrant Maxentius and then sent to take care of the beasts which were fed at the public cost, in the which service he died, clad in sack-cloth,.

entries.lat: Marróchii, in Africa, pássio sanctórum quinque Protomártyrum Ordinis Minórum, scílicet Berárdi, Petri atque Othónis Sacerdótum, Accúrsii et Adjúti Laicórum; qui, ob Christiánæ fídei prædicatiónem ac Mahuméticæ reprobatiónem legis, post vária torménta et ludíbria, a Saracenórum Rege, scissis gládio capítibus, enecáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Morocco, in Africa, the holy martyrs Berard (de Carbis), Peter, Accursius, Adjutus, and Otho, of the Order of Friars Minors.

entries.lat: Rhinocolúræ, in Ægýpto, sancti Melæ Epíscopi, qui, sub Valénte exsílium et ália grávia pro fide cathólica passus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Rhinocolura, in Egypt, the holy Bishop Melas, who, having suffered under Valens exile and other grievous things for the Catholic faith, rested in peace.

entries.lat: Areláte, in Gállia, sancti Honoráti, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus vita tam doctrína quam miráculis fuit illústris.
entries.eng: At Arles, the holy Confessor Honoratus, Bishop of that see, whose life was rendered famous by his teaching and miracles.

entries.lat: Opitérgii, in Venetórum fínibus, sancti Titiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Moerzo, the holy Confessor Titian, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Fundis, in Látio, sancti Honoráti Abbátis, cujus méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: At Fondi, in Campania, (in the sixth century,) the holy Abbot Honoratus, (who was set over the monastery of Fondi) of whom mention is made by blessed Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: In castro cui nomen Macériæ, ad Altéjam flúvium, in Gállia, sancti Furséi Confessóris, cujus corpus ad monastérium Perónæ póstmodum translátum est.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Perouse, the holy Confessor Fursey, (Abbot of Lagny, in the year 650.).

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Priscíllæ, quæ se súaque pio Mártyrum obséquio mancipávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Priscilla, who gave up herself and all that she had to the service of the martyrs.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Antónii Abbátis, qui, multórum Monachórum Pater, vita et miráculis præclaríssimus vixit; cujus gesta sanctus Athanásius insígni volúmine prosecútus est. Ejus autem sacrum corpus, sub Justiniáno Imperatóre, divína revelatióne repértum et Alexandríam delátum, in Ecclésia sancti Joánnis Baptístæ humátum fuit.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, the holy Abbot Anthony, father of many monks, very illustrious for his life and miracles. Holy Athanasius hath chronicled his acts in a famous book. His sacred body was found by the revelation of God in the time of the Emperor Justinian and brought to Alexandria, where it is buried in the Church of St. John the Baptist.

entries.lat: Apud Língonas, in Gállia, sanctórum tergeminórum Speusíppi, Eleusíppi et Meleusíppi; qui, cum ávia sua Leonílla, martýrio coronáti sunt, témpore Marci Aurélii Imperatóris.
entries.eng: At Langres, the holy triplets Speusippus, Eleusippus, and Meleusippus, who were crowned with martyrdom in the time of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius, along with their grandmother Leonilla.

entries.lat: Apud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, deposítio sancti Sulpícii Epíscopi, cognoménto Pii, cujus vita et mors pretiósa gloriósis miráculis commendátur.
entries.eng: At Bourges, holy Sulpicius, Bishop of that see, surnamed the Pious, whose life and precious death are rendered famous by glorious miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ, in monastério sancti Andréæ, beátorum Monachórum Antónii, Méruli et Joánnis, de quibus scribit sanctus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: In the monastery of St. Andrew at Rome, (in the sixth century,) the blessed monks Anthony, Merulus, and John, of whom writeth holy Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: In fínibus Edessénæ regiónis, in Mesopotámia, sancti Juliáni Eremítæ, cognoménto Sabæ, qui, Valéntis Imperatóris témpore, fidem cathólicam, Antiochíæ ferme collápsam, virtúte miraculórum eréxit.
entries.eng: In the borders of the region of Edessa, in Mesopotamia, the holy Hermit Julian, surnamed Sabas, who, in the time of the Emperor Valens, raised up again by the power of miracles the Catholic faith, which had almost collapsed at Antioch.

entries.lat: Romæ Invéntio sanctórum Mártyrum Diodóri Presbýteri, Mariáni Diáconi, et Sociórum, qui, sancto Stéphano Papa Ecclésiam Dei regénte, martýrium Kaléndis Decémbris sunt assecúti.
entries.eng: At Rome is commemorated the finding of the bodies of the holy martyrs Diodorus the Priest, Marian the Deacon, and their Companions, who were keeping the feasts of the martyrs in the Catacombs in the time of holy Pope Stephen, when the persecutors closed up the entrance of the Catacomb and buried it up, so that they also died as martyrs.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctæ Priscæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ sub Cláudio Imperatóre, post multa torménta, martýrio coronáta est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Prisca, who after suffering many torments was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Claudius.

entries.lat: In Ponto natális sanctórum Mártyrum Moséi et Ammónii, qui, cum essent mílites, primo ad metálla damnáti sunt, ac novíssime igni tráditi.
entries.eng: In Pontus, the birthday of the holy Martyrs Moseus and Ammonius, who, being soldiers, were first condemned to the mines, and at last delivered to the fire.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Athenógenis, antíqui Theólogi, qui, per ignem consummatúrus martýrium, hymnum lætus cecinit, quem et discípulis scriptum relíquit.
entries.eng: In Pontus, the holy soldiers Moseus and Ammonius, who were first condemned to penal servitude in the mines and then burnt, (under the Emperor Decius.) Likewise in Pontus, (probably in the year 196,) the holy martyr Athenogenes the Old, called the Theologian, who, when he was about to suffer martyrdom by fire, joyfully sang an hymn, which also he left unto his disciples in writing.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Volusiáni Epíscopi, qui, a Gothis captus, in exsílio spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Tours, in France, the holy Bishop Volusian, who, taken captive by the Goths, gave up his spirit to God in exile.

entries.lat: In monastério Lutrénsi, in Burgúndia, sancti Deícolæ Abbátis, qui, natióne Hibérnus, discípulus fuit beáti Columbáni.
entries.eng: In Brittany, holy Deicola, Abbot (of Lure,) a disciple of blessed Columbanus.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Leobárdi reclúsi, qui mira abstinéntia et humilitáte refúlsit.
entries.eng: There also, the holy hermit (of Tourance,) Leobard, who was a bright light of self-denial and lowliness.

entries.lat: Novocómi sanctæ Liberátæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Como, the holy virgin Liberata.

entries.lat: Budæ, in Hungária, sanctæ Margarítæ, Vírginis, e régia Arpadénsium família, Ordinis sancti Domínici Moniális, virtúte castitátis et arctíssima pæniténtia insígnis, quam Pius Duodécimus, Póntifex Máximus, sanctárum Vírginum catálogo adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Buda, in Hungary, holy Margaret, Virgin, of the royal family of the Arpads, a Nun of the Order of St. Dominic, renowned for the virtue of chastity and for most rigorous penance, whom Pope Pius XII inscribed in the catalogue of holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Cornélia, sanctórum Mártyrum Márii et Marthæ conjúgum, et filiórum Audifácis et Abachum, nobílium Persárum; qui Romam, tempóribus Cláudii Príncipis, ad oratiónem vénerant. Ex eis vero, post tolerátos fustes, equúleum, ignes, ungues férreos manuúmque præcisiónem, Martha in Nympha necáta est; ceteri sunt decolláti, et córpora eórum incénsa.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Cornelian Way, the holy martyrs Maris, and Martha, his wife, and their sons Audifax and Abachum. These were noble Persians, who came to Rome for prayer's sake in the time of the Emperor Claudius. They were cudgelled, racked, burnt, torn with iron hooks, and had their hands cut off. At length Martha was drowned and the others beheaded, and their bodies cast into the fire.

entries.lat: Item sancti Canúti, Regis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: Likewise holy Canute, King and Martyr.

entries.lat: Smyrnæ natális beáti Germánici Mártyris, qui, sub Marco Antoníno et Lúcio Aurélio, cum primǽvæ ætátis venustáte floréret, damnátus a Júdice, et, per grátiam virtútis Dei, metum córporeæ fragilitátis exclúdens, præparátam sibi béstiam sponte provocávit; cujus déntibus comminútus, vero pani Dómino Jesu Christo, pro ipso móriens, méruit incorporári.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, in the time of the Emperors Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius, the blessed martyr Germanicus. He was a very beautiful youth, but by the power of God's grace he laid aside all the weakness of bodily fear, and of his own accord provoked the beast by which he had been condemned by the judge to be killed and so being ground through its teeth, and so dying for the Lord Jesus Christ, he earned to be made one body with Him who is Himself the very Bread which came down from heaven.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, Geróntii, Januárii, Saturníni, Succéssi, Júlii, Cati, Piæ et Germánæ.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Paul, Gerontius, Januarius, Saturninus, Successus, Julius, Catus, Pia, and Germana, (and others to the number in all of 600.).

entries.lat: Apud Spolétum pássio sancti Pontiáni Mártyris, qui, témpore Antoníni Imperatóris, a Fabiáno Júdice, pro Christo vehementíssime virgis cæsus, jussus est super carbónes nudis pédibus ambuláre, sed a carbónibus nil læsus, equúleo et uncínis férreis jussus est suspéndi, et sic in cárcerem trudi, ubi Angélica visitatióne méruit confortári; postque leónibus expósitus et plumbo fervénti perfúsus, tandem gládio percússus est.
entries.eng: At Spoleto, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, the holy martyr Pontian. Fabian, the judge, caused him to be first most grievously beaten with rods and then to walk barefoot upon live coals by these he was unhurt, and was therefore racked, lacerated with iron hooks, and cast into prison, where he was comforted by a visitation of angels. Lastly he was thrown to the lions, had molten lead poured over him, and was then beheaded.

entries.lat: Laudæ, in Insúbria, sancti Bassiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui advérsus hæréticos, una cum sancto Ambrósio, strénue decertávit.
entries.eng: At Lodi, the holy Confessor Bassian, Bishop of that see, who fought manfully along with holy Ambrose against the heretics.

entries.lat: Wigórniæ, in Anglia, sancti Wulstáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, méritis et miráculis conspícui; qui ab Innocéntio Papa Tértio inter Sanctos relátus est.
entries.eng: At Worcester, in England, holy Wulstan, Bishop and Confessor, famous for merits and miracles; who was enrolled among the Saints by Pope Innocent III.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Fabiáni, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, Décii témpore, martýrium passus est, atque in cœmetério Callísti sepúltus.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Fabian, who suffered in the time of the Emperor Decius, and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, ad Catacúmbas, sancti Sebastiáni Mártyris, qui, Diocletiáno Imperatóre, cum habéret principátum primæ cohórtis, jussus est, sub título christianitátis, ligári in médio campo, et sagittári a milítibus, atque ad últimum fústibus cædi, donec defíceret.
entries.eng: There also, at the Catacombs, the holy martyr Sebastian, commander of the first cohort under the Emperor Diocletian. Being convicted of Christianity, he was tied up in the midst of a field and shot at by the soldiers, but in the end he was beaten to death with cudgels.

entries.lat: Nicǽæ, in Bithýnia, sancti Neóphyti Mártyris, qui, quintumdécimum annum ætátis agens, flagris cæsus, in fornácem immíssus, feris objéctus, et, cum illǽsus permanéret et Christi fidem constánter profiterétur, gládio tandem occísus est.
entries.eng: At Nice, in Bithynia, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Neophitus, who in the fifteenth year of his age was flogged, cast into a furnace, and thrown to wild beasts, and for as much as he remained unhurt and constantly professed the faith of Christ, he was at length beheaded.

entries.lat: Cæsénæ sancti Mauri Epíscopi, virtútibus et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Caesena, (in the tenth century,) holy Maurus, Bishop of that see, famous for graces and miracles.

entries.lat: In Palæstína natális sancti Euthýmii Abbátis, qui zelo cathólicæ disciplínæ et virtúte miraculórum, témpore Marciáni Imperatóris, in Ecclésia flóruit.
entries.eng: In Palestine, holy Euthymius, (surnamed the Great,) Abbot (near Jerusalem,) who flourished in the Church in the time of the Emperor Marcian, filled with zeal for catholic discipline, and marked by the power of working miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctæ Agnétis, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Præfécto Urbis Symphrónio, ígnibus injécta, sed iis per oratiónem ejus exstínctis, gládio percússa est. De ea beátus Hierónymus hæc scribit: « Omnium géntium lítteris atque linguis, præcípue in Ecclésiis, Agnétis vita laudáta est; quæ et ætátem vicit et tyránnum, et títulum castitátis martýrio consecrávit ».
entries.eng: At Rome, under Symphronius, Prefect of the city, the holy Virgin and martyr Agnes. She was cast into the fire, but the fire died out at her prayer, and then she was smitten with the sword, Blessed Jerome writeth concerning her. The life of Agnes hath been praised in the writings and in the tongues of all nations, and most chiefly in the churches. She overcame not only the tyrant but also the weakness of her own age, and hallowed by martyrdom the title of virgin.

entries.lat: Athénis natális sancti Públii Epíscopi, qui Atheniénsium Ecclésiam, post sanctum Dionýsium Areopagítam, nobíliter rexit; et, præclárus virtútibus ac doctrínæ laude præfúlgens, ob Christi martýrium glorióse coronátur.
entries.eng: At Athens, the birthday of the holy Bishop Publius, who nobly ruled the Church of the Athenians after St. Denis the Areopagite; and, renowned for his virtues and shining forth in the praise of his learning, was gloriously crowned with martyrdom for Christ.

entries.lat: Tarracóne, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Fructuósi Epíscopi, Augúrii et Eulógii Diaconórum. Hi, témpore Galliéni, primo in cárcerem trusi, deínde flammis injécti, et, exústis vínculis, mánibus in modum crucis expánsis orántes, martýrium complevérunt; in quorum die natáli sanctus Augustínus sermónem ad pópulum hábuit.
entries.eng: Holy Augustin preached to the people upon their feast-day.

entries.lat: In monastério Einsidlénsi, apud Helvétios, sancti Meinrádi, Presbýteri et Mónachi; qui eódem in loco, ubi póstea monastérium ipsum excrévit, eremíticæ inténtus vitæ, a latrónibus interféctus est. Ipsíus vero beáti viri corpus, olim in Augiénsi Germániæ monastério sepúltum, ad Einsidlénse monastérium deínde relátum fuit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Einsiedeln, in Switzerland, holy Meinrad, Priest and Monk; who, intent upon the eremitical life in that same place where the monastery itself afterwards grew up, was slain by robbers. The body of this blessed man, formerly buried in the monastery of Reichenau in Germany, was afterwards brought back to the monastery of Einsiedeln.

entries.lat: Trecis, in Gállia, sancti Pátrocli Mártyris, qui martýrii corónam sub Aureliáno Imperatóre proméruit.
entries.eng: At Troyes, (in Champagne,) the holy martyr Patroclus, who gained the crown of martyrdom under the Emperor Aurelian.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Epiphánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Confessor Epiphanius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Valéntiæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Vincéntii, Levítæ et Mártyris; qui, sub impiíssimo Prǽside Daciáno, cárceres, famem, equúleum, distorsiónes membrórum, láminas candéntes, férream cratem ignítam áliaque tormentórum génera perpéssus, ad martýrii prǽmium evolávit in cælum; cujus passiónis nóbilem triúmphum Prudéntius luculénter vérsibus exséquitur, et beátus Augustínus ac sanctus Leo Papa summis láudibus comméndant.
entries.eng: At Valentia, in Spain, the holy Levite and martyr Vincent. Under the wicked Prefect Dacian he suffered imprisonment, starvation, racking, twisting of his limbs, red-hot plates, and bed of red-hot iron, and other kinds of torments, and passed away to heaven to receive there a martyr's reward, The glorious triumph of his passion hath been set forth by Prudentius in noble poetry, and the blessed Augustine and the holy Pope Leo have praised him in the highest language.

entries.lat: Apud Bethsáloën, in Assýria, sancti Anastásii Persæ Mónachi, qui, post plúrima torménta cárceris, vérberum et vinculórum, quæ in Cæsaréa Palæstínæ perpéssus fúerat, a Persárum Rege Chósroa multis pœnis afféctus, ad últimum decollátus est, cum prius septuagínta Sócios, qui fúerant in fluénta demérsi, ad martýrium præmisísset. Ejus caput Romam, ad Aquas Sálvias, delátum est, una cum veneránda ejus imágine, cujus aspéctu fugári dǽmones morbósque curári, Acta secúndi Concílii Nicǽni testántur.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy monk Anastasius, who, after enduring many torments of imprisonment, stripes, and bonds at Caesarea, in Palestine, suffered much again under Chosroes, King of the Persians, and was at length beheaded, when he had sent before him seventy companions who suffered martyrdom by drowning, His head and his venerable image were afterwards brought to Rome, and the acts of the Second Council of Nicea bear witness that at the sight of them devils fly and diseases are healed.

entries.lat: Ebredúni, in Gálliis, sanctórum Mártyrum Vincéntii, Oróntii et Victóris, qui martýrio in Diocletiáni persecutióne coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Embrun, in France, the holy Martyrs Vincent, Orontius and Victor, who were crowned with martyrdom in the persecution of Diocletian.

entries.lat: Nováriæ sancti Gaudéntii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Novara, holy Gaudentius, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: Soræ sancti Domínici Abbátis, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Sora, the holy Abbot Dominic, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Sancti Raymúndi de Péñafort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, cujus dies natális octávo Idus Januárii recólitur.
entries.eng: Holy Raymund of Peñafort, of the Order of Preachers, Confessor, whose birthday is kept on the 6th day of January.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Emerentiánæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ adhuc catechúmena, dum oráret ad sepúlcrum sanctæ Agnétis, cujus fúerat collactánea, a Gentílibus lapidáta est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Emerentiana, who while as yet she was making her ready to be baptized, was stoned to death by the Gentiles while she was praying at the grave of her holy foster-sister Agnes.

entries.lat: Philíppis, in Macedónia, sancti Pármenæ, qui fuit unus de septem primis Diáconis. Hic, tráditus grátiæ Dei, injúnctum sibi a frátribus offícium prædicatiónis plena fide consúmmans, martýrii glóriam, sub Trajáno, est adéptus.
entries.eng: At Philippi, in Macedonia, holy Parmenas, one of the first seven Deacons. He yielded himself wholly to the grace of God, discharged in the fulness of faith the office of preaching which had been laid upon him by the brethren, and obtained the glory of martyrdom under the Emperor Trajan.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, sancti Cleméntis Epíscopi, qui, sǽpius cruciátus, tandem, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, in Galatia, (in the fourth century,) holy Clement, Bishop of that see, who had often been put to the torture, but at length achieved martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Agathángeli, qui eódem die, sub Lúcio Prǽside, passus est.
entries.eng: There likewise, (in the fourth century,) upon the same day, and under the President Lucius, the holy martyr Agathangelus.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Mauritánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Severiáni et Aquilæ uxóris, ígnibus combustórum.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Morocco, of the holy martyrs Severian and Aquila, his wife, who were burnt.

entries.lat: Apud Antínoum, Ægýpti urbem, sancti Asclæ Mártyris, qui, post divérsa torménta, pretiósam Deo ánimam, in flumen præcipitátus, réddidit.
entries.eng: At Antinoe, in Egypt, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Aselas, who after suffering diverse torments was cast into the Nile, and rendered up his precious soul to God.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Joánnis Eleemosynárii, ejúsdem urbis Epíscopi, misericórdia in páuperes celebérrimi.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, holy John, surnamed the Almoner, Pope of that city, very famous for his pity toward the poor.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, sancti Ildefónsi Epíscopi, qui, ob singulárem vitæ integritátem, susceptámque fídei defensiónem advérsus hæréticos, sanctíssimæ Dei Genitrícis virginitátem impugnántes, ab eádem Vírgine María donátus est candidíssima veste ac demum, sanctitáte célebris, in cælum vocátus.
entries.eng: At Toledo, holy Ildefonsus, Archbishop of that city, who on account of the singular purity of his life, and the defence of the virginity of the Mother of God against the heretics who impugned it which he took up, was first gifted, by the same most Blessed Virgin with a chasuble of the purest white, and afterwards called away to heaven, famous for holiness,.

entries.lat: In Província Valériæ sancti Martýrii Mónachi, cujus méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: In the province of Valeria, (in the sixth century,) the holy monk Martyrius, of whom the blessed Pope Gregory maketh mention.

entries.lat: Apud Ephesum sancti Timóthei, qui fuit discípulus beáti Pauli Apóstoli; atque, ab eódem Ephesi ordinátus Epíscopus, ibi post multos pro Christo agónes, cum Diánæ immolántes argúeret, lapídibus óbrutus est, ac paulo post obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: Holy Timothy, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul, by whom he was ordained Bishop of Ephesus. After many contendings for Christ, because he rebuked them that were offering sacrifice to Diana, they stoned him, and a short while thereafter he fell asleep in the Lord,.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Bábilæ Epíscopi, qui, in persecutióne Décii, póstea quam frequénter passiónibus suis ac cruciátibus glorificáverat Deum, gloriósæ vitæ finem sortítus est in vínculis férreis, cum quibus et suum corpus sepelíri mandávit. Referúntur étiam passi cum eo tres púeri, scílicet Urbánus, Prilidiánus et Epolónius, quos ille in Christi fide instrúxerat.
entries.eng: At Antioch, holy Babilas, Patriarch of that city. After he had oftentimes glorified God by the sufferings and torments which he bore, and in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, he ended his glorious life in iron fetters, which he commanded should be buried with him. It is recorded also that there suffered with him three children Urban, Prilidian, and Epolonius whom he had instructed in the faith of Christ.

entries.lat: Fulgínei, in Umbria, sancti Feliciáni, qui, a sancto Victóre Papa Primo Epíscopus ejúsdem civitátis ordinátus, illic, post multos labóres, in última senectúte, sub Décio Imperatóre, martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: At Foligno, holy Felician, who was ordained by Pope Victor Bishop of that city, and after many labours was crowned with martyrdom in extreme old age, in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: Neocæsaréæ, in Mauritánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Mardónii, Musónii, Eugénii et Metélli; qui omnes igni tráditi sunt, et eórum relíquiæ in flumen dispérsæ.
entries.eng: At Neo-Caesarea, the holy martyrs Mardonius, Musonius, Eugenius, and Metellus, these all were burnt and their ashes thrown into the river.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Thyrsi et Projécti.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Thyrsus, (third century,) and Projectus, (Bishop of Clermont, in the year 674.).

entries.lat: Cínguli, in Picéno, sancti Exsuperántii Confessóris, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, ob miraculórum famam illústris.
entries.eng: At Cingoli, in Piceno, the holy Confessor Exsuperantius, Bishop of that city, illustrious for the fame of his miracles.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Zamæ, qui, a sancto Dionýsio, Románo Pontífice, primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus, illic Christiánam fidem mirífice propagávit.
entries.eng: At Bologna, holy Zama, who, ordained first Bishop of that city by St. Dionysius, the Roman Pontiff, wonderfully propagated the Christian faith there.

entries.lat: Item beáti Suráni Abbátis, qui, témpore Longobardórum, sanctitáte flóruit.
entries.eng: Likewise (in the sixth century,) the blessed Abbot Suran, who flourished in holiness in the time of the Lombards.

entries.lat: Convérsio sancti Pauli Apóstoli, quæ fuit anno secúndo ab Ascensióne Dómini.
entries.eng: The Conversion of St. Paul the Apostle, which took place in the second year after the Ascension of the Lord.

entries.lat: Apud Damáscum natális sancti Ananíæ, qui fuit discípulus Dómini, et eúndem Paulum Apóstolum baptizávit. Ipse autem, cum Damásci, et Eleutherópoli, alibíque Evangélium prædicásset, tandem, sub Licínio Júdice, nervis cæsus et laniátus, ac lapídibus oppréssus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Damascus, holy Ananias, who baptized the aforesaid apostle. He preached the Gospel at Damascus and at other places, and was first scourged and rent with thongs, and then stoned to death under the judge Licinius.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sanctórum Præjécti Epíscopi, et Amaríni, Abbátis Cloroangiénsis, qui ambo a procéribus ejúsdem urbis passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Clermont, in France, the holy Bishop Praejectus, and Amarinus, Abbot of Cloroange, who both suffered at the hands of the chief men of that city.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Juventíni et Máximi, qui, sub Juliáno Apóstata, martýrio coronáti sunt; in quorum die natáli sanctus Joánnes Chrysóstomus sermónem ad pópulum hábuit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Juventinus and Maximus, who were crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and on whose feast-day holy John Chrysostom preached unto the people.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Donáti, Sabíni et Agapis.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Donatus, Sabinus, and Agapis.

entries.lat: Tomis, in Scýthia, sancti Bretanniónis Epíscopi, qui mira sanctitáte et cathólicæ fídei zelo, sub Ariáno Imperatóre Valénte, cui fórtiter réstitit, in Ecclésia flóruit.
entries.eng: At Tomis, in Scythia, holy Bretannion, Bishop (of that see), who flourished in the Church in wonderful holiness and zeal for the Catholic faith under the Arian Emperor Valens, whom he withstood stoutly.

entries.lat: Marciánis, in Gállia, sancti Poppónis, Presbýteri et Abbátis, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Marchiennes, in France, holy Poppo, Priest and Abbot, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Sancti Polycárpi, Epíscopi Smyrnénsis et Mártyris, qui martýrii corónam séptimo Kaléndas Mártii consecútus est.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, holy Polycarp, a disciple of the blessed Apostle John, and by him ordained Bishop of that city, having the charge of all Asia. In the reign of Mark Antony, and Lucius Aurelius Commodus, as the Pro-consul was sitting in the amphitheatre all the people cried out against Polycarp, and to please them he was cast into the fire, but forasmuch as it burned him not he was pierced with the sword, and so received the crown of martyrdom, With him there suffered also twelve others that were come from Philadelphia unto the city aforesaid.

entries.lat: Hippóne Régio, in Africa, sanctórum Theógenis Epíscopi, et aliórum trigínta sex, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, contemnéntes temporálem mortem, corónam ætérnæ vitæ adépti sunt.
entries.eng: At Hippo, in Africa, the holy martyrs Theogenes, Bishop of that city, and thirty-six others, who in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian reckoned cheaply death here in time, and received the crown of life eternal,.

entries.lat: Apud Béthlehem Judæ dormítio sanctæ Paulæ Víduæ, quæ, cum esset e nobilíssimo Senatórum génere, cum beata Vírgine Christi Eustóchio, fília sua, renúntians sǽculo, facultátes suas paupéribus distríbuit, et ad Præsépe Dómini se recépit; ibíque, multis virtútibus prǽdita et longo coronáta martýrio, ad cæléstia regna transívit. Ipsíus autem vitam, virtútibus admirándam, sanctus Hierónymus scripsit.
entries.eng: At Bethlehem of Judah, the holy widow Paula, mother of Eustochium, the virgin of Christ. She was of a very noble senatorial family, that gave up the world and distributed all her goods to feed the poor and betook herself to the manger of the Lord, and thence passed away into the kingdom of heaven endowed with many graces and crowned with a long martyrdom, Jerome hath written of her life, full of graces.

entries.lat: Sancti Joánnis Chrysóstomi, Epíscopi Constantinopolitáni, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cæléstis Oratórum sacrórum Patróni; qui décimo octávo Kaléndas Octóbris obdormívit in Dómino. Ejus sacrum corpus, sub Theodósio junióre, hac die Constantinópolim, inde póstea Romam translátum fuit, et in Basílica Príncipis Apostolórum cónditum.
entries.eng: The feast of holy John, Patriarch of Constantinople, surnamed Chrysostom that is to say, golden mouth on account of the golden stream of his eloquence, whose word and example much profited the Church, but after many toils he ended his life in exile. Mention is made of him upon the 14th day of September, but the 27th of January is the day whereon his sacred body was brought to Constantinople under the Emperor Theodosius the younger, whence it was afterward brought to Rome, and buried in the Basilica of the Prince of the Apostles.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ natális sanctæ Angelæ Meríci Vírginis, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, quæ Societátem Vírginum sanctæ Ursulæ instítuit, quarum præcípuum munus esset dirígere adolescéntulas in vias Dómini. Ejus tamen festívitas Kaléndas Júnii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Virgin Angela Merici, Foundress of the Society of Nuns of St. Ursula, whose first duty is to lead young maidens into the paths of the Lord. We keep her festival upon the last day of May, in accordance with an ordinance of Pius VII.

entries.lat: Apud Cenómanos, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Juliáni, ejúsdem urbis primi Epíscopi, quem sanctus Petrus illuc ad prædicándum Evangélium misit.
entries.eng: At Le Mans, in France, the burial of holy Julian, first Bishop of that city, whom St. Peter sent thither to preach the Gospel.

entries.lat: Soræ sancti Juliáni Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Antoníni, sub Flaviáno Prǽside, comprehénsus est, et, cum idolórum templum, dum ipse torquerétur, corruísset, martýrii corónam, truncáto cápite, accépit.
entries.eng: At Sora, the holy martyr Julian. He was arrested in the persecution under the Emperor Antonine, and while he was being tortured, the temple of the idols fell down, whereupon he was beheaded, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Avíti Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Africa, (in the third century,) the holy martyr Avitus.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Dátii, Reátri et Sociórum, qui in persecutióne Wandálica passi sunt.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyrs Datius, Reater, and their companions, who suffered in the persecution under the Vandals.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Datívi, Juliáni, Vincéntii atque aliórum vigínti septem Mártyrum.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyrs Dativus, Julian, Vincent, and twenty-seven others.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Vitaliáni Papæ.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Pope Vitalian.

entries.lat: In monastério Bodacénsi, in Gállia, sancti Mauri Abbátis.
entries.eng: At the monastery of La Val-Benois, the holy Maurus, Abbot of Val-Benois.

entries.lat: Sancti Petri Nolásci Confessóris, qui Ordinis beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum éxstitit Fundátor, et octávo Kaléndas Januárii obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: Holy Peter Nolasco, Confessor, who was the Founder of the Order of Blessed Mary of Mercy for the ransom of captives, and fell asleep in the Lord on the 25th day of December.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Agnétis, Vírginis et Mártyris, secúndo.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Agnes, Virgin and Martyr, for the second time.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ natális sancti Cyrílli, ejúsdem urbis Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, cathólicæ fídei præclaríssimus propugnátor, doctrína et sanctitáte illústris quiévit in pace. Ejus tamen festívitas quinto Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, a multitude of holy martyrs, who upon this day were gathered together in a church at Communion, when they were massacred in diverse ways by the followers of the Arian Duke Syrianus, Likewise at Alexandria, the holy Confessor Cyril, Pope of that city a most eminent champion of the Catholic faith, and illustrious for his teaching and holiness, who fell asleep in peace, whose feast we keep upon the 9th day of February.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Flaviáni Mártyris, qui sub Diocletiáno passus est.
entries.eng: At Rome likewise, the holy martyr Flavian, who suffered in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, hac ipsa die, a factióne Syriáni, Ducis Ariáni, dum in Ecclésia synáxim ágerent, divérso mortis génere sunt interémpti.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the passion of many holy Martyrs, who on this very day, while they were celebrating the synaxis in the Church, were put to death by divers kinds of death by the faction of Syrianus, an Arian general.

entries.lat: Apollóniæ sanctórum Mártyrum Leúcii, Thyrsi et Calliníci; qui, témpore Décii Imperatóris, váriis tormentórum genéribus cruciáti, ac primus et últimus abscissióne cápitis, médius cælésti voce evocátus spíritum reddens, martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: At Apollonia, the holy martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius, Callinicus. In the time of the Emperor Decius they were tortured in diverse ways. Whereafter, Thyrsus and Callinicus were beheaded, and a voice from heaven called away Leucius, and he gave up the ghost,.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sanctórum Mártyrum Leónidæ et Sociórum, qui, témpore Diocletiáni, palmam martýrii sunt assecúti.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, the holy martyrs Leonides and his companions, who secured the palm of martyrdom in the time of the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Cæsaraugústæ, in Hispánia, sancti Valérii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Zaragoza, holy Valerius, Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Conchæ, in Hispánia, natális sancti Juliáni Epíscopi, qui, érogans in páuperes bona Ecclésiæ, ópera mánuum sibi more Apostólico victum quærens, clarus miráculis quiévit in pace.
