entries.eng: At Cuenca, in Spain, the birthday of the holy Bishop Julian, who, bestowing the goods of the Church upon the poor and seeking his living, after the Apostolic manner, by the labour of his hands, rested in peace, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: In monastério Reomaénsi, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Joánnis Presbýteri, viri Deo devóti.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Réome, in France, the burial of the holy Priest John, a man devoted to God.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sancti Jacóbi Eremítæ, qui, post lapsum, diu, pæniténtiæ causa, in sepúlcro látuit, et clarus miráculis migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: In Palestine, the holy Hermit James, who, after a fall, lay hidden for a long time in a sepulchre for the sake of penance, and, famous for miracles, passed to the Lord.

entries.lat: Sancti Francísci Salésii, Epíscopi Gebennénsis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, ómnium Scriptórum catholicórum, diáriis aliísve scriptis in vulgus edéndis sapiéntiam Christiánam illustrántium ac provehéntium et tutántium, peculiáris apud Deum Patróni; qui migrávit in cælum quinto Kaléndas Januárii, sed hac die, ob Translatiónem córporis ejus, potíssimum cólitur.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Francis de Sales, Bishop of Geneva, of whom mention is made upon the 28th day of December.

entries.lat: Tréviris deposítio beáti Valérii Epíscopi, qui fuit discípulus sancti Petri Apóstoli.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Valerius, Bishop of that see, (in the first century,) a disciple of the holy Apostle Peter.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Nomentána, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Pápiæ et Mauri mílitum, témpore Diocletiáni Imperatóris; quorum ora jussit Laodícius, Urbis Præféctus, ad primam Christi confessiónem lapídibus contúndi, et sic eos in cárcerem trahi, ac póstea fústibus cædi, atque ad últimum plumbátis pércuti, donec exspirárent.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Nomentan Way, the holy soldiers Papias and Maurus, martyrs in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, (fourth century.) At their first confession of Christ, Laodicius, the Prefect of the city, ordered their mouths to be bruised with stones and committed them to prison where they were afterwards cudgelled and then lashed to death with scourges loaded with lead.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sancti Constántii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, una cum Sóciis, sub Marco Aurélio Imperatóre, ob fídei defensiónem, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Perugia, the holy martyrs Constantius, Bishop of that see, and his companions, who were crowned for defending the faith in the persecution under the Emperor Marcus Aurelius.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Aquilíni Presbýteri, qui, ab Ariánis gládio in gutture transfíxus, martýrio coronátur.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Priest Aquilinus, who was crowned with martyrdom, (in the eighth century,) by being run through the neck with a sword by the Arians.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sanctórum Mártyrum Sarbélii et Bárbeæ soróris, qui, a beáto Barsimǽo Epíscopo baptizáti, ambo, in persecutióne Trajáni, sub Lýsia Prǽside, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, the holy martyrs Sarbelius and his sister, Barbea, who were baptized by blessed Barsimceus, Bishop of that city, and were crowned with martyrdom under the President Lysias, in the persecution under the Emperor Trajan, (in the second century.).

entries.lat: In território Tricassíno sancti Sabiniáni Mártyris, qui, jubénte Aureliáno Imperatóre, pro fide Christi decollátus est.
entries.eng: In the country of Trois, the holy martyr Sabinian, who was beheaded for Christ's faith's sake, by order of the Emperor Aurelian.

entries.lat: Apud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, sancti Sulpícii Sevéri Epíscopi, virtútibus et eruditióne conspícui.
entries.eng: At Bourges, holy Sulpicius Severus, Bishop of that see, famous for his graces and learning.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Martínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, cujus dies natális Kaléndis Januárii recólitur.
entries.eng: Holy Martina, Virgin and Martyr, whose birthday is kept on the 1st day of January.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sancti Barsimǽi Epíscopi, qui, cum Gentíles plúrimos convertísset ad fidem et præmisísset ad corónam, eos secútus est, sub Trajáno, cum palma martýrii.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, the holy martyr Barsimceus, Bishop of that city, who converted many Gentiles to the faith, and sent them before him to the crown, but himself followed them with the palm of martyrdom under the Emperor Trajan, (second century.) Likewise, at Edessa, holy Barsen, Bishop of that See, who was famous for the grace of healing, but who on account of his Catholic belief was banished to the uttermost parts of that country by the Arian Emperor Valens, and there finished his earthly life,.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ pássio beáti Hippólyti Presbýteri, qui, decéptus aliquándiu schísmate Nováti, sed, operánte grátia Christi, corréctus, ad unitátem Ecclésiæ rédiit, pro qua et in qua póstea illústre martýrium consummávit. Hic, rogátus a suis quænam secta vérior esset, exsecrátus est dogma Nováti, et, eam fidem dicens esse servándam quam Petri Cáthedra custodíret, júgulum prǽbuit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the blessed martyr Hippolytus, (third century.) He was a Priest who had been led astray into the Novatian schism, but by the operation of the grace of Christ had corrected himself, and had returned into the unity of the Church, for which and within which he afterwards achieved a noble martyrdom. When he was asked by his people which were the true Body, he denied the doctrine of Novatus, and declared that the faith which men ought to keep is the faith which the See of Peter keepeth, and so offered his neck to the executioner.

entries.lat: In Africa pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Feliciáni, Philippiáni et aliórum centum vigínti quátuor.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Felician, Philappian, and 124 others.

entries.lat: Item beáti Alexándri, qui, in persecutióne Décii, comprehénsus est, ac, longǽvæ ætátis veneránda canítie et confessióne iteráta respléndens, inter carníficum torménta réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: Likewise the blessed Alexander. He was arrested in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, and died under the torture, venerable for his grey hairs and illustrious for his repeated confession.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sancti Barsis Epíscopi, dono curatiónum illústris; qui, a Valénte, Imperatóre Ariáno, in díssitas regiónes ob fidem cathólicam relegátus, ac tríplici mutatióne fatigátus exsílii, vitam finívit.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, the holy Bishop Barses, illustrious for the gift of healing; who, banished by Valens, the Arian Emperor, into remote regions for the Catholic faith, and worn out by a threefold change of exile, ended his life.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis natális sancti Matthíæ Epíscopi, de quo mira et plena fídei gesta narrántur; qui, sub Hadriáno, multa pro Christo perpéssus est, ac demum in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, holy Matthias, Patriarch of that place, (in the second century,) of whom are narrated wondrous acts of faith. He suffered much for Christ's sake under the Emperor Hadrian, but at length fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Armentárii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Confessor Armentarius, Bishop of that See,.

entries.lat: In Malbódio, Hannóniæ monastério, sanctæ Aldegúndis Vírginis, témpore Dagobérti Regis.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Maubeuge, in Hainaut, in the time of King Dagobert, the holy Virgin Aldegundis,.

entries.lat: Vitérbii sanctæ Hyacínthæ de Mariscóttis Vírginis, ex tértio sancti Francísci Ordine Sanctimoniális, pæniténtia et caritáte insígnis; quam Pius Papa Séptimus Sanctis adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Viterbo, the holy Virgin Hyacinth de' Mariscotti, a nun of the Third Order of St. Francis, eminent for penitence and for love, whose name Pope Pius VII enrolled with those of the saints.

entries.lat: Medioláni sanctæ Savínæ, féminæ religiosíssimæ, quæ, ad sepúlcra sanctórum Nabóris et Felícis Mártyrum orans, obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Savina, a devout woman, who fell asleep in the Lord, while she was praying at the graves of the holy martyrs Nabor and Felix.

entries.lat: In território Parisiénsi sanctæ Bathíldis Regínæ, sanctitáte et miraculórum glória præcláræ.
entries.eng: In the territory of Paris, the holy Queen Bathildis, renowned for holiness and the glory of her miracles.

entries.lat: Augústæ Taurinórum sancti Joánnis Bosco, Confessóris, Societátis Salesiánæ ac Institúti Filiárum Maríæ Auxiliatrícis Fundatóris, animárum zelo et fídei propagándæ conspícui, quem Pius Papa Undécimus Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Turin, holy John Bosco, Confessor, Founder of the Salesian Society and of the Institute of the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians, famous for his zeal for souls and for the spreading of the faith, whom Pope Pius XI inscribed in the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Portuénsi, sanctórum Mártyrum Cyri et Joánnis, qui, pro confessióne Christi, post multa torménta, cápite truncáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Via Portuensis, the holy Martyrs Cyrus and John, who, for the confession of Christ, after many torments, were beheaded.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ natális sancti Metráni Mártyris, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre, cum ad jussiónem Paganórum nollet ímpia verba proférre, hi totum ejus corpus fústibus collisérunt, vultúmque et óculos præacútis cálamis terebrántes, cum cruciátibus expulérunt ipsum extra urbem, ibíque lapídibus oppréssum interemérunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Metranus. In the time of the Emperor Decius he refused to utter unlawful words at the command of the Pagans. Wherefore they bruised his whole body with cudgels, pierced his face and eyes with sharp reeds, and continued to torture him while they cast him out of the city, where they stoned him to death, There, likewise, the holy martyrs Saturninus, Thyrsus, and Victor.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni, Thyrsi et Victóris.
entries.eng: In the same place, the holy Martyrs Saturninus, Thyrsus and Victor.

entries.lat: Item Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Tharsícii, Zótici, Cyríaci et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In the same city, the holy martyrs Tharsicius, Zoticus, Cyriacus, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Cýzici, in Hellespónto, sanctæ Tryphǽnæ Mártyris, quæ, plúrimis torméntis superátis, a tauro demum necáta, martýrii palmam proméruit.
entries.eng: At Cyzicus, on the Hellespont, the holy martyr Triphenes, who overcame diverse torments, and then gained the palm of martyrdom by being killed by a bull.

entries.lat: Mútinæ sancti Geminiáni Epíscopi, miraculórum glória conspícui.
entries.eng: At Modena, holy Geminian, (after the year 390,) Bishop of that see, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: In Província Mediolanénsi sancti Júlii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, témpore Imperatóris Theodósii.
entries.eng: In the province of Milan, in the time of the Emperor Theodosius, (fifth century,) the holy Confessor Julius the Priest.

entries.lat: Neápoli sancti Francísci Xavérii-Maríæ Biánchi, Confessóris, Clérici Reguláris sancti Pauli, signis, donis cæléstibus et admirábili patiéntia illústris, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus ad suprémos honóres Sanctórum éxtulit.
entries.eng: At Naples, holy Francis Xavier Mary Bianchi, Confessor, a Clerk Regular of St. Paul, illustrious for signs, heavenly gifts and wonderful patience, whom Pope Pius XII raised to the supreme honours of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Marcéllæ Víduæ, cujus præcláras laudes beátus Hierónymus scripsit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy widow Marcella, whose excellences have been written by blessed Jerome.

entries.lat: Item Romæ Beátæ Ludovícæ Albertóniæ, Víduæ Románæ, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, virtútibus claræ.
entries.eng: At Rome, likewise, the blessed widow Louisa Albertoni, of the 3rd Order of St. Francis, illustrious for her graces.

entries.lat: Eódem die Translátio sancti Marci Evangelístæ, cum sacrum ejus corpus ex Alexandría, a bárbaris tunc occupáta, Venétias allátum, ibídem in majóri Ecclésia, ejus nómine consecráta, honorificentíssime cónditum fuit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day is commemorated the translation of the holy Evangelist Mark, when his sacred body was taken from Alexandria, in Egypt, already occupied by the Mohammedans, and brought to Venice, where it is honourably buried in the great cathedral church consecrated in his name.

entries.lat: Sancti Ignátii, Epíscopi Antiochéni et Mártyris, qui glorióse martýrium consummávit tertiodécimo Kaléndas Januárii.
entries.eng: The holy martyr Ignatius, who ruled the church of Antioch as the third Bishop of that See in succession to the blessed Apostle Peter.

entries.lat: Smyrnæ sancti Piónii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, post apologías pro fide Christiána conscríptas, post squalórem cárceris, ubi multos fratrum ad martýrii tolerántiam suis exhortatiónibus roborávit, tandem, cruciátibus multis vexátus, clavis confíxus et ardénti rogo superpósitus, beátum pro Christo finem sortítus est. Cum ipso autem et álii quíndecim passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, the holy martyr Pionius. He was a Priest who had written much controversial matter on behalf of the Christian faith. After suffering a foul imprisonment, during the which he strengthened many brethren by his exhortations to the enduring of martyrdom, he was put to many tortures and nailed upon a pyre, where he obtained a blessed end by being burnt for Christ's sake. And with him suffered fifteen others,.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Sevéri Epíscopi, qui, ob præclára mérita, signo colúmbæ fuit eléctus.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, holy Severus, Bishop of that city, to the which place he was chosen, on account of his extraordinary merits, through a miraculous sign in the form of a dove.

entries.lat: In civitáte Tricastína, in Gállia, sancti Pauli Epíscopi, cujus vita virtútibus cláruit, et mors pretiósa miráculis commendátur.
entries.eng: At Tron, in Gaul, (in the fifth century,) holy Paul, Bishop of that see, whose life shone with grace, and the preciousness of whose death is attested by miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Kildáriam, in Hibérnia, sanctæ Brígidæ Vírginis, quæ cum lignum altáris tetigísset in testimónium virginitátis suæ, lignum ipsum statim víride factum est.
entries.eng: In Ireland, the holy Virgin Brigid. At the moment that she bowed down her head to receive the hallowed veil, she chanced to touch the wooden steps of the altar with her hand, and in witness to her virginity the dry wood at once became green.

entries.lat: Apud Castrum Florentínum, in Etrúria, beátæ Viridiánæ, Vírginis reclúsæ, ex Ordine Vallis Umbrósæ.
entries.eng: At Castelfiorentino, in Tuscany, blessed Verdiana, Virgin and recluse, of the Order of Vallombrosa.

entries.lat: Purificátio beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, quæ a Græcis Hypapánte Dómini appellátur.
entries.eng: The Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which is called by the Greeks the Hypapante of the Lord.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Cornélii Centuriónis, quem beátus Petrus Apóstolus baptizávit, et apud præfátam urbem Episcopáli sublimávit honóre.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, (in the first century,) the holy centurion Cornelius, who was baptized by the holy Apostle St Peter, and by him also raised to be Bishop in that city.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Salária, pássio sancti Aproniáni Commentariénsis, qui, adhuc Gentílis, cum sanctum Sisínium e cárcere edúceret ut Laodício Præfécto præsentáret, vocémque de cælo factam audíret: « Veníte, benedícti Patris mei, percípite regnum, quod vobis parátum est a constitutióne mundi », credens baptizátur, et póstea, in confessióne Dómini, vitæ finem senténtia capitáli accépit.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Apronian. He was a notary, who, while he was a Gentile, was leading the holy Licinius out of prison to present him before the Prefect Laodicius, when he heard a voice from heaven saying, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom which is prepared for you from the foundation of the world," whereupon he believed, and was baptized, and was afterwards put to death confessing the Lord.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Fortunáti, Feliciáni, Firmi et Cándidi.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyrs Fortunatus, Felician, Firmus, and Candidus.

entries.lat: Aureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Flósculi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Orleans, holy Flosculus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Cantuáriæ, in Anglia, natális sancti Lauréntii Epíscopi, qui, post sanctum Augustínum, eam Ecclésiam gubernávit, et Regem ipsum ad fidem convértit.
entries.eng: At Canterbury, in England, holy Laurence, Archbishop of that see, which he governed in succession to holy Augustin, and converted king Ethelbert himself to the faith. We keep his feast upon the morrow after.

entries.lat: Prati, in Etrúria, sanctæ Catharínæ de Rícciis, Vírginis Florentínæ, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, ob cæléstium donórum cópiam insígnis; quam Benedíctus Décimus quartus, Póntifex Máximus, sanctárum Vírginum fastis adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Prato, in Tuscany, the holy Florentine Virgin Katherine di Ricci, of the Order of Friars Preachers, eminent for the abundance of her gifts from heaven, whose name the Supreme Pontiff Bendict XIV. enrolled among those of holy virgins.

entries.lat: Burdígalæ sanctæ Joánnæ de Lestonnác, Víduæ, Institúti Filiárum beátæ Vírginis Maríæ Fundatrícis, caritátis stúdio ac puellárum instituendárum cura insígnis, quam Pius Papa Duodécimus Sanctárum número accénsuit.
entries.eng: At Bordeaux, holy Joan de Lestonnac, Widow, Foundress of the Institute of the Daughters of the Blessed Virgin Mary, renowned for her zeal of charity and her care for the education of girls, whom Pope Pius XII added to the number of the Saints.

entries.lat: Sebáste, in Arménia, pássio sancti Blásii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, multórum patrátor miraculórum, sub Agricoláo Prǽside, post diútinam cæsiónem, atque in ligno suspensiónem, ubi férreis pectínibus carnes ejus dirúptæ sunt, post tetérrimum cárcerem et in lacum demérsionem, unde salvus exívit, tandem, jubénte eódem Júdice, una cum duóbus púeris, cápite truncátur. Ante ipsum vero septem mulíeres, quæ guttas sánguinis, ex ejúsdem Mártyris córpore defluéntes, dum torquerétur, colligébant, proptérea, deprehénsæ quod essent Christiánæ, omnes, post dira torménta, gládio percússæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, in Armenia, the holy martyr Blase, Bishop of that city, and the worker of many miracles. Under the President Agricolaus he was long flogged, then hung to a beam, where his flesh was rent with iron combs, then he suffered a foul imprisonment, after which he was cast into the lake, and, forasmuch as he came out thence unhurt, he was beheaded, by order of the same judge, along with two lads.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Celeríni Diáconi, qui, decem et novem dies custódia cárceris septus, in nervo et ferro variísque pœnis gloriósus fuit Christi Conféssor; et, dum inexpugnábili firmitáte certáminis sui vicit adversárium, vincéndi céteris viam fecit.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy Deacon Celerinus, who, shut up in prison for nineteen days, in the stocks and in irons and in divers torments, was a glorious Confessor of Christ; and, while he overcame the adversary by the invincible steadfastness of his combat, he made a way for others to conquer.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum trium Mártyrum, ipsíus Celeríni Diáconi consanguineórum, scílicet Laurentíni pátrui, Ignátii avúnculi, et Celérinæ áviæ, qui ántea martýrio coronáti fúerant; de quorum ómnium gloriósis láudibus exstat beáti Cypriáni epístola.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy Deacon Celerinus, who was kept nineteen days in prison, and was a glorious confessor of Christ under the lash, and in iron chains and other sufferings, and while he overcame the adversary of his contending by his invincible firmness, he led the way for victories for others, Likewise the holy martyrs Laurentinus, (these martyrs mentioned by Cyprian, Letter 34,) and Ignatius, his father's and mother's brothers, and Celerina his grandmother, who had before him been crowned with martyrdom, to the glorious praises of all whom there remaineth to witness an epistle of blessed Cyprian.

entries.lat: Item in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Felícis, Symphrónii, Hippólyti et Sociórum.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyrs Felix, Symphronius, Hippolytus, and their Companions,.

entries.lat: In óppido Vapíngo, in Gállia, sanctórum Tigídis et Remédii Episcopórum.
entries.eng: In the town of Gap, (in the second century,) the holy Bishops Tigides and Remedius.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sanctórum Lupicíni et Felícis, itidem Episcopórum.
entries.eng: At Lyon, holy Lupicinus and Felix, Bishops of that see.

entries.lat: Bremæ sancti Anschárii, Hamburgénsis ac póstea Breménsis simul Epíscopi, qui Suévos et Danos ad Christi fidem convértit, et a Gregório Papa Quarto Legátus Apostólicus totíus Septentriónis fuit institútus.
entries.eng: At Bremen, holy Anschar, Bishop of Hamburg and afterwards of Bremen together, who converted the Swedes and Danes to the faith of Christ, and was appointed by Pope Gregory IV Apostolic Legate of all the North.

entries.lat: Sancti Andréæ Corsíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fæsuláni et Confessóris, cujus dies natális ágitur octávo Idus Januárii.
entries.eng: Holy Andrew Corsini, of the Order of Carmelites, Bishop of Fiesole and Confessor, whose birthday is kept on the 6th day of January.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Eutýchii Mártyris, qui illústre martýrium consummávit, ac sepúltus est in cœmetério Callísti; ejúsque sepúlcrum póstea sanctus Dámasus Papa vérsibus exornávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Eutychius, who gained an illustrious martyrdom and is buried in the cemetery of Callistus. Holy Pope Damasus adorned his grave with some verses.

entries.lat: Thmui, in Ægýpto, pássio beáti Philéæ, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, et Philóromi, Tribúni mílitum; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cum a cognátis et amícis suadéri non possent ut sibi párcerent, ambo, datis cervícibus, palmas a Dómino meruérunt. Cum ipsis innúmera étiam multitúdo fidélium ex eádem urbe, pastóris sui vestígia sequens, martýrio coronáta est.
entries.eng: At Thmuis, in Egypt, the blessed martyr Philaeas, Bishop of that city, and Philoromus, Tribune of the troops, who in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian could not be persuaded by their kinsfolk and friends to have pity on themselves, but stretched forth their necks and won palm branches of victory from the Lord's hand and a countless multitude of the faithful of the same city, following after the example of their shepherd, were likewise crowned with martyrdom.

entries.lat: Foro Semprónii sanctórum Mártyrum Aquilíni, Gémini, Gelásii, Magni et Donáti.
entries.eng: At Fossambrono, the holy martyrs Aquilinus, Geminus, Gelasius, Magnus, and Donatus.

entries.lat: In regno Maravénsi, apud Indos Orientáles, sancti Joánnis de Britto, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu, qui, cum multos infidéles ad fidem convertísset, glorióso martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: In the kingdom of Marava, in the East Indies, holy John de Britto, Priest of the Society of Jesus, who, having converted many infidels to the faith, was crowned with a glorious martyrdom.

entries.lat: Trecis, in Gállia, sancti Aventíni, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Troyes, the holy Confessor Aventinus,.

entries.lat: Pelúsii, in Ægýpto, sancti Isidóri, Presbýteri et Mónachi, méritis et doctrína conspícui.
entries.eng: At Pelusium, in Egypt, the holy monk Isidore, (monk in desert of Lychnos, about the year 449,) eminent for his merits and teaching.

entries.lat: Sempringhámiæ, in Anglia, sancti Gilbérti, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis Sempringhamiénsis fuit Institútor.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Confessor Gilbert, founder of the Order of Sempringham, whose feast we keep upon the 11th day of this present month of February.

entries.lat: In óppido Amatrícis, in Aprútio, deposítio sancti Joséphi a Leoníssa, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum Capuccinórum et Confessóris; quem, ob fídei prædicatiónem a Mahumetánis dira perpéssum, labóribus apostólicis et miráculis clarum, Benedíctus Décimus quartus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctórum cánonem rétulit.
entries.eng: In the town of Amatrice, in the diocese of Reate, the holy Confessor Joseph of Leonissa, of the Order of Friars Minors Capuchins, who suffered much from the Mohammedans for his preaching of the faith, and was famous for his apostolic labours and his miracles whose name the Supreme Pontiff Benedict XIV. enrolled among those of the holy confessors.

entries.lat: Bremæ commemorátio sancti Rembérti, qui, sancti Anschárii discípulus, in ipsíus locum, hac die, óbitum magístri sui próxime subsequenti, olim Hamburgénsis simul ac Breménsis Epíscopus eléctus est.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Rembert, Bishop of Bremen.

entries.lat: Bitúricis, in Aquitánia, sanctæ Joánnæ de Valois, Gálliæ Regínæ, Ordinis sanctíssimæ Annuntiatiónis beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Fundatrícis, pietáte et singulári Crucis participatióne illústris, a Pio Papa Duodécimo Sanctárum fastis adscríptæ.
entries.eng: At Bourges, in Aquitaine, holy Joan of Valois, Queen of France, Foundress of the Order of the most holy Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, illustrious for piety and for a singular sharing in the Cross, inscribed by Pope Pius XII in the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: Cátanæ, in Sicília, natális sanctæ Agáthæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, tempóribus Décii Imperatóris, sub Quinctiáno Júdice, post álapas et cárcerem, post equúleum et torsiónes, post mamillárum abscissiónem, post volutatiónem in téstulis et carbónibus, tandem in cárcere, Deum precans, consummáta est.
entries.eng: At Catania, in Sicily, the holy Virgin and martyr Agatha. In the time of the Emperor Decius, under the Judge Quinctian, she endured buffeting and imprisonment, racking and torments. Her breasts were cut off, and she was rolled upon potsherds and coals, and at last died in prison, in prayer to God.

entries.lat: Nangasáchii, in Japónia, pássio vigínti sex Mártyrum, e quibus tres Sacerdótes atque unus Cléricus et duo Láici ad Ordinem Minórum, tres, et in eis unus quidem Cléricus, ad Societátem Jesu, ac septémdecim ad tértium sancti Francísci Ordinem revocántur. Hi omnes pro cathólica fide, in crucem acti et lanceárum íctibus perfóssi, inter divínas laudes ejusdémque fídei prædicatiónem, glorióse occubuérunt; et a Pio nono, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum fastis adscrípti sunt.
entries.eng: At Nagasaki, in Japan, the passion of twenty-six Martyrs, of whom three Priests, one Cleric and two Laymen belonged to the Order of Friars Minor, three (and among them one Cleric) to the Society of Jesus, and seventeen to the Third Order of St. Francis. All these, for the Catholic faith, being fastened to crosses and pierced with thrusts of lances, died gloriously amid the praises of God and the preaching of that same faith; and were inscribed in the roll of the Saints by Pope Pius IX.

entries.lat: In Ponto commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, in persecutióne Maximiáni; quorum álii plumbo liquénti perfúsi, álii acútis arundínibus in únguibus cruciáti, ac multis horréndis vexáti torméntis, iisdémque sǽpius iterátis, palmas a Dómino et corónas illústri passióne meruérunt.
entries.eng: In Pontus, are commemorated very many holy martyrs in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, (fourth century.) Some had molten lead poured upon them, some were tortured by having sharp reeds thrust under their nails, and were tormented with many most grievous sufferings, which were renewed again and again, and so by their illustrious passion earned palms and crowns from the Lord.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Isidóri, mílitis et Mártyris; qui, in persecutióne Décii, a Numeriáno, exércitus Duce, ob Christi fidem, cápite cæsus est.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Isidore, who in the persecution under the Emperor Decius was beheaded by Numerian, chief of the army, for Christ's faith's sake.

entries.lat: Viénnæ beáti Avíti, Epíscopi et Confessóris, cujus fide, indústria atque admirábili doctrína ab Ariánæ hǽresis infestatióne sunt Gálliæ defénsæ.
entries.eng: At Vienne, (in Dauphinais,) the blessed Confessor Avitus, Bishop of that see, by whose faith, labour, and wonderful teaching Gaul was shielded against the Arian heresy.

entries.lat: Sabióne, in Rhǽtia secúnda, sancti Ingenuíni Epíscopi, cujus vita miráculis éxstitit gloriósa. Sacrum vero ipsíus corpus Brixinónem póstea translátum fuit, ibíque honorífice asservátum.
entries.eng: At Säben, in Rhaetia Secunda, the holy Bishop Ingenuinus, whose life was glorious for miracles. His sacred body was afterwards translated to Brixen, and is there honourably preserved.

entries.lat: Brixinóne sancti Albuíni Epíscopi, qui eam in civitátem e Sabióne Cáthedram Episcopálem tránstulit, et ibídem, virtútum signis émicans, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Brixen, the holy Bishop Albuin, who transferred the Episcopal See from Säben to that city, and there, shining with the signs of virtues, passed to the Lord.

entries.lat: Sancti Titi, Epíscopi Creténsium et Confessóris, cujus dies natális occúrrit prídie Nonas Januárii.
entries.eng: Holy Titus, Bishop of the Cretans and Confessor, whose birthday falls on the 4th day of January.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, natális sanctæ Dorótheæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Saprício, illíus Provínciæ Prǽside, primum per equúlei extensiónem vexáta, dehinc palmis diutíssime cæsa, capitáli senténtia ad últimum puníta est. In ejus confessióne Theóphilus quidam scholásticus ad Christi fidem convérsus, et mox equúleo acérrime tortus, novíssime gládio cæsus est.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy Virgin and martyr Dorothy, who under Sapricius, President of that province, was first racked, then long scourged with palm-branches, and at length put to death. At the sight of her sufferings a certain student, named Theophilus, was converted to Christ, and forthwith grievously racked, and at length beheaded.

entries.lat: Eméssæ, in Phœnícia, sancti Silváni Epíscopi, qui, cum eídem Ecclésiæ annis quadragínta præfuísset, tandem, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, una cum duóbus áliis, objéctus feris membratímque discérptus, martýrii palmam accépit.
entries.eng: At Emessa, in Phoenicia, the holy Bishop Silvan, who, when he had been forty years in rule over that church, was cast to wild beasts along with two others, under the Emperor Maximian, and, torn to pieces, received the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni, Theóphili et Revocátæ.
entries.eng: On the same day the holy martyrs Saturninus, Theophilus, and Revocata.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Antholiáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Auvergne, in Gaul, the holy martyr Antholian.

entries.lat: Atrébati, in Gálliis, sancti Vedásti, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, cujus vita et mors plúrimis miráculis éxstitit gloriósa.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Bishop Vedastus, and holy Bishop Amandus, the first of whom ruled over the Church of Arras, the second the Church of Maastricht, whose lives and deaths were rendered glorious by diverse miracles.

entries.lat: Elnóne, in Gállia, sancti Amándi, Epíscopi Trajecténsis, qui miráculis, cum vivus tum mórtuus, glorióse refúlsit; cujus nómine póstmodum insignítum est óppidum, in quo ille monastérium exstrúxerat et mortálem vitam absólverat.
entries.eng: At Elnon, in France, holy Amandus, Bishop of Maestricht, who shone gloriously with miracles, both living and dead; from whose name the town was afterwards called, in which he had built a monastery and ended his mortal life.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Guaríni, Cardinális et Epíscopi Prænestíni, vitæ sanctitáte conspícui.
entries.eng: At Bologna, holy Guarinus, Cardinal Bishop of Palestrina, eminent for the holiness of his life.

entries.lat: Sancti Romuáldi Abbátis, Monachórum Camaldulénsium Patris, cujus dies natális tertiodécimo Kaléndas Júlii recensétur, sed festívitas hac die, ob Translatiónem córporis ejus, potíssimum celebrátur.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Abbot Romuald, father of the monks of the Camaldolese Institute, of whom mention is made upon the 19th day of June.

entries.lat: Augústæ, cui nunc Londíni nomen, in Británnia, natális beáti Auguli Epíscopi, qui, ætátis cursu per martýrium expléto, ætérna prǽmia suscípere méruit.
entries.eng: In London, the blessed Augulus, Bishop of that city, who ended his life by martyrdom, and so secured the everlasting prize.

entries.lat: In Phrýgia sancti Adáuci Mártyris, qui, ex Itálico génere clarus, et omni fere dignitátum gradu ab Imperatóribus insignítus, tandem, cum adhuc Quæstóris offício fungerétur, martýrii coróna pro fídei defensióne dignátus est.
entries.eng: In Phrygia, the holy martyr Adaucus, who, of an illustrious Italian family, and honoured by the Emperors with almost every degree of dignity, at length, while still discharging the office of Quaestor, was counted worthy of the crown of martyrdom for the defence of the faith.

entries.lat: Ibídem plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, urbis uníus cívium, quorum dux erat idem Adáucus; qui, cum omnes Christiáni essent, et constánter in fídei confessióne persísterent, a Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre sunt igne consúmpti.
entries.eng: In Phrygia, the holy martyr Adaucus. He was an Italian of noble birth, and had been honoured by the emperors with dignities of almost every rank, and was still quaestor when he gained the crown of martyrdom in defence of the faith, Likewise many other holy martyrs, citizens of the same city, who followed with Adaucus. They were all Christians and remained steadfast in the confession of the faith, and the Emperor Galerius Maximian caused them all to be burned with fire.

entries.lat: Heracléæ, in Ponto, sancti Theodóri, ductoris mílitum, qui, Licínio imperánte, post multa torménta, truncátus cápite, victor migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Heraclea, the holy martyr Theodore. He was a trainer of the soldiery, and in the reign of the Emperor Licinius was beheaded after suffering many torments, and so passed away a conqueror to heaven,.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Móysis, Epíscopi venerábilis, qui primum in erémo vitam solitáriam duxit; deínde, peténte Regína Saracenórum Máuvia, Epíscopus factus, gentem illam ferocíssimam magna ex parte ad fidem convértit, et gloriósus méritis quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: In Egypt, holy Moses, the venerable Bishop of He first lived as a hermit in the desert, but afterwards was made Bishop at the desire of Mauvia, Queen of the Saracens, converted many of that fierce people to the faith, and at length fell asleep in peace, glorious for worthy works.

entries.lat: Lucæ, in Túscia, deposítio sancti Richárdi, Regis Anglórum, qui pater éxstitit sancti Willebáldi, Eystetténsis Epíscopi, ac sanctæ Walbúrgæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Lucca, in Tuscany, holy Richard, Prince of the West Saxons in England, and father of holy Winibald, Willibald, and Walburg.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sanctæ Juliánæ Víduæ.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy widow Juliana.

entries.lat: Sancti Joánnis de Matha, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis sanctíssimæ Trinitátis redemptiónis captivórum fuit Institútor, et sextodécimo Kaléndas Januárii obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: Holy John of Matha, Priest and Confessor, who was the Founder of the Order of the most holy Trinity for the ransom of captives, and fell asleep in the Lord on the 17th day of December.

entries.lat: Somáschæ, in território Bergoménsi, natális sancti Hierónymi Æmiliáni Confessóris, qui Congregatiónis Somáschæ Fundátor éxstitit; atque, plúribus in vita et post mortem miráculis illústris, a Cleménte Décimo tértio, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum fastis adscríptus est, et a Pio Papa Undécimo universális orphanórum ac derelíctæ juventútis Patrónus apud Deum eléctus et declarátus. Ejus tamen festívitas tertiodécimo Kaléndas Augústi recólitur.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Jerome Miani, founder of the Congregation of Somascha, whose name was enrolled among those of the saints by Clement XIII, and whose feast we keep upon the 20th day of July.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, Lúcii et Cyríaci.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Paul, Lucius, and Cyriacus.

entries.lat: In Arménia minóre pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Dionýsii, Æmiliáni et Sebastiáni.
entries.eng: In the Lesser Armenia, the holy martyrs Denis, Aemilian, and Sebastian.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli natális sanctórum Mártyrum Monachórum monastérii Dii, qui, ob defensiónem fídei cathólicæ, cum tulíssent lítteras sancti Felícis Papæ Tértii advérsus Acácium, diríssime cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the martyr monks of the monastery of Dim, who were slain in defence of the Catholic faith, for that they brought the letter of holy Pope Felix against the Acacius.

entries.lat: In Pérside commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, sub Rege Persárum Cábade, ob Christiánam fidem, divérsis supplíciis necáti sunt.
entries.eng: In Persia are commemorated those holy martyrs who were put to death in diverse ways, for the Christian faith's sake, under Gabades, King of Persia.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio sanctæ Coínthæ Mártyris, quam Pagáni, sub Décio Imperatóre, corréptam et ad idóla perdúctam, hæc adoráre cogébant; quod cum illa éxsecrans recusáret, ipsíus pedes vínculis innexuérunt, eámque, trahéntes sic vinctam per civitátis platéas, horréndo supplício discerpsérunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, under the Emperor Decius, the holy martyr Cointhe. The heathen took her and led her before the idols to make her worship them, and when she would not, they tied her feet with chains and dragged her through the streets of the city until she was mangled to death,.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Juvéntii Epíscopi, qui strénue in Evangélio laborávit.
entries.eng: At Pavia, holy Juventius, Bishop of that see, who laboured earnestly in the Gospel,.

entries.lat: Medioláni deposítio sancti Honoráti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Honoratus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Virodúni, in Gállia, sancti Pauli Epíscopi, miraculórum dono illústris.
entries.eng: At Verdun, in Gaul, holy Paul, Bishop of that see, famous for the glory of his miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Murétum, in agro Lemovicénsi, natális sancti Stéphani Abbátis, qui Grandimonténsis Ordinis Institútor fuit, ac virtútibus et miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Muret, in the country of Limoges, the holy Abbot Stephen, founder of the Order of Grandmont, famous for his graces and miracles.

entries.lat: In monastério Vallis Umbrósæ Beáti Petri, Cardinális et Epíscopi Albanénsis, ex Ordine Vallis Umbrósæ, cognoménto Ignei, quia per ignem illǽsus transívit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Vallombrosa, blessed Peter, Cardinal and Bishop of Albano, of the Order of Vallombrosa, surnamed Igneus, because he passed unharmed through fire.

entries.lat: Sancti Cyrílli, Epíscopi Alexandríni, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cujus dies natális quinto Kaléndas Februárii recensétur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy Virgin Apollonia. The persecutors under the Emperor Decius first beat out all her teeth, then they built and kindled a funeral fire and threatened to burn her alive upon it unless she would join them in uttering sinful words. She thought a little while within herself, and then the fire of the Holy Ghost flaming up within her, she tore herself suddenly out of the hands of those wicked men and leapt of her own accord into the fire which they had made ready, so that the very actors in this cruelty were awestruck to find a woman more ready to die than were they to kill her.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ natális sanctæ Apollóniæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, cui persecutóres, sub Décio, dentes omnes primum excussérunt. Deínde, constrúcto ac succénso rogo, iídem commináti sunt, nisi cum eis ímpia verba proférret, vivam se eam incensúros; at illa, cum páululum intra semetípsam deliberásset, repénte se de mánibus impiórum prorípuit, et in ignem, quem paráverant, majóre Sancti Spíritus flamma intus ǽstuans, sponte ita prosilívit, ut perterreréntur étiam ipsi crudelitátis auctóres, quod prómptior invénta esset ad mortem fémina quam persecútor ad pœnam.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander, and thirty-eight others who were crowned at the same time.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Alexándri et aliórum trigínta octo coronatórum.
entries.eng: At Solis, in Cyprus, the holy martyrs Ammonius and Alexander.

entries.lat: In castéllo Lemelénsi, in Africa, sanctórum Mártyrum Primi et Donáti Diaconórum, qui, cum altáre in Ecclésia tutaréntur, a Donatístis occísi sunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, in the castle of Lemele, the holy Deacons Primus and Donates, who suffered martyrdom in defending the altar in the church against the Donatists,.

entries.lat: Solis, in Cypro, sanctórum Mártyrum Ammónii et Alexándri.
entries.eng: At Soli, in Cyprus, the holy Martyrs Ammonius and Alexander.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Nicéphori Mártyris, qui sub Valeriáno Imperatóre, cápite cæsus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyr Nicephorus, who received his crown by being beheaded, under the Emperor Valerian.

entries.lat: In monastério Fontanéllæ, in Gállia, sancti Ansbérti, Rotomagénsis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Fontenelle, in France, holy Ansbert, Bishop of Rouen.

entries.lat: Canúsii, in Apúlia, sancti Sabíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui (ut beátus Gregórius Papa refert), prophétiæ spíritu ac miraculórum dono prǽditus, sibi jam cæco exhíbitum a fámulo, prǽmiis corrúpto, venéni póculum divíno agnóvit instinctu, sed, prænuntiáta mox a Deo suménda de corruptóre vindícta signóque Crucis facto, venénum secúrus ébibit ac nullum ex eo nocuméntum accépit.
entries.eng: At Canosa, in Apulia, the holy Confessor Sabinus, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Apud montem Cassínum sanctæ Scholásticæ Vírginis, soróris sancti Benedícti Abbátis, qui ejus ánimam, instar colúmbæ, migrántem e córpore in cælum ascéndere vidit.
entries.eng: At Monte Cassino, the holy Virgin Scholastica, sister of the holy Abbot Benedict, who saw her soul leave her body and soar heavenward in a bodily shape, like a dove.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Zótici, Irenǽi, Hyacínthi et Amántii.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Zoticus, Irenaeus, Hyacinth, and Amantius,.

entries.lat: Ibídem, via Lavicána, sanctórum decem mílitum Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Rome likewise, upon the Lavican Way, ten holy martyrs, all soldiers.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Appia, sanctæ Sotéris, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ (ut scribit sanctus Ambrósius), nóbili génere nata, paréntum Consulátus et Præfectúras ob Christum contémpsit. Hæc, jussa idólis immoláre, et non acquiéscens, gráviter et diutíssime álapis cæsa est; et, cum cétera quoque pœnárum génera vicísset, demum, percússa gládio, læta migrávit ad Sponsum.
entries.eng: Also at Rome, upon the Appian Way, the holy Virgin and martyr Soteres, who, as holy Ambrose writeth, was born of a noble family, but for Christ's sake despised the consular and prefectural dignities of her race. When she was commanded to offer sacrifice and would not, she was long and heavily buffeted, and when she had overcome other punishments also, she was smitten with the sword and so departed joyfully hence, to be ever with Christ the Bridegroom.

entries.lat: In Campánia sancti Silváni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Campania, the holy Confessor Silvan, Bishop of.

entries.lat: In Stábulo Rhodis, in território Senénsi, sancti Guiliélmi Eremítæ.
entries.eng: At Stabulum Rhodis, in the territory of Siena, the holy Hermit William.

entries.lat: In pago Rotomagénsi sanctæ Austrebértæ Vírginis, miráculis célebris.
entries.eng: At Rouen, the holy Virgin Austreberta, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Lapúrdi, in Gállia, Apparítio beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Immaculátæ.
entries.eng: At Lourdes, in France, the Apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary Immaculate.

entries.lat: Hadrianópoli, in Thrácia, sanctórum Mártyrum Lúcii Epíscopi, et Sociórum ejus, sub Constántio. Ipse Lúcius, ab Ariánis multa perpéssus, in vínculis martýrium consummávit; céteri vero nobilióres cívium, cum Ariános, in Sardicénsi Concílio tunc damnátos, recípere noluíssent, a Philágrio Cómite capitálem senténtiam excepérunt.
entries.eng: At Adrianople, the holy martyrs Lucius, Bishop and his Companions. He suffered much from the Arians under the Emperor Constantius, and finished his testimony in chains, The others were some of the nobler of the citizens who were condemned to death by Count Philagrius because they refused to receive the Arians who had been then condemned in the Council of Sardica.

entries.lat: In Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni Presbýteri, Datívi, Felícis, Ampélii et Sociórum, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cum ad Domínicum ex more celebrándum conveníssent, idcírco, a milítibus comprehénsi, sub Anolíno Procónsule passi sunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs the Priest Saturninus, Dativus, Felix, Ampelius, and their Companions, who were taken by the soldiers in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian when they came together in one, as the use is, to hold the Lord's Supper, and suffered under the proconsul Anolinus.

entries.lat: In Numídia commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui in eádem persecutióne comprehénsi sunt, et, cum juxta Imperatóris edíctum divínas Scriptúras trádere noluíssent, gravíssimis excruciáti sunt supplíciis, ac tandem occísi.
entries.eng: In Numidia are commemorated many holy martyrs who were arrested, in the persecution aforesaid, and for as much as they would not obey the edict of the Emperor to give up the Scriptures of God, they were put to grievous torments and slain.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Gregórii Papæ Secúndi, qui Leónis Isaúrici impietáti acérrime réstitit, et sanctum Bonifátium ad prædicándum Evangélium in Germániam misit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Gregory II, who most vigorously resisted the impiety of Leo the Isaurian, and sent St. Boniface into Germany to preach the Gospel.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Paschális Papæ Primi, qui plúrima sanctórum Mártyrum córpora levávit e cryptis, eáque in divérsis Urbis Ecclésiis honorífice collocávit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy Pope Paschal I, who raised very many bodies of the holy Martyrs from the crypts, and placed them with honour in divers Churches of the City.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Calóceri, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor Calocerus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Lázari Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Lazarus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Castrénsis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Capua, holy Castrensis, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Castro Nantoniénsi, in Gállia, sancti Severíni, qui fuit Abbas monastérii Agaunénsis, suísque précibus cultórem Dei, Regem Clodovéum, a diútina infirmitáte liberávit.
entries.eng: At Château-Landon, in France, holy Severinus, who was Abbot of the monastery of Agaunum, and by his prayers delivered King Clovis, a worshipper of God, from a long-continued sickness.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Jonæ Mónachi, virtútibus clari.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy monk Jonah, renowned for his graces.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, Translátio córporis sancti Desidérii, Epíscopi et Mártyris, ex território Lugdunénsi, in quo ipse olim passus fúerat décimo Kaléndas Júnii.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy martyr Desiderius, Bishop of Vienne,.

entries.lat: Sanctórum septem Fundatórum Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, Confessórum, quorum deposítio respectívis diébus recólitur. Quos autem in vita unus veræ fraternitátis spíritus sociávit, et indivísa post óbitum venerátio pópuli prosecúta est, eos Leo Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, una páriter Sanctórum fastis accénsuit.
entries.eng: The seven holy Founders of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Confessors, whose burial is kept on their respective days. These, whom one spirit of true brotherhood united in life, and an undivided veneration of the people followed after death, Pope Leo XIII together inscribed alike in the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Damiáni, mílitis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy soldier and martyr Damian.

entries.lat: Carthágine sanctórum Mártyrum Modésti et Juliáni.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy martyrs Modestus and Julian.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Modésti et Ammónii infántum.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy children Modestus and Ammonius.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, sanctæ Euláliæ Vírginis, quæ, témpore Diocletiáni Imperatóris, equúleum, úngulas flammásque perpéssa, demum, cruci affíxa, gloriósam martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, in Spain, the holy Virgin Eulalia, who received a glorious crown in the time of the Emperor Diocletian. She suffered racking, tearing with hooks, and scorching with fire, and was finally crucified,.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Melétii, Epíscopi Antiochéni, qui, pro fide cathólica sæpe exsílium passus, demum in eádem urbe migrávit ad Dóminum. Ejus virtútes sanctus Joánnes Chrysóstomus et sanctus Gregórius Nyssénus summis láudibus celebrárunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Meletius, Patriarch of Antioch, who passed away to be ever with the Lord, when he was in exile, which he oftentimes suffered for the Catholic faith's sake. Holy John Chrysostom and Gregory of Nyssa have greatly praised him.

entries.lat: Item Constantinópoli sancti Antónii Epíscopi, témpore Leónis sexti Imperatóris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, in the time of the Emperor Leo VI, holy Anthony, Bishop.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Gaudéntii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Confessor Gaudentius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sancti Agábi Prophétæ, de quo beátus Lucas in Actibus Apostólicis scribit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy prophet Agabus, of whom blessed Luke writeth in the Acts of the Apostles.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sancti Benígni, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, Diocletiáni et Maximiáni Imperatórum témpore, cum fidem Christiánam verbo et exémplo propagáre non desísteret, ab idolórum cultóribus captus est, ac, váriis afféctus supplíciis, sacerdotále munus honóre martýrii cumulávit.
entries.eng: At Todi, the holy martyr Benignus.

entries.lat: Melitínæ, in Arménia, sancti Polyeúcti Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Décii, multa passus, martýrii corónam adéptus est.
entries.eng: At Melitina, in Armenia, the holy martyr Polyeuctus, who suffered many things in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, and received the crown of martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Juliáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy martyr Julian.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sanctárum Fuscæ Vírginis, ejúsque nutrícis Mauræ, quæ, Décio imperánte, multa sub Quinctiáno Prǽside perpéssæ, demum gládio transfíxæ, martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy women the Virgin Fusca, and Maura her fostermother, who after suffering many things under the President Quinctian, by order of the Emperor Decius were run through with the sword, and so finished their testimony,.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Stéphani, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Lyons, in France, holy Stephen, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: Reáte sancti Stéphani Abbátis, miræ patiéntiæ viri; in cujus tránsitu (ut refert beátus Gregórius Papa) sancti Angeli, céteris étiam vidéntibus, adfuérunt.
entries.eng: At Riete, the holy Abbot Stephen, a man of wonderful patience, at whose passing away the presence of the holy angels, as is stated by blessed Pope Gregory, was visible.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Flamínia, natális sancti Valentíni, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui, post multa sanitátum et doctrínæ insígnia, fústibus cæsus et decollátus est, sub Cláudio Cǽsare.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Flaminian Way, the blessed martyr Valentine, a Priest, who after much healing and teaching was cudgelled and beheaded under Claudius Caesar,.

entries.lat: Ibídem deposítio sancti Cyrílli, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, una cum sancto Methódio, simíliter Epíscopo et fratre suo, cujus dies natális octávo Idus Aprílis recensétur, multas Slávicas gentes earúmque Reges ad fidem Christi perdúxit. Horum tamen Sanctórum festívitas Nonis Júlii celebrátur.
entries.eng: In the same place, the burial of holy Cyril, Bishop and Confessor; who, together with holy Methodius, likewise a Bishop and his brother, whose birthday is recorded on the 6th day of April, brought many Slavonic nations and their Kings to the faith of Christ. The feast of these Saints, however, is kept on the 7th day of July.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Vitális, Felículæ et Zenónis.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyrs Vitalis, Felicula, and Zeno.

entries.lat: Interámnæ sancti Valentíni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, post diútinam cædem mancipátus custódiæ, et, cum superári non posset, tandem, médiæ noctis siléntio ejéctus de cárcere, decollátus est, jussu Præfécti urbis Plácidi.
entries.eng: At Terni, holy Valentine, Bishop and Martyr, who, after a long scourging, was committed to prison, and, when he could not be overcome, at length, being cast out of prison in the silence of midnight, was beheaded by order of Placidus, Prefect of the city.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Cyriónis Presbýteri, Bassiáni Lectóris, Agathónis Exorcístæ, et Móysis; qui omnes, igne combústi, evolavérunt ad cælum.
entries.eng: Likewise at Alexandria, the Priest Cyrion, Bassian the Reader, Agatho the Exorcist, and Moses, who were all burnt with fire and passed away to heaven.

entries.lat: Interámnæ sanctórum Próculi, Ephébi et Apollónii Mártyrum, qui, cum ad sancti Valentíni corpus vigílias ágerent, Leóntii Consuláris jussu comprehénsi sunt, et gládio cæsi.
entries.eng: At Teramo, the holy martyr Valentine, Bishop of that see. He was heavily flogged and committed to jail, but as he would not yield he was thrown out of the prison in the silence of midnight and beheaded by command of Placidus, Prefect of the city. There likewise, the holy martyrs Proculus, Ephebus, and Apollonius, who were watching by the body of holy Valentine when they were apprehended by order of Leontius, the consular, and slain with the sword.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Bassi, Antónii et Protólici, qui demérsi sunt in mare.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Bassus, Anthony, and Protolicus, who were drowned in the sea.

entries.lat: Item Alexandríæ sanctórum Dionýsii et Ammónii decollatórum.
entries.eng: Also likewise at Alexandria, the holy martyrs Denis and Ammonius, who were beheaded.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Nostriáni Epíscopi, qui in cathólica fide contra hæréticam pravitátem tuénda éxstitit insígnis.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy Bishop Nostrianus, who was renowned in defending the Catholic faith against heretical depravity.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Eleuchádii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor Eleuchadius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Bithýnia sancti Auxéntii Abbátis.
entries.eng: In Bithynia, the holy Abbot Auxentius.

entries.lat: Apud Surréntum sancti Antoníni Abbátis, qui e monastério Cassinénsi, a Longobárdis devastáto, in solitúdinem ejúsdem urbis secéssit; ibíque, sanctitáte célebris, obdormívit in Dómino. Ipsíus corpus multis quotídie miráculis, et præsértim in energúmenis liberándis, effúlget.
entries.eng: At Sorrento, the holy Abbot Antonino. He was in the monastery of Monte Cassino when it was destroyed by the Lombards, and he went thence to a solitude hard by the city of Sorrento, and there fell asleep in the Lord, famed for holiness. His body is daily remarkable for many miracles, most chiefly in the delivery of them that are vexed by evil spirits.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Faustíni et Jovítæ fratrum, qui sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, post multa præclára ob Christi fidem suscépta certámina, victrícem martýrii corónam accepérunt.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy martyrs Faustinus and Jovita, who under the Emperor Hadrian, after many glorious contendings for Christ's faith, received by martyrdom a crown of victory,.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Cratónis Mártyris, qui, cum uxóre sua et univérsa domo a beáto Valentíno Epíscopo baptizátus, non multo post, una cum illis, martýrio consummátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Crato, who was baptized by blessed Valentine, Bishop along with his wife and his whole house and no long while after, he and they together attained unto martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Interámnæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni, Cástuli, Magni et Lúcii.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Saturninus, Castulus, Magnus, and Lucius.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctæ Agapis, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Terni, the holy Virgin and martyr Agapis.

entries.lat: Vasióne, in Gálliis, sancti Quinídii Epíscopi, cujus mortem in conspéctu Dómini pretiósam mirácula crebra testántur.
entries.eng: At Vaison, in Gaul, holy Quinidius, Bishop of that see, whose death, how precious it was in the sight of the Lord miracles do oftentimes witness.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Decorósi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy Confessor Decorosus, Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: In Província Valériæ sancti Sevéri Presbýteri, qui (ut beátus Gregórius Papa scribit), fusis lácrimis, defúnctum revocávit ad vitam.
entries.eng: In the province of Valeria, the holy Priest Severus, of whom blessed Gregory writeth that by his tears he recalled a dead man to life.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Joséphi Diáconi.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy Deacon Joseph.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sanctæ Geórgiæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: In Auvergne, the holy Virgin Georgia.

entries.lat: Romæ beáti Onésimi, de quo sanctus Paulus Apóstolus ad Philémonem scribit; quem étiam, post sanctum Timótheum, Ephesiórum Epíscopum ordinávit, prædicationísque verbum illi commísit. Ipse autem Onésimus, vinctus Romam perdúctus ac pro fide Christi lapidátus, primo ibídem sepúltus fuit; inde ad locum ubi Epíscopus fúerat ordinátus, corpus ejus delátum est.
entries.eng: Blessed Onesimus, of whom the holy Apostle Paul writeth unto Philemon, and whom also he ordained Bishop of Ephesus after holy Timothy, and committed unto him the preaching of the Word. In the end he was brought to Rome in chains, and there stoned to death for Christ's faith's sake. His body was first buried there, but was thence taken to the place where he had been ordained bishop.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Juliáni Mártyris, cum áliis quinque míllibus.
entries.eng: On the same day is commemorated at Camee in Campania the translation of the holy Virgin and martyr Juliana.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum Ægyptiórum Elíæ, Jeremíæ, Isaíæ, Samuélis et Daniélis; qui, cum spontánee ministrássent Confessóribus in Cilícia ad metálla damnátis, et inde reverteréntur, sunt comprehénsi, et a Firmiliáno Prǽside, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, sævíssime torti, gládio demum percússi sunt. Post eos sanctus Porphýrius, Pámphili Mártyris fámulus, et sanctus Seléucus Cáppadox, qui iterátis certamínibus sæpe vícerant, rursus cruciáti sunt, atque alter incéndio, gládio alter corónam martýrii accepérunt.
entries.eng: After whom holy Porphyry, the servant of the martyr Pamphilus, and holy Seleucus the Cappadocian, who had oftentimes contended and always been conquerors, were put to the torture again, and received their crowns Porphyry by fire, and Seleucus by the sword.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctæ Juliánæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, primum a patre suo Africáno gráviter cæsa, deínde ab Evilásio Præfécto, cui núbere recusáverat, várie cruciáta, et póstmodum in cárcerem detrúsa, ubi palam cum diábolo conflíxit, demum, cum flammas ígnium et ollam fervéntem superásset, cápitis decollatióne martýrium consummávit. Ipsíus autem corpus póstea Cumas, in Campánia, translátum est.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, under the Emperor Maximian, she was cruelly beaten by her own father Africanus, then put to diverse torments by the Prefect Evilasius, whom she refused to marry, and afterwards cast into prison, where she fought visibly with the devil she overcame fire and boiling water, and at length finished her martyrdom by being beheaded,.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Faustíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Confessor Faustinus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ natális sancti Aléxii Falconérii Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis; qui, décimo supra centésimum vitæ suæ anno, Christi Jesu et Angelórum præséntia recreátus, beáto fine quiévit. Ipsíus tamen ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Florence, the blessed Confessor Alexis de' Falconieri, one of the seven founders of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary. He died a blessed death in the hundred and tenth year of his life, strengthened by the presence of Christ Jesus and of the angels.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sancti Faustíni, quem álii quadragínta quátuor secúti sunt ad corónam.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Faustinus, and forty-four others, who followed him to his crown.

entries.lat: In Pérside natális beáti Polychrónii, Epíscopi Babylónis, qui, in persecutióne Décii, ore lapídibus cæso, mánibus exténsis, ad cælum óculos élevans, emísit spíritum.
entries.eng: In Persia, holy Polychronius, Bishop of Babylon, who in the persecution of Decius had his mouth broken with stones, and then with his hands stretched out and his eyes lifted up to heaven, gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Concórdiæ, in Venetórum fínibus, sanctórum Mártyrum Donáti, Secundiáni et Rómuli, cum áliis octogínta sex, ejúsdem corónæ consórtibus.
entries.eng: At Concordia, the holy martyrs Donatus, Secundianus, and Romulus, together with eighty-six others, who were partakers in their crown.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Theodúli senis, qui, cum esset ex família Prǽsidis Firmiliáni, et, Mártyrum excitátus exémplo Christum constánter confiterétur, martýrii palmam, cruci affíxus, nóbili triúmpho proméruit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, holy Theodulus the Elder, of the household of the President Firmilian. He was stirred up by the example of the martyrs steadfastly to confess Christ, and being himself crucified gained by a noble victory the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Juliáni Cappádocis, qui, exosculátus necatórum Mártyrum córpora, et ídeo ut Christiánus delátus et ad Prǽsidem ductus, lento igne jussus est combúri.
entries.eng: There also the holy martyr Julian the Cappadocian. He kissed the bodies of the slaughtered martyrs, and was therefore accused of Christianity, brought before the President, and burnt on a slow fire.

entries.lat: In pago Tarvanénsi, in Gállia, sancti Silvíni, Epíscopi Tolosáni.
entries.eng: In the country of Tervan, holy Silvin, Bishop of Toulouse.

entries.lat: In monastério Cluain-ednechénsi, in Hibérnia, sancti Fintáni, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
entries.eng: In Ireland, the holy Priest and Confessor Fintan,.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis natális sancti Simeónis, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui fílius Cleóphæ et propínquus Salvatóris secúndum carnem fuísse tráditur. Hic, Hierosolymórum Epíscopus post Jacóbum, fratrem Dómini, ordinátus, et, in Trajáni persecutióne, multis supplíciis afféctus, martýrio consummátus est, ómnibus qui áderant et Júdice ipso mirántibus ut centum vigínti annórum senex fórtiter constantérque supplícium crucis pertulísset.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the blessed martyr Simeon, Bishop of that holy city This is he of whom it is recorded that he was the son of Cleophas and the kinsman of the Saviour according to the flesh. He was ordained Bishop of Jerusalem next after James, the brother of the Lord. In the persecution under Trajan he was put to many torments and suffered martyrdom, and the judge and all men marvelled to see with how great boldness and firmness he endured the grievous torment of the cross at his great age, for he was an hundred and twenty years old.

entries.lat: Apud Ostia Tiberína sanctórum Mártyrum Máximi et Cláudii fratrum, et Præpedígnæ, uxóris Cláudii, cum duóbus fíliis Alexándro et Cútia; qui, cum essent præclaríssimi géneris, omnes, jubénte Diocletiáno, tenti atque in exsílium deportáti sunt, ac deínde, incéndio concremáti, Deo ipsi odoríferum martýrii sacrifícium obtulérunt. Eórum relíquiæ, in flumen projéctæ et a Christiánis perquisítæ, juxta eándem civitátem sepúltæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Ostia, the holy brethren Maximus and Claudius, and Praeperdigna, the wife of Claudius, and their two sons, Alexander and Cutias, all martyrs, They were a very noble race, and by command of the Emperor Diocletian they were arrested and sent into exile, then they were consumed with fire, and so offered a sacrifice of sweet savour unto God himself. Their relics were cast into the river, but the Christians sought for them and buried them hard by the city.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Lúcii, Silváni, Rútuli, Clássici, Secundíni, Frúctuli et Máximi.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Lucius, Sylvan, Rutulus, Classicus, Secundinus, Fructulus, and Maximus.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Flaviáni Epíscopi, qui, cum fidem cathólicam Ephesi propugnáret, ab ímpii Dióscori factióne pugnis et cálcibus percússus est, et, in exsílium actus, ibídem post tríduum vitam finívit.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Flavian, Bishop of that see, who, because he defended the Catholic faith at Ephesus, was assailed by the followers of the wicked Dioscorus with cuffs and kicks, and sent into exile, where he died after three days.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, sancti Helládii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui a sancto Ildefónso, Toletáno Epíscopo, multis láudibus celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Toledo, in Spain, holy Helladius, Bishop and Confessor, who is celebrated with many praises by St. Ildephonsus, Bishop of Toledo.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Gabíni, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui fuit frater beáti Caji Papæ, atque, a Diocletiáno diu in custódia vínculis afflíctus, pretiósa morte sibi cæli gáudia comparávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Gavin, a Priest who was the brother of the blessed Pope Caius, and who was long kept in prison and chains by the Emperor Diocletian, and gained the gladness of heaven through a death precious in the sight of the Lord.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Públii, Juliáni, Marcélli et aliórum.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Publius, Julian, Marcellus, and others.

entries.lat: In Palæstína commemorátio sanctórum Monachórum, et aliórum Mártyrum, qui a Saracénis, sub Duce Alamúndaro, ob Christi fidem, sævíssime cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Palestine are commemorated the holy monks and other martyrs who were cruelly slain for Christ's faith's sake by the Saracens under Al Mundar, their general.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Quod-vult-Deus, Carthaginénsis Epíscopi, qui, una cum Clero, a Rege Ariáno Genseríco in fractas et absque remígiis ac velis naves impósitus, præter spem Neápolim áppulit, ibíque, in exsílio pósitus, Conféssor occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Quodvultdeus, Bishop of Carthage, who, together with his Clergy, was put by the Arian King Genseric on board broken ships without oars or sails, and beyond all hope came to land at Naples, where, living in exile, he died a Confessor.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Zambdæ Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, holy Zambdas, Bishop of that holy city.

entries.lat: Solis, in Cypro, sancti Auxíbii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Soli, holy Auxibius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Apud Benevéntum sancti Barbati Epíscopi, qui, sanctitáte célebris, Longobárdos et eórum Ducem convértit ad Christum.
entries.eng: At Beneventum, holy Barbatus, Bishop of that see, famous for his holiness, who brought the Lombards and their leader to Christ.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Mansuéti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Mansuetus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Tyri, in Phœnícia, commemorátio beatórum Mártyrum, quorum númerum solíus sciéntia Dei cólligit. Hi omnes, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, a Vetúrio, mílitum magístro, multis tormentórum genéribus, sibi invícem succedéntibus, occísi sunt; nam, primo quidem flagris toto córpore dilaniáti, inde divérsis bestiárum genéribus tráditi, sed ab illis divína virtúte nil læsi, post, áddita feritáte ignis ac ferri, martýrium consummárunt. Eórum vero gloriósam multitúdinem ad victóriam incitábant Epíscopi Tyránnio, Silvánus, Péleus et Nilus, ac Présbyter Zenóbius, qui, felíci agóne, una cum illis, martýrii palmam adépti sunt.
entries.eng: The blessed martyrs of Tyre, in Phoenicia, whose number is known only to God. They were slain by Veturius, military instructor under the Emperor Diocletian, with a great number and variety of torments. They were first lacerated with stripes, then given to diverse kinds of beasts but as these, through the power of God, would not hurt them, they were savagely tortured anew with fire and iron and put to death. This glorious multitude were cheered on to victory by the Bishops Tyrannio, Silvan, Peleus, and Nilus, and the Priest Zenobius, who by a happy contention, along with them, gained the same palm of martyrdom together with them.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Eleuthérii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyr Eleutherius, Patriarch of that city.

entries.lat: In Pérside natális sancti Eleuthérii, Epíscopi, et aliórum centum vigínti octo; qui, sub Rege Persárum Sápore, cum Solem adoráre renuíssent, crudéli nece præcláras sibi corónas comparárunt.
entries.eng: In Persia, holy Sadoth,bishop and an hundred and twentyeight others who refused to worship the sun, under Sapor, King of the Persians, and by cruel deaths gained glorious crowns.

entries.lat: In Cypro sanctórum Mártyrum Potámii et Nemésii.
entries.eng: On the same 20th day of February, were also born into the better life: In the island of Cyprus, the holy martyrs Pothamius and Nemesius.

entries.lat: Cátanæ, in Sicília, sancti Leónis Epíscopi, qui virtútibus atque miráculis coruscávit.
entries.eng: At Catania, in Sicily, holy Leo, Bishop of that see, who shone with graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Euchérii, Aurelianénsis Epíscopi, qui eo magis miráculis cláruit, quo plúribus invidórum calúmniis fuit oppréssus.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Eucherius, Bishop of Orleans, who shone with more miracles the more he was belied by his enemies.

entries.lat: Tornáci, in Gálliis, sancti Eleuthérii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Tournai, in Hainaut, the holy Confessor Eleutherius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Scythópoli, in Palæstína, sancti Severiáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, Eutychiánis acérrime se oppónens, gládio perémptus est.
entries.eng: At Bethsan, the holy martyr Severian, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Sicília natális sanctórum Mártyrum septuagínta novem, qui sub Diocletiáno, per divérsa torménta, confessiónis suæ corónam percípere meruérunt.
entries.eng: In Sicily, under the Emperor Diocletian, seventy-nine holy martyrs, who through diverse torments won the crown of their confession.

entries.lat: Adruméti, in Africa, sanctórum Mártyrum Véruli, Secundíni, Sirícii, Felícis, Sérvuli, Saturníni, Fortunáti et aliórum séxdecim, qui in persecutióne Wandálica, ob cathólicæ fídei confessiónem, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Adrumetum, in Africa, the holy martyrs Verulus, Secundinus, Syricius, Felix, Servulus, Saturninus, Fortunatus, and sixteen others, who were crowned with martyrdom for their confession of the Catholic faith in the persecution under the Vandals.

entries.lat: Damásci sancti Petri Maviméni, qui, cum díceret Arábibus quibúsdam, ad se ægrótum veniéntibus: «Omnis qui fidem Christiánam cathólicam non ampléctitur, damnátus est, sicut et Máhumet, pseudoprophéta vester,» ab illis est necátus.
entries.eng: At Damascus, holy Peter Mavimeno. Some Arabs came to see him while he was ill, and to them he said, "Whoever does not embrace the Catholic Christian religion will be damned, as your false prophet Mohammed is," whereupon they killed him.

entries.lat: Metis, in Gállia, sancti Felícis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Metz, in France, the holy Bishop Felix.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Patérii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, holy Paterius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Cáthedra sancti Petri Apóstoli, qua primum Romæ sedit.
entries.eng: The Chair of St. Peter the Apostle, on which he first sat at Rome.

entries.lat: Favéntiæ, in Æmília, natális sancti Petri Damiáni, Cardinális atque Epíscopi Ostiénsis et Confessóris, ex Ordine Camaldulénsi, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris, quem Leo Papa Duodécimus Doctórem universális Ecclésiæ declarávit. Ipsíus autem festum sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Faenza, in Emilia, the birthday of holy Peter Damian, Cardinal and Bishop of Ostia and Confessor, of the Order of Camaldoli, famous for learning and holiness, whom Pope Leo XII declared a Doctor of the universal Church. His feast, however, is kept on the following day.

entries.lat: Salamínæ, in Cypro, sancti Aristiónis, qui (ut mox memorándus Pápias testátur) fuit unus de septuagínta duóbus Christi discípulis.
entries.eng: At Salamis, in Cyprus, holy Aristion, who, as the said Papias doth testify, was one of the seventy-two disciples of Christ.

entries.lat: Hierápoli, in Phrýgia, beáti Pápiæ, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui sancti Joánnis Senióris audítor, Polycárpi autem sodális fuit.
entries.eng: At Hierapolis, in Phrygia, holy Papias, Bishop of that city, who was the hearer of the holy elder John, and the companion of Polycarp.

entries.lat: In Arábia commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, sævíssime cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Arabia are commemorated many holy martyrs who were cruelly slain under the Emperor Galerius Maximian.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Abílii Epíscopi, qui, secúndus post beátum Marcum, factus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, sacerdótium virtúte conspícuus ministrávit.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, holy Abilius, Pope of that see, who was the second who held it after the blessed Evangelist Mark, and administered his office with an eminent manifestation of grace.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Paschásii Epíscopi, eruditióne et morum sanctitáte præclári.
entries.eng: At Vienne, holy Paschasius, Bishop of that see, very famous for his learning and the holiness of his life.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Maximiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, holy Maximian, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: Cortónæ, in Túscia, sanctæ Margarítæ, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci; quæ admirábili pæniténtia et ubérrimis lácrimis máculas anteáctæ vitæ indesinénter abstérsit. Ipsíus corpus, mirabíliter incorrúptum, suávem spirans odórem et crebris miráculis clarum, ibídem magno cum honóre cólitur.
entries.eng: At Cortona, in Tuscany, holy Margaret, of the third order of St. Francis, whose body hath marvellously remained incorrupt for more than four hundred years, breathing a sweet savour, and famous for many miracles, and is there deeply honoured.

entries.lat: Sancti Petri Damiáni, ex Ordine Camaldulénsi, Cardinális et Epíscopi Ostiénsis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, qui evolávit in cælum prídie hujus diéi.
entries.eng: At Faenza, the holy Peter Damian, Cardinal Bishop of Ostia, famous for his teaching and holiness, whom Pope Leo XII declared to be a Doctor of the Universal Church.

entries.lat: Smyrnæ natális sancti Polycárpi, qui, beáti Joánnis Apóstoli discípulus, et ab eo ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus, totíus Asiæ Princeps fuit. Póstea, sub Marco Antoníno et Lúcio Aurélio Cómmodo, sedénte Procónsule et univérso pópulo in theátro advérsus eum personánte, igni tráditus est; et, cum ab igne mínime læderétur, martýrii corónam, gládio confóssus, accépit. Cum illo étiam álii duódecim, qui ex Philadélphia vénerant, in eádem Smyrnénsi urbe, martýrio consummáti sunt. Ipsíus tamen Polycárpi festum séptimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, the birthday of holy Polycarp, who, a disciple of blessed John the Apostle, and ordained by him Bishop of that city, was the chief of all Asia. Afterwards, under Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Commodus, the Proconsul sitting in judgment and all the people in the theatre crying out against him, he was delivered to the fire; and, when he was in no wise hurt by the fire, he received the crown of martyrdom, being pierced with the sword. With him also twelve others, who had come from Philadelphia, were made perfect by martyrdom in the same city of Smyrna. The feast of Polycarp, however, is kept on the 26th day of January.

entries.lat: Apud Sírmium beáti Siréni, Mónachi et Mártyris, qui, jubénte Maximiáno Imperatóre, reténtus est, et, cum se Christiánum esse confiterétur, cápite obtruncátus.
entries.eng: At Sirmium, the blessed martyr Sirenus a monk who was apprehended by order of the Emperor Maximian, and when he confessed himself to be a Christian was beheaded.

entries.lat: Ibídem natális sanctórum septuagínta duórum Mártyrum, qui, martýrii certámen in præfáta urbe consummántes, mansúra percepérunt regna.
entries.eng: In the same place, the birthday of seventy-two holy Martyrs, who, finishing the combat of martyrdom in the aforesaid city, received the everlasting kingdom.

entries.lat: In civitáte Asturicénsi, in Hispánia, sanctæ Marthæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, sub Décio Imperatóre et Patérno Procónsule, dire ob Christi fidem est cruciáta et gládio tandem occísa.
entries.eng: In the city of Astorga, the holy Virgin Martha, martyred under the Emperor Decius and the Proconsul Paternus.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Lázari Mónachi, qui, cum sacras Imágines píngeret, idcírco, Imperatóris Iconoclástæ Theóphili jussu, diris supplíciis excruciátur, et ei manus candénti ferro combúritur; sed, Dei virtúte sanátus, abrásas Imágines sanctas pingéndo restítuit, ac demum in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy monk Lazarus. Because he painted holy images, the Emperor Theophilus, the Iconoclast, put him to grievous tortures, and burnt his hands with a white-hot iron but he was healed by the power of God, restored the painting upon the holy images that had been defaced, and at length fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Felícis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Bishop Felix.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Polycárpi Presbýteri, qui, cum beáto Sebastiáno, plúrimos ad Christi fidem convértit, atque ad martýrii glóriam exhortándo perdúxit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Priest Polycarp, who, along with the blessed Sebastian, brought many to believe in Christ, and by his exhortations led them to the glory of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Híspali, in Hispánia, sancti Floréntii Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Seville, in Spain, the holy Confessor Florence.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sanctæ Románæ Vírginis, quæ, a sancto Silvéstro Papa baptizáta, in antris et spelúncis cæléstem vitam duxit, et miraculórum glória cláruit.
