entries.eng: At Todi, the holy Virgin Romana, who was baptized by holy Pope Sylvester, led a heavenly life in dens and caves of the earth, and shone with the glory of miracles.

entries.lat: In Anglia sanctæ Milbúrgis Vírginis, fíliæ Regis Merciórum.
entries.eng: In England, the holy Virgin Milburga, daughter of the king of the Mercians,.

entries.lat: (In anno Bissextili bis pronuntiatur Sexto Kaléndas Mártii, et eadem Luna, scilicet die 24 et 25. Prima die, id est 24, hoc modo: Sexto Kaléndas Mártii. Luna..., quota fuerit. Deinde: Commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum. Secunda die, id est 25: Sexto Kaléndas Mártii. Luna... In Judǽa..., et cetera, ut in sequenti Lectione.)
entries.eng: (In Leap Year this is announced twice on the sixth day before the Kalends of March, and with the same Moon, namely on the 24th and 25th. On the first day, that is the 24th, in this manner: The sixth day before the Kalends of March. Moon..., whatever it may be. Then: The commemoration of many holy Martyrs and Confessors, and of holy Virgins. On the second day, that is the 25th: The sixth day before the Kalends of March. Moon... In Judea..., and so forth, as in the following Lesson.)

entries.lat: (24 aut 25 in anno Bissextili.)
entries.eng: (The 24th or the 25th in Leap Year.)

entries.lat: In Judǽa natális sancti Matthíæ Apóstoli, qui, post Ascensiónem Dómini ab Apóstolis in Judæ proditóris locum sorte eléctus, pro Evangélii prædicatióne martýrium passus est.
entries.eng: In Judea, the holy Apostle Matthias, who was chosen by the Apostles right after the Ascension of the Lord to take the place of the traitor Judas, and who suffered martyrdom for preaching the Gospel.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Primitívæ Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Primitiva.

entries.lat: Rotómagi pássio sancti Prætextáti, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Rouen, the passion of holy Praetextatus, Bishop and Martyr.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Sérgii Mártyris, cujus gesta præclára habéntur.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Sergius, whose acts are held most famous.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Montáni, Lúcii, Juliáni, Victórici, Flaviáni et Sociórum, qui discípuli fuérunt sancti Cypriáni, et, sub Valeriáno Imperatóre, martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Montanus, Lucius, Julian, Victoricus, Flavian, and their Companions, who were disciples of holy Cyprian, and finished their testimony under the Emperor Valerian.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Modésti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Trier, the holy Confessor Modestus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Apud Stylum, in Calábria, sancti Joánnis, cognoménto Therésti, monásticæ vitæ laude et sanctitáte insígnis,
entries.eng: At Stilo, in Calabria, holy John, surnamed Theristus, renowned for the praise of his monastic life and for holiness.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Edilbérti, Regis Cantiórum, quem sanctus Augustínus, Anglórum Epíscopus, ad Christi fidem convértit.
entries.eng: In England, holy Ethelbert, King of Kent, whom St. Augustine, Bishop of the English, converted to the faith of Christ.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis prima Invéntio cápitis sancti Joánnis Baptístæ Præcursóris Dómini.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the first Finding of the head of St. John the Baptist, the Precursor of the Lord.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto natális sanctórum Mártyrum Victoríni, Victóris, Nicéphori, Claudiáni, Dióscori, Serapiónis et Pápiæ, sub Numeriáno Imperatóre. Horum duo primi, pro confessióne fídei, exquisíta suppliciórum génera constánter passi, cápite plectúntur; Nicéphorus, post cratículas candéntes ignésque superátos, minutátim concísus est; Claudiánus et Dióscorus flammis incénsi; Serápion vero et Pápias gládio cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: Nicephorus was laid upon a hot iron bed, and when he had overcome the fire was cut joint from joint. Claudian and Dioscorus were burnt. Serapion and Papias were slain with the sword.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Donáti, Justi, Herénæ et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Donatus, Justus, Herenas, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Tharásii Epíscopi, eruditióne et pietáte insígnis; ad quem exstat Hadriáni Papæ Primi epístola pro defensióne sanctárum Imáginum.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Tharasius, Patriarch of that see, famous for his learning and godliness. There remaineth an epistle addressed unto him by Pope Adrian I in defence of holy images.

entries.lat: Naziánzi, in Cappadócia, sancti Cæsárii, qui beátæ Nonnæ fílius ac beatórum Gregórii Theólogi et Gorgóniæ fuit frater, et quem idem Gregórius inter ágmina beatórum se vidísse testátur.
entries.eng: At Nazianzum, holy Caesarius, brother of blessed Gregory the Theologian, whom the aforementioned Gregory doth testify that he saw among the multitude of the blessed.

entries.lat: In monastério Heidenhémii, diœcésis Eystetténsis, in Germánia, sanctæ Walbúrgæ Vírginis, quæ fuit fília sancti Richárdi, Anglórum Regis, et soror sancti Willebáldi, Eystetténsis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Heidenheim, in the diocese of Eichstätt, in Germany, the holy Virgin Walburga, who was the daughter of St. Richard, King of the English, and sister of St. Willibald, Bishop of Eichstätt.

entries.lat: Perge, in Pamphýlia, natális beáti Néstoris Epíscopi, qui, in persecutióne Décii, cum diu noctúque oratióni insísteret póstulans ut grex Christi custodirétur, comprehénsus est, ac, nomen Dómini mira libertáte et alacritáte conféssus, Prǽsidis Polliónis jussu equúleo sævíssime est cruciátus; ac demum, cum se Christo semper adhæsúrum constánter profiterétur, crucis suspéndio victor in cælum migrávit.
entries.eng: At Perga, in Pamphylia, blessed Nestor, Bishop During the persecution under Decius he was instant in prayer by day and by night that Christ's flock might be kept safe. When he was arrested he confessed the name of the Lord with wonderful freedom and readiness. By command of the President Pollio he was most cruelly racked, and as he steadfastly declared that he would alway cleave unto Christ, he was at last crucified, and from the cross passed to heaven a conqueror.

entries.lat: Ibídem pássio sanctórum Pápiæ, Diodóri, Conónis et Claudiáni, qui sanctum Néstorem martýrio præcessérunt.
entries.eng: At Perga likewise, the holy martyrs Papias, Diodorus, Conon, and Claudian, who suffered before holy Nestor.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Fortunáti, Felícis et aliórum vigínti septem.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Fortunatus Felix, and twenty-seven others.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Alexándri Epíscopi, gloriósi senis, qui, post beátum Petrum, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopum, zelo fídei succénsus, Aríum, Presbýterum suum, hærética impietáte depravátum et divína veritáte convíctum, de Ecclésia ejécit; ac póstea, inter trecéntos decem et octo Patres, in Nicǽno Concílio eúndem damnávit.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy Bishop Alexander, a glorious old man, who, after blessed Peter, Bishop of that city, burning with zeal for the faith, cast out of the Church Arius, his own Priest, corrupted by heretical impiety and convicted by divine truth; and afterwards, among the three hundred and eighteen Fathers in the Council of Nicaea, condemned the same.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Faustiniáni Epíscopi, qui eam Ecclésiam, Diocletiáni persecutióne vexátam, verbo prædicatiónis firmávit et auxit.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy Bishop Faustinian, who by the preaching of the word of God strengthened and increased that Church when it had been troubled in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Gazæ, in Palæstína, sancti Porphýrii Epíscopi, qui, témpore Arcádii Imperatóris, Marnam idólum ejúsque templum evértit, ac, multa passus, quiévit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Gaza, in Palestine, holy Porphyry, Bishop of that see, who in the time of the Emperor Arcadius cast down the idol Mama and its temple, and after many sufferings fell asleep in the Lord.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ sancti Andréæ, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Florence, the holy Confessor Andrew, Bishop of that city,.

entries.lat: In território Archiacénsi, in Gállia, sancti Victóris Confessóris, cujus laudes sanctus Bernárdus conscrípsit.
entries.eng: In the country of Troyes, the holy Confessor Victor, whose praises have been written by holy Bernard.

entries.lat: Insulæ, in Aprútio, sancti Gabriélis a Vírgine Perdolénte, Clérici Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Dómini nuncupátæ, et Confessóris; qui, magnis intra breve vitæ spátium méritis et post mortem miráculis clarus, a Benedícto Papa Décimo quinto in Sanctórum cánonem relátus est.
entries.eng: At Isola, in the Abruzzi, holy Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows, Cleric of the Congregation called of the Cross and Passion of the Lord, and Confessor; who, famous for great merits within the short span of his life and for miracles after his death, was enrolled in the canon of the Saints by Pope Benedict XV.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Alexándri, Abúndii, Antígoni et Fortunáti.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander, Abundius, Antigonus, and Fortunatus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio sancti Juliáni Mártyris, qui, cum ita pódagra constríctus esset, ut neque incédere neque stare posset, una cum duóbus fámulis, qui eum in sella gestábant, Júdici offértur; quorum alter fidem negávit, alter, nómine Eunus, cum dómino suo perdurávit in confessióne Christi. Ipse porro Juliánus et Eunus, camélis impósiti, per totam urbem circumdúci jubéntur, et flagris laniári, ac tandem, incénso rogo, hinc inde spectánte pópulo, combúri.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Julian. He was so crippled by the gout that he could neither walk nor stand, and was carried before the judge in a chair by two servants. Of these two servants one denied the faith the other, whose name was Eunus, persisted in confessing Christ along with Julian. They were both placed upon camels and led about the whole city, lashed, and at length publicly burnt upon a pyre.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Besæ mílitis, qui, cum insultántes in prædíctos Mártyres cohibéret, delátus est ad Júdicem, et, pro fide constánter agens, cápite truncátus.
entries.eng: In the same place, the holy soldier Besas, who, when he restrained those who insulted the aforesaid Martyrs, was brought before the Judge, and, standing steadfast for the faith, was beheaded.

entries.lat: Híspali, in Hispánia, natális sancti Leándri, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui, sanctórum Isidóri Epíscopi ac Florentínæ Vírginis frater, sua prædicatióne et indústria gentem Visigothórum, adjuvánte Reccarédo, eórum Rege, ab Ariána impietáte ad cathólicam fidem convértit.
entries.eng: At Seville, in Spain, holy Leander, Bishop of that city, by whose preaching and labours, assisted by Reccared, King of the Visigoths, that nation were converted from the Arian misbelief to the Catholic faith.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Confessórum Basilíi et Procópii, qui, témpore Leónis Imperatóris, pro cultu sanctárum Imáginum strénue decertárunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Confessors Basil and Procopius, who in the time of the Emperor Leo the Isaurian, contended valiantly for the honouring of holy images.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Baldoméri Subdiaconi, viri Deo devóti, cujus sepúlcrum crebris miráculis illustrátur.
entries.eng: At Lyon, holy Baldomer, the man of God whose grave is famous on account of the miracles which are oftentimes wrought there.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Macárii, Rufíni, Justi et Theóphili.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Macarius, Rufinus, Justus, and Theophilus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio sanctórum Cæreális, Púpuli, Caji et Serapiónis.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Caerealis, Pupulus, Caius, and Serapion.

entries.lat: Ibídem commemorátio sanctórum Presbyterórum, Diaconórum et aliórum plurimórum; qui, témpore Valeriáni Imperatóris, cum pestis sævíssima grassarétur, morbo laborántibus ministrántes, libentíssime mortem oppetiére, et quos velut Mártyres religiósa piórum fides venerári consuévit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Alexandria are commemorated the holy Priests, Deacons, and many others who cheerfully met death in ministering to the sick in the great plague which devastated that city, in the time of the Emperor Valerian, and whom the godly reverence of the faithful hath been used to honour as martyrs.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Hílari, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Hilary, Pope and Confessor.

entries.lat: In território Lugdunénsi, locis Jurénsibus, deposítio sancti Románi Abbátis, qui primus illic eremíticam vitam duxit, et, multis virtútibus ac miráculis clarus, plurimórum póstea Pater éxstitit Monachórum.
entries.eng: In the territory of Lyons, in the region of the Jura, the burial of the holy Abbot Romanus, who first led the eremitical life there, and, famous for many virtues and miracles, afterwards became the Father of very many Monks.

entries.lat: Pápiæ Translátio córporis sancti Augustíni Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, ex Sardínia ínsula, ópera Luitprándi, Regis Longobardórum.
entries.eng: At Pavia is commemorated the translation of the body of holy Augustine, Bishop of Hippo, which was brought from the island of Sardinia by the care of Luitprand, King of the Lombards.

entries.lat: Sexto Kaléndas Mártii
entries.eng: The sixth day before the Kalends of March

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum ducentórum sexagínta, quos jussit primo Cláudius, pro Christi nómine damnátos, extra portam Saláriam arénam fódere, deínde in amphitheátro sagíttis mílitum intérfici.
entries.eng: At Rome, two hundred and sixty holy martyrs whom for Christ's name's sake the Emperor Claudius first condemned to dig sand outside the Salarian Gate, and then to be shot to death with arrows in the amphitheatre.

entries.lat: Item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Leónis, Donáti, Abundántii, Nicéphori et aliórum novem.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Leo, Donatus, Abundantius, Nicephorus, and nine others.

entries.lat: Massíliæ, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Hermétis et Hadriáni.
entries.eng: At Marseilles, the holy martyrs Hermes and Hadrian.

entries.lat: Heliópoli, apud Líbanum, sanctæ Eudóciæ Mártyris, quæ, in persecutióne Trajáni, a Theódoto Epíscopo baptizáta et ad certámen muníta, ibídem, Vincéntii Prǽsidis jussu percússa gládio, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Heliopolis, the holy martyr Eudocia during the persecution under the Emperor Trajan. She was baptized by Theodotus, Bishop of and, armed for the battle, the President Vincentius ordered her to be smitten with the sword, and thus she received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Antonínæ Mártyris, quæ in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cum Gentílium deos irrisísset, ídeo, post vários cruciátus, in vase quodam inclúsa, in palúdem urbis Ceæ demérsa est.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy martyr Antonina. During the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian she laughed at the gods of the Gentiles, for the which cause she was diversely tortured, shut up in a barrel, and drowned in the marsh at the city of Cea.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Felícis Papæ Tértii, qui sancti Gregórii Magni átavus fuit; qui étiam (ut ipse Gregórius refert), sanctæ Tharsíllæ nepti appárens, illam ad cæléstia regna vocávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the birthday of the holy Pope Felix III, who was the great-great-grandfather of St. Gregory the Great; who also (as Gregory himself relates), appearing to his descendant St. Tharsilla, called her to the heavenly kingdom.

entries.lat: Apud civitátem Werdam sancti Suitbérti Epíscopi, qui, témpore sancti Sérgii Papæ Primi, apud Frísones, Bátavos et álios Germániæ pópulos Evangélium prædicávit.
entries.eng: In the city of Kaiserswerth, the holy Bishop Suitbert, who, in the time of the holy Pope Sergius I, preached the Gospel among the Frisians, Batavians and other peoples of Germany.

entries.lat: Andégavi, in Gállia, sancti Albíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, viri præclaríssimæ virtútis et sanctitátis.
entries.eng: At Angers, the holy Confessor Albinus, Bishop of that see, a man of eminent graces and holiness.

entries.lat: Apud Cenómanos, in Gállia, sancti Siviárdi Abbátis.
entries.eng: At Mans, the holy Siviard, Abbot.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ Translátio sancti Herculáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui jussu Totílæ, Gothórum Regis, decollátus est. Ipsíus autem corpus ita cápiti unítum atque sanum, quadragésimo post abscissiónem die (ut scribit sanctus Gregórius Papa), repértum est, ac si nulla ferri incísio illud tetigísset.
entries.eng: At Perugia is commemorated the translation of the holy martyr Herculanus, Bishop of that see, of whom mention is made upon the 7th day of November. He was beheaded by order of Totila, King of the Goths, and it is written by holy Pope Gregory that, forty days after his head was cut off, head and body were found united again, as though the iron had never touched him.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Latína, sanctórum Mártyrum Jovíni et Basiléi, qui passi sunt sub Valeriáno et Galliéno Imperatóribus.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Latin Way, under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, the holy martyrs Jovinus and Basileus.

entries.lat: Item Romæ plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui sub Alexándro Imperatóre et Ulpiáno Præfécto, diu cruciáti, ad extrémum capitáli senténtia damnáti sunt.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, under the Emperor Alexander and the Prefect Ulpian, many holy martyrs, who were long tortured, and at length put to death.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Mártyrum Lúcii Epíscopi, Absalónis et Lórgii.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyrs Lucius the Bishop, Absolom, Lorgius.

entries.lat: In Portu Románo sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, Heráclii, Secundíllæ et Januáriæ.
entries.eng: At Porto, the holy martyrs Paul, Heraclius, Secundilla, and Januaria.

entries.lat: In Campánia commemorátio sanctórum octogínta Mártyrum, qui, cum nollent carnes immolátas comédere nec caput capræ adoráre, a Longobárdis sævíssime cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Campania are commemorated eighty holy martyrs, who would not eat meat sacrificed unto idols, nor adore a she-goat's head, and therefore, were cruelly slain by the Lombards.

entries.lat: Lichféldiæ, in Anglia, sancti Ceáddæ, Epíscopi Merciórum et Lindisfarnórum, cujus præcláras virtútes sanctus Beda Venerábilis commémorat.
entries.eng: In England, holy Chad, Bishop of the Mercians and of Lindisfarne, whose eminent graces are recorded by Bede.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum Maríni mílitis, et Astérii Senatóris, in persecutióne Valeriáni. Horum prior, cum accusátus esset a commilitónibus ut Christiánus, et, interrogátus a Júdice, se Christiánum esse voce claríssima testarétur, martýrii corónam abscissióne cápitis accépit; cumque Astérius corpus Mártyris, cápite truncátum, subjéctis húmeris et substráta veste, qua induebátur, excíperet, honórem quem Mártyri détulit, contínuo et ipse Martyr accépit.
entries.eng: Marinus was accused by his comrades of being a Christian, and when asked by the judge so declared with a loud voice, and was beheaded.

entries.lat: Calagúrri, in Hispánia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Hemitérii et Cheledónii fratrum, qui, cum apud Legiónem, Gallǽciæ urbem, in castris militárent, ambo, exsurgénte persecutiónis procélla, pro confessióne nóminis Christi, Calagúrrim usque profécti, ibi, plúribus torméntis afflícti, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Calahorra, in Spain, the birthday of the holy Martyrs Emeterius and Chelidonius, brothers, who, while serving as soldiers in the camp at León, a city of Galicia, when the storm of persecution arose, both went as far as Calahorra for the confession of the name of Christ, and there, afflicted with many torments, were crowned with martyrdom.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sanctórum Felícis, Lucíoli, Fortunáti, Márciæ et Sociórum.
entries.eng: Upon the same day the holy martyrs Felix, Luciolus, Fortunatus, Marcia, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum mílitum Cleoníci, Eutrópii et Basilísci, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, sub Asclepíade Prǽside, crucis supplício felíciter triumphárunt
entries.eng: Likewise the holy soldiers Cleonicus, Eutropius, and Basiliscus, who won a happy triumph upon the cross under the President Asclepiades, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Titiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Confessor Titian, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Bambérgæ sanctæ Cunegúndis Augústæ, quæ, sancto Henríco Primo, Romanórum Imperatóri, nupta, perpétuam virginitátem, ipso annuénte, servávit; ac, bonórum óperum méritis cumuláta, sancto fine quiévit, et post óbitum miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Bamberg, holy Cunegunda, Empress of the Romans, bride of the Emperor Henry the First, with whose consent she remained always a Virgin. She fell asleep in peace, richly adorned with good works, and after her death was famous for miracles,.

entries.lat: Vilnæ, in Lithuánia, beáti Casimíri Confessóris, e Casimíro Rege progéniti: quem Leo Décimus, Románus Póntifex, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
entries.eng: At Vilnius, in Lithuania, the blessed Casimir, son of Casimir III, King of Poland, whose name the Roman Pontiff, Leo X, numbered with those of the Saints,.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, natális sancti Lúcii Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, primo in persecutióne Valeriáni ob Christi fidem exsílio relegátus, et póstmodum divíno nutu ad Ecclésiam suam redíre permíssus, tandem, cum plúrimum advérsus Novatiános laborásset, cápitis obtruncatióne martýrium complévit. Eum vero sanctus Cypriánus summis láudibus celebrávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, the holy martyr Pope Lucius. He was first banished in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, but was afterwards permitted by the will of God to return to his church, and after toiling much against the Novatians, finished his testimony by being beheaded. He is highly praised by holy Cyprian.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Hadriáni Mártyris, cum áliis vigínti tribus, qui omnes, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, martýrium crurifrágio consummárunt. Eórum relíquiæ, a Christiánis Byzántium delátæ, reverénti honóre sepúltæ fuérunt; inde póstea sancti Hadriáni corpus Romam translátum fuit sexto Idus Septémbris, quo die festívitas ejus potíssimum celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyr Hadrian, and twenty-three others, who, under the Emperor Diocletian, all had their legs broken, and were so left to die. The principal feast in memory of Hadrian is kept upon the 8th day of September, when his body was brought to Rome.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, sanctórum Mártyrum nongentórum, qui pósiti sunt in cœmetério ad sanctam Cæcíliam.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Appian Way, nine hundred holy Martyrs, who were laid in the cemetery at St. Cecilia's.

entries.lat: Apud Chersonésum pássio sanctórum Episcopórum Basilíi, Eugénii, Agathodóri, Elpídii, Æthérii, Capitónis, Ephræm, Néstoris et Arcádii.
entries.eng: In the Crimea, the holy Bishops Basil, Eugenius, Agathodormus, Elpidius, Aetherius, Capito, Ephrem, Nestor, and Arcadius.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Caji Palatíni, in mare demérsi, et aliórum vigínti septem.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Caius, an officer of the palace, drowned in the sea, and twenty-seven others.

entries.lat: Item pássio sanctórum Archelái, Cyrílli et Phótii.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Archelaus, Cyril, and Photius.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sancti Phocæ Mártyris, qui, post multas, quas pro nómine Redemptóris passus est, injúrias, quáliter de antíquo illo serpénte triumpháverit, hódie quoque pópulis eo miráculo declarátur, quod, si quíspiam a serpénte morsus fúerit, hic, ut jánuam Basílicæ Mártyris credens attígerit, conféstim, evacuáta venéni virtúte, sanátur.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyr Phocas. For the Redeemer's name's sake he gained the victory over many an assault of the old serpent, and that victory is still held forth before the people, with this miracle, that if any be bitten of a serpent and touch in faith the door of this martyr's church, he is forthwith healed of the poison.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Hadriáni Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, jussu Firmiliáni Prǽsidis, prius ob Christi fidem leóni objéctus, deínde gládio jugulátus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Cassarea, in Palestine, the holy martyr Hadrian, who was crowned by command of the President Firmilian, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian. He was first thrown to a lion, but afterward slain with the sword.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sanctórum Eusébii Palatíni, et aliórum novem Mártyrum.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Eusebius, and nine others.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Theóphili Epíscopi, qui sub Sevéro Príncipe, sapiéntia et vitæ integritáte conspícuus, emícuit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, holy Theophilus, Bishop of that see, who was a great light for wisdom and good living in the time of the Emperor Severus.

entries.lat: Ad ripam Jordánis, item in Palæstína, sancti Gerásimi, Anachorétæ et Abbátis, qui témpore Zenónis Imperatóris flóruit.
entries.eng: Likewise in Palestine, on the bank of the Jordan, the holy hermit Gerasimus, who flourished in the time of the Emperor Zeno.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, deposítio sancti Joánnis-Joséphi a Cruce, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Confessóris, qui, sanctórum Francísci Assisiénsis et Petri de Alcántara stúdia æmulátus, Ordini Seráphico insígne decus áddidit, atque a Gregório Papa Décimo sexto in Sanctórum cánonem est relátus.
entries.eng: At Naples, holy John Joseph of the Cross, barefooted Friar Minor, first Provincial of the Italian followers of holy Peter of Alcantara. He strove to tread in the footsteps of holy Francis of Assisi and Peter of Alcantara, was a bright ornament of the Seraphic Order, and was numbered among the saints by Pope Gregory XVI.

entries.lat: Sanctárum Perpétuæ et Felicitátis Mártyrum, quæ sequénti die gloriósam martýrii corónam a Dómino recepérunt.
entries.eng: The holy Martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas, who on the following day received from the Lord the glorious crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Dertónæ sancti Marciáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, sub Trajáno, pro Christi glória occísus, coronátur.
entries.eng: At Tortona, the holy martyr Marcian, Bishop of that see, who was crowned under the Emperor Trajan, being slain for Christ's greater glory.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Victóris et Victoríni, qui, per triénnium, cum Claudiáno et uxóre ejus Bassa, torméntis multis afflícti et retrúsi in cárcerem, ibídem vitæ suæ cursum implevérunt.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Victor and Victorinus, who were imprisoned for three years, and many ways tormented, along with Claudian and Bassa his wife, and being still recommitted to prison, died therein,.

entries.lat: In Cypro sancti Conónis Mártyris, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre, clavis confíxus pedes et ante currum jussus cúrrere, in génua procúbuit, atque in oratióne réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: In Cyprus, the holy martyr Conon, who under the Emperor Decius had nails driven through his feet, and was then made to run in front of a chariot, under the which torment he fell upon his knees and gave up his soul in prayer to God.

entries.lat: In Sýria pássio sanctórum quadragínta duórum Mártyrum, qui, in Amório comprehénsi et illuc perdúcti, ibi, egrégio perácto certámine, victóres palmam martýrii percepérunt.
entries.eng: Likewise, forty-two holy martyrs, who were apprehended in Amorium and brought to Syria, where they passed through a noble conflict and triumphantly grasped the palm of martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Evágrii, qui, témpore Valéntis a Cathólicis eléctus Epíscopus, et ab eódem Imperatóre in exsílium missus, Conféssor migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Evagrius, who was elected Patriarch of that see by the Catholics in the time of the Emperor Valens, but was sent by the Emperor into exile, and there passed away to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Basilíi Epíscopi, qui, a sancto Silvéstro Papa ordinátus, verbo et exémplo créditam sibi Ecclésiam sanctíssime gubernávit.
entries.eng: At Bologna, holy Basil, Bishop of that city, who was ordained by holy Pope Sylvester, and both by his word and example governed in holiness the church committed unto his care,.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, beáti Ollegárii, primum Canónici, et póstea Epíscopi Barcinonénsis, et Archiepíscopi Tarraconénsis.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, in Spain, blessed Ollegarius, first a Canon, and afterwards Bishop of Barcelona, and Archbishop of Tarragona.

entries.lat: Vitérbii beátæ Rosæ Vírginis, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci.
entries.eng: At Viterbo, the blessed Virgin Rose, of the Third Order of St. Francis.

entries.lat: Apud Gandávum, in Flándria, sanctæ Colétæ Vírginis, quæ, primum tértii Ordinis Franciscális régulam proféssa, deínde, divíno Spíritu affláta, quamplúra Moniálium secúndi ejúsdem Ordinis monastéria primǽvæ restítuit disciplínæ; atque, divínis exornáta virtútibus et innúmeris clara miráculis, a Pio Séptimo, Pontífice Máximo, in albo Sanctórum adscrípta est.
entries.eng: At Gent, in Flanders, the holy Virgin Coletta, who first professed in the Third Order of Friars Minors, and then being filled with the Holy Ghost, set up many monasteries of sisters of the Second Order under the primitive discipline. She was ennobled by the grace of God, and famous for countless miracles, and the Supreme Pontiff Pius VII enrolled her name among those of the saints.

entries.lat: In monastério Fossæ Novæ, prope Tarracínam, in Campánia, sancti Thomæ Aquinátis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, nobilitáte géneris, vitæ sanctitáte et Theológiæ sciéntia illustríssimi; quem Leo Papa Décimus tértius cæléstem Scholárum ómnium catholicárum Patrónum declarávit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Fossa Nuova, near Terracina, the holy Confessor Thomas of Aquino, of the Order of Friars Preachers, Doctor of the Church, illustrious for the nobility of his birth, the holiness of his life, and the depth of his knowledge of theology. Leo XIII declared him the patron in heaven of all Catholic schools.

entries.lat: Carthágine natális sanctárum Perpétuæ et Felicitátis Mártyrum; e quibus Felícitas, cum esset prægnans (ut sanctus Augustínus ait), juxta leges exspectáta ut páreret, dum parturiébat, dolébat, objécta feris gaudébat. Passi quoque sunt cum eis Sátyrus, Saturnínus, Revocátus et Secúndulus; quorum últimus quiévit in cárcere, réliqui omnes a váriis béstiis sunt vexáti, ac demum gládiorum íctibus confécti, sub Sevéro Príncipe. Sanctárum vero Perpétuæ et Felicitátis festum prídie hujus diéi recólitur.
entries.eng: At Tuburbe, in Morocco, under the Emperor Severus, the holy martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas. Felicitas was with child, and therefore was respited, in accordance with the law, until after she was delivered. Holy Augustine saith that when she was in travail she had sorrow, but when she was set before the wild beasts she rejoiced. There suffered along with them Revocatus, Saturninus, and Secundolus, of whom the last died in prison, but the others were all killed by beasts.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, pássio sancti Eubúli, qui fuit sócius sancti Hadriáni, atque, bíduo post illum, laniátus a leónibus et gládio trucidátus, martýrii corónam, últimus ómnium in ea civitáte, accépit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyr Eubulus. He was a Companion of holy Hadrian, and two days after him was mangled by the lions and then despatched with the sword, being the last of all those who received the crown of martyrdom in that city,.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Theóphili Epíscopi, qui, ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum in exsílium pulsus, illic defúnctus est.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, holy Theophilus, Bishop of that see, who for his honouring of holy images was sent into exile and there died,.

entries.lat: Pelúsii, in Ægýpto, sancti Pauli Epíscopi, qui, eándem ob causam, exsul occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Pelusium, in Egypt, holy Paul, Bishop of that see, who likewise died in exile for the same cause.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Gaudiósi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Confessor Gaudiosus, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Pauli, cognoménto Símplicis.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, holy Paul, surnamed the Simple.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ, in Etrúria, sanctæ Terésiæ Margarítæ Redi, Vírginis, Ordinis Carmelitárum Excalceatárum, vitæ puritáte ac simplicitáte admirábilis, quam Pius Papa Undécimus, sanctárum Vírginum albo adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Florence, in Tuscany, holy Teresa Margaret Redi, Virgin, of the Order of Discalced Carmelites, admirable for the purity and simplicity of her life, whom Pope Pius XI inscribed in the roll of holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Granátæ, in Hispánia, sancti Joánnis de Deo Confessóris, qui Ordinis Fratrum Hospitalitátis infirmórum fuit Institútor, ac misericórdia in páuperes et sui despéctu éxstitit insígnis; quem Leo Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, cæléstem ómnium hospitálium et infirmórum Patrónum renuntiavit.
entries.eng: At Granada, in Spain, holy John of God, founder of the Order of brethren Hospitallers of the Sick. Famous for his pity toward the poor, and for his lowly esteem of himself, whom the Supreme Pontiff Leo XIII. declared the patron in heaven of all the sick and those who nurse them, whose feast we keep upon the 11th day of this present month of March.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Quinctílis, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyr Quinctilis, Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Cyrílli Epíscopi, Rogáti, Felícis, item Rogáti, Beátæ, Heréniæ, Felicitátis, Urbáni, Silváni et Mamílli.
entries.eng: In Africa likewise, the holy Bishop Cyril, Rogatus, Felix, another Rogatus, Beata, Herenia, Felicitas, Urban, Silvan, and Mamillus.

entries.lat: Apud Antínoum, Ægýpti urbem, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Apollónii Diáconi, et Philémonis; qui, tenti et ad Júdicem addúcti, et, cum sacrificáre idólis constánter renuíssent, ambo, perforátis calcáneis, per civitátem horribíliter tracti, ac novíssime, gládio cæsi, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: At Antinoe, in Egypt, the holy martyrs Philemon and Apolonius the Deacon. They were arrested, and brought before the judge, but as they steadfastly refused to sacrifice to idols their heels were bored through, and they were cruelly dragged about the city until at last they were dispatched with the sword.

entries.lat: Ibídem pássio sanctórum Ariáni Prǽsidis, Theótici et aliórum trium, quos Judex submérsos in mare necávit, sed delphinórum obséquio córpora eórum ad littus deláta sunt.
entries.eng: There also the holy martyrs the President Arian, Theoticus, and three others whom the judge caused to be drowned in the sea, but their bodies were brought to the shore by dolphins,.

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Póntii, qui fuit Diáconus beáti Cypriáni Epíscopi, et, usque ad diem mortis illíus sústinens cum ipso exsílium, vitæ et passiónis ejus egrégium volúmen relíquit, atque, in suis passiónibus Dóminum semper gloríficans, corónam vitæ proméruit.
entries.eng: At Carthage, holy Pontius, Deacon to blessed Bishop Cyprian, with whom he remained in exile even unto the day of his death, and hath left unto us an excellent book of his life and passion.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, deposítio beáti Juliáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, sanctitáte et doctrína celebérrimi.
entries.eng: At Toledo, in Spain, the blessed Confessor Julian, Bishop of that see, Very famous for his holiness and teaching,.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Felícis Epíscopi, qui orientáles Anglos ad fidem convértit.
entries.eng: In England, the holy Bishop Felix, who converted the East Angles to the faith.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Francíscæ Víduæ, nobilitáte géneris, vitæ sanctitáte et miraculórum dono célebris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy widow Frances, famous for her nobleness of birth, the holiness of her life, and the grace of working miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Sebásten, in Arménia, natális sanctórum quadragínta mílitum Cappádocum, qui, témpore Licínii Imperatóris, sub Prǽside Agricoláo, post víncula et cárceres tetérrimos, post cæsas lapídibus fácies, nudi sub dio, frigidíssimo híemis témpore, supra stagnum rigens pernoctáre jussi sunt, ubi gelu constrícta eórum córpora disrumpebántur, ac demum crurifrágio martýrium consummárunt. Erant autem inter eos nobilióres Cýrion et Cándidus; eorúmque ómnium præcláras glórias sanctus Basilíus aliíque Patres scriptis suis celebrárunt. Ipsórum porro Mártyrum festívitas sequénti die recólitur.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, in Armenia, the forty holy Cappadocian soldiers. Under the President Agricolaus, in the time of the Emperor Licinius, after undergoing bonds and a foul imprisonment, and after their faces had been bruised with stones, they were stripped naked, and exposed all night upon the surface of a frozen pool during the bitterest cold of winter, where their bodies perished by the frost, and at length by the breaking of their legs. The illustrious glory of them all hath been celebrated by holy Basil, and the other Fathers in their writings, the chief among them were named Cyrion and Candidus. We keep their feast upon the morrow after.

entries.lat: Nyssæ deposítio sancti Gregórii Epíscopi, qui sanctórum Basilíi et Emméliæ fílius, et sanctórum item Basilíi Magni ac Petri Sebasténsis Episcopórum et Macrínæ Vírginis frater éxstitit; atque, vita et eruditióne claríssimus, ob fídei cathólicæ defensiónem, sub Ariáno Imperatóre Valénte, civitáte sua pulsus est.
entries.eng: At Nyssa, holy Gregory, Bishop of that see, brother of blessed Basil the Great. He is very famous for his life and learning. For defending the Catholic faith he was driven out of his own city by the Arian Emperor Valens.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, sancti Paciáni Epíscopi, tam vita quam sermóne conspícui; qui, témpore Theodósii Príncipis, in última senectúte finem vitæ sortítus est.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, in Spain, holy Pacian, Bishop of that see, famous not only for his life but also for his words, who died in a good old age in the time of the Emperor Theodosius.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sanctæ Catharínæ Vírginis, e secúndo Ordine sancti Francísci, quæ vitæ sanctitáte fuit illústris. Ipsíus autem corpus magno cum honóre ibídem cólitur.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy Virgin Catherine, of the Second Order of St. Francis, who was illustrious for holiness of life. Her body is venerated there with great honour.

entries.lat: Sanctórum Quadragínta Mártyrum, quorum natális prídie hujus diéi recensétur.
entries.eng: The Forty holy Martyrs, whose birthday is recorded on the day before this.

entries.lat: Apaméæ, in Phrýgia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Caji et Alexándri, qui (ut scribit Apollináris, Hierapolitánus Epíscopus, in libro advérsus Cataphrýgas hæréticos), in persecutióne Marci Antoníni et Lúcii Veri, glorióso martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Apamea, in Phrygia, the holy martyrs Caius and Alexander, who were crowned with a glorious martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperors Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Verus, as is written by Appolinaris, Bishop of Hierapolis, in his book against the heretics called Cataphrygians.

entries.lat: In Pérside pássio sanctórum quadragínta duórum Mártyrum.
entries.eng: In Persia, the passion of forty-two holy Martyrs.

entries.lat: Corínthi sanctórum Mártyrum Codráti, Dionýsii, Cypriáni, Anécti, Pauli et Crescéntis, qui, in persecutióne Décii et Valeriáni, sub Jásone Prǽside, gládio cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Corinth, the holy martyrs Codratus, Denis, Cyprian, Anectus, Paul, and Crescens, who were slain with the sword under the President Jason, in the persecution under the Emperors Decius and Valerian.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Victóris Mártyris, in cujus solemnitáte sanctus Augustínus ad pópulum de ipso tractátum hábuit.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyr Victor, on whose feast day holy Augustine addressed a discourse to the people.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Simplícii, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope and Confessor Simplicius.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Macárii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus hortátu loca sancta a Constantíno Magno et beáta Heléna, ejus matre, expurgáta sunt et sacris Basílicis illustráta.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the holy Confessor Macarius, Patriarch of that see, at whose exhortation Constantine and Helen cleansed the holy places, and adorned them with hallowed churches,.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum deposítio sancti Droctovéi Abbátis, qui fuit discípulus beáti Germáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Paris, holy Drostovseus, Abbot the disciple of blessed Germain, Bishop.

entries.lat: In monastério Bobiénsi sancti Attalæ Abbátis, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Bobbio, holy Attala, Abbot famous for miracles,.

entries.lat: Sardis sancti Euthýmii Epíscopi, qui, ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum, a Michaéle, Imperatóre Iconoclásta, in exsílium missus est; ac demum, Theóphilo imperánte, búbulis nervis inhumániter cæsus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Sardis, holy Euthymius, Bishop of that see, who for his honouring of holy images was banished by the Iconoclast Emperor Michael, and martyred under Theophilus.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sancti Eulógii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, in persecutióne Saracenórum, ob præcláram et intrépidam Christi confessiónem, verbéribus et álapis cæsus ac decollátus gládio, adjúngi ejúsdem urbis Martýribus méruit, quorum pro fide certámina scribéndo fúerat æmulátus.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy Priest Eulogius, who deserved a place among the martyrs of the said city, in the persecution under the Saracens, by striving by his writings to rival their contendings for the faith,.

entries.lat: Carthágine sanctórum Mártyrum Heráclii et Zósimi.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy martyrs Heraclius and Zosimus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio sanctórum Cándidi, Piperiónis et aliórum vigínti.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Candidus, Piperion, and twenty others.

entries.lat: Laodicéæ, in Sýria, sanctórum Mártyrum Tróphimi et Thali, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, post multa sǽvaque torménta, corónas glóriæ sunt assecúti.
entries.eng: At Laodicea, in Syria, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Trophimus and Thalus, who after many cruel torments gained crowns of glory.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, quorum álii, Maximiáni Imperatóris mandáto, candéntibus cratículis superpósiti, non ad mortem sed ad diutúrnum cruciátum assáti, álii áliis sævíssimis affécti supplíciis, ad palmam martýrii pervenérunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, are commemorated many holy martyrs, of whom some were laid upon beds of red-hot iron by command of the Emperor Maximian, not until they died, but until their flesh was cooked, so as to ensure their prolonged suffering and others were put to other most cruel torments, before they received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Gorgónii et Firmi.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Gorgonius and Firmus.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Sophrónii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, holy Sophronius, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Benedícti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Benedict, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: In fínibus Ambianénsium sancti Firmíni Abbátis.
entries.eng: In the neighbourhood of Amiens, the holy Abbot Firmin.

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Constantíni Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy Confessor Constantine.

entries.lat: Babúci, in Hérnicis, sancti Petri Confessóris, miraculórum glória conspícui.
entries.eng: At Bauco, among the Hernici, the holy Confessor Peter, famous for the glory of his miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Gregórii Primi, Papæ, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris exímii; qui, ob res præcláre gestas atque Anglos ad Christi fidem convérsos, Magnus est dictus et Anglórum Apóstolus appellátus.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Gregory I, Confessor and eminent Doctor of the Church, who, for his illustrious deeds and for the conversion of the English to the faith of Christ, was called the Great, and named the Apostle of the English.

entries.lat: Ibídem deposítio sancti Innocéntii Primi, Papæ et Confessóris. Ipsíus autem festum quinto Kaléndas Augústi celebrátur.
entries.eng: In the same place, the burial of the holy Pope and Confessor Innocent I. His feast is kept on the 28th day of July.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Mamiliáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyr Mamilian,.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctórum Egdúni Presbýteri, et aliórum septem, qui sínguli diébus síngulis suffocáti sunt, ut céteris metus incuterétur.
entries.eng: There likewise the holy martyrs Egdunus the Priest, and seven others, of whom one was strangled every day in order to terrify the others,.

entries.lat: Ibídem pássio sancti Petri Mártyris, qui, cum esset cubiculárius Diocletiáni Imperatóris, et libérius de imménsis Mártyrum supplíciis quererétur, proptérea, jubénte eódem, in médium addúcitur, ac primo suspénsus, diutíssime flagris torquétur, deínde acéto ac sale perfúsus, ad últimum in cratícula lento igne assátur, sicque vere Petri éxstitit et fídei heres et nóminis.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the blessed martyr Peter. He was a chamberlain to the Emperor Diocletian, and because he bewailed the fearful slaughter of martyrs, the Emperor commanded him to be brought forth, hung up, and lashed for a long time. After which he was covered with vinegar and salt, and at length roasted upon a grating upon a slow fire, and thus is he worthy to be reckoned a true inheritor of Peter's faith, as well as Peter's name.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Theóphanis, qui, ex ditíssimo pauper Mónachus efféctus, ab ímpio Leóne Arméno, pro cultu sacrárum Imáginum, biénnio deténtus est in cárcere, et inde in Samothráciam deportátus, ibídem, ærúmnis conféctus, réddidit spíritum, multísque miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Theophanes. He was originally a very rich man, but became a monk. The wicked Emperor Leo, the Armenian, kept him for two years in prison for honouring holy images, and then banished him to Samo-Thrace, where he sank under his sufferings and gave up the ghost, He is famous for many miracles.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Bernárdi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy Confessor Bernard, Bishop of Calenum,.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Ruderíci Presbýteri, et Salomónis.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy martyrs Roderick the Priest and Salomon,.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Macedónii, Patríciæ uxóris, et Modéstæ fíliæ.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Macedonius, Patricia his wife, and Modesta their daughter,.

entries.lat: Nicǽæ, in Bithýnia, sanctórum Mártyrum Theusétæ, ejúsque fílii Horris, Theodóræ, Nymphodóræ, Marci et Arábiæ; qui omnes pro Christo igni tráditi sunt.
entries.eng: At Nice, the holy martyrs Theusetas and Horres his son, Theodora, Nymphodora, Mark, and Arabia, who were all delivered over to the flames for Christ's sake.

entries.lat: Hermópoli, in Ægýpto, sancti Sabíni Mártyris, qui multa passus, tandem, projéctus in flumen, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Eshman, in Egypt, the holy martyr Sabinus, who after suffering many things, was at length drowned in the Nile,.

entries.lat: In Pérside sanctæ Christínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy Virgin and martyr Christina.

entries.lat: Apud Camerínum sancti Ansovíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Camerino, the holy Confessor Ansovinus, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: In Thebáide deposítio sanctæ Euphrásiæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, the holy Virgin Euphrasia,.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli Translátio sancti Nicéphori, Epíscopi ejúsdem urbis et Confessóris; cujus corpus e Proconnéso, Propóntidis ínsula, ubi ipse quarto Nonas Júnii ob sanctárum Imáginum cultum exsul obíerat, Constantinópolim relátum est, atque a sancto illíus civitátis Epíscopo Methódio, honorífice in templo sanctórum Apostolórum sepúltum, hac ipsa recurrénte die, in qua olim idem Nicéphorus in exsílium fúerat deportátus.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Nicephorus, Bishop of that see. He was a zealous upholder of the traditions of the Fathers, and for the honouring of holy images constantly withstood the Iconoclast Emperor Leo the Armenian, by whom he was sent into exile, where he suffered a lingering martyrdom for fourteen years, and then passed away to be ever with the Lord,.

entries.lat: Romæ, in agro Veráno, sancti Leónis, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the Veranian field, the holy martyr Leo, Bishop.

entries.lat: Item Romæ natális sanctórum quadragínta septem Mártyrum, qui baptizáti sunt a beáto Apóstolo Petro, cum tenerétur in custódia Mamertíni cum Coapóstolo suo Paulo, ubi novem menses deténti sunt; qui omnes, sub devotíssima fídei confessióne, Neroniáno gládio consúmpti sunt.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, forty-seven holy martyrs, who were all baptized by the blessed Apostle Peter during the nine months during which he and his fellow-Apostle Paul were imprisoned in the Mamertine prison, and who, all for the loyal confession of their faith, were slain by the sword, under the Emperor Nero.

entries.lat: In Província Valériæ sanctórum duórum Monachórum, quos Longobárdi suspéndio necavérunt in árbore; in qua Mártyres, licet defúncti, ab hóstibus ipsis audíti sunt psállere.
entries.eng: In the Province of Valeria, two holy Monks, whom the Lombards put to death by hanging on a tree; and in that tree the Martyrs, though dead, were heard by their very enemies to sing psalms.

entries.lat: In ea étiam persecutióne Diáconus Ecclésiæ Marsicánæ, in confessióne fídei, cápite truncátus est.
entries.eng: In the same persecution also, a Deacon of the Church of the Marsi was beheaded for the confession of the faith.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Petri et Aphrodísii, qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, martýrii corónam percepérunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Peter and Aphrodisius, who received their crown in the persecution under the Vandals.

entries.lat: Carrhis, in Mesopotámia, sancti Eutýchii patrícii, et Sociórum, qui ab Evelid, Arabum Rege, ob fídei confessiónem, interémpti sunt.
entries.eng: At Haran, in Mesopotamia, the holy martyrs Eutychius the Patrician and his Companions, who were slain by Evelid, King of the Arabs, for confessing their faith,.

entries.lat: Halberstátti, in Germánia, dormítio beátæ Mathíldis Regínæ, matris Othónis Primi, Romanórum Imperatóris, humilitáte et patiéntia conspícuæ.
entries.eng: At Halberstadt, in Germany, the blessed Matilda, Queen of the Romans, Mother of the Emperor Otto I, who fell asleep in peace, illustrious for her lowliness and long suffering,.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, pássio sancti Longíni mílitis, qui Dómini latus láncea perforásse perhibétur.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Longinus, who is said to have been the soldier who pierced the Lord's side with a spear.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális sancti Aristobúli, Apostolórum discípuli, qui, cursu prædicatiónis perácto, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, holy Aristobulus, the disciple of the Apostles, who when the work of his preaching was done, suffered martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Hellespónto sancti Menígni fullónis, qui sub Décio Imperatóre passus est.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Menignus, a fuller, who suffered under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Nicándri Mártyris, qui, cum sanctórum Mártyrum relíquias studióse perquíreret, et ipse méruit éffici Martyr, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy martyr Nicander, who would make careful search for the relics of holy martyrs, and earned to become a martyr himself under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctæ Leocrítiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ ob Christi fidem, in persecutióne Arábica, divérsis cruciátibus afflícta et gládio decolláta est.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy Virgin and martyr Leocritia,.

entries.lat: Thessalonícæ sanctæ Matrónæ, quæ, cum esset ancílla cujúsdam Judǽæ, et occúlte Christum cóleret, ac furtívis oratiónibus quotídie Ecclésiam frequentáret, a dómina sua est deprehénsa et multiplíciter afflícta, atque novíssime, robústis fústibus usque ad mortem cæsa, in confessióne Christi, incorrúptum Deo spíritum réddidit.
entries.eng: At Thessalonica, holy Matrona. She was a slave, belonging to a certain Jewess. She was a Christian in secret, and went to the church every day for private prayer. Her mistress found this. She afflicted her in many ways, and at last caused her to be cudgelled, until, still confessing Christ, she gave up her pure spirit to God,.

entries.lat: Reáte sancti Probi Epíscopi, cui moriénti Juvenális et Eleuthérius Mártyres adfuérunt.
entries.eng: At Riete, holy Probus, Bishop of that see, at whose death, the martyrs Juvenal and Eleutherius were present.

entries.lat: Vindobónæ, in Austria, sancti Cleméntis-Maríæ Hofbauer, Sacerdótis proféssi Congregatiónis a sanctíssimo Redemptóre nuncupátæ, plúrimis in Dei glória et animárum salúte promovénda ac dilatánda ipsa Congregatióne exantlátis labóribus insígnis; quem, virtútibus et miráculis clarum, Pius Décimus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctórum cánonem rétulit.
entries.eng: At Vienna, in Austria, St. Clement Mary Hofbauer, a professed Priest of the Congregation called of the Most Holy Redeemer, renowned for the very many labours he endured in promoting the glory of God and the salvation of souls and in spreading that same Congregation; whom, famous for virtues and miracles, the Sovereign Pontiff Pius X enrolled in the canon of the Saints.

entries.lat: Apud Cápuam sancti Speciósi Mónachi, cujus ánimam (ut scribit beátus Gregórius Papa) germánus ejus deférri vidit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy monk, Speciosus, whose soul his brother saw being borne heavenward.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sanctæ Ludovícæ de Marillac, víduæ Le Gras, Societátis Puellárum a Caritáte una cum sancto Vincéntio a Paulo Fundatrícis, egénis sublevándis addictíssimæ, quam Pius Papa Undécimus Sanctárum fastis accénsuit.
entries.eng: At Paris, St. Louise de Marillac, widow Le Gras, Foundress together with St. Vincent de Paul of the Society of the Daughters of Charity, most devoted to the relief of the needy, whom Pope Pius XI added to the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sancti Cyríaci Diáconi, qui, post longam cárceris maceratiónem, liquáta pice perfúsus et in catásta exténsus, attráctus étiam nervis et fústibus cæsus, ad últimum, cum Largo et Smarágdo et áliis vigínti, jubénte Maximiáno, cápite truncátus est. Sanctórum vero Cyríaci, Largi et Smarágdi festívitas sexto Idus Augústi recólitur, quo die a beáto Marcéllo Papa córpora eorúndem vigínti trium Mártyrum leváta sunt ac venerabíliter tumuláta.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy deacon Cyriacus.

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ natális beáti Hilárii Epíscopi, et Tatiáni Diáconi, qui, sub Numeriáno Imperatóre et Berónio Prǽside, post equúleum atque ália torménta, una cum Felíce, Largo et Dionýsio, martýrium terminárunt.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, the blessed martyrs Hilary, Bishop of that see, and the Deacon Tatian, who after suffering the rack and other torments were martyred, along with Felix, Largus, and Denis, under the President Beronius, in the persecution under the Emperor Numerian.

entries.lat: In Lycaónia sancti Papæ Mártyris, qui, ob Christi fidem, verbéribus cæsus, úngulis férreis lacerátus, clavátis cálceis incédere jussus est; deínde arbóri alligátus, eándem arbórem, migrans ad Dóminum, ex stérili réddidit fructuósam.
entries.eng: In Lycaonia, the holy martyr Papas, who for Christ's faith's sake was hided, torn with iron hooks, and made to walk in shoes with nails through them, and then tied up to a barren tree, which became fruitful when he passed away to be with the Lord,.

entries.lat: Anazárbi, in Cilícia, sancti Juliáni Mártyris, qui, sub Marciáno Prǽside, diutíssime cruciátus, demum, in sacco una cum serpéntibus inclúsus, in mare demérsus est.
entries.eng: At Anazarba, in Cilicia, the holy martyr Julian, who suffered a long course of torture under the President Martian, and was at length put into a sack along with serpents and drowned in the sea,.

entries.lat: In dicióne Canadénsi sanctórum Mártyrum Joánnis de Brébeuf, Gabriélis Lalemant, Antónii Daniel, Cároli Garnier et Natális Chabanel, Presbyterórum Societátis Jesu, qui in Hurónica Missióne, hac aliísque diébus, post multos labóres et sævíssimos cruciátus, mortem pro Christo fórtiter obiérunt.
entries.eng: In the dominion of Canada, the holy Martyrs John de Brébeuf, Gabriel Lalemant, Anthony Daniel, Charles Garnier and Noel Chabanel, Priests of the Society of Jesus, who in the Huron Mission, on this and other days, after many labours and most cruel torments, bravely met death for Christ.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Agapíti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor Agapitus, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ sancti Heribérti Epíscopi, sanctitáte célebris.
entries.eng: At Cologne, holy Heribert, Bishop of that see, famous for his holiness,.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Patrícii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In Auvergne, holy Bishop Patrick.

entries.lat: In Sýria sancti Abrahæ Eremítæ, cujus res gestas beátus Ephræm Diáconus conscrípsit.
entries.eng: In Syria, the holy hermit Abraham, whose acts have been written by the blessed Deacon Ephrem.

entries.lat: Apud civitátem Dunum, in Hibérnia, natális sancti Patrícii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui primus in ea ínsula Christum evangelizávit, et máximis miráculis et virtútibus cláruit.
entries.eng: At the city of Down, in Ireland, the birthday of the holy Bishop and Confessor Patrick, who was the first to preach Christ in that island, and was renowned for very great miracles and virtues.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Joseph ab Arimathǽa, qui nóbilis Decúrio et discípulus Dómini éxstitit; atque ipsíus Dómini corpus, de cruce depósitum, in monuménto suo novo sepelívit.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, holy Joseph of Arimathea, the honourable councillor, the disciple of the Lord, who took down His Body from the cross and laid it in his own new tomb.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Alexándri et Theodóri Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander and Theodore.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui a Serápidis cultóribus comprehénsi, et, cum adoráre idólum constánter renuíssent, sævíssime cæsi sunt, témpore Theodósii Imperatóris; qui mox rescríptum dedit, ut Serápidis templum destruerétur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria are commemorated many holy martyrs, who were seized by the worshippers of Serapis, and because they would not worship that idol were cruelly murdered by them, in the time of the Emperor Theodosius, who presently afterward sent a rescript to destroy the temple of Serapis.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Pauli Mártyris, qui, sub Constantíno Coprónymo, cum sanctárum Imáginum cultum defénderet, igne combústus est.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyr Paul, who was burnt under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus for defending the honouring of holy images.

entries.lat: Cabillóne, in Gálliis, sancti Agrícolæ Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Chalons in Gaul, holy Agricola, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Nivigéllæ, in Brabántia, sanctæ Gertrúdis Vírginis, quæ, claríssimo génere orta, despíciens mundum et toto vitæ suæ cursu in ómnibus sanctitátis offíciis se exércens, Christum sponsum in cælis habére méruit.
entries.eng: At Nivelles, in Brabant, the holy Virgin Gertrude, the daughter of an illustrious race, who despised this world, and busied herself all her life in holy deeds, so that she won to be espoused to Christ in heaven,.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Cyrílli Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, ab Ariánis multas pro fídei causa perpéssus injúrias et ex Ecclésia sua sæpe depúlsus, tandem, sanctitátis glória clarus, in pace quiévit. Ipsíus porro intemerátam fidem prima Constantinopolitána Sýnodus œcuménica, sancto Dámaso Papæ scribens, præcláro testimónio commendávit.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the holy Bishop Cyril, Confessor and Doctor of the Church, who suffered many injuries from the Arians for the cause of the faith, and was often driven from his Church; at length, famous for the glory of his holiness, he rested in peace. Moreover the first Ecumenical Council of Constantinople, writing to the holy Pope Damasus, commended his unblemished faith by an illustrious testimony.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, natális beáti Alexándri Epíscopi, qui de Cappadócia, ex própria civitáte, ubi erat Epíscopus, sanctórum locórum desidério Hierosólymam pétiit; atque ibi, cum a Narcísso, ejúsdem urbis Epíscopo, jam sene, illa regerétur Ecclésia, ipsíus gubernácula, divína edóctus revelatióne, suscépit. Póstmodum vero, in persecutióne Décii, cum jam longǽvæ ætátis veneránda canítie præfulgéret, ductus est Cæsaréam, et clausus in cárcere, ob confessiónem Christi, martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the blessed martyr Alexander, Bishop He came to Jerusalem from his own city, in Cappadocia, whereof he was Bishop, in order to visit the holy places. Narcissus, who was already very old, was then ruling the Church of Jerusalem, and Alexander by the revelation of God received the government thereof, afterward, and when he himself was in the venerable glory of grey hairs he was brought to Caesarea in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, and was put in prison, and finished his testimony confessing Christ.

entries.lat: Augústæ sancti Narcíssi Epíscopi, qui primus in Rhǽtia Evangélium prædicávit; deínde in Hispániam proféctus est, et, cum Gerúndæ multos ad Christi fidem convertísset, ibídem, in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, una cum Felíce Diácono, martýrii palmam accépit.
entries.eng: At Augsburg, the holy martyrs Narcissus, Bishop of Augsburg, and the Deacon Felix. Narcissus was the first who preached the gospel in Rhaetia. He afterwards went into Spain, and after he had brought many to believe in Christ at Girona he there received the palm of martyrdom, along with the Deacon Felix, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctórum decem míllium Mártyrum, qui, pro Christi confessióne, gládio percússi sunt.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the ten thousand holy martyrs who were slain with the sword for confessing Christ.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Tróphimi et Eucárpii.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Trophimus and Eucarpius,.

entries.lat: In Británnia sancti Eduárdi Regis, qui, dolis novércæ necátus, multis miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: In Britain, the holy King Edward, who, slain by the treachery of his stepmother, was famous for many miracles.

entries.lat: Lucæ, in Túscia, natális sancti Frigdiáni Epíscopi, virtúte miraculórum illústris.
entries.eng: At Lucca, in Tuscany, the birthday of the holy Bishop Frigidian, illustrious for the power of his miracles.

entries.lat: Mántuæ sancti Ansélmi, Epíscopi Lucénsis et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Mantua, the holy Confessor Anselm, Bishop of the see,.

entries.lat: Cárali, in Sardínia, sancti Salvatóris ab Horta, Confessóris, ex Ordine Fratrum Minórum, qui, virtútibus et singulári miraculórum dono cláruit, et a Pio Papa Undécimo inter sanctos Cǽlites adnumerátus est.
entries.eng: At Cagliari, in Sardinia, the holy Confessor Salvator of Horta, of the Order of Friars Minor, who was famous for his virtues and for a singular gift of miracles, and was numbered among the holy Citizens of heaven by Pope Pius XI.

entries.lat: In Judǽa natális sancti Joseph, Sponsi beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ, Confessóris; quem Pius Nonus, Póntifex Máximus, votis et précibus ánnuens totíus cathólici Orbis, universális Ecclésiæ Patrónum declarávit.
entries.eng: In Judea, holy Joseph, the husband of the most Blessed Virgin Mary. The Supreme Pontiff Pius IX., in answer to the wish and request of the whole Catholic world, declared him Patron of the universal Church.

entries.lat: Surrénti sanctórum Mártyrum Quincti, Quinctíllæ, Quartíllæ et Marci, cum áliis novem.
entries.eng: At Sorrento, the holy martyrs Quintus, Quintilla, Quartilla, Mark, and nine others.

entries.lat: Nicomédiæ sancti Panchárii Románi, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, in hujus grátiam Christum pro diis inánibus ejurávit, sed, matre ac soróre instántibus, ad veram fidem mox rédivit, et ob immótam in ea constántiam, nervis cæsus et cápite truncátus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, holy Pancharius, the Roman, who was beheaded under the Emperor Diocletian, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Apollónii et Leóntii Episcopórum.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Bishops Apollonius and Leontius.

entries.lat: Gandávi, in Flándria, sanctórum Landoáldi, Presbýteri Románi, et Amántii Diáconi; qui, a sancto Martíno Papa ad prædicándum Evangélium missi, ambo apostólicum sibi commíssum opus fidéliter implevérunt, ac multis post óbitum sunt illustráti miráculis.
entries.eng: At Gent, the holy Roman Priest Landoald, and Amantius the Deacon, who were sent by holy Pope Martin to preach the gospel, and were famed for many miracles after their deaths,.

entries.lat: Apud Pinnénsem civitátem natális beáti Joánnis, magnæ sanctitátis viri; qui de Sýria ad Itáliam venit, atque ibi, constrúcto monastério, multórum servórum Dei per quátuor et quadragínta annos Pater éxstitit, et, clarus virtútibus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: In the city of Pinna, blessed John, a man of great holiness, who came from Syria to Italy, and there built a monastery, wherein he remained, the Father of many servants of God, for forty-and-four years, and fell asleep in peace, famous for many graces,.

entries.lat: In Judǽa natális sancti Jóachim, patris immaculátæ Vírginis Genetrícis Dei Maríæ, Confessóris. Ipsíus tamen festum ágitur décimo séptimo Kaléndas Septémbris.
entries.eng: In Judea, holy Joachim, father of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God. We keep his feast upon the Lord's day within the octave of the Assumption of the same Blessed Virgin Mary.

entries.lat: In Asia item natális sancti Archíppi, qui beáti Pauli Apóstoli éxstitit commílito, et cujus ipse in Epístola ad Philémonem et ad Colossénses méminit.
entries.eng: In Asia, holy Archippus, the fellowsoldier of the blessed Apostle Paul, of whom the same Apostle doth make mention in his Epistles unto Philemon and unto the Colossians.

entries.lat: In Sýria sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, Cyrílli, Eugénii et aliórum quátuor.
entries.eng: In Syria, the holy martyrs Paul, Cyril, Eugene, and four others.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Photínæ Samaritánæ, Joseph et Victóris filiórum, itémque Sebastiáni Ducis, Anatólii, Phótii, Phótidis, Parascéves et Cyríacæ germanárum; qui omnes, Christum conféssi, martýrium sunt assecúti.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Photina of Samaria and her sons Joseph and Victor, also Sebastian the general, Anatolius, Photius, Photis, Parasceve, and Cyriaca, sisters, who all confessed Christ and obtained martyrdom.

entries.lat: Amísi, in Paphlagónia, sanctárum septem mulíerum, scílicet Alexándræ, Cláudiæ, Euphrásiæ, Matrónæ, Juliánæ, Euphémiæ et Theodósiæ; quæ in fídei confessióne sunt cæsæ, eásque secútæ sunt Derphúta et soror ipsíus.
entries.eng: At Amisus, in Paphlagonia, the seven holy women, Alexandra, Claudia, Euphrasia, Matrona, Juliana, Euphemia, and Theodosia, who were slain for confessing the faith, and to whom were added afterward Derphuta and her sister.

entries.lat: Apollóniæ sancti Nicétæ Epíscopi, qui, pro sanctárum Imáginum cultu ejéctus in exsílium, illic réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Apollonia, holy Nicetas, Bishop of that see, who was driven into banishment for the honouring of holy images, and there gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: In monastério Fontanéllæ, in Gállia, sancti Wulfránni, Epíscopi Senonénsis, qui, relícto Episcopátu, ibídem, clarus miráculis, decéssit e vita.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Fontenelle, in France, holy Wulfran, Bishop of Sens, who, having resigned his Bishopric, departed this life there, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: In Británnia deposítio sancti Cuthbérti, Epíscopi Lindisfarnénsis, qui, a puerítia ad óbitum usque, sanctis opéribus et miraculórum signis effúlsit.
entries.eng: In England, holy Cuthbert, Bishop of Lindisfarne, who from his childhood until his death shone with holy works and miraculous signs.

entries.lat: Senis, in Túscia, Beáti Ambrósii, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, sanctitáte, prædicatióne et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Siena, in Tuscany, blessed Ambrose, of the Order of Preachers, famous for holiness, preaching and miracles.

entries.lat: In monte Cassíno natális sancti Benedicti Abbátis, qui in Occidénte fere collapsam Monachórum disciplínam restituit ac mirifice propagávit; cujus vitam, virtútibus et miraculis gloriosam, beátus Gregórius Papa conscripsit.
entries.eng: At Monte Cassino, the holy Abbot Benedict, who restored Monasticism in the West, when it was almost fallen away, and wonderfully spread it. Blessed Pope Gregory hath written his life, which was rendered glorious by his graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Cátanæ, in Sicília, sancti Birilli, qui, a beato Petro ordinátus Epíscopus, ibidem, cum multos Gentílium convertísset ad fidem, in ultima senectute quievit in pace.
entries.eng: At Catanae holy Birillus, who was ordained Bishop of that see by the blessed Apostle Peter, and after he had converted many Gentiles to the faith fell asleep in peace in extreme old age.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, sub Constantio Imperatóre et Præfecto Philagrio, irruéntibus Ariánis et Gentilibus in Ecclésias, in die Parascéves cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, are commemorated those holy martyrs who were massacred when the Arians and Gentiles broke into the churches on Good Friday, under the Emperor Constantius and the Prefect Philagrius.

entries.lat: Eodem die sanctórum Mártyrum Philémonis et Domníni.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Philemon and Domninus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ beáti Serapiónis, Anachoretæ et Epíscopi Thmúeos, magnárum virtútum viri; qui, Arianórum furóre in exsílium actus, Conféssor migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the blessed Hermit Serapion, Bishop of Thmuis, a man of great power, who was driven into exile by the rage of the Arians, and there passed away to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: In território Lugdunénsi sancti Lupicini Abbátis, cujus vita ob sanctitátis et miraculórum glóriam fuit illústris.
entries.eng: In the country of Lyon, holy Lupicinus, Abbot whose life was made illustrious by the fame of his holiness and miracles.

entries.lat: In loco Ranft, prope Sachseln, in Helvetia, sancti Nicolai de Flüe, patris familias, dein Anachoretæ, arctíssima pæniténtia et mundi contemptu insignis, ab Helvetiis pater patriæ appellati, quem Pius Papa Duodecimus Sanctórum fastis adscripsit.
entries.eng: In the place called Ranft, near Sachseln, in Switzerland, St. Nicholas of Flüe, a father of a family and afterwards a Hermit, renowned for his most rigorous penance and contempt of the world, called by the Swiss the father of his country, whom Pope Pius XII inscribed on the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: Narbóne, in Gállia, natális sancti Pauli Epíscopi, Apostolórum discípuli, quem tradunt fuísse Sérgium Paulum Procónsulem. Hic, a beáto Apóstolo Paulo baptizátus, et ab eo, cum in Hispániam pérgeret, apud Narbónem relíctus, ibídem Episcopáli dignitáte donátus est; ibíque, prædicatiónis offício non ségniter expléto, clarus miráculis migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Narbonne, in Gaul, holy Paul, Bishop of that see. A disciple of the Apostle, who is said to have been the same person as the Proconsul Sergius Paulus, baptized by the blessed Apostle Paul, and on his way into Spain left at Narbonne, where he received the dignity of Bishop, laboured much in the office of preaching, and passed away to heaven, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Tarracínæ, in Campánia, sancti Epaphrodíti, Apostolórum discípuli, qui a beáto Petro Apóstolo Epíscopus illíus civitátis ordinátus fuit.
entries.eng: At Terracina, holy Epaphroditus, the disciple of the Apostles, who was ordained Bishop of the said city, by the blessed Apostle Peter.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, sancti Basilíi, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui sub Juliáno Apóstata, gravíssimis cruciátibus afféctus, ánimam Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, the holy martyr Basil, a Priest, who was put to most grievous torments under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and gave up his soul to God.

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Octaviáni Archidiáconi, et multórum míllium Mártyrum, qui, ob fidem cathólicam, a Wándalis cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy Archdeacon Octavian and many thousand martyrs, who were slaughtered by the Vandals for the Catholic faith's sake.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni et aliórum novem.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Saturninus and nine others.

entries.lat: In Galátia natális sanctárum Mártyrum Callinícæ et Basilíssæ.
entries.eng: In Galatia, the holy martyrs Callinice and Basilissa.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Zacharíæ Papæ, qui Dei Ecclésiam summa vigilántia gubernávit, et clarus méritis quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Zachary, who governed the Church of God with the utmost vigilance, and, famous for his merits, rested in peace.

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Deográtias, Epíscopi Carthaginénsis, qui plúrimos, a Wándalis captívos ex Urbe ductos, redémit, aliísque sanctis opéribus célebris quiévit in Dómino.
entries.eng: There also, holy Deogratias, Bishop of Carthage, who redeemed many captives whom the Vandals had brought from Rome, and fell asleep in the Lord, famous for holy works,.

entries.lat: Auximi, in Picéno, sancti Benvenúti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Osimo, in Picenum, holy Benvenuto, Bishop of that see,.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Leæ Víduæ, cujus virtútes et tránsitum ad Deum sanctus Hierónymus scribit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy widow Lea, whose virtues and passing to God St. Jerome describes.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Victoriáni, Procónsulis Cartháginis, et duórum germanórum, Aquisregénsium; item Fruméntii et altérius Fruméntii, mercatórum. Hi omnes, in persecutióne Wandálica (ut scribit Victor, Africánus Epíscopus), sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, pro constántia cathólicæ confessiónis, immaníssimis supplíciis cruciáti, egrégie coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Victorian, Pro-consul of Carthage, and two brethren from Aquae Regiae, also two merchants, both named Frumentius, all in the persecution by the Vandals, were, on account of the steadfastness of their Catholic confession, put to the most grievous torments under the Arian king Hunneric, and gloriously crowned,.

entries.lat: Item in Africa sancti Fidélis Mártyris.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyr Faithful there also holy Felix and twenty others.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Felícis et aliórum vigínti Mártyrum.
entries.eng: In the same place, the holy Felix and twenty other Martyrs.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum Nicónis et aliórum nonagínta novem.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Nicon, and ninety-nine others.

entries.lat: Item corónæ sanctórum Mártyrum Domítii, Pelágiæ, Aquilæ, Epárchii et Theodósiæ.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Domitius, Pelagia, Aquila, Eparchius, and Theodosia,.

entries.lat: Limæ, in Perúvia, sancti Turíbii Epíscopi, cujus virtúte fides et disciplína ecclesiástica per Amerícam diffúsæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Lima, in the kingdom of Peru, holy Turibius, Archbishop of that see, by whose work the faith and discipline of the church were spread abroad in America.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Theodúli Presbýteri.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy Priest Theodulus.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, sancti Joséphi Oriol Presbýteri, Ecclésiæ sanctæ Maríæ Regum Beneficiárii, omnígena virtúte ac præsértim córporis afflictatióne, paupertátis cultu atque in egénos et infírmos caritáte célebris; quem, in vita et post mortem miráculis gloriósum, Pius Papa Décimus in Sanctórum número recénsuit.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, in Spain, the holy Priest Joseph Oriol, Beneficiary of the Church of St. Mary of the Kings, renowned for every kind of virtue, and especially for the mortification of his body, his love of poverty and his charity towards the needy and the sick; whom, glorious for miracles in life and after death, Pope Pius X numbered among the Saints.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ sancti Juliáni Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, the holy Confessor Julian.

entries.lat: In Campánia sancti Benedícti Mónachi, qui, a Gothis in ardénti clíbano inclúsus, sequénti die invéntus est illǽsus.
entries.eng: In Campania, the holy monk Benedict, who was shut up by the Goths in a glowing furnace, but upon the morrow was found unhurt,.

entries.lat: Festum sancti Gabriélis Archángeli, qui ad annuntiándum Incarnatiónis divíni Verbi mystérium a Deo missus est.
entries.eng: The Feast of St. Gabriel the Archangel, who was sent by God to announce the mystery of the Incarnation of the divine Word.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Epigménii Presbýteri, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Túrpio Júdice, gládio cæsus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: There also the holy martyr Epigmenius, a Priest, who was slain with the sword, by order of the judge Turpius, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Ibídem pássio beáti Pigménii Presbýteri, qui, sub Juliáno Apóstata, pro fide Christi, præcipitátus in Tíberim, necátus est.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the blessed martyr Pigmenius, a Priest, who was cast into the river Tiber for Christ's faith's sake, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Marci et Timóthei, qui martýrio coronáti sunt sub Antoníno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Mark and Timothy, who were crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Timolái, Dionýsii, Páusidis, Rómuli, Alexándri, altérius Alexándri, Agápii et altérius Dionýsii; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Urbáno Prǽside, secúris ictu percússi, vitæ corónas meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, were born into the better life: the holy martyrs Timolaus, Denis, Pausides, Romulus, Alexander, another Alexander, Agapius, and another Denis, who won crowns of life by the axe, under the president Urban, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: In Mauritánia item natális sanctórum fratrum Rómuli et Secúndi, qui pro Christi fide passi sunt.
