entries.lat: Pragæ, in Bohémia, sancti Joánnis Nepomucéni, Metropolitánæ Ecclésiæ Canónici; qui, frustra tentátus ut sigílli sacramentális fidem próderet, martýrii palmam, in flumen Moldávam dejéctus, eméruit.
entries.eng: At Prague, in Bohemia, holy John of Nepomuc, Canon of the Metropolitical Cathedral Church in that city, who, when he had been vainly tried to make him violate the seal of sacramental confession, was cast into the river Moldau, and so earned the palm of martyrdom. We keep feast in his honour upon the 30th day of this present month of May.

entries.lat: In Isáuria natális sanctórum Mártyrum Aquilíni et Victoriáni.
entries.eng: In Isauria, the holy martyrs Aquilinus and Victorian.

entries.lat: Uzali, in Africa, sanctórum Mártyrum Felícis et Gennádii.
entries.eng: At Usal, in Africa, the holy martyrs Felix and Gennadius.

entries.lat: In Palæstína pássio sanctórum Monachórum, a Saracénis in laura sancti Sabbæ interfectórum.
entries.eng: In Palestine, the passion of the holy monks who were massacred by the Saracens in the Monastery of St Saba.

entries.lat: Janóviæ, apud Pinsk, in Polésia, sancti Andréæ Bobóla, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu, qui, a schismáticis innumerabília tormentórum génera perpéssus, illústri martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: At Janów, near Pinsk, in Polesia, St. Andrew Bobola, Priest of the Society of Jesus, who, having endured innumerable kinds of torments from the schismatics, was crowned with an illustrious martyrdom.

entries.lat: Ambiáni, in Gállia, sancti Honoráti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Amiens, in France, the holy Bishop Honoratus.

entries.lat: Apud Cenómanos, in Gállia, sancti Dómnoli Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Mans, the holy Confessor Domnolus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Mirándulæ, in Æmília, sancti Possídii, Calaménsis in Numídia Epíscopi, qui fuit sancti Augustíni discípulus, ejúsque præcláram vitam scripsit.
entries.eng: At Mirandola, in Emilia, the holy Possidius, Bishop of Calama, in Numidia, a disciple of holy Augustine, and writer of his famous life.

entries.lat: In monastério Enachduinénsi, in Hibérnia, tránsitus sancti Brendáni, Presbýteri et Clonferténsis Abbátis.
entries.eng: In Ireland, the holy Brendan, Abbot.

entries.lat: Trecis, in Gállia, sancti Fídoli Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Troyes, the holy Confessor Fidolus,.

entries.lat: Apud Forum Júlii, in Gállia, sanctæ Máximæ Vírginis, quæ, multis clara virtútibus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Frejus, the holy Virgin Maxima, who fell asleep in peace, famous for many excellences.

entries.lat: Apud Villam Regálem, in Hispánia, sancti Paschális, ex Ordine Minórum, Confessóris, miræ innocentiæ et pæniténtiæ viri; quem Leo Papa Décimus tértius cæléstem eucharisticórum Cóetuum et Societátum a sanctíssima Eucharístia Patrónum declarávit.
entries.eng: At Villa Real, in the kingdom of Valencia, the holy Paschal, of the Order of Friars Minors, a man of wonderful innocency, and wonderful contrition.

entries.lat: Noviodúni, in Gálliis, sanctórum Mártyrum Herádii, Pauli et Aquilíni, cum duóbus áliis.
entries.eng: At Noyon, the holy martyrs Heradius, Paul, and Aquilinus, along with two others.

entries.lat: Chalcedóne sanctórum Mártyrum Solochónis et Sociórum mílitum, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Chalcedon, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Solochan, and the soldiers, his Companions.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Adriónis, Victóris et Basíllæ.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Adrion, Victor, and Basilla.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Restitútæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, in Africa, Valeriáno imperánte, a Próculo Júdice várie torta, et in navículam pice et stupa refértam, ut in mari comburerétur, impósita, tandem, cum in incensóres, immisso igne, flamma converterétur, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit. Ipsíus corpus cum eádem navícula, Dei nutu, ad Ænáriam ínsulam, prope Neápolim, in Campánia, devéctum est, et a Christiánis magna veneratióne suscéptum; ac póstmodum in ejus honórem Constantínus Magnus Basílicam in ipsa urbe Neápoli erigéndam curávit.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Virgin and martyr Restituta. In the reign of the Emperor Valerian, Proculus, the judge in Africa, caused her to be tortured in diverse ways, and put into a ship with pitch and tow that she might burn on the sea, but when fire was put to it the flame turned upon them that kindled it. Restituta gave up her spirit to God in prayer, and, by the will of God, the ship containing her body came to shore in the island of Ischia, near Naples, where her remains were received with great worship by the Christians. In after-days the Emperor Constantine the Great caused a church to be built in her honour at Naples.

entries.lat: Cameríni sancti Venántii Mártyris, qui, annos quíndecim natus, sub Décio Imperatóre et Antíocho Prǽside, una cum áliis decem, gloriósi certáminis cursum, cervícibus abscíssis, implévit.
entries.eng: At Camarino, in the neighbourhood of Ancona, the holy martyr Venantius, who, at fifteen years of age, under Decius the Emperor and Antiochus the President, along with ten others, finished the course of a glorious contention by being beheaded.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ natális sancti Joánnis Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, ab Ariáno Itáliæ Rege Theodoríco illuc dolo evocátus, ibídem, ab eo propter orthodóxam fidem diu macerátus in cárcere, vitam finívit. Ipsíus autem festum recólitur sexto Kaléndas Júnii, quo die sacrum ejus corpus, Romam relátum, in Basílica sancti Petri, Apostolórum Príncipis, sepúltum est.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the birthday of the holy Pope and Martyr John I; who, treacherously summoned thither by Theodoric, the Arian King of Italy, and long worn down by him in prison there for the orthodox faith, ended his life. His feast is kept on the 27th day of May, on which day his sacred body, brought back to Rome, was buried in the Basilica of St. Peter, Prince of the Apostles.

entries.lat: Spoléti sancti Felícis Epíscopi, qui, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, martýrii palmam adéptus est.
entries.eng: At Spoleto, the holy Felix, Bishop who gained the palm of martyrdom, under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: Heracléæ, in Ægýpto, sancti Potamónis Epíscopi, qui primum, sub Maximiáno Galério, Conféssor fuit; deínde, sub Constántio Imperatóre et Ariáno Prǽside Philágrio, martýrio coronátus est. Ipsum vero beátum virum sancti Ecclésiæ Patres Athanásius et Epiphánius suis láudibus celebrárunt.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy Potamion, Bishop who was first a Confessor of the faith under the Emperor Maximian Gallerius, and afterwards crowned with martyrdom, under the Emperor Constantius and the Arian President Philagrius.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Dióscori Lectóris, in quem Præses multa et vária torménta ita exércuit, ut ungues ejus effóderet et lampádibus látera inflammáret, sed, cæléstis lúminis fúlgore pertérriti, cecidérunt minístri; novíssime autem ipse Dióscorus, láminis ardéntibus adústus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy Reader Dioscorus, upon whom the President practiced many and diverse tortures, so that he had his nails dug out, and his sides scarified with lamps, but a sudden light from heaven terrified the tormentors so that they fell down; lastly, he was roasted with hot plates of metal, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, sancti Theódoti Mártyris, et sanctárum septem Vírginum et Mártyrum, scílicet Thecúsæ, quæ ipsíus Theódoti erat ámita, Alexándræ, Cláudiæ, Phaínæ, Euphrásiæ, Matrónæ et Julíttæ. Hæ a Prǽside primum prostitútæ, sed Dei virtúte servátæ, deínde, lapídibus ad colla ligátis, in palúdem mersæ sunt; quarum relíquias colléctas cum Theódotus honorífice sepelísset, ídeo, comprehénsus a Prǽside, sævíssime dilaniátus est, ac demum, ense percússus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, in Galatia, the holy martyrs Theodotus, and the Virgins Thecusa his aunt, Alexandra, Claudia, Faina, Euphrasia, Matrona, and Julitta, who were sentenced by the President to the stews, but were preserved by the power of God whereupon stones were tied to their necks and they were sunk in a swamp. Theodotus gathered their remains and buried them honourably, whereupon he was arrested by the President and savagely mangled, and at length received the crown of his testimony by being stricken with the sword.

entries.lat: Upsali, in Suécia, sancti Eríci, Regis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Uppsala, in Sweden, the holy martyr Eric, King of that land.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Felícis Confessóris, ex Ordine Minórum Capuccinórum, evangélica simplicitáte et caritáte conspícui; quem Clemens Undécimus, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Felix of Cantalicio, of the Order of Friars Minors Capuchins, who was remarkable for his Gospel simplicity and charity, and whom the Supreme Pontiff Clement XI numbered among the Saints.

entries.lat: Natális sancti Petri de Moróno Confessóris, qui, ex Anachoréta Summus Póntifex creátus, dictus est Cæléstinus Quintus. Sed Pontificátu se póstmodum abdicávit, et in solitúdine religiósam vitam agens, virtútibus et miráculis clarus, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: Holy Peter Morone, who was a hermit when he was created Supreme Pontiff, and was called Celestine V. He resigned the Papacy and led a religious life in solitude, and so, famous for graces and wonders, passed away, to be for ever with the Lord. His feast we keep upon the 21st day of this same month of May.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Pudentiánæ Vírginis, quæ, post innúmeros agónes, post multórum Mártyrum venerabíliter exhíbitas sepultúras, post omnes facultátes suas pro Christo paupéribus erogátas, tandem de terris ad cælos migrávit.
entries.eng: There also the holy Senator Pudens, the father of the said virgin. He put on Christ in baptism by the ministry of the Apostles, and kept his robe in innocency undefiled till he received the crown of life.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Pudéntis Senatóris, qui ejúsdem sanctæ Pudentiánæ ac sanctæ item Praxédis Vírginis fuit pater; atque, ab Apóstolis Christo in baptísmo vestítus, innocéntem túnicam usque ad vitæ corónam immaculáte custodívit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin Pudentiana, who, after countless contendings, after worshipfully burying many martyrs, and after distributing all her goods to feed the poor for Christ's sake, at length passed from earth to heaven.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Appia, natális sanctórum Calóceri et Parthénii eunuchórum; quorum prior, cum esset præpósitus cubículi uxóris Décii Imperatóris, postérior vero altérius múneris primicérius, et ambo nollent idólis sacrificáre, idcírco, ejúsdem Imperatóris jussu váriis ac diris sunt excruciáti supplíciis, ac tandem, cervícibus ardénti fuste contúsis, spíritum Deo tradidérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome also, upon the Appian Way, the holy eunuchs Calocerus and Parthenius. Calocerus was master of the bed-chamber to the wife of the Emperor Decius, and Parthenius was one of the chief officers of the court, and Decius slew them both because they would not sacrifice to idols.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Philóteri Mártyris, qui Paciáni Procónsulis fílius éxstitit, et sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, multa passus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyr Philoter, son of the Pro-Consul Pacian, who suffered much under the Emperor Diocletian, and received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctárum sex Vírginum et Mártyrum, quarum præcípua erat Cyríaca, quæ, cum líbere Maximiánum impietátis objurgásset, diríssime cæsa et dilaniáta est, atque ad últimum, igne cremáta, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: There also six holy Virgin martyrs, of whom the chiefest was Cyriaca, who boldly rebuked Maximian for his wickedness, and therefore was most direfully rent and torn, and at last burnt with fire.

entries.lat: Cantuáriæ, in Anglia, sancti Dunstáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep the feast of holy Dunstan, Archbishop of Canterbury.

entries.lat: Lohanéti, in Británnia minóre, sancti Ivónis, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui, pro Christi amóre, causas pupillórum, viduárum ac páuperum defendébat.
entries.eng: In Brittany, the holy Priest and Confessor Yves, who for the love of Christ pled the cause of orphans, widows, and the poor.

entries.lat: Ficécli, in Etrúria, sancti Theóphili a Curte, Confessóris, Sacerdótis Ordinis Fratrum Minórum, sacrórum recéssuum propagatóris, quem Pius Papa Undécimus inter Sanctos rétulit.
entries.eng: At Fucecchio, in Tuscany, the holy Confessor Theophilus of Corte, Priest of the Order of Friars Minor, a propagator of houses of sacred retreat, whom Pope Pius XI enrolled among the Saints.

entries.lat: Aquilæ, in Vestínis, sancti Bernardíni Senénsis, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Confessóris, qui verbo et exémplo Itáliam illustrávit.
entries.eng: At Aquila, in the Abruzzi, holy Bernardine of Sienna, of the Order of Friars Minors, who enlightened Italy both by word and example.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Plautíllæ, féminæ Consuláris, quæ beatórum Mártyrum Flávii Cleméntis Cónsulis soror et Fláviæ Domitíllæ Vírginis mater éxstitit; atque, a sancto Petro Apóstolo baptizáta, ómnium virtútum laude refúlgens, quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Plautilla, a woman of Consular rank and mother of the blessed Flavia Domitilla. She was baptized by the holy Apostle Peter, and after being eminent for excellency, fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Salária, natális sanctæ Basíllæ Vírginis, quæ, cum esset ex regio génere, et illustríssimum sponsum habéret illúmque dimisísset, accusáta fuit ab eo quod esset Christiána, et mox decrétum est a Galliéno Augústo ut aut sponsum recíperet, aut gládio interíret; cumque ipsa Virgo, convénta de hoc, respondísset se Regem regum habére sponsum, gládio transverberáta est.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Salarian Way, the holy Virgin Basilla. She was of the blood of kings and illustriously betrothed, but rejected her spouse, whereupon he accused her of being a Christian, and the Emperor Gallienus ordered that she should either take him back or perish by the sword. She answered that the King of kings was her Bridegroom, and the sword was accordingly passed through her.

entries.lat: Nemáusi, in Gálliis, sancti Baudélii Mártyris, qui comprehénsus est a Pagánis, et, cum sacrificáre nollet idólis et in Christi fide inter vérbera et torménta immóbilis persísteret, martýrii palmam pretiósa morte suscépit.
entries.eng: At Nimes, in Gaul, the holy martyr Baudelius. He was apprehended and would not sacrifice, and so remaining inmovable amidst stripes and torments, grasped the palm of martyrdom by a death precious in the sight of the Lord.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, apud Ægas, in Cilícia, sanctórum Mártyrum Thalelǽi, Astérii, Alexándri et Sociórum, qui sub Numeriáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, the holy martyrs Thalalaeus, Asterius, Alexander, and their companions, who suffered under the Emperor Numerian.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Aquilæ Mártyris, qui pectínibus pro Christo dilaniátus fuit.
entries.eng: In the Thebai'd, the holy martyr Aquila, who was lacerated with combs, for Christ's sake.

entries.lat: Apud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, sancti Austregísili, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Bourges, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Austregisilus,.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Anastásii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Anastasius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Theodóri Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Theodore, Bishop.

entries.lat: Sancti Valéntis Epíscopi, qui, una cum tribus púeris, necátus est.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Valens, Bishop who was murdered along with three lads.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum Secúndi Presbýteri, et aliórum; quos sacris diébus Pentecóstes, sub Constántio Imperatóre, Ariánus Epíscopus Geórgius sævíssime occídi præcépit.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, are commemorated the holy martyrs Secundus the Priest, and others, whom George, the Arian Bishop under the Emperor Constantius, savagely ordered to be slain during the Whitsuntide holidays.

entries.lat: In Mauritánia Cæsariénsi natális sanctórum Mártyrum Diaconórum Timóthei, Pólii et Eutýchii, qui, in eádem regióne disseminántes verbum Dei, páriter coronári meruérunt.
entries.eng: In Morocco, the holy Deacons Timothy, Polius, and Eutychius, who spread the Word of God in that country, and won the crown of martyrdom together.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Polyeúcti, Victórii et Donáti.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyrs Polyeuctus, Victorius, and Donatus.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sancti Secundíni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy martyr Secundinus.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Synésii et Theopómpi.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy martyrs Synesius and Theopompus.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ Philíppi natális sanctórum Mártyrum Nicostráti et Antíochi Tribunórum, cum áliis milítibus.
entries.eng: At Caesarea Philippi, the holy Nicostratus and Antiochus, along with other soldiers, all martyrs.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ commemorátio sanctórum Episcopórum et Presbyterórum; qui, ab Ariánis exsílio relegáti, sanctis Confessóribus sociári meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the commemoration of the holy Bishops and Priests; who, banished into exile by the Arians, deserved to be associated with the holy Confessors.

entries.lat: Níciæ, apud Varum flúvium, sancti Hospítii Confessóris, abstinéntiæ virtúte ac prophetíæ spíritu insígnis.
entries.eng: At Nice, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Hospitius, remarkable for the grace of self-denial, and for the spirit of prophecy.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Faustíni, Timóthei et Venústi.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Faustinus, Timothy, and Venustus.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Casti et Æmílii, qui per passiónis ignem martýrium consummárunt. Hos (ut beátus Cypriánus scribit), in prima congressióne devíctos, Dóminus victóres in secúndo prǽlio réddidit, ut fortióres ígnibus fíerent qui ígnibus ante cessíssent.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Castus and Emilius, who finished their testimony by the suffering of fire; of them blessed Cyprian writeth that in the first skirmish they were conquered, but in the second battle the Lord made them conquerors, that they who had first yielded to the flames might become stronger than the flames.

entries.lat: Cománæ, in Ponto, sancti Basilísci Mártyris, qui, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre et Agríppa Prǽside, férreas calceátus crépidas, ignítis clavis confíxas, múltaque ália passus, demum, cápite obtruncátus et in flumen projéctus, martýrii glóriam consecútus est.
entries.eng: At Comana, in Pontus, the holy martyr Basiliscus, who obtained the glory of martyrdom under the Emperor Maximian and the President Agrippa. He was shod with iron boots pierced with fiery nails, and suffered many other things likewise, before his head was cut off and he was cast into the river.

entries.lat: In Córsica sanctæ Júliæ Vírginis, quæ crucis supplício coronáta est.
entries.eng: In Corsica, the holy Virgin Julia, who endured the Cross, and so was crowned.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctæ Quitériæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy Virgin martyr Quiteria.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Marciáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor Marcian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Pistórii, in Túscia, beáti Atthónis Epíscopi, ex Ordine Vallis Umbrósæ.
entries.eng: At Pistoja, in Tuscany, the blessed Attho, monk of the Order of Valombrosa,.

entries.lat: In pago Antisiodorénsi beáti Románi Abbátis, qui sancto Benedícto ministrávit in specu; inde, in Gállias proféctus, ibi, ædificáto monastério relictísque multis sanctitátis alúmnis, quiévit in Dómino.
entries.eng: In the country of Auxerre, the blessed Abbot Romanus, who ministered to holy Benedict when he was in the cave, and afterwards went into Gaul, where he built a monastery, and fell asleep in the Lord, leaving many heirs of his holiness.

entries.lat: Apud Aquínum sancti Fulci Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Aquino, the holy Confessor Fulco.

entries.lat: Antisiodóri sanctæ Hélenæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Auxerre, the holy Virgin Helen.

entries.lat: Cássiæ, in Umbria, sanctæ Ritæ Víduæ, Moniális ex Ordine Eremitárum sancti Augustíni; quæ, post sǽculi núptias, ætérnum sponsum Christum únice diléxit.
entries.eng: At Cassia, in Umbria, the blessed Rita, a widow, a nun of the Order of Augustine Hermits, who, after having been married in the world, loved only the Eternal Bridegroom Christ.

entries.lat: Apud Língonas, in Gállia, pássio sancti Desidérii Epíscopi, qui, cum plebem suam ab exércitu Wandalórum vexári cérneret, ad Regem eórum pro ea supplicatúrus accéssit; a quo statim jugulári jussus, pro óvibus sibi créditis cervícem libénter exténdit, et, percússus gládio, migrávit ad Christum. Passi sunt autem cum ipso et álii plures de número gregis sui, qui apud eándem urbem cónditi sunt.
entries.eng: At Langres, in Gaul, the holy Desiderius, Bishop When he saw how the army of the Vandals were harrying his flock he went to plead for them with the Vandal king, who forthwith commanded his throat to be cut upon the spot and he cheerfully stretched out his neck for the sake of his sheep, and with the stroke of the sword passed away to be with Christ. There suffered along with him many others of his people, who are all buried in the same city.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctórum Mártyrum Epitácii Epíscopi, et Basiléi.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyrs Epitacius the Bishop, and Basil.

entries.lat: In território Lugdunénsi sancti Desidérii, Epíscopi Viennénsis; qui, Theodoríci Regis jussu lapídibus óbrutus, martýrio coronátur.
entries.eng: In the country of Lyon, the holy Desiderius, Bishop of Vienne, who was stoned to death by order of King Theodoric, and so obtained the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Quinctiáni, Lúcii et Juliáni, qui, in persecutióne Wandálica passi, ætérnas corónas meruérunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Quintian, Lucius, and Julian, who suffered in the persecution under the Vandals, and so obtained crowns that fade not away.

entries.lat: In Cappadócia commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni Galérii, confráctis crúribus, necáti sunt; item eórum, qui eódem témpore, in Mesopotámia, appénsi pédibus in sublíme, cápite verso deórsum, suffocáti fumo et lento igne consúmpti, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: In Cappadocia are commemorated those holy martyrs who, in the persecution under Maximian Galerius, were slain by having their thighs broken also they who, in Mesopotamia, were hung head downwards, and so finished their testimony by being choked with smoke and consumed by slow fire.

entries.lat: Sýnnadæ, in Phrýgia, sancti Michaélis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Synnada, the holy Michael, Bishop.

entries.lat: Ipso die sancti Mercuriális Epíscopi.
entries.eng: On the same day the holy Mercurial, Bishop.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Euphébii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy Euphebius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Joánnis Baptístæ de Rossi, Presbýteri et Confessóris, patiéntia et caritáte in evangelizándis paupéribus insígnis.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor John de' Rossi, famous for his patience and charity in preaching the Gospel to the poor.

entries.lat: Apud Núrsiam sanctórum Eutýchii et Floréntii Monachórum, quorum méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: At Nursia, the holy monks Eutychius and Florence, of whom mention is made by blessed Pope Gregory the Great.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sancti Mánahen, qui fuit Heródis Tetrárchæ collactáneus, atque, Doctor et Prophéta exsístens sub grátia novi Testaménti, in eádem urbe quiévit.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy Manahen, foster-brother of Herod the Tetrarch, a teacher and prophet under the grace of the New Testament, who sleepeth in that city.

entries.lat: Item beátæ Joánnæ, uxóris Chusæ, procuratóris Heródis, quam Lucas Evangelísta commémorat.
entries.eng: Also, the blessed Johanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, of whom maketh mention the Evangelist Luke.

entries.lat: In Portu Románo natális sancti Vincéntii Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Porto, the holy martyr Vincent.

entries.lat: Nannéte, in Británnia minóre, beatórum Mártyrum Donatiáni et Rogatiáni fratrum, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, pro constántia fídei, in cárcerem missi, et in equúleo suspénsi ac laniáti, deínde láncea militári confóssi, novíssime cápite præcísi sunt.
entries.eng: At Nantes, in Brittany, the blessed brothers Donatian and Rogatian, both martyrs. They were cast into prison, under the Emperor Diocletian, because of the steadfastness of their faith, hung on the rack and mangled, then pierced through with a spear, and in the end beheaded.

entries.lat: In Istria sanctórum Mártyrum Zoélli, Servílii, Felícis, Silváni et Dióclis.
entries.eng: In Istria, the holy martyrs Zoellus, Servilius, Felix, Silvanus, and Diodes,.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Melétii, ducis exércitus, ac Sociórum ejus ducentórum et quinquagínta duórum mílitum; qui divérso mortis génere martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Martyrs Meletius, a general of the army, and his Companions, two hundred and fifty-two soldiers; who completed their martyrdom by divers kinds of death.

entries.lat: Item sanctárum Mártyrum Susánnæ, Marciánæ et Palládiæ, eorúndem mílitum uxórum, quæ, una cum párvulis suis, confráctæ sunt.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Susannah, Marciana, and Palladia, wives of three of the aforesaid soldiers, who were slain, together with their little children.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Robustiáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy martyr Robustian.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sanctæ Afræ Mártyris, quæ sub Hadriáno Imperatóre passa est.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy martyr Afra, who suffered under the Emperor Hadrian.

entries.lat: In monastério Lirinénsi, in Gállia, sancti Vincéntii Presbýteri, doctrína et sanctitáte conspícui.
entries.eng: At the monastery of Lerins, the holy Priest Vincent, distinguished for his teaching and holiness.

entries.lat: Marróchii, in Africa, Beáti Joánnis de Prado, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Mártyris; qui, in prædicatióne Evangélii, post víncula, cárceres, flagélla plurimáque ália torménta, pro Christo fórtiter toleráta, per ignem martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: In Morocco, in Africa, blessed John de Prado, of the strictest observance of the bare-footed Friars Minors. For the preaching of the Gospel he manfully endured bonds, imprisonment, stripes, and many other torments, and finished his testimony for Christ by fire.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ Translátio sancti Domínici Confessóris, témpore Gregórii Papæ Noni.
entries.eng: At Bologna is commemorated the translation of the holy Confessor Dominic, in the time of Pope Gregory IX.

entries.lat: Salérni deposítio beáti Gregórii Séptimi, Papæ et Confessóris, ecclesiásticæ libertátis propugnatóris ac defensóris acerrimi.
entries.eng: At Salerno, the blessed Pope Gregory VII, a right stout champion and defender of the freedom of the Church, whose feast we keep upon the 28th day of this same month of May.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Nomentána, natális beáti Urbáni Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, cujus exhortatióne et doctrína complúres (in quibus fuére Tibúrtius et Valeriánus) Christi suscepérunt fidem, et pro ea martýrium subiérunt. Ipse quoque, in persecutióne Alexándri Sevéri, multa passus pro Ecclésia Dei, tandem, cervícibus abscíssis, martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Nomentan Way, the blessed martyr, Pope Urban I, who by his exhortation and teaching turned to the faith of Christ many who suffered martyrdom therefore, among whom were Tiburtius and Valerian. He himself also suffered many things for the Church of God in the persecution under the Emperor Alexander Severus, and at length, being beheaded, was crowned with martyrdom.

entries.lat: Girvi, in Anglia, tránsitus sancti Bedæ Venerábilis, Presbýteri, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, sanctitáte et eruditióne celebérrimi. Ipsíus autem festum recólitur sexto Kaléndas Júnii.
entries.eng: At Jarrow, in England, the passing of St. Bede the Venerable, Priest, Confessor and Doctor of the Church, most famous for holiness and learning. His feast is kept on the 27th day of May.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ natális sanctæ Maríæ-Magdalénæ de Pazzis Vírginis, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, vita et sanctitáte illústris. Ejus vero festívitas quarto Kaléndas Júnii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Florence, the holy Virgin, Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi, of the Order of Carmelites, famous for her holy life, whose feast we keep upon the 3rd day of June.

entries.lat: Doróstori, in Mýsia inferióre, item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Pasícratis, Valentiónis et aliórum duórum, simul coronatórum.
entries.eng: At Dorostorum, in Bulgaria, the holy martyrs Pasicrates, Valention, and two others, who were all crowned together.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Dionýsii Epíscopi, qui, ab Ariáno Imperatóre Constántio in Cappadóciam pro fide cathólica relegátus, ibídem, propióre Martýribus título, spíritum Deo réddidit. Ejus sacrum corpus ab Aurélio Epíscopo transmíssum est Mediolánum ad beátum Ambrósium Epíscopum; cui piæ actióni offícium quoque sancti Basilíi Magni accessísse tráditur.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Bishop Denis. He was banished into Cappadocia by the Arian Emperor Constantius for the Catholic faith's sake, and so there gave up his spirit to God with a near approach to martyrdom. His sacred body was sent to Milan to blessed Bishop Ambrose by Bishop Aurelius, prompted to that godly act, as is said, by holy Basil the Great.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ natális sancti Zenóbii, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, vitæ sanctitáte ac miraculórum glória conspícui.
entries.eng: At Florence, holy Zenobius, Bishop of that city, distinguished for the holiness of his life and the fame of his wondrous works.

entries.lat: In Británnia sancti Aldélmi, Epíscopi Schireburgénsis.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep in England the feast of the holy Confessor Aldhelm, Bishop of Sherborne.

entries.lat: In território Tricassíno sancti Leónis Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the territory of Troyes, the holy Confessor Leo.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sanctæ Magdalénæ-Sophíæ Barat, Fundatrícis Institúti Sorórum a Sacro Corde Jesu; quæ pro Christiána puellárum informatióne valde adlaborávit, et a Pio Papa Undécimo in sanctárum Vírginum catalógum fuit reláta.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy Madeleine Sophie Barat, Foundress of the Institute of the Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, who laboured greatly for the Christian education of girls, and was enrolled among the holy Virgins by Pope Pius XI.

entries.lat: Vérulis, in Hérnicis, Translátio sanctæ Maríæ Jacóbi; cujus sacrum corpus plúrimis miráculis illustrátur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Boniface IV, who consecrated the Pantheon as the Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary and All holy Martyrs.

entries.lat: Assísii, in Umbria, item Translátio sancti Francísci Confessóris, témpore Gregórii Papæ Noni.
entries.eng: At Assisi, in Umbria, is commemorated the translation of the holy Confessor Francis, in the time of Pope Gregory IX.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Philíppi Nérii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Congregatiónis Oratórii Fundátor fuit, ac virginitáte, prophetíæ dono, et miráculis éxtitit insígnis.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Philip Neri, founder of the Congregation of the Oratory, famous for his virginity, his gift of prophecy, and his wondrous works.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Eleuthérii, Papæ et Mártyris, qui multos nóbiles Romanórum ad fidem Christi perdúxit, et sanctos Damiánum et Fugátium in Británniam misit, qui Lúcium Regem, cum uxóre ipsíus ac toto fere pópulo, baptizárunt.
entries.eng: Also at Rome, the holy Pope and martyr Eleutherius, who led many noble Romans to believe in Christ, and who sent into Britain holy Dyfan and Ffagan, who baptized Lleurwg, Prince along with his wife and nearly all his people. We keep his feast upon the 29th day of this present month of May.

entries.lat: Cantuáriæ, in Anglia, natális sancti Augustíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, una cum áliis, a beáto Gregório Papa missus, genti Anglórum sacrum Christi Evangélium prædicávit, ibíque, virtútibus et miráculis gloriósus, obdormívit in Dómino. Ejus tamen festívitas quinto Kaléndas Júnii recólitur.
entries.eng: Also in England the feast of the holy Augustine, first Archbishop of Canterbury, called Apostle of England. He was sent hither, along with others, by the blessed Pope Gregory. He preached the Gospel of Christ to the English people. He fell asleep in the Lord at Canterbury, glorious for his graces and wondrous works.

entries.lat: Athénis item natális beáti Quadráti, Apostolórum discípuli, qui, in persecutióne Hadriáni, fide et indústria sua cóngregans Ecclésiam grandi terróre dispérsam, librum pro Christiánæ religiónis defensióne, valde útilem et Apostólica doctrína dignum, eídem Imperatóri porréxit.
entries.eng: At Athens, the blessed Quadratus, a disciple of the Apostles. During the persecution under Hadrian the Church was scattered in great fear, but he gathered it together again by his faith and labour, and gave unto it a book very useful for the defending of the Christian religion, and worthy of the teaching of the Apostles.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Simítrii Presbýteri, et aliórum vigínti duórum; qui sub Antoníno Pio passi sunt.
entries.eng: Also at Rome, the holy Priest Simitrius, and twenty-two others, who suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Antoninus Pius.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Zacharíæ, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui sub Trajáno passus est.
entries.eng: At Vienne, in Dauphiny, the holy Zachary, Bishop who suffered martyrdom under Trajan.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Quadráti Mártyris, in cujus solemnitáte sanctus Augustínus sermónem hábuit.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyr Quadratus, on whose feast-day holy Augustine preached a sermon.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Felicíssimi, Heráclii et Paulíni.
entries.eng: At Todi, the holy martyrs Felicissimus, Heraclius, and Paulinus.

entries.lat: In território Antisiodorénsi pássio sancti Prisci Mártyris, qui, cum ingénti multitúdine fidélium Christi, cápite cæsus est.
entries.eng: In the country of Auxerre, the holy Priscus and a vast multitude of Christ's faithful people suffered martyrdom.

entries.lat: In civitáte Quiténsi, Æquatoriánæ Ditiónis, sanctæ Maríæ Annæ a Jesu de Parédes, Vírginis, e tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, austeritáte et in próximum caritáte præcláræ, quam Pius Papa Duodécimus sanctárum Vírginum catálogo adnumerávit.
entries.eng: In the city of Quito, in Ecuador, the holy Virgin Mary Anne of Jesus de Paredes, of the Third Order of St. Francis, renowned for her austerity and her charity towards her neighbour, whom Pope Pius XII numbered in the catalogue of the holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Sancti Bedæ Venerábilis, Presbýteri, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui migrávit in cælum octávo Kaléndas Júnii.
entries.eng: St. Bede the Venerable, Priest, Confessor and Doctor of the Church, who departed to heaven on the 25th day of May.

entries.lat: Sancti Joánnis Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; cujus dies natális quintodécimo Kaléndas Júnii refértur, sed festívitas hac die, ob Translatiónem córporis ejus, potíssimum celebrátur.
entries.eng: St. John I, Pope and Martyr, whose birthday is recorded on the 18th day of May, but whose feast is chiefly kept on this day, on account of the Translation of his body.

entries.lat: Doróstori, in Mýsia inferióre, pássio beáti Júlii, qui, témpore Alexándri Imperatóris, cum esset veteránus et eméritæ milítiæ, comprehénsus est ab officiálibus, et Máximo Prǽsidi oblátus; quo præsénte, cum exsecrarétur idóla, et Christi nomen constantíssime confiterétur, capitáli senténtia punítus est.
entries.eng: At Dorostorum, in Bulgaria, the blessed Julius, a retired Roman soldier, who was arrested in the time of the Emperor Alexander Severus, and brought before the President Maximus, in whose presence he denounced the idols, and steadfastly confessed the Name of Christ, and so was put to death.

entries.lat: In pago Atrebaténsi sancti Ranúlfi Mártyris.
entries.eng: in Artois, the holy martyr Ranulph.

entries.lat: Apud Soram sanctæ Restitútæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre et Agáthio Procónsule, fídei certámine suscépto, dǽmonum ímpetus, paréntum blandítias et tortórum sævítiam superávit, ac demum, cum áliis Christiánis, cápite truncáta, martýrio decoráta est.
entries.eng: At Sora, the holy Virgin and martyr Restituta. She fought the fight of faith under the Emperor Aurelian and the pro-Consul Agathius. She conquered the attacks of devils, the cajolery of her kinsfolk, and the cruelty of the tormentors. At last she was beheaded, along with other Christians, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Aráusicæ, in Gálliis, sancti Eutrópii Epíscopi, virtútibus atque miráculis illústris.
entries.eng: At Orange, in Gaul, holy Eutropius, Bishop famous for his graces and wondrous works.

entries.lat: Herbípoli, in Germánia, sancti Brunónis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Würzburg, in Germany, the holy Bishop and Confessor Bruno.

entries.lat: Sancti Augustíni, Epíscopi Cantuariénsis et Confessóris, cujus dies natális ágitur séptimo Kaléndas Júnii.
entries.eng: St. Augustine, Bishop of Canterbury and Confessor, whose birthday is kept on the 26th day of May.

entries.lat: In Sardínia sanctórum Mártyrum Æmílii, Felícis, Príami et Luciáni, qui, pro Christo certántes, ab eo glorióse coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: In Sardinia, the holy martyrs Emilius, Felix, Priam, and Lucian, who contended for Christ, and were crowned.

entries.lat: Carnóti, in Gállia, sancti Caráuni Mártyris, qui sub Domitiáno Imperatóre, cápite amputátus, martýrium sumpsit.
entries.eng: At Chartres, in Gaul, the holy martyr Caraunus, who received martyrdom by being beheaded, under the Emperor Domitian.

entries.lat: Item pássio sanctórum Crescéntis, Dioscóridis, Pauli et Helládii.
entries.eng: Also the holy martyrs Crescens, Dioscorides, Paul, and Helladius.

entries.lat: Thécuæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Monachórum Mártyrum, qui, témpore Theodósii junióris, a Saracénis occísi sunt, quorum sacras relíquias collegérunt áccolæ, et summa veneratióne illas habuérunt.
entries.eng: At Tekoah, in Palestine, the holy martyrs, monks, who were massacred by the Saracens in the time of the Emperor Theodosius the Younger. Their sacred remains were gathered together by the country-folk, who treated them with great reverence.

entries.lat: Corínthi sanctæ Helicónidis Mártyris, témpore Gordiáni Imperatóris. Hæc primum, sub Perénnio Prǽside, multis torméntis afflícta; deínde, sub ejus successóre Justíno, íterum cruciáta, sed ab Angelis liberáta est; demum, disséctis mammis, ferísque objécta atque igne probáta, cápitis obtruncatióne martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: At Corinth, the holy martyr Helconides. She was first tried with many torments, under the President Perennius, in the time of the Emperor Gordian then was tortured again under the next President Justinus, but was delivered by an Angel. At length her breasts were cut off and she was thrown to wild beasts, and tried with fire, and thereafter finished her testimony by being beheaded.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sancti Germáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui quantæ sanctitátis quantíque fúerit mériti, quibus étiam miráculis clarúerit, litterárum moniméntis Fortunátus Epíscopus consignávit.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy Confessor Germanus, Bishop How saintly he was, how worthy, with what wondrous works he shone, hath been written by Fortunatus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Senatóris Epíscopi, virtútibus et eruditióne claríssimi.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Senator, Bishop very famous for his graces and learning.

entries.lat: Urgéllæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Justi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Urgel, in Spain, the holy Justus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Floréntiæ sancti Pódii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Florence, the holy Confessor Podius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Apud Nováriam sancti Bernárdi a Menthóne Confessóris, qui in monte Jovis, super Alpes, in Valésia, celebérrimum cœnóbium et hospítium exstrúxit, atque a Pio Papa Undécimo, non modo Alpium íncolis vel viatóribus, sed iis étiam qui eárum juga ascendéndo se exércent, cæléstis Patrónus est attribútus.
entries.eng: At Novara, the holy Confessor Bernard of Menthon, who built a most famous monastery and hospice on the Mount of Jove, in the Alps, in the Valais, and was appointed by Pope Pius XI heavenly Patron not only of the dwellers in the Alps and of travellers, but also of those who exercise themselves in climbing their heights.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Maríæ-Magdalénæ de Pazzis, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Vírginis, cujus dies natális octávo Kaléndas Júnii recensétur.
entries.eng: St. Mary Magdalen de Pazzi, Virgin, of the Order of Carmelites, whose birthday is recorded on the 25th day of May.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Aurélia, natális sancti Restitúti Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Restitutus.

entries.lat: Apud Icónium, in Lycaónia, pássio sanctórum Conónis, et fílii annórum duódecim, qui, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre, cratículæ, prunis suppósitis et óleo superinfúso candéntis, suspensiónis in equúleo atque ignis pœnam constánter passi, ad extrémum, málleo ligneo mánibus eórum contrítis, spíritum emisérunt.
entries.eng: At Iconium, a city of Isauria, the holy martyrs Conon and his son aged twelve years. Under the Emperor Aurelian they suffered with great firmness from being basted with oil upon a grating over live coals, stretching upon the rack and fire, and at length gave up the ghost as their hands were being pounded with a wooden mallet.

entries.lat: In agro Tridentíno natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sisínii, Martýrii et Alexándri; qui, témpore Honórii Imperatóris, in Anáuniæ pártibus (ut scribit in vita sancti Ambrósii Paulínus), persequéntibus Gentílibus, martýrii corónam adépti sunt.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Sisinius, Martyrius, and Alexander, who are stated by Paulinus, in his life of holy Ambrose, to have gained the crown of martyrdom in the parts of Val-d'Anagna, under the persecution of the heathen in the time of the Emperor Honorius.

entries.lat: Cameríni pássio sanctórum mille quingentórum et vigínti quinque Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Camerino, the passion of one thousand five hundred and twenty-five holy Martyrs.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ Philíppi sanctárum Mártyrum Theodósiæ, quæ sancti Procópii Mártyris éxstitit mater, et aliárum duódecim nobílium matronárum; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cápitis obtruncatióne consummátæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea Philippi, the holy martyrs Theodosia, mother of the holy martyr Procopius, and twelve other noble matrons, who were beheaded in the persecution under Diocletian.

entries.lat: Tréviris beáti Maximíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; a quo sanctus Athanásius Epíscopus, ob persecutiónem Arianórum éxsulans, honorífice suscéptus fuit.
entries.eng: At Trier, the blessed Confessor Maximin, Bishop who honourably welcomed the holy Bishop Athanasius when he was in exile from the persecution of the Arians.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Máximi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Maximus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Arcáni, in Látio, sancti Eleuthérii Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Arci, in Latium, the holy Confessor Eleutherius.

entries.lat: Sancti Felícis Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, cujus dies natális tértio Kaléndas Januárii recensétur.
entries.eng: St. Felix I, Pope and Martyr, whose birthday is recorded on the 30th day of December.

entries.lat: Túrribus, in Sardínia, sanctórum Mártyrum Gabíni et Críspuli.
entries.eng: At Torre, in Sardinia, the holy martyrs Gabinus and Crispulus.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Syci et Palatíni, qui, pro Christi nómine, multa torménta passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, holy Sycus and Palatinus, who suffered many torments for Christ's Name's sake.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Exsuperántii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy Confessor Exuperantius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Anastásii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Anastasius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Basilíi et Emméliæ uxóris, qui fuérunt paréntes beatórum Basilíi Magni et Gregórii Nysséni ac Petri Sebasténsis Episcopórum, atque Macrínæ Vírginis. Hi vero sancti cónjuges, témpore Galérii Maximiáni, extórres facti, Pónticas solitúdines incoluére; et post persecutiónem, fíliis suárum relíctis virtútum herédibus, in pace quievérunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy Basil and Emmelia his wife, father and mother of holy Basil the Great. In the time of the Emperor Galerius Maximian they were banished, and dwelt in the wilderness in Pontus; but they fell asleep in peace after the persecution was over, leaving their children inheritors of their goodness.

entries.lat: Híspali, in Hispánia, sancti Ferdinándi Tértii, Castéllæ et Legiónis Regis, ob virtútum præstántiam cognoménto Sancti; qui, fídei propagándæ zelo clarus, tandem, devíctis Mauris, ad cæléste regnum, terréno relícto, felíciter evolávit.
entries.eng: At Seville, in Spain, holy Ferdinand III, King of Castile and Leon, surnamed the Saint for the excellence of his virtues; who, renowned for his zeal in spreading the faith, at length, having overcome the Moors, left his earthly kingdom and passed happily to the heavenly one.

entries.lat: Rotómagi, sanctæ Joánnæ Arcénsis Vírginis, Puéllæ Aurelianénsis appellátæ, quæ cum fórtiter pro pátria dimicásset, tandem, in hóstium potestátem trádita, iniquo judício condemnáta est et igne combústa; atque a Benedícto Décimo quinto, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum fastis adscrípta.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Pope Felix, who was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Aurelian.

entries.lat: Festum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Regínæ.
entries.eng: The Feast of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Queen.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Petroníllæ Vírginis, fíliæ beáti Petri Apóstoli, quæ, conjúgium nóbilis viri Flacci spernens, et, accéptis triduánis ad deliberándum indúciis, ínterim jejúniis et oratiónibus vacans, tértia die, mox ut Christi Sacraméntum accépit, emísit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin Petronilla, daughter of the blessed Apostle Peter. She looked down upon an offer of marriage from the noble Flaccus, and took three days to consider the matter, the which time she spent in fasting and prayer, and upon the third day, immediately after receiving the Sacrament of Christ, she gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ sanctórum Mártyrum fratrum Cántii, Cantiáni et Cantianíllæ, qui, cum essent ex illústri Aniciórum progénie, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Imperatóribus, ob Christiánæ fídei constántiam, una cum pædagógo suo Proto, cápite plexi sunt.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, the holy brothers Cantius and Cantian, and their sister Cantianilla, all martyrs of the noble family of the Anicii, who, along with their schoolmaster Protus, were beheaded under the Emperors reigned A.D. 269-274. Diocletian and Maximian on account of their firmness in the Christian faith.

entries.lat: Túrribus, in Sardínia, sancti Crescentiáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Torre, in Sardinia, the holy martyr Crescentian.

entries.lat: Apud Comános, in Ponto, sancti Hérmiæ mílitis, qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, de innúmeris et sævíssimis torméntis divína ope liberátus, carníficem convértit ad Christum, et ejúsdem martýrii corónæ partícipem fecit; quam tamen ipse primus, gládio obtruncátus, accépit.
entries.eng: At Comana, in Pontus, the holy soldier Hermias. He was delivered by God's help from countless and savage tortures, under the Emperor Antoninus. He converted his executioner to Christ, and made him a sharer in the crown of his own martyrdom, but he himself was the first to grasp it, by being beheaded.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Lupicíni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Lupicinus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Paschásii, Diáconi et Confessóris, cujus méminit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Deacon Paschasius, a Confessor of whom doth make mention the blessed Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Angelæ Meríci Vírginis, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci; quæ fuit Institútrix Societátis Vírginum sanctæ Ursulæ, et ad accipiéndam corónam immarcescíbilem, sexto Kaléndas Februárii cælésti Sponso vocáta est.
entries.eng: St. Angela Merici, Virgin, of the Third Order of St. Francis, who was the Foundress of the Society of the Virgins of St. Ursula, and was called by her heavenly Spouse on the 27th day of January to receive the crown that fadeth not away.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Juvéntii Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Juventius.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sanctórum Reveriáni Epíscopi, et Pauli Presbýteri, cum áliis decem, qui, sub Aureliáno Príncipe, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Autun, holy Reverian, Bishop the Priest Paul, and ten others, who were crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Aurelian.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, beáti Pámphili, Presbýteri et Mártyris, viri admirándæ sanctitátis et doctrínæ, atque in páuperes munífici; qui, ob Christi fidem, in persecutióne Galérii Maximiáni, primum, sub Urbáno Prǽside, cruciátus et in cárcerem trusus, deínde, sub Firmiliáno, íterum revocátus ad pœnas, una cum áliis martýrium consummávit. Passi sunt étiam tunc Valens Diáconus, et Paulus, aliíque novem; quorum memória áliis diébus celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the blessed martyr Pamphilus, the Priest. He was a man wonderful for his holiness, his teaching, and his goodness towards the poor. In the persecution under the Emperor Galerius Maximian, he was first tortured for Christ's faith's sake, under the President Urban, and cast into prison then under Fermilian he was called back again to suffer, and then along with others finished his testimony. There then suffered also the Deacon Valens, Paul, and nine others whose memory is celebrated upon other days.

entries.lat: In Cappadócia sancti Thespésii Mártyris, qui, sub Alexándro Imperatóre et Simplício Præfécto, post ália torménta, decollátus est.
entries.eng: In Cappadocia, the holy martyr Thespesius, who, after being tortured, was beheaded under the Emperor Alexander Severus and the Prefect Simplicius.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sanctórum Mártyrum Ischyriónis, ductóris mílitum, et aliórum quinque mílitum; qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, pro fide Christi, divérso mortis génere perémpti sunt.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy Martyrs Ischyrion, a commander of soldiers, and five other soldiers, who under the Emperor Diocletian were put to death for the faith of Christ by divers kinds of death.

entries.lat: Item sancti Firmi Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, acerbíssimis plagis afféctus, lapídibus percússus, ac demum cápite cæsus est.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy martyrs, the sergeant Ischyrion, and five other soldiers, who were put to diverse kinds of death, under the Emperor Diocletian, for believing in Christ; also the holy martyr Firmus, who, in the persecution under Maximian, was terribly scourged, bruised with stones, and at last beheaded.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sanctórum Mártyrum Felíni et Gratiniáni mílitum, qui, sub Décio, váriis torméntis cruciáti, martýrii palmam gloriósa morte percepérunt.
entries.eng: At Perugia, the holy soldiers Felin and Gratinian, who were diversely tormented under the Emperor Decius, and by a glorious death obtained the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Próculi Mártyris, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre passus est.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy martyr Proculus, who suffered under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: Amériæ, in Umbria, sancti Secúndi Mártyris, qui sub Diocletiáno, in Tíberim projéctus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Amelia, the holy martyr Secundus, who was thrown into the Tiber, under the Emperor Diocletian, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Apud Tiférnum, in Umbria, sancti Crescentiáni, mílitis Románi, qui, sub eódem Imperatóre, martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: At Citta-di-Castello, in Umbria, the holy Roman soldier Crescentian, who was crowned with martyrdom under the same Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: In monastério Lirinénsi, in Gállia, sancti Caprásii Abbátis.
entries.eng: At the Monastery of Lerins, the holy Abbot Caprasius.

entries.lat: In monastério Onniénsi, apud Burgos, in Hispánia, sancti Enecónis, Abbátis Benedictíni, ob sanctitátis et miraculórum glóriam illústris.
entries.eng: At Burgos, in Spain, in the Monastery of Ogna, the holy Benedictine Abbot Enecon, illustrious for his holiness and the fame of his miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Montem Falcum, in Umbria, sancti Fortunáti Presbýteri, virtútibus et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: In Umbria also, the holy Priest Fortunatus, famous for graces and wonders.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Simeónis Mónachi, qui a Benedícto Papa Nono in Sanctórum númerum relátus est.
entries.eng: At Trier, the holy monk Simeon, who was enrolled among the Saints by Pope Benedict IX.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Marcellíni Presbýteri, et Petri Exorcístæ, qui, sub Diocletiáno, cum multos in cárcere ad fidem erudírent, ídeo, post dira víncula et plúrima torménta, a Seréno Júdice decolláti sunt in loco qui dicebátur Silva Nigra; quæ deínde, in honórem Sanctórum, commutáto nómine, Silva Cándida appelláta est. Horum córpora in crypta, juxta sanctum Tibúrtium, sepúlta sunt; eorúmque sepúlcrum sanctus Dámasus Papa vérsibus póstea exornávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Marcellinus the priest, and Peter the Exorcist.

entries.lat: In Campánia sancti Erásmi, Epíscopi et Mártyris. Hic, sub Diocletiáno Augústo, primum plumbátis cæsus, deínde fústibus gráviter mactátus, post resína, súlphure, plumbo, pice, cera oleóque perfúsus, illǽsus appáruit; deínde Fórmiis, sub Maximiáno, divérsis atque immaníssimis supplíciis íterum tortus, sed ad confirmándum céteros a Deo servátus; tandem, vocánte Dómino, martýrio clarus, sancto fine quiévit. Ipsíus autem corpus Cajétam póstea translátum est.
entries.eng: In Campania, the holy martyr Elmo, Patriarch Under the Emperor Diocletian he was first hided with scourges laden with lead, then heavily beaten with cudgels, after which resin, sulphur, lead, pitch, wax, and oil were poured over him, but he still appeared unharmed.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Pothíni Epíscopi, Sancti Diáconi, Vétii, Epagáthi, Maturi, Póntici, Bíblidis, Attali, Alexándri et Blandínæ, cum áliis multis; quorum fórtia et iteráta certámina, témpore Marci Aurélii Antoníni et Lúcii Veri, Ecclésiæ Lugdunénsis epístola, ad Ecclésias Asiæ et Phrýgiæ scripta, recénset. In his sancta Blandína, sexu infírmior, córpore imbecíllior, conditióne dejéctior, diuturnióra et acerbióra certámina súbiens, et fortis adhuc pérmanens, gládio juguláta, céteros secúta est, quos hortabátur ad palmam.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy martyrs Photinus the Bishop, Sanctus the Deacon, Vetius, Epagathus, Maturus, Ponticus, Biblides, Attalus, Alexander, and Blandina, with many others, whose mighty and constant contendings, in the time of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Verus, are written in the Epistle of the Church of Lyon to the Churches of Asia and Phrygia; among these the holy Blandina, weaker by sex, frailer in body, lower in social position, underwent contendings more long and more sharp, and remaining still inflexible, was slain by the sword, and so followed the others whom she had exhorted to victory.

entries.lat: In ínsula Proconnéso, in Propóntide, sancti Nicéphori, Epíscopi Constantinopolitáni, qui, paternárum traditiónum propugnátor acérrimus, pro cultu sanctárum Imáginum se Leóni Arméno, Imperatóri Iconoclástæ, constánter oppósuit; a quo mulctátus exsílio, ibídem, cum per quatuórdecim annos longum duxísset martýrium, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: On the island of Proconnesus, in the Propontis, holy Nicephorus, Bishop of Constantinople, who, a most zealous defender of the traditions of the fathers, steadfastly withstood Leo the Armenian, the Iconoclast Emperor, for the veneration of the holy Images; by whom he was punished with exile, and there, after enduring a long martyrdom for fourteen years, he departed to the Lord.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Eugénii Primi, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Pope Eugenius I.

entries.lat: Trani, in Apúlia, sancti Nicolái Peregríni Confessóris, cujus mirácula in Concílio Románo, cui beátus Urbánus Papa Secúndus prǽfuit, recitáta sunt.
entries.eng: At Trani, in Apulia, the holy Confessor Nicholas Peregrini, whose wonderful works were published in a Council at Rome under Pope Urban II.

entries.lat: Arétii, in Túscia, sanctórum Mártyrum Pergentíni et Laurentíni fratrum, qui, in persecutióne Décii, sub Tibúrtio Prǽside, cum essent púeri, ibídem, post dira supplícia toleráta et magna mirácula osténsa, gládio cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Arezzo, in Tuscany, the holy brethren Pergentinus and Laurentinus, both martyrs. They were boys, who, in the persecution under Decius, after bearing horrid torments and showing forth great works of power, were slain by the sword under the President Tiburtius.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Lucilliáni et quátuor puerórum, scílicet Cláudii, Hypátii, Pauli et Dionýsii. His cum púeris Lucilliánus, ex idolórum sacerdóte Christiánus factus, in fornácem, post vária torménta, injéctus est, sed, flamma imbre exstíncta, omnes illǽsi evasérunt; dénique, ipse cruci affíxus, púeri autem gládio obtruncáti, sub Silváno Prǽside, consummáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyr Lucillian and his four sons, Claud, Hypatius, Paul, and Denis. Lucillian, before he became a Christian, had been a priest of idols. All the five, after they had been put to various tortures, were cast into a furnace, but rain put out the fire, and they all escaped unhurt. Then Lucillian was crucified, and the children were beheaded, and so under Silvanus the President they finished their testimony.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, beáti Isaac Mónachi, qui, pro Christi fide, gládio necátus est.
entries.eng: At Cordova, in Spain, the blessed monk Isaac, who, was slain with the sword, for Christ's faith's sake.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctæ Paulæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, cum prædictórum Mártyrum Lucilliáni ac Sociórum sánguinem collígeret, ídeo, comprehénsa, virgis percússa, et in ignem conjécta sed liberáta, demum et ipsa eódem loco, ubi sanctus Lucilliánus crucifíxus fúerat, decolláta est.
entries.eng: At the same place, the holy Virgin and martyr Paula, who was arrested while she was gathering up the blood of the aforesaid martyrs. She was beaten with rods, and cast into the fire, but was delivered, and at last beheaded at the same place where the holy Lucillian had been crucified.

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Cæcílii Presbýteri, qui sanctum Cypriánum ad Christi fidem perdúxit.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy Priest Caecilius, who brought holy Cyprian to believe in Christ.

entries.lat: In território Aurelianénsi sancti Liphárdi, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the country of Orleans, the holy Confessor Liphard the Priest.

entries.lat: Lucæ, in Túscia, sancti Davíni Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Lucca, in Tuscany, the holy Confessor Davin,.

entries.lat: Anániæ sanctæ Olívæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Anagni, the holy Virgin Oliva.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sanctæ Clotíldis Regínæ, cujus précibus vir ejus Clodovéus, Rex Francórum, Christi fidem suscépit.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy Queen Clotilde, at whose entreaties her husband, King Clovis, accepted the faith of Christ.

entries.lat: Agnóni, in Aprútio citerióre, sancti Francísci, ex nóbili Neapolitána família Carácciolo, Confessóris, Congregatiónis Clericórum Regulárium Minórum Fundatóris, qui mira in Deum et próximum caritáte et ardentíssimo sacræ Eucharístiæ cultus propagándi stúdio flagrávit; atque a Pio Séptimo, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum cánoni adscríptus est. Ipsíus corpus Neápolim, in Campánia, translátum fuit, ibíque religiosíssime cólitur.
entries.eng: At Agnone, in the Abruzzi, holy Confessor Francis, of the noble Neapolitan family of Caracciolo, founder of the congregation of Regular Clerks Minors. He was a burning and a shining light of love towards God and his neighbor, and intense earnestness in spreading abroad the worship of the Holy Eucharist. His body lieth at Naples, and is held in great veneration. Pius VII added his name to the list of those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Arétii et Daciáni.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Aretius and Dacian.

entries.lat: Sísciæ, in Illýrico, sancti Quiríni Epíscopi, qui, sub Galério Prǽside, pro fide Christi (ut Prudéntius scribit), molári saxo ad collum ligáto, in flumen præcipitátus est; sed, lápide supernatánte, cum circumstántes Christiános, ne ejus terreréntur supplício neve titubárent in fide, diu fuísset hortátus, ipse, ut martýrii glóriam assequerétur, précibus a Deo, ut mergerétur, obtínuit.
entries.eng: At Sisseg, in Illyricum, holy Quirinus, Bishop Prudentius writeth of him that, under the President Galerius, for Christ's faith's sake, a millstone was tied about his neck and he was cast into the river, but the millstone swam, and he was a long time exhorting the Christians who stood by not to be scared at the sight of his execution, nor to be shaken in the faith, and then obtained from God the glory of martyrdom, and so was allowed to sink.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Clatéi, Epíscopi Brixiénsis et Mártyris, qui, sub Neróne Imperatóre, jussu Præfécti urbis illíus tentus, et, cum renuntiáre Christo nollet, multis verbéribus afflíctus et cápite obtruncátus est.
entries.eng: At Brescia, under the Emperor Nero, the holy martyr Clateus, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Pannónia sanctórum Mártyrum Rútili et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In Hungary, the holy martyrs Rutilus and his companions.

entries.lat: Tíbure sancti Quiríni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Tivoli, the holy martyr Quirinus.

entries.lat: Atrébati, in Gálliis, sanctæ Saturnínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Arras, the holy Virgin and martyr Saturnina.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Metrophánis, Epíscopi et Confessóris insígnis.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Metrophanes, Archbishop an eminent Confessor.

entries.lat: Milévi, in Numídia, sancti Optáti Epíscopi, doctrína et sanctitáte conspícui, quem sancti Ecclésiæ Patres Augustínus et Fulgéntius suis láudibus celebrárunt.
entries.eng: At Milevitanus, in Numidia, holy Optatus, Bishop famous for his teaching and holiness.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Alexándri Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, holy Alexander, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Frísia sancti Bonifátii, Epíscopi Moguntíni et Mártyris. Hic de Anglia Romam venit, indéque a beáto Gregório Papa Secúndo in Germániam missus est ut Christi fidem illis géntibus evangelizáret, et, cum máximam ibi multitúdinem, præsértim Frísonum, Christiánæ religióni subjugásset, Germanórum Apóstolus méruit appellári; novíssime in Frísia, a furéntibus Gentílibus gládio perémptus, una cum Eobáno Coepíscopo et quibúsdam áliis servis Dei, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: Holy Boniface, Archbishop of Mainz. He came from England to Rome, and was sent by Gregory II into Germany to preach the faith of Christ to those nations, and he earned the title of Apostle of the Germans by turning a vast multitude, more especially of Frisians, to the religion of Christ. At last he, along with Eoban and some other servants of God in Friesland, received martyrdom by the sword at the hand of raging heathens.

entries.lat: Tyri, in Phœnícia sancti Doróthei Presbýteri, qui, sub Diocletiáno, multa passus est; et, usque ad Juliáni témpora supérstes, sub eo, annum agens séptimum supra centésimum, venerándam senéctam martýrio honestávit.
entries.eng: At Tyre, the holy Priest Dorotheus. He suffered much under Diocletian, but survived till the time of Julian, in whose reign, and the hundred and seventh year of his own age, he crowned his venerable years with the glory of martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto natális sanctórum Mártyrum Marciáni, Nicánoris, Apollónii et aliórum, qui, in persecutióne Galérii Maximiáni, illústre martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy martyrs Martian, Nicanor, Apollonius, and others, who finished an illustrious testimony, in the persecution under Galerius Maximian.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sanctórum Mártyrum Floréntii, Juliáni, Cyríaci, Marcellíni et Faustíni, qui omnes, in persecutióne Décii Imperatóris, cápite cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Perugia, the holy martyrs Florence, Julian, Cyriacus, Marcellinus, and Faustinus, who were beheaded in the persecution under Decius.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, beáti Sáncii adolescéntis, qui, etsi in aula régia educátus, pro Christi tamen fide, in persecutióne Arábica, martýrium subíre non dubitávit.
entries.eng: At Cordova, in Spain, blessed Sancius, a youth, who, although brought up in the royal court, yet did not hesitate to undergo martyrdom for the faith of Christ in the persecution of the Arabs.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, pássio sanctárum Zenáidis, Cýriæ, Valériæ et Márciæ; quæ, per multa torménta, gaudéntes ad martýrium pervenérunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy Zenais, Cyria, Valeria, and Marcia, who with rejoicing attained unto martyrdom through many torments.

entries.lat: Magdebúrgi sancti Norbérti, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui Fundátor éxstitit Ordinis Præmonstraténsis.
entries.eng: Holy Norbert, Archbishop of Magdeburg, founder of the Order of the Premonstratensian Canons Regular.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, natális beáti Philíppi, qui fuit unus de septem primis Diáconis. Hic, signis et prodígiis clarus, Samaríam ad Christi fidem convértit, et Regínæ Æthíopum Candácis Eunúchum baptizávit, ac demum apud Cæsaréam requiévit. Juxta ipsum tres Vírgines, ejus fíliæ ac Prophetíssæ, tumulátæ jacent; nam quarta fília ejus, plena Spíritu sancto, Ephesi occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the blessed Philip, who was one of the first seven Deacons. He was illustrious for signs and wonders. He turned Samaria to believe in Christ, and baptized the eunuch of Candace, Queen of the Ethiopians. He fell asleep at last at Caesarea. Three of his virgin daughters, who were prophetesses, lie buried beside him. His fourth daughter died at Ephesus, full of the Holy Ghost.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Artémii, cum uxóre sua Cándida, et fília Paulína. Ex his Artémius, ad prædicatiónem et mirácula sancti Petri Exorcístæ, ad Christum convérsus, et, cum omni domo sua, a sancto Marcéllino Presbýtero baptizátus, Seréni Júdicis jussu plumbátis cæsus et gládio percússus est; uxor vero ejus et fília, in cryptam impúlsæ, lapídibus ruderibúsque sunt óbrutæ.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Artemius, with Candida his wife and Paulina his daughter. This Artemius was brought to believe in Christ by the preaching and miracles of the holy Exorcist Peter, and was baptized with all his house by the holy Priest Marcellinus. He was first hided with scourges loaded with lead by order of Serenus the Judge, and afterwards beheaded. His wife and daughters were thrown into a vault, and buried in stones and rubbish.

entries.lat: In agro Bononiénsi sancti Alexándri, Epíscopi Fæsuláni et Mártyris; qui, rédiens ex urbe Pápia, ubi Ecclésiæ suæ bona apud Longobardórum Regem ab usurpatóribus vindicáverat, ab his in Rhenum flúvium est dejéctus et aquis præfocátus.
entries.eng: At Fiesole, in Tuscany, the holy martyr Alexander, Bishop.

entries.lat: Tarsi, in Cilícia, sanctórum Mártyrum vigínti, qui, tempóribus Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, sub Simplício Júdice, per divérsa torménta glorificavérunt Deum in corpóribus suis.
entries.eng: At Tarsus, in Cilicia, twenty holy martyrs, who in the time of Diocletian and Maximian, under Simplicius the Judge, by diverse torments glorified God in their bodies.

entries.lat: Noviodúni, in Gálliis, sanctórum Mártyrum Amántii, Alexándri et Sociórum.
entries.eng: At Noyon, in Gaul, the holy martyrs Amantius, Alexander, and their companions.

entries.lat: Medioláni deposítio sancti Eustórgii Secúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, deceased, the holy Confessor Eustorgius, second of that name, Bishop.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Joánnis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, holy John, Bishop.

entries.lat: Vesontióne, in Gálliis, sancti Cláudii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Besançon, in Gaul, holy Claud, Archbishop.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli natális sancti Pauli, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui sæpe ab Ariánis ob fidem cathólicam pulsus, et a sancto Júlio Primo, Románo Pontífice, restitútus est; ac demum, ab Ariáno Imperatóre Constántio relegátus ad Cucúsum, Cappadóciæ oppídulum, ibídem, Arianórum insídiis crudéliter strangulátus, ad cæléstia regna migrávit. Ipsíus autem corpus, Theodósio Imperatóre, Constantinópolim summo honóre translátum fuit.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Paul, Archbishop of that city. He was oftentimes thrust out by the Arians because of the Catholic faith, and brought back again by the holy Roman Pontiff, Julius I. At length he was banished by the Arian Emperor Constantius to Cucusus, a little town in Cappadocia, where he was cruelly strangled by Arian plotters, and so passed into the kingdom of heaven. His body was brought to Constantinople with great reverence in the time of the Emperor Theodosius.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Monachórum et Mártyrum Petri Presbýteri, Wallabónsi Diáconi, Sabiniáni, Wistremúndi, Habéntii et Jeremíæ, qui pro Christo, in persecutióne Arábica, sunt juguláti.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy Monks Peter, Wallabond, Sabinian, Wistremund, Habentius, and Jeremiah, of whom Peter was a Priest and Wallabond a 1154,] the holy Confessor William, Deacon, martyrs Archbishop.

entries.lat: Hermópoli, in Ægýpto, sancti Lycariónis Mártyris, qui laniátus, virgis férreis ignítis cæsus, alíaque sævíssima passus est, ac demum, gládio percússus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: In Egypt, the holy martyr Licarion, who was mangled, beaten with red-hot iron rods, and suffered other dreadful torments before he was smitten with the sword, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Placéntiæ sancti Antónii Maríæ Gianélli, Bobiénsis Epíscopi, Fundatóris Congregatiónis Filiárum Maríæ sanctíssimæ ab Horto nuncupatárum, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus inter sanctos Cǽlites adnumerávit.
entries.eng: At Piacenza, holy Anthony Mary Gianelli, Bishop of Bobbio, Founder of the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary most holy of the Garden, whom Pope Pius XII numbered among the Saints in heaven.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Robérti Abbátis, ex Ordine Cisterciénsi.
entries.eng: In England, the holy Abbot Robert, of the Cistercian Order. His grave did raise three dead men to life, and who was written in the list of the Saints by Pope Honorius.

entries.lat: Aquis, in Gállia, sancti Maximíni, qui éxstitit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, ac Dómini discípulus fuísse tráditur.
entries.eng: At Aix in France, St. Maximin, first bishop of that city, who is said to have been a disciple of the Lord.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Callíopæ Mártyris, quæ, ob Christi fidem, abscíssis mammis atque adústis cárnibus, super téstulas volutáta, demum, truncáta cápite, martýrii palmam accépit.
entries.eng: On the same day, St. Calliopa, martyr, who for the faith of Christ received the palm of martyrdom. Her breasts had been cut away, her flesh burned, she was rolled on broken pottery, and was at last beheaded.

entries.lat: Eboráci, in Anglia, sancti Willhélmi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui, inter cétera ad ejus sepúlcrum patráta mirácula, tres mórtuos suscitávit, atque ab Honório Papa Tértio in Sanctórum cánonem relátus est.
entries.eng: At York, in England, the holy Bishop and Confessor William, who, among the other miracles wrought at his tomb, raised three dead men to life, and was enrolled in the canon of the Saints by Pope Honorius III.

entries.lat: Apud Suessiónes, in Gálliis, natális sancti Medárdi, Epíscopi Novioménsis; cujus vita et mors pretiósa gloriósis miráculis commendátur.
entries.eng: At Soissons, in Gaul, the birthday of holy Medard, Bishop of Noyon, whose life and precious death are commended by glorious miracles.

entries.lat: Rotómagi sancti Gildárdi Epíscopi, qui fuit frater ejúsdem sancti Medárdi. Ambo autem fratres, eódem die nati eodémque die Epíscopi consecráti, uno quoque die de hac vita subtrácti, simul in cælum migrárunt.
entries.eng: At Rouen, St. Gildard, bishop, brother of this same St. Medard. They were born on the same day, consecrated bishops at the same time, and were taken from this life on the same day, entering heaven together.

entries.lat: Apud Senónas sancti Heráclii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Sens, the bishop St. Heraclius.

entries.lat: Metis, in Gállia, sancti Clodúlphi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Metz, the bishop St. Clodulph.

entries.lat: In Picéno sancti Severíni, Septempedáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In Piceno, St. Severin, bishop of Septempeda.

entries.lat: In Sardínia sancti Sallustiáni Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Sardinia, St. Sallustian, confessor.

entries.lat: Cameríni sancti Victoríni Confessóris, qui fuit prædícti sancti Severíni, Septempedáni Epíscopi, germánus frater.
entries.eng: At Camerino, St. Victorinus, confessor, the twin brother of St. Severin, bishop of Septempeda.

entries.lat: Noménti, in Sabínis, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Primi et Feliciáni fratrum, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Imperatóribus. Hi gloriósi Mártyres, cum longǽvam in Dómino vitam duxíssent, et nunc simul pária, nunc singillátim divérsa et exquisíta pertulíssent torménta, ambo tandem felícis pugnæ cursum, a Nomentáno Prǽside Promóto animadvérsi gládio, consummavérunt. Ipsórum autem Mártyrum córpora, póstea Romam transláta, in Ecclésia sancti Stéphani Protomártyris, in monte Cǽlio, honorífice collocáta sunt.
entries.eng: Upon the Celian Mount of Rome, the holy Martyrs Primus and Felician, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian. These glorious martyrs had led a long life together, and had suffered diverse and dreadful torments sometimes together, and sometimes apart. At length they brought their happy fight to a close, being beheaded under Promotus, President of Mentana.

entries.lat: Agénni, in Gállia, pássio sancti Vincéntii, Levítæ et Mártyris, qui, ob Christi fidem, verbéribus diríssime cæsus et gládio decollátus est.
entries.eng: At Agen, in Gaul, suffered the holy martyr Vincent the Levite.

entries.lat: Apud Antiochíam sanctæ Pelágiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quam sancti Ambrósius et Joánnes Chrysostómus magnis éfferunt láudibus.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy Virgin martyr Pelagia, whom holy Ambrose and John Chrysostom do greatly praise.

entries.lat: Syracúsis, in Sicília, sancti Maximiáni Epíscopi, cujus sanctus Gregórius Papa sǽpius méminit.
entries.eng: At Syracuse, holy Maximian, Bishop of whom holy Pope Gregory the Great doth oftentimes make mention.

entries.lat: Andriæ, in Apúlia, sancti Richárdi, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, et miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Andria, in Apulia, holy Richard, the first Bishop of that city, famous for wondrous works.

entries.lat: In Ióna, Scótiæ ínsula, sancti Colúmbæ, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
entries.eng: In Scotland, holy Colum, Priest and Confessor,.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sancti Juliáni Mónachi, cujus præclára gesta sanctus Ephræm Diáconus scripsit.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, the holy monk Julian, whose illustrious acts are written by the holy Deacon Ephraim.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Margarítæ Víduæ, Scotórum Regínæ, quæ sextodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: In Scotland, the holy Queen Margaret, famous for her love for the poor and her voluntary poverty.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Salária, pássio beáti Getúlii, claríssimi et doctíssimi viri, ac susceptórum e sancta uxóre Symphorósa beatórum septem fratrum Mártyrum patris, ejúsque Sociórum Cæreális, Amántii et Primitívi. Hi omnes, Hadriáni Imperatóris jussu, a Licínio Consulári tenti, primum cæsi sunt, deínde in cárcerem trusi; postrémum, incéndio tráditi, sed nullo modo ab igne læsi, martýrium suum, fústibus illiso cápite, complevérunt. Ipsórum autem córpora Symphorósa, beáti Getúlii uxor, collégit, et in arenário prǽdii sui honorífice sepelívit.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, the blessed Getulius, a man of great eminence and learning, and his Companions Cerealis, Amantius, and Primitivus. At the command of the Emperor Hadrian they were tortured by Licinius the Consular first hided, then thrust into prison, lastly committed to the flames, but as the fire would nowise hurt them, their heads were beaten in with clubs, and so they finished their testimony. Sympharosa, the wife of blessed Getulius, gathered their bodies together and honourably buried them in a sand-pit upon her own farm.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Aurélia, natális sanctórum Basílidis, Trípodis, Mándalis et aliórum vigínti Mártyrum, sub Imperatóre Aureliáno et Urbis Præfécto Platóne.
entries.eng: Also at Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, holy Basilides, Tripodes, Mandales, and twenty other martyrs, who suffered under the Emperor Aurelian and Plato, the Prefect of the city.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Máximi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, ob strénuam Nicǽnæ fídei confessiónem, a Constántio Imperatóre in exsílium pulsus, ibídem, ærúmnis conféctus, decéssit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy martyr Maximus, Bishop who was banished by the same Emperor Constantius for his unshaken confession of the Nicene faith, and there died worn out by suffering.

entries.lat: Prusæ, in Bithýnia, sancti Timóthei, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, sub Juliáno Apóstata, cum Christum ejuráre noluísset, idcírco, ipsíus Imperatóris jussu, cápite abscíssus est.
entries.eng: In the dominions of Prusias, in Bithynia, holy Timothy, Bishop martyr under Julian the Apostate.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ sancti Mauríni, Abbátis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Cologne, the holy martyr the Abbot Maurinus.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Zacharíæ Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyr Zacharia.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctórum Mártyrum Críspuli et Restitúti.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyrs Crispulus and Restitutus.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Arésii, Rogáti et aliórum quíndecim.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Aresius, Rogatus, and fifteen others.

entries.lat: Petræ, in Arábia, sancti Astérii Epíscopi, qui, ob fidem cathólicam, ab Ariánis multa passus et ab Imperatóre Constántio in Africam relegátus est, ac tandem, in Ecclésiam suam restitútus, Conféssor gloriósus occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Petra, in Arabia, the holy Asterius, Bishop who, for the Catholic faith's sake, suffered many things of the Arians, and by the Emperor Constantius was banished into Africa and died a glorious Confessor.

entries.lat: Antisiodóri sancti Censúrii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Auxerre, holy Censurius, Bishop.
