entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Abdon and Sennen. These were Persians who were brought to Rome in bonds under Decius. They were first hided with scourges loaded with lead, and then slain with the sword.

entries.lat: Assísii, in Umbria, sancti Rufíni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Assisi, in Umbria, the holy martyr Rufinus.

entries.lat: Tubúrbi Lucernáriæ, in Africa, pássio sanctárum Vírginum Máximæ, Donatíllæ et Secúndæ; quarum duæ primæ, in persecutióne Valeriáni et Galliéni, acéto et felle potátæ, deínde plagis acérrimis cæsæ et equúlei extensióne cruciátæ, cratículis étiam exústæ et calce perfricátæ, póstmodum cum Secúnda, Vírgine duódecim annórum, ad béstias simul projéctæ, sed ab his intáctæ, novíssime gládio jugulátæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Tuburbe, in Africa, the holy Virgin martyrs Maxima, Donatilla, and Secunda. In the persecution under Valerian and Gallienus, Maxima and Donatilla were given vinegar and gall to drink, then severely hided and racked, burnt over gratings, and rubbed with lime. Afterward, they were thrown to the beasts along with Secunda, a virgin of twelve years of age, but as the beasts would not touch them they were all slain with the sword.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctæ Julíttæ Mártyris, quæ, cum bona sua, a quodam poténte sibi usurpáta, in judício repéteret, atque ille exceptiónem daret quod ut Christiána non debéret audíri, mox a Júdice jussa est thus idólis offérre, ut posset audíri. Quod illa constánter recúsans, in ignem conjécta est, sicque spíritum Deo réddidit; corpus autem a flamma remánsit illǽsum. Ejus præcláras laudes sanctus Basilíus Magnus egrégio encómio celebrávit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Julitta. She raised a law plea against a certain great man who had spoiled her goods, and he pleaded against her that being a Christian she could not be heard, whereupon the judge commanded her to offer some incense to the idols in order that she might be able to plead. She firmly refused, and was cast into the fire, where she resigned her soul to God, but the fire did not hurt her body. Her famous praises have been set forth by holy Basil the Great in a noble discourse.

entries.lat: Antisiodóri sancti Ursi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Auxerre, holy Ursus, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Ignátii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Fundátor éxstitit Societátis Jesu, atque vir fuit sanctitáte et miráculis clarus, ac religiónis cathólicæ ubíque dilatándæ studiosíssimus; quem Pius Undécimus, Póntifex Máximus, cæléstem ómnium Exercitiórum spirituálium Patrónum constítuit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the birthday of St. Ignatius, confessor, founder of the Society of Jesus, renowned for sanctity and miracles, and most zealous for propagating the Catholic religion in all parts of the world.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Calimérii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, in Antoníni persecutióne, comprehénsus, vulnéribus confóssus, cervicibúsque gládio transverberátis, præceps in púteum dejéctus, martýrii cursum confécit.
entries.eng: At Milan, during the persecution of Antoninus, St. Calimerius, bishop and martyr, who was arrested, covered with wounds, and pierced through the neck with a sword. He terminated his martyrdom by being precipitated into a well.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Mauritánia, pássio beáti Fábii Mártyris, qui, cum ferre vexílla præsidália recusáret, primo in cárcerem trusus est, ibíque diébus áliquot deténtus; deínde, cum in confessióne Christi, interrogátus semel et íterum, immóbilis perduráret, senténtia capitáli a Júdice condemnátur.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Mauretania, the martyrdom of the blessed martyr Fabius. As he refused to carry the ensign of the governor of the province, he was thrown into prison for some days, and as he persisted twice in confessing Christ when brought before the judge, he was condemned to capital punishment.

entries.lat: Sýnnadæ, in Phrýgia Pacatiána, sanctórum Mártyrum Demócriti, Secúndi et Dionýsii.
entries.eng: At Synnada, in Phrygia, the holy martyrs Democritus, Secundus and Denis.

entries.lat: In Sýria sanctórum trecentórum quinquagínta Monachórum Mártyrum, qui, ob defensiónem Sýnodi Chalcedonénsis, ab hæréticis sunt occísi.
entries.eng: In Syria, three hundred and fifty monks, who became martyrs by being slain by the heretics for defending the Council of Chalcedon.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ tránsitus sancti Germáni, Antisiodorénsis Epíscopi, génere, fide, doctrína et miraculórum glória claríssimi; qui Británniam a Pelagianórum hærésibus pénitus liberávit.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the departure from this world of St. Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, a man most renowned for his birth, faith, learning, and glorious miracles, who freed England completely from the heretical doctrines of the Pelagians.

entries.lat: Tagáste, in Africa, sancti Firmi Epíscopi, confessiónis glória conspícui.
entries.eng: At Tagaste, in Africa, St. Firmus, bishop, illustrious by a glorious confession of the faith.

entries.lat: Senis, in Túscia, natális beáti Joánnis Columbíni, qui fuit Institútor Ordinis Jesuatórum, et sanctitáte ac miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Siena, in Tuscany, the birthday of blessed John Colombini, who was the Founder of the Order of the Jesuati, and was renowned for his holiness and miracles.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ pássio sanctórum septem fratrum Machabæórum Mártyrum, qui, cum matre sua, passi sunt sub Antíocho Epipháne Rege. Eórum relíquiæ, Romam translátæ, in eádem Ecclésia sancti Petri ad Víncula cónditæ fuérunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the seven holy Maccabee brethren and their mother, who suffered under King Antiochus Epiphanes. Their relics have been brought to Rome and buried in the aforesaid Church of St. Peter-in-Chains.

entries.lat: Vercéllis natális sancti Eusébii, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, ob confessiónem fídei cathólicæ, a Constántio Príncipe Scythópolim, in Palæstína, et inde in Cappadóciam relegátus, póstmodum ad Ecclésiam suam revérsus, martýrium, persequéntibus Ariánis, passus est. Ipsíus autem memória étiam décimo octávo Kaléndas Januárii solémniter habétur, quo die fuit Epíscopus ordinátus; ejúsque festum recólitur décimo séptimo Kaléndas Januárii.
entries.eng: At Vercelli, the holy martyr Eusebius, Bishop of that city, who was banished by the Emperor Constantius, first to Bethshan and then into Cappadocia, on account of his confession of the Catholic faith, but at length returned unto his own Church. He suffered martyrdom under the persecution of the Arians. His memory is chiefly kept upon the 15th day of December, which is that of his ordination as Bishop.

entries.lat: Nucériæ Paganórum, in Campánia, item natális sancti Alfónsi-Maríæ de Ligório, Fundatóris Congregatiónis a sanctíssimo Redemptóre nuncupátæ, Epíscopi sanctæ Agathæ Gothórum et Confessóris, zelo animárum, scriptis, verbo et exémplo insígnis; quem Summus Póntifex Gregórius Décimus sextus albo Sanctórum adscrípsit, et Pius Nonus Doctórem universális Ecclésiæ declarávit, et Pius Duodécimus ómnium Confessariórum ac Moralistárum cæléstem apud Deum Patrónum constítuit. Ipsíus vero festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Nocera de' Pagani, in Campania, likewise the birthday of holy Alphonsus Mary de Liguori, Founder of the Congregation of the most Holy Redeemer, Bishop of Sant' Agata dei Goti and Confessor, distinguished for his zeal for souls, his writings, his word and his example; whom the Sovereign Pontiff Gregory XVI enrolled in the register of the Saints, and Pius IX declared a Doctor of the universal Church, and Pius XII appointed heavenly Patron with God of all Confessors and Moralists. His feast is kept on the following day.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Latína, sanctórum Mártyrum Boni Presbýteri, Fausti et Mauri, cum áliis novem; qui in Actis sancti Stéphani Papæ describúntur.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, upon the Latin Way, the holy martyrs Bonus the Priest, Faustus, and Maurus, and nine others, of whom it is written in the Acts of holy Pope Stephen.

entries.lat: Item Romæ pássio sanctárum Vírginum Fídei, Spei et Caritátis, e sancta Sophía matre progenitárum, quæ, sub Hadriáno Príncipe, martýrii corónam adéptæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgins, Faith, Hope, and Charity, who gained the crown of martyrdom under the Emperor Hadrian.

entries.lat: Philadelphíæ, in Arábia, sanctórum Mártyrum Cyrílli, Aquilæ, Petri, Domitiáni, Rufi et Menándri, una die coronatórum.
entries.eng: At Philadelphia, in Arabia, the holy martyrs Cyril, Aquila, Peter, Domitian, Rufus, and Menander, who were all crowned upon one and the same day.

entries.lat: Perge, in Pamphýlia, sanctórum Mártyrum Leóntii, Attii, Alexándri, et aliórum sex agricolárum; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Flaviáno Prǽside, decolláti sunt.
entries.eng: At Perge, in Pamphylia, the holy martyrs Leontius, Attius, Alexander, and six other husbandmen, who were beheaded under the President Flavian in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Gerúndæ, in Hispánia, natális sancti Felícis Mártyris, qui, post divérsa tormentórum génera, a Daciáno támdiu jussus est laniári, donec invíctum Christo spíritum rédderet.
entries.eng: At Gerona, in Spain, the birthday of the holy martyr Felix, who, after divers kinds of torments, was by order of Dacian torn so long until he rendered up to Christ his unconquered spirit.

entries.lat: In território Parisiénsi sancti Justíni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy martyr Justinus.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Veri Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Vienne, holy Verus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Wintóniæ, in Anglia, sancti Ethelwóldi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Winchester, in England, holy Ethelwold, Bishop.

entries.lat: In pago Lisuíno, in Gállia, sancti Nemésii Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the district of Lisieux, the holy Confessor Nemesius.

entries.lat: Romæ, in Exquíliis, Dedicátio sancti Petri Apóstoli ad Víncula.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Esquiline, the Dedication of St. Peter the Apostle in Chains.

entries.lat: Sancti Alfónsi-Maríæ de Ligório, Fundatóris Congregatiónis a sanctíssimo Redemptóre nuncupátæ, Epíscopi sanctæ Agathæ Gothórum, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, qui requiévit in Dómino prídie hujus diéi.
entries.eng: At Nocera-dei-Pagani, holy Alphonsus Mary de Liguori, Bishop of Santa-Agata-de'-Goti, and Founder of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer. Illustrious for the zeal for the salvation of souls shown both by his writings, his words, and his ensample. Pope Gregory XVI. enrolled his name with those of the Saints, and the Supreme Pontiff Pius IX. gave him the title of Doctor of the Church.

entries.lat: Romæ, in cœmetério Callísti, natális sancti Stéphani Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, dum Missæ Sacrum perágeret, et, superveniéntibus milítibus, ante altáre intrépidus et immóbilis cœpta mystéria perfíceret, in sede sua decollátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the cemetery of Callistus, the holy Pope and martyr Stephen. He was celebrating Mass during the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, when the soldiers broke in. He finished his office before the altar without fear or trembling, and then was beheaded as he sat upon his throne.

entries.lat: Nicǽæ, in Bithýnia, pássio sanctæ Theodótæ, cum tribus fíliis suis. Ex his primogénitum, nómine Evódium, cum Christum fiduciáliter confiterétur, fecit primo Nicétius, Consuláris Bithýniæ, fústibus cædi; deínde matrem, cum ómnibus fíliis, igne consúmi.
entries.eng: At Nice, in Bithynia, the holy Theodota and her three sons, who were all burned in the fire together by the order of Neretius, Consular of Bithynia, after he had first caused the eldest son, whose name was Evodius, to be beaten with clubs for his faithful confession of Christ.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Rutílii Mártyris, qui cum sǽpius, de loco in locum fúgiens, persecutiónem declinásset, et perículum intérdum étiam pecúnia redemísset, ex inopináto aliquándo comprehénsus est, et, Prǽsidi oblátus, torméntis cruciátur plúrimis; demum, ígnibus tráditus, egrégio martýrio coronátur.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyr Rutilius. He had fled from one place to another in order to escape the persecution, and had sometimes bought himself out of danger, when he was unexpectedly arrested and brought before the President. He was long put to the torture, then given over to the fire, and so crowned with a noble testimony.

entries.lat: Patávii sancti Máximi, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui, miráculis clarus, beáto fine quiévit.
entries.eng: At Padua, the holy Maximus, Bishop of that city, who died a blessed death, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Philíppis, in Macedónia, sanctæ Lýdiæ purpuráriæ, quæ, prædicánte ibídem sancto Paulo Apóstolo, ut beátus Lucas in Actibus Apostólicis refert, ómnium prima crédidit Evangélio.
entries.eng: At Philippi, in Macedonia, holy Lydia, a seller of purple, who was the first of all to believe the Gospel there at the preaching of the holy Apostle Paul.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Aspréni Epíscopi, qui a sancto Petro Apóstolo, curátus ab infirmitáte ac deínde baptizátus, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus fuit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Aspren, Bishop of Naples, who was healed of sickness by the holy Apostle Peter, and thereupon procuring himself to be baptized was ordained Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli natális sancti Hermélli Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyr Hermellus.

entries.lat: Apud Indos, Persis finítimos, pássio sanctórum Monachórum, et aliórum fidélium, quos Abénner Rex, pérsequens Ecclésiam Dei, divérsis afflíctos supplíciis, cædi jussit.
entries.eng: In India, upon the coasts of Persia, the holy Monks and others whom King Abenner, when he was persecuting the Church of God, caused to be tormented and slain in diverse ways.

entries.lat: Augustodúni deposítio sancti Euphrónii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy Confessor Euphronius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Anágniæ sancti Petri Epíscopi, qui, monástica primum observántia, deínde pastoráli vigilántia clarus, quiévit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Anagni, holy Peter, Bishop who fell asleep in the Lord, famous for his observance as a Monk first, and afterwards for his carefulness as a shepherd.

entries.lat: Beróeæ, in Sýria, sanctárum mulíerum Maránæ et Cyræ.
entries.eng: At Bercea, in Syria, the holy women Marana and Cyra,.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis Invéntio beatíssimi Stéphani Protomártyris, et sanctórum Gamaliélis, Nicodémi et Abibónis, sicut Luciáno Presbýtero divínitus revelátum est, Honórii Príncipis témpore.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the Finding of the most blessed Stephen, the first Martyr, and of the holy Gamaliel, Nicodemus and Abibon, as was divinely revealed to the Priest Lucian, in the time of the Emperor Honorius.

entries.lat: Sancti Domínici Confessóris, qui Ordinis Fratrum Prædicatórum Fundátor fuit, atque octávo Idus mensis hujus in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Dominic, who was the Founder of the Order of Friars Preachers, and rested in peace on the 6th day of this month.

entries.lat: In vico Ars, diœcésis Bellicénsis, in Gállia, natális sancti Joánnis Baptístæ-Maríæ Vianney, Presbýteri et Confessóris, in parochiáli múnere obeúndo insígnis, quem Pius Papa Undécimus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit, et ómnium parochórum cæléstem Patrónum constítuit. Ipsíus tamen festum sexto Idus hujus mensis recólitur.
entries.eng: In the village of Ars, in the diocese of Belley, in Gaul, the birthday of holy John Baptist Mary Vianney, Priest and Confessor, distinguished in the discharge of his office as a parish priest, whom Pope Pius XI enrolled among the Saints, and appointed heavenly Patron of all parish priests. His feast, however, is kept on the 8th day of this month.

entries.lat: Thessalonícæ item natális beáti Aristárchi, qui discípulus et comes indivíduus fuit sancti Pauli Apóstoli, de quo ipse Paulus ad Colossénses scribit: « Salútat vos Aristárchus, concaptívus meus ». Is, ab eódem Apóstolo Epíscopus Thessalonicénsium ordinátus, tandem, post longos agónes, sub Neróne, coronátus a Christo, quiévit.
entries.eng: At Thessalonica, the blessed Aristarchus, the disciple and close companion of the holy Apostle Paul, concerning whom the same Apostle writeth unto the Colossians, (iv, 10) "Aristarchus, my fellow-prisoner, saluteth you." He was by the same Apostle ordained Bishop of the Thessalonians, and after long contendings under Nero he was crowned by Christ, and fell asleep.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Perpétuæ, quæ, a beáto Petro Apóstolo baptizáta, Nazárium fílium et Africánum virum ad Christi fidem perdúxit, et multa sanctórum Mártyrum córpora sepelívit; ac tandem, bonórum óperum méritis cumuláta, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Perpetua, who was baptized by the blessed Apostle Peter. She turned her son Naserius and her husband Africanus to believe in Christ, and buried a great number of bodies of the holy martyrs, and passed away to be with the Lord, full of good works.

entries.lat: Item Romæ, via Latína, pássio beáti Tertullíni, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, sub Valeriáno Imperatóre, post ímpiam fústium mactatiónem, ígnium circa látera exustiónem, oris quassatiónem, atque in equúleo extensiónem nervorúmque cæsiónem, data senténtia, cápitis amputatióne martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Latin Way, the blessed martyr Tertullinus. He was a Priest who, under the Emperor Valerian, was horridly beaten with clubs, had his sides burnt and his mouth crushed, was stretched upon a rack and had his muscles cut, and then sentence was given to behead him, and so he finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Eleuthérii Mártyris, ex órdine Senatório viri, qui pro Christo, in persecutióne Maximiáni, gládio cæsus est.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyr Eleutherius, of the Senatorial Order, who was slain with the sword for Christ's sake, in the persecution under Maximian.

entries.lat: In Pérside sanctárum Mártyrum Iæ et Sociárum; quæ, cum novem míllibus Christiánis captívis, sub Sápore Rege, divérsis pœnis afflíctæ, martýrium subiérunt.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy martyrs Ia and her Companions, who were diversely afflicted and underwent martyrdom along with nine thousand Christian prisoners under King Sapor.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Agábii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Confessor Agabius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Euphrónii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Tours, holy Euphronius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ commemorátio sancti Protásii Mártyris; qui Medioláni, una cum Gervásio fratre, passus est tertiodécimo Kaléndas Júlii.
entries.eng: At Cologne, the holy martyr Protasius.

entries.lat: Romæ, in Exquíliis, Dedicátio Basílicæ sanctæ Maríæ ad Nives.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Esquiline, the Dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary of the Snow.

entries.lat: Cataláuni, in Gállia, sancti Mémmii, civis Románi, qui, a sancto Petro Apóstolo consecrátus illíus civitátis Epíscopus, pópulum sibi commíssum ad Evangélii veritátem perdúxit.
entries.eng: At Châlons, in Gaul, holy Memmius, a Roman citizen, who, having been consecrated Bishop of that city by St. Peter the Apostle, led the people committed to him to the truth of the Gospel.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctórum Mártyrum vigínti trium, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, via Salária véteri, cápite obtruncáti sunt, et, ad clivum Cucúmeris, ibídem sepúlti.
entries.eng: At Rome, twenty three holy martyrs, who, in the persecution under Diocletian, were beheaded on the old Salarian Way, and buried there at Cucumber Hill.

entries.lat: Asculi, in Picéno, sancti Emýgdii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, a sancto Marcéllo Papa Epíscopus ordinátus et illuc ad prædicándum Evangélium missus, ibídem, in confessióne Christi, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Ascoli, in Picenum, the holy Bishop and martyr Emygdius, who was ordained Bishop by holy Pope Marcellus and sent thither to preach the Gospel, and he received a crown of martyrdom for confessing Christ, under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Eusígnii mílitis, qui annum agens centésimum décimum, cum Constantíni Magni fidem, sub quo militáverat, Juliáno Apóstatæ exprobráret, eúmque ut pátriæ pietátis desertórem redargúeret, ab eódem jussus est cápite cædi.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy soldier Eusignius. He was in the hundred and tenth year of his age when he cast in the teeth of the Emperor Julian the Apostate the faith of Constantine the Great, under whom he had served, and rebuked Julian himself for a renegade from the religion of his Fathers, whereupon Julian commanded him to be beheaded.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Ægyptiórum Cantídii, Cantidiáni et Sobélis.
entries.eng: Also, in Egypt, the holy martyrs Cantidius, Cantidian, and Sobel.

entries.lat: Augústæ Vindelicórum natális sanctæ Afræ Mártyris, quæ, cum esset pagána, per doctrínam sancti Narcíssi Epíscopi ad Christum est convérsa, et, cum ómnibus domus suæ membris, ab eódem Epíscopo baptizáta; póstmodum vero, ob Christi confessiónem igni trádita, martýrium suum, septem diébus ántequam beáta Hilária mater ac tres ancíllæ eódem cruciátus génere coronaréntur, felíciter explévit.
entries.eng: At Augsburg, the holy martyr Afra. She was turned from paganism to Christ by the teaching of the holy Bishop Narcissus, and baptized with all her house, and for confessing Christ she was burnt.

entries.lat: Augustodúni beáti Cassiáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Autun, blessed Cassian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Apud Theánum, in Campánia, sancti Páridis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Teano, holy Paris, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Oswáldi Regis, cujus gesta sanctus Beda Venerábilis commémorat.
entries.eng: In England, holy King Oswald, whose deeds are recorded by St. Bede the Venerable.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Nonnæ, quæ fuit mater beatórum Gregórii Nazianzéni, Cæsárii et Gorgóniæ.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, holy Nonna, the mother of blessed Gregory of Nazianzus.

entries.lat: In monte Thabor Transfigurátio Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
entries.eng: On Mount Thabor, the Transfiguration of our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, in cœmetério Callísti, natális beáti Xysti Secúndi, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, gládio animadvérsus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the cemetery of Callistus, upon the Appian Way, the blessed Pope and martyr Sixtus II, who received the crown of martyrdom by the sword in the persecution under Valerian. Likewise the holy martyrs Felicissimus and Agapitus, deacons of the aforesaid blessed Xystus, and his subdeacons Januarius, Magnus, Vincent, and Stephen, who were all beheaded along with him, and were buried in the cemetery of Pretextatus. Along with them suffered also the blessed Quartus, as is written by holy Cyprian.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Felicíssimi et Agapíti, ipsíus beáti Xysti Diaconórum; Januárii, Magni, Vincéntii et Stéphani, Subdiaconórum. Hi omnes, una cum eódem Pontífice páriter decolláti sunt, atque in Prætextáti cœmetério sepúlti. Passus est étiam cum eis beátus Quartus, ut scribit sanctus Cypriánus.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy Martyrs Felicissimus and Agapitus, Deacons of the same blessed Sixtus, and Januarius, Magnus, Vincent and Stephen, Subdeacons. All these were beheaded together with the same Pontiff, and buried in the cemetery of Praetextatus. Blessed Quartus also suffered with them, as St. Cyprian writes.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ natális sancti Domínici Confessóris, qui Ordinis Fratrum Prædicatórum Fundátor éxstitit. Hic vir, sanctitáte et doctrína claríssimus, virginitátem perpétuo illibátam custodívit, et, ob singulárem meritórum grátiam, tres mórtuos suscitávit; cumque prædicatióne sua compressísset hǽreses, ac plúrimos ad religiósam et piam vitam instituísset, in pace quiévit. Ejus autem festívitas prídie Nonas mensis hujus celebrátur, ex constitutióne Pauli Papæ Quarti.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the birthday of St. Dominic, confessor and founder of the Order of Friars Preachers. He was a man of great renown for holiness and learning. Until death he preserved without stain his virginity, and by the singular grace of his merits raised three dead men to life. By his preaching he curbed heresies, and established many persons in a religious and godly manner of life. He died on this day, but his festival, by an ordinance of Pope Paul IV, is celebrated on August 4.

entries.lat: In monastério sancti Petri de Cardégna, Ordinis sancti Benedícti, apud Burgos, in Hispánia, pássio ducentórum Monachórum cum Stéphano Abbáte, qui a Saracénis pro Jesu Christi fide interfécti sunt, atque ibídem in claustro a Christiánis sepúlti.
entries.eng: At Burgos, in Spain, in the Monastery of St. Peter de Cardena, of the Order of St. Benedict, the Abbot Stephen and two hundred monks, who were massacred by the Saracens for their faith in Jesus Christ, and by the Christians then buried inside their cloister.

entries.lat: Complúti, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Justi et Pastóris fratrum, qui, cum adhuc púeri lítteris imbueréntur, sponte ad martýrium, projéctis in schola tábulis, cucurrérunt; et mox, a Daciáno Prǽside tenéri jussi et fústibus cædi, ambo, cum se mútuis exhortatiónibus constantíssime corroborárent, extra civitátem perdúcti sunt, et ibi a carnífice juguláti.
entries.eng: At Alcala, in Spain, the holy brethren Justus and Pastor, both martyrs. They were boys learning at school when they threw away their slates, and ran of their own wish to be martyred. The President Dacian ordered them to be taken and cudgelled, and when they continued to call on each other to stand firm he had them led outside the city, where the executioner cut their throats.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Hormísdæ, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Pope Hormisdas.

entries.lat: Amidæ, in Mesopotámia, sancti Jacóbi Eremítæ, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Diarbekr, the holy hermit James, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Cajetáni Thienǽi Confessóris, Clericórum Regulárium Fundatóris, qui, singulári in Deum fidúcia, prístinam Apostólicam vivéndi formam suis coléndam trádidit, et, miráculis clarus, a Cleménte Papa Décimo inter Sanctos relátus est.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy Confessor Gaetan of Tiene, Founder of the Clerks Regular, who with wonderful confidence in God enjoined upon them the first way of living of the Apostles. He was famous for miracles, and Clement X. enrolled his name among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Arétii, in Túscia, natális sancti Donáti, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, inter cétera virtútis ópera (ut scribit beátus Gregórius Papa), cálicem sanctum, a Pagánis fractum, orándo instaurávit. Is, in persecutióne Juliáni Apóstatæ, a Quadratiáno Augustáli comprehénsus, et, cum sacrificáre idólis renuísset, gládio percússus, martýrium consummávit. Passus est étiam cum eo beátus Hilarínus Mónachus; cujus memória décimo séptimo Kaléndas Augústi recólitur, quo die sacrum ipsíus corpus ad Ostia Tiberína translátum fuit.
entries.eng: At Arezzo, in Tuscany, the holy martyr Donatus, Bishop, who among other miraculous deeds, by his prayers (as is related by blessed Pope Gregory) made whole again a sacred chalice which had been broken by pagans. He was arrested by the imperial officer Quadratian in the persecution under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and for as much as he refused to sacrifice to idols he was beheaded, and so finished his testimony. There suffered also along with him the blessed monk Hilarinus, whose feast is kept upon the 16th day of July, being the day whereon his body was brought to Ostia.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Petri et Juliáni, cum áliis decem et octo.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Peter and Julian, and eighteen others.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Fausti mílitis, qui, sub Aurélio Cómmodo, post multa certámina, martýrii palmam adéptus est.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy soldier Faustus, who under the Emperor Aurelius Commodus, after many contendings, gained the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Novocómi pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Carpóphori, Exánthi, Cássii, Severíni, Secúndi et Licínii; qui, in confessióne Christi, cápite truncáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Como, the holy martyrs Carpophorus, Exanthus, Cassius, Severinus, Secundus, and Licinius, who were beheaded, for confessing Christ.

entries.lat: Nísibi, in Mesopotámia, sancti Dométii, Mónachi Persæ, qui cum duóbus discípulis, sub Juliáno Apóstata, lapidátus est.
entries.eng: At Nisibis, in Mesopotamia, holy Dometius, a Persian monk, who was stoned to death with two of his disciples, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate.

entries.lat: Rotómagi sancti Victrícii Epíscopi, qui adhuc miles, sub eódem Juliáno, abjíciens pro Christo cíngulum, a Tribúno multis torméntis affícitur, et cápitis damnátur; sed, carnífice, qui ad eum cædéndum missus fúerat, cæcitáte percússo, ipse, vínculis solútis, liber evásit. Póstea, Epíscopus factus, indómitas Morinórum et Nerviórum gentes divíni prædicatióne verbi ad Christi fidem perdúxit, et demum Conféssor in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Rouen, holy Vitricius, Bishop He was a soldier who threw away his belt for Christ's sake under the same Emperor Julian. He was put to many torments by his Tribune, and condemned to death, but the executioner who had been sent to behead him was struck blind, and he got his bonds loosed, and escaped. He afterwards became a Bishop, and by his preaching of the word brought the unconquered tribes of the Morini and Nervii to believe in Christ, and at the last fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Cataláuni, in Gállia, sancti Donatiáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Châlons in Gaul, holy Donatian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Messánæ, in Sicília, sancti Albérti Confessóris, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Messina, in Sicily, the holy Confessor Albert, of the Order of Carmelites, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Sancti Joánnis Baptístæ-Maríæ Vianney, Presbýteri et Confessóris, cæléstis ómnium parochórum Patróni; cujus dies natális prídie Nonas mensis hujus recensétur.
entries.eng: St. John Baptist Mary Vianney, Priest and Confessor, heavenly Patron of all parish priests, whose birthday is recorded on the 4th day of this month.

entries.lat: Sanctórum Mártyrum Cyríaci Diáconi, Largi et Smarágdi, qui, cum áliis vigínti Sóciis, passi sunt décimo séptimo Kaléndas Aprílis. Eórum córpora, via Salária a Joánne Presbýtero sepúlta, sanctus Marcéllus Papa in prǽdium Lucínæ, via Ostiénsi, hoc die tránstulit; quæ póstea, in Urbem deláta, in Diaconía sanctæ Maríæ in via Lata fuérunt recóndita.
entries.eng: The holy Martyrs Cyriacus, Deacon, Largus and Smaragdus, who suffered with twenty other Companions on the 16th day of March. Their bodies, buried on the Salarian Way by the Priest John, holy Pope Marcellus on this day translated to the estate of Lucina, on the Ostian Way; and afterwards, being carried into the City, they were laid up in the Deaconry of St. Mary in Via Lata.

entries.lat: Anazárbi, in Cilícia, sancti Maríni senis, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Lýsia Prǽside, cæsus flagris, in ligno suspénsus ac laniátus, feris tandem objéctus intériit.
entries.eng: At Anazarbus, in Cilicia, holy Marinus the Elder. Under the Emperor Diocletian and the President Lysias he was flogged, tied to a beam, and mangled, and at last thrown to wild beasts. Likewise, the holy martyrs Eleutherius and Leonides, who finished their martyrdom, by fire.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Eleuthérii et Leónidæ, qui per ignem martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy Martyrs Eleutherius and Leonides, who consummated their martyrdom by fire.

entries.lat: In Pérside sancti Hormísdæ Mártyris, sub Sápore Rege.
entries.eng: In Persia, under King Sapor, the holy martyr Hormisdas.

entries.lat: Cýzici, in Hellespónto, sancti Æmiliáni Epíscopi, qui, pro sacrárum Imáginum cultu a Leóne Imperatóre multa passus, demum in exsílio vitam finívit.
entries.eng: At Cyzicus, upon the Hellespont, holy Aemilianus, Bishop who suffered much at the hands of the Emperor Leo on account of the worship of the holy images, and at last died in exile.

entries.lat: In Creta sancti Myrónis Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: In Crete, holy Myron, Bishop famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Sevéri, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui ex India, Evangélii prædicándi causa, laboriósam peregrinatiónem suscépit, et, cum ad præfátam urbem devenísset, ingéntem Paganórum multitúdinem verbo et miráculis ad Christi fidem convértit.
entries.eng: At Vienne, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Severus, a Priest, who undertook a wearisome pilgrimage from India in order to preach the Gospel, and when he came to the aforesaid city, by his word and miracles brought a vast multitude of heathen to believe in Christ.

entries.lat: Vigília sancti Lauréntii Mártyris.
entries.eng: The Vigil of the holy martyr Laurence.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Románi, mílitis et Mártyris; qui, confessióne beáti Lauréntii compúnctus, pétiit ab eo baptizári, et, mox exhíbitus ac fústibus cæsus, ad últimum decollátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy soldier Romanus, who was so wrought upon by the confession of the blessed Lawrence that he sought baptism at his hands, and was presently arraigned, beaten with clubs, and then beheaded.

entries.lat: In Túscia natális sanctórum Mártyrum Secundiáni, Marcelliáni et Veriáni; qui, témpore Décii, a Promóto Consulári primum cæsi sunt, deínde in equúleo suspénsi, et abrási úngulis, atque igne latéribus appósito assáti, ac tandem triumphálem martýrii palmam, cápite cæsi, meruérunt.
entries.eng: In Tuscany, the holy martyrs Secundian, Marcellian, and Verian. In the time of the Emperor Decius the Consular Promotus caused them first to be hided, then hung upon the rack, scarified with hooks, and burnt in the sides, thereafter they were beheaded, and so gained the palm of victory through martyrdom.

entries.lat: Verónæ sanctórum Mártyrum Firmi et Rústici, qui, témpore Maximiáni Imperatóris, sub Anolíno Júdice, cum sacrificáre idólis renúerent et constánter in Christi fide persísterent, ambo jussi sunt, post ália superáta supplícia, fústibus cædi et cápite amputári.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy martyrs Firmus and Rusticus, in the time of the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, hortánte eos ad constántiam sancto Numídico, in ignem conjécti, martýrii palmam adépti sunt. Ipse autem Numídicus, licet cum áliis in rogum injéctus et lapídibus óbrutus fuísset, a fília tamen, effóssus et semivívus repértus, curátus est; ac póstea, ob ejus virtútem, in Ecclésiæ Carthaginénsis Presbýterum a beáto Cypriáno méruit cooptári.
entries.eng: In Africa, many holy martyrs, who at the exhortation of holy Numidicus gained the palm of martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian by being cast into the fire. Numidicus himself was thrown upon the burning fire along with the others, and then covered with stones but when his daughter dug him out there was still some life left in him, he was healed, and afterwards by his worthy life obtained from blessed Cyprian admission as a Priest to the Church at Carthage.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Juliáni, Marciáni et aliórum octo; qui, ob Salvatóris imáginem, quam in porta ǽnea constitúerant, omnes, ímpii Leónis Imperatóris jussu, post multa torménta, gládio necáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyrs Julian, Marcian, and eight others, who were long tortured, and then slain with the sword by command of the wicked Emperor Leo, on account of the image of the Saviour which they had set up in the Brazen Gate.

entries.lat: Cataláuni, in Gállia, sancti Domitiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Châlons, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Domitian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Tiburtína, natális beáti Lauréntii Archidiáconi, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, post plúrima torménta cárceris, vérberum diversórum, fústium, ac plumbatárum et laminárum ardéntium, ad últimum, in cratícula férrea assátus, martýrium complévit; ejúsque corpus a beáto Hippólyto et Justíno Presbýtero sepúltum fuit in cœmetério Cyríacæ, in agro Veráno.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Tiburtine Way, the blessed Archdeacon Lawrence. In the persecution under the Emperor Valerian he suffered many torments, diverse stripes, armed scourges, cudgels, and whips loaded with lead, and plates of heated metal, and at the last he was laid upon a bed of iron bars over a slow fire, and so finished his testimony. His body was buried in the cemetery of St. Cyriaca in the Veran field by blessed Hippolytus and Justin the Priest.

entries.lat: In Hispánia Apparítio beátæ Maríæ Vírginis de Mercéde nuncupátæ, quæ Ordinis redemptiónis captivórum sub ejus nómine Institútrix fuit. Ipsíus autem festívitas octávo Kaléndas Octóbris recólitur.
entries.eng: In Spain, the Apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary called of Mercy, who was the Foundress of the Order for the redemption of captives under her name. Her feast is kept on the 24th day of September.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctórum centum sexagínta quinque mílitum Mártyrum, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, one hundred and sixty-five holy soldiers, who suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Aurelian.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, sub Prǽside Æmiliáno, divérsis exquisitísque torméntis diútius cruciáti, vario mortis génere corónam martýrii sunt adépti.
entries.eng: At Alexandria are commemorated the holy martyrs, who under the President Aemilian, in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, were long tortured with diverse and terrible torments, and gained the crown of martyrdom by diverse kinds of death.

entries.lat: Bérgomi sanctæ Astériæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni Imperatórum.
entries.eng: At Bergamo, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy Virgin and martyr Asteria.

entries.lat: Carthágine sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum Bassæ, Paulæ et Agathonícæ.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy Virgins Bassa, Paula, and Agathonica, all martyrs.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Deúsdedit Confessóris, qui quod in hebdómada mánibus suis operándo lucrabátur, die sábbati paupéribus erogábat.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Deusdedit, who bestowed upon the poor on Saturday what he had earned during the week by the work of his hands.

entries.lat: Romæ, inter duas Lauros, natális sancti Tiburtii Mártyris, qui, sub Júdice Fabiáno, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cum Christum, nudis plantis super carbónes ardéntes ingréssus, majóri confiterétur constántia, duci in tértium ab Urbe milliárium atque ibídem gládio animadvérti jubétur.
entries.eng: At Rome, between the two Laurel trees, the holy martyr Tiburtius. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian the judge Fabian caused him to walk with bare feet upon burning coals, and as he confessed Christ all the more firmly, commanded him to be led to the third mile-stone outside the city, and there beheaded.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctæ Susánnæ Vírginis, quæ, cum ex nóbili prosápia esset orta et beáti Caji Pontíficis neptis, martýrii palmam, témpore Diocletiáni, cápitis obtruncatióne proméruit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy Virgin Susanna, a damsel of noble birth, a niece to blessed Pope Caius. She was beheaded in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Assísii, in Umbria, natális sanctæ Claræ Vírginis, primæ plantæ Páuperum Dominárum Ordinis Minórum; quam, vita et miráculis célebrem, Alexánder Papa Quartus in númerum sanctárum Vírginum rétulit. Ipsíus tamen festum sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Assisi, in Umbria, the birthday of the holy Virgin Clare, the first plant of the Poor Ladies of the Order of Minors, whom, renowned for her life and miracles, Pope Alexander IV enrolled among the holy Virgins. Her feast, however, is kept on the following day.

entries.lat: Cománæ, in Ponto, sancti Alexándri Epíscopi, cognoménto Carbonárii, qui, ex philósopho disertíssimo eminéntem Christiánæ humilitátis sciéntiam adéptus, et a sancto Gregório Thaumatúrgo in thronum illíus Ecclésiæ sublimátus, non solum prædicatióne, sed étiam consummáto per ignem martýrio fuit illústris.
entries.eng: At Comana, in Pontus, holy Alexander, Bishop of that city, surnamed the charcoal-burner. He was a most learned philosopher, who learnt to be eminent for humility as a Christian. He was raised by holy Gregory the wonder-worker to fill that see, and was illustrious not only for his preaching but because he suffered martyrdom by fire.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sanctórum Rufíni, Marsórum Epíscopi, et Sociórum ejus, sub Maximíno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, under the Emperor Maximinus, the holy martyr Rufinus, Bishop of the Marsi, and his Companions.

entries.lat: Apud Ebroicénses, in Gállia, sancti Tauríni Epíscopi, qui, a beáto Cleménte Papa ordinátus illíus civitátis Epíscopus, Evangélii prædicatióne Christiánam fidem propagávit, ac, multis pro ea suscéptis labóribus, miraculórum glória conspícuus obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Évreux, the holy Confessor Taurinus, who was ordained Bishop of that city by blessed Pope Clement. He spread the Christian faith by his preaching of the gospel, and after much labour for that end fell asleep in the Lord, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Cameráci, in Gállia, sancti Gaugeríci, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Cambrai, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Gaugeric, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: In província Valériæ sancti Equítii Abbátis, cujus sánctitas testimónio beáti Gregórii Papæ comprobátur.
entries.eng: In the province of Valeria, on the Danube, the holy Abbot Equitius, whose holiness is attested by the witness of blessed Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sanctæ Dignæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Todi, the holy Virgin Digna.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Claræ Vírginis, primæ plantæ Páuperum Dominárum Ordinis Minórum; quæ ad ætérnas Agni núptias evocáta est prídie hujus diéi.
entries.eng: At Assisi, in Umbria, the holy Virgin Clare, the first of the women of the Order of Friars Minors Her life and miracles were famous, and Pope Alexander IV enrolled her name among those of the holy virgins.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Porcárii, Abbátis monastérii Lirinénsis, et Sociórum ejus quingentórum Monachórum; qui pro fide cathólica, a bárbaris cæsi, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Porcarius, Abbot of the monastery of Lerins, and five hundred monks, crowned with martyrdom, slain by the barbarians for the Catholic faith's sake.

entries.lat: Cátanæ, in Sicília, natális sancti Eúpli Diáconi, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Augústis; qui, cum diutíssime pro confessióne Dómini tortus esset, tandem martýrii palmam, gládio cædénte, percépit.
entries.eng: At Catania, in Sicily, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy Deacon Euplius. He was long put to the torture for confessing the Lord, and at length beheaded, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Augústæ Vindelicórum sanctæ Hiláriæ, quæ, cum esset beátæ Afræ Mártyris mater et ad sepúlcrum illíus excubáret, ibídem, pro fide Christi, a persecutóribus igni trádita est cum Digna, Euprépia et Eunómia, ancíllis suis. Passi sunt étiam eódem die, in præfáta urbe, Quiríacus, Lárgio, Crescentiánus, Nímmia et Juliána, cum áliis vigínti.
entries.eng: In the same city, upon the same day, there suffered also Quiriacus, Largis, Crescentian, Nimmia, Juliana, and twenty others.

entries.lat: In Sýria sanctórum Mártyrum Macárii et Juliáni.
entries.eng: In Syria, the holy martyrs Macarius and Julian.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Anicéti Cómitis, et Photíni fratris, cum áliis plúribus, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Count Anicete, his brother Photinus, and many others.

entries.lat: Falériæ, in Túscia, pássio sanctórum Graciliáni, et Felicíssimæ Vírginis, quorum pro fídei confessióne ora lapídibus primo contúsa sunt; dehinc ambo, gládio percússi, optátam martýrii palmam suscepérunt.
entries.eng: At Civita Castellana, in Tuscany, the holy martyr Gracilian and the Virgin Felicissima. Because they confessed the faith, their mouths were first bruised with stones, and then they were smitten with the sword, and so received that palm of martyrdom which they had desired.

entries.lat: Medioláni deposítio sancti Eusébii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Eusebius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Herculáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, holy Herculanus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ beáti Hippólyti Mártyris, qui pro confessiónis glória, sub Valeriáno Imperatóre, post ália torménta, ligátis pédibus ad colla indomitórum equórum, per carduétum et tríbulos crudéliter tractus est, ac, toto córpore laceráto, emísit spíritum. Passi sunt étiam eódem die beáta Concórdia, ejus nutrix, quæ ante ipsum, plumbátis cæsa, migrávit ad Dóminum; et álii decem et novem de domo sua, qui extra portam Tiburtínam decolláti sunt, et, una cum ipso, in agro Veráno sepúlti.
entries.eng: Upon the same day there suffered his nurse, the blessed Concordia, who was beaten to death with scourges loaded with lead, and passed away.

entries.lat: Apud Forum Syllæ natális sancti Cassiáni Mártyris, qui cum adoráre idóla noluísset, ídeo, vocátis a persecutóre púeris, quibus exósus docéndo factus fúerat, data est eis facúltas eum periméndi; quorum quanto infírmior erat manus, tanto graviórem martýrii pœnam, diláta morte, faciébat.
entries.eng: At Imola, the holy martyr Cassian. When he refused to worship idols the persecutors called for the boys to whom he had become hateful while teaching them, and gave them permission to kill him, and the weaker their hands were the greater were his sufferings through the delay of death.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sancti Cassiáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Todi, under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Cassian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Burgis, in Hispánia, sanctárum Centóllæ et Hélenæ Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Burgos, in Spain, the holy martyrs Centolla and Helen.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Máximi Abbátis, doctrína et cathólicæ veritátis zelo insígnis; qui, cum advérsus Monothelítas strénue decertáret, ab hærético Imperatóre Constánte, præcísis mánibus ac lingua, in Chersonésum relegátus est, ibíque, glória confessiónis clarus, spíritum Deo réddidit. Tunc étiam duo Anastásii, qui ejus erant discípuli, aliíque plures divérsa torménta et dura exsília sunt expérti.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy monk Maximus, famous for his teaching and zeal for Catholic truth. He vigorously contended against the Monothelites, and the heretical Emperor Constans cut away his hands and tongue, and banished him to the Crimea, where he gave up the ghost. At the same time the two Anastasii, his disciples, and many others, suffered diverse torments and were sent into hard banishments.

entries.lat: Fritesláriæ, in Germánia, sancti Wigbérti, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Germany, the holy Confessor Wigbert the Priest.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Joánnis Berchmans, scholástici e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris, vitæ innocéntia et religiósæ disciplínæ custódia præclári; cui Leo Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, cǽlitum Sanctórum honóres decrévit.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy John Berchmans, a scholastic of the Society of Jesus, illustrious for the innocency of his life and his observance of the discipline of his Institute, to whom the supreme Pontiff Leo XIII decreed the honours paid to the Saints in heaven.

entries.lat: Pictávis, in Gállia, sanctæ Radegúndis Regínæ, cujus vita miráculis et virtútibus cláruit.
entries.eng: At Poitiers, the holy Queen Radegundis, whose life was famous for miracles and graces.

entries.lat: Vigília Assumptiónis beátæ Maríæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: The Vigil of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

entries.lat: Romæ natális beáti Eusébii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui, ab Ariáno Imperatóre Constántio, ob cathólicæ fídei defensiónem, in quodam domus suæ cubiculo inclúsus, ibi, cum menses septem in oratióne constánter perseverásset, dormitiónem accépit. Ipsíus autem corpus collegérunt Gregórius et Orósius Presbýteri, et in cœmetério Callísti, via Appia, sepeliérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Priest Eusebius. On account of his defence of the Catholic faith the Arian Emperor Constantius caused him to be imprisoned in a bedchamber in his own house, where he lived for seven months, continuing instant in prayer, and then fell asleep. His body was taken by the Priests Gregory and Orosius and buried in the cemetery of Callistus, upon the Appian Way.

entries.lat: Apaméæ, in Sýria, sancti Marcélli, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum Jovis delúbrum diruísset, a furéntibus Gentílibus occísus est.
entries.eng: At Apamea, in Syria, the holy martyr Marcellus, Bishop who was destroying a shrine of Jupiter when he was slain by the infuriated Gentiles.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sancti Callísti, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Todi, the holy martyr Callistus, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Illýrico sancti Ursícii Mártyris, qui, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre et Aristíde Prǽside, post multa et divérsa torménta, pro Christi nómine, gládio cæsus est.
entries.eng: In Illyricum, under the Emperor Maximian and the President Aristides, the holy martyr Ursicius, who was beheaded for Christ's name's sake after many and diverse torments.

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Demétrii Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyr Demetrius.

entries.lat: In Ægína ínsula sanctæ Athanásiæ Víduæ, monástica observántia et miraculórum dono illústris.
entries.eng: In the island of Jegima, in the Grecian Archipelago, the holy widow Athanasia, famous for her monastic observance and her power of working miracles.

entries.lat: Assúmptio sanctíssimæ Dei Genetrícis Vírginis Maríæ.
entries.eng: The Assumption of the most holy Virgin Mary, Mother of God.

entries.lat: Cracóviæ, in Polónia, natális sancti Hyacínthi, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, quem Clemens Octávus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ipsíus autem festum sextodécimo Kaléndas Septémbris celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Cracow, in Poland, the birthday of the holy Confessor Hyacinth, of the Order of Preachers, whom the Sovereign Pontiff Clement VIII enrolled among the Saints. His feast is kept on the 17th day of August.

entries.lat: Apud Albam Regálem, in Pannónia, item natális sancti Stéphani, Regis Hungarórum et Confessóris; qui, divínis virtútibus exornátus, primus Húngaros ad Christi fidem convértit, et a Deípara Vírgine, ipso die Assumptiónis suæ, in cælum recéptus fuit. Ejus vero festívitas quarto Nonas Septémbris, quo die munitíssima Budæ arx, sancti Regis ope, ab exércitu Christiáno strénue recuperáta fuit, potíssimum recólitur, ex dispositióne Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi.
entries.eng: At Alba, in Pannonia, in the year 1038,] holy Stephen, King of Hungary, whose feast is kept upon the 2nd day of September.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, sancti Tharsícii Acolythi, quem Pagáni, cum inveníssent Córporis Christi Sacraménta portántem, cœpérunt disquírere quid géreret. At ipse, indígnum júdicans porcis pródere margarítas, támdiu ab illis mactátus est fústibus et lapídibus, donec exhaláret spíritum; et, revolúto ejus córpore, sacrílegi discussóres nihil Sacramentorum Christi in occísi mánibus aut in vestibus invenerunt. Christiáni autem collegerunt Mártyris corpus, et in cœmetério Callísti honorífice sepeliérunt.
entries.eng: The pagans found him bearing the Sacraments of the Body of Christ, and began to ask him what he was carrying, but he deemed it unseemly to produce pearls before swine, and they maltreated him so with sticks and stones that he gave up the ghost. When they sacrilegiously searched his body, they did not find any trace of the Sacraments of Christ either in his hands or among his clothes, but the Christians took up the body of the martyr and buried it honourably in the cemetery of Callistus.

entries.lat: Tagáste, in Africa, sancti Alípii Epíscopi, qui beáti Augustíni olim discípulus, póstea in conversióne sócius, in múnere pastoráli colléga, et in certamínibus advérsus hæréticos commílito strénuus, ac demum in cælésti glória consors fuit.
entries.eng: At Tagaste, in Africa, the holy Alypius, Bishop first the disciple of blessed Augustine, then his companion in his conversion, his comrade in his work as a shepherd of souls, his brave fellow-soldier in his contendings against the heretics, and now a sharer in his glory in heaven.

entries.lat: Suessíone, in Gálliis, sancti Arnúlphi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Soissons, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Arnulf, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Stanislái Kostka; Polóni, novítii e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris; qui, consummátus in brevi, per angélicam vitæ innocéntiam explévit témpora multa, et a Benedícto Décimo tértio, Pontífice Máximo, in Sanctórum album relátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Polish Confessor Stanislaus Kostka, of the Society of Jesus, who was made perfect in a little while and finished the work of many years in angelic innocency of life, and whose name the Supreme Pontiff Benedict XIII enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Sancti Jóachim, patris immaculátæ Vírginis Genetrícis Dei Maríæ, Confessóris, cujus dies natális refértur tertiodécimo Kaléndas Aprílis.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Joachim, father of the immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God, whose birthday is recorded on the 20th day of March.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Titi Diáconi, qui, Urbe a Gothis occupáta, pecúnias paupéribus distríbuens, a Tribúno bárbaro jussus est occídi.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Deacon Titus, who, when the City was occupied by the Goths, while distributing money to the poor, was ordered to be slain by a barbarian Tribune.

entries.lat: Nicǽæ, in Bithýnia, sancti Diomédis médici, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, pro Christi fide cæsus gládio, martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: At Nice, in Bithynia, the holy physician Diomede, who in the persecution under Diocletian was for Christ's faith's sake slain with the sword, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sanctórum trigínta trium Mártyrum.
entries.eng: In Palestine, thirty-three holy Martyrs.

entries.lat: Ferentíni, in Hérnicis, sancti Ambrósii Centuriónis, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, váriis modis cruciátus, et novíssime, cum per ignem illǽsus transísset, demérsus in aquam, edúctus est in refrigérium.
entries.eng: At Ferentino, in Latium, the holy centurion Ambrose, who in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian was tortured in diverse ways, and when he had passed unhurt through the fire was sunk in water, and so entered into rest.

entries.lat: Medioláni deposítio sancti Simpliciáni Epíscopi, sanctórum Ambrósii et Augustíni testimónio célebris.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Simplician, Bishop famed through the testimony of holy Ambrose and Augustine.

entries.lat: Antisiodóri sancti Eleuthérii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Auxerre, holy Eleutherius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Arsácii Confessóris, qui, sub Licínio persecutóre, milítia relícta, solitáriam vitam ducens, tantis virtútibus cláruit, ut et dǽmones expulísse et orándo interemísse ingéntem dracónem legátur; dénique, futúram civitátis cladem prænúntians, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy Confessor Arsacius. Under the persecutor Licinius he deserted from the army, and took to the life of a hermit, wherein he shone with such graces that it is written that he cast out devils and by his prayers killed a huge dragon. At length he foretold the sack which was coming upon the city, and gave up his soul to God in prayer.

entries.lat: Apud Montem Pessulánum, in Gállia Narbonénsi, deposítio beáti Rochi Confessóris, qui multas Itáliæ urbes signo Crucis a morbo epidémiæ liberávit. Ipsíus corpus Venétias póstea translátum, et in Ecclésia, ejus nómine consecráta, honorificentíssime cónditum fuit.
entries.eng: At Montpellier, in Languedoc, the blessed Confessor Roch, who by the sign of the Cross delivered many cities of Italy from the plague. His body hath been taken to Venice, and buried with great honour in the church consecrated in his name.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Serénæ, uxóris quondam Diocletiáni Augústi.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Serena, once the wife of the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Sancti Hyacínthi, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, qui décimo octávo Kaléndas Septémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Hyacinth, of the Order of Preachers, who fell asleep in the Lord on the 15th day of August.

entries.lat: Carthágine sanctórum Mártyrum Liberáti Abbátis, Bonifátii Diáconi, Servi et Rústici Subdiaconórum, Rogáti et Séptimi Monachórum, et Máximi púeri; qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Hunneríco Rege, pro confessióne cathólicæ fídei et pro unici Baptismátis defensióne, váriis et inaudítis supplíciis exagitáti, demum super ligna, quibus concremándi erant, clavis confíxi, et, cum ignis sǽpius accénsus fuísset ac divínitus semper exstínctus, Regis jussu remórum véctibus percússi, et, comminútis cérebris, enecáti, speciósum cursum certáminis sui, coronánte Dómino, perfecérunt.
entries.eng: At Carthage, in Africa, the holy martyrs Liberatus the Abbot, Boniface the Deacon, Servus and Rusticus the Sub-Deacons, the monks Rogatus and Septimus, and the boy Maximus. In the persecution by the Vandals under King Hunneric, they were put to diverse and unheard-of tortures, on account of their confession of the Catholic faith and their defence of one baptism at last they were nailed to the wood upon which they were to be burnt, and the fire was several times kindled but by the power of God always extinguished. Then the king commanded to beat in their heads with the handles of oars, and so they finished the lovely course of their fight, and were crowned by the Lord.

entries.lat: In Acháia sancti Myrónis, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre et Antípatre Prǽside, Cýzici, post multa torménta, cápite truncátus est.
entries.eng: In Achaia, the holy martyr Myron, a Priest, who was beheaded at Cyzicus, after many torments, under the President Antipater, in the time of the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, natális sancti Mamántis Mártyris, qui, sanctórum Theódoti et Rufínæ Mártyrum fílius, longum a puerítia ad senectútem usque martýrium duxit, et tandem, imperánte Aureliáno, sub Alexándro Prǽside, illud felíciter consummávit; quem sancti Patres Basilíus et Gregórius Nazianzénus summis láudibus celebrárunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Mamas, who endured one long martyrdom from his childhood to his old age, and at last happily finished it under the President Alexander in the reign of the Emperor Aurelian. The holy fathers Basil and Gregory of Nazianzus highly extol him.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Stratónis, Philíppi et Eutychiáni; qui, damnáti ad béstias et nil læsi, per ignem martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Straton, Philip, and Eutychian. They were condemned to the beasts, but as these left them unhurt they finished their testimony by fire.

entries.lat: Ptolemáide, in Palæstína, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, ejúsque soróris Juliánæ Vírginis; qui ambo, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre, cum in Christi confessióne permanérent immóbiles, jussi sunt váriis et diríssimis torméntis afflígi ac tandem cápite obtruncári.
entries.eng: At Ptolemais, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Paul and Juliana his sister, who suffered under the Emperor Valerian.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Eusébii Papæ.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Pope Eusebius.

entries.lat: Interámnæ sancti Anastásii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Terni, the holy Confessor Anastasius, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Monte Falco, in Umbria, sanctæ Claræ, Moniális ex Ordine Eremitárum sancti Augustíni, Vírginis; in cujus viscéribus renováta Domínicæ passiónis mystéria fidéles, máxima cum devotióne, venerántur. Eam Leo Décimus tértius, Summus Póntifex, sanctárum Vírginum albo adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Montefalco, in Umbria, the holy Virgin Clare, a Nun of the Order of Hermits of St. Augustine, in whose heart the faithful venerate with the greatest devotion the mysteries of the Lord's Passion renewed. Pope Leo XIII enrolled her among the holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Prænéste natális sancti Agapíti Mártyris, qui cum esset annórum quíndecim, et amóre Christi fervéret, jussu Aureliáni Imperatóris tentus, ac primo nervis crudis diutíssime cæsus, deínde sub Antíocho Præfécto gravióra supplícia passus; exínde cum ex præcépto Imperatóris leónibus objicerétur, et mínime læsus esset, gládio ministrórum coronándus percútitur.
entries.eng: At Palestrina, Italy, the holy martyr Agapitus,; he was fifteen years of age, and hot with the love of Christ. He was tried by command of the Emperor Aurelian, and was first scourged for a very long time with raw thongs, afterwards he suffered worse under the Prefect Antiochus. By command of the Emperor he was thrown to lions, but as these hurt him not at all the servants smote him with the sword, and so he went to be crowned.

entries.lat: Romæ beatórum Joánnis et Crispi Presbyterórum, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni multa Sanctórum córpora officiosíssime sepeliérunt, quorum méritis et ipsi póstmodum sociáti, gáudia vitæ ætérnæ meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the blessed Priests John and Crispus. During the persecution under Diocletian they busied themselves in burying many bodies of the Saints, with whom they themselves were afterward made fellows, and gained the gladness of life eternal.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Hermæ, Serapiónis et Polyǽni, qui per angústa, saxósa et áspera loca raptáti, ánimas Deo reddidérunt.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyrs Hermas, Serapion, and Polysenus, who were dragged through strait, rocky, and rough places until they gave up their souls to God.

entries.lat: In Illýrico sanctórum Mártyrum Flori et Lauri artis lapicidínæ, qui, consúmptis martýrio eórum magístris Próculo et Máximo, sub Licióne Prǽside post multa torménta in profúndum púteum sunt demérsi.
entries.eng: In Illyricum, the holy martyrs Florus and Laurus, quarrymen, who, after their masters Proculus and Maximus had been martyred, were put to many torments, under the President Licion, and then thrown into a well.

entries.lat: Myræ in Lýcia sanctórum Mártyrum Leónis et Juliánæ.
entries.eng: At Myra, in Lycia, the holy martyrs Leo and Juliana.

entries.lat: Metis in Gállia sancti Firmíni Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Metz, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Firmin, Bishop.

entries.lat: Romæ via Lavicána sanctæ Hélenæ matris Constantíni Magni piíssimi Imperatóris, qui primus Ecclésiæ tuéndæ atque amplificándæ exémplum céteris Princípibus prǽbuit.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, holy Helen, mother of that most religious Emperor Constantine the Great, who was the first to leave to other princes the pattern of how to protect and spread the Church.

entries.lat: Cadómi, in Gállia, sancti Joánnis Eudes Confessóris, Missionárii Apostólici, Fundatóris Congregatiónis Presbyterórum Jesu et Maríæ necnon Ordinis Moniálium Dóminæ Nostræ a Caritáte, et promotóris litúrgici cultus erga Sacratíssima Christi ejúsque Genitrícis Corda; quem Pius Papa Undécimus fastis Sanctórum adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Caen, in France, the holy Confessor John Eudes, Apostolic Missionary, Founder of the Congregation of the Priests of Jesus and Mary and of the Order of Nuns of Our Lady of Charity, and promoter of the liturgical worship of the Most Sacred Hearts of Christ and of his Mother; whom Pope Pius XI enrolled in the calendar of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ Sancti Júlii, Senatóris et Mártyris; qui, Vitéllio Júdici tráditus et ab eo in cárcerem trusus, támdiu, jubénte Cómmodo Imperatóre, fústibus cæsus est, donec emítteret spíritum. Ipsíus autem corpus in cœmetério Calepódii via Aurélia, sepúltum fuit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Julius. He was a Senator who was denounced to the judge Vitellius and by him committed to prison, thereafter by command of the Emperor Cornmodus he was beaten with cudgels until he gave up the ghost. His body was buried in the cemetery of Calipodius, upon the Aurelian Way.

entries.lat: Anágniæ sancti Magni Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Décii necátus est.
entries.eng: At Anagni, the holy martyr Magnus, Bishop who was slain in the persecution under Decius.

entries.lat: In Cilícia natális sancti Andréæ Tribúni et Sociórum mílitum; qui, victória de Persis divínitus adépta, ad fidem Christi convérsi, et hoc nómine accusáti, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre in angústiis Tauri montis ab exércitu Seléuci Prǽsidis trucidáti sunt.
entries.eng: In Cilicia, the holy soldiers Andrew the Tribune, and his companions. After obtaining a victory over the Persians by God's help, they were turned to the faith of Christ, and being accused therefore, they were massacred by the army of the President Seleucus in the straits of the Taurus mountain, under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sancti Timóthei Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni sub Urbáno Prǽside, post multa superáta supplícia, lento igne combústus est. Passi sunt étiam ibídem Thecla et Agápius: illa feris expósita, eárum déntibus laniáta transívit ad Sponsum: Agápius vero, plúrima torménta perpéssus, ad majóra certámina fuit dilátus.
entries.eng: In Palestine, the holy martyr Timothy, who after overcoming many torments was burnt at a slow fire, under Urban the President, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian. There suffered there at the same place Thecla and Agapius.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Xysti Tértii, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope and Confessor Sixtus III.

entries.lat: Apud castrum Bríncolam, in Província, deposítio sancti Ludovíci, ex Ordine Minórum, Epíscopi Tolosáni, vitæ sanctitáte et miráculis clari; cujus corpus, inde Massíliam translátum, in Ecclésia Fratrum Minórum honorífice cónditum fuit, ac póstea Valéntiam, in Hispánia, devéctum est, atque in cathedráli Ecclésia collocátum.
entries.eng: At the castle of Brignoles, in Provence, the burial of the holy Louis, of the Order of Friars Minor, Bishop of Toulouse, famous for the holiness of his life and his miracles; his body was translated thence to Marseilles and honourably laid in the Church of the Friars Minor, and was afterwards carried to Valencia, in Spain, and placed in the cathedral Church.

entries.lat: In pago Sigistérico, in Gállia, beáti Donáti, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui, ab ipsis usque infántiæ rudiméntis mira Dei grátia prǽditus, anachoréticam vitam multis annis exégit, et miraculórum glória clarus migrávit ad Christum.
entries.eng: At Sisteron, in Gaul, the blessed Confessor Donatus, a Priest, who had been from his very infancy marvellously gifted with the grace of God. He lived as a hermit for many years, and passed away to be with Christ, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: In território Bituricénsi sancti Mariáni Confessóris, cujus virtútes et mirácula beátus Gregórius, Turonénsis Epíscopus, magnis láudibus celebravit.
entries.eng: In Berry, the holy Confessor Marian.

entries.lat: Mántuæ sancti Rufíni Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Mantua, the holy Confessor Rufinus.

entries.lat: Norimbérgæ sancti Sebáldi Eremítæ, virtútibus et miráculis præclári, qui Sanctórum catálogo a Martíno Papa Quinto adjéctus est.
entries.eng: At Nuremberg, the holy Hermit Sebald, renowned for virtues and miracles, who was added to the catalogue of the Saints by Pope Martin V.

entries.lat: In território Lingoniénsi deposítio sancti Bernárdi, primi Clarævallénsis Abbátis, vita, doctrína et miráculis gloriósi, quem Pius Octávus Póntifex Máximus universális Ecclésiæ Doctórem declarávit, et confirmávit.
entries.eng: In the country of Langres, holy Bernard, the first Abbot of Clairvaux, glorious for his life, his teaching, and his miracles, whom the Supreme Pontiff Pius VIII declared and confirmed a Doctor of the Universal Church.

entries.lat: Romæ deposítio sancti Pii décimi, Papæ et Confessóris, fídei integritáte et ecclesiásticæ libertátis propugnatóris invícti, religionísque zelo insígnis, cujus festum tértio Nonas Septémbris recólitur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the burial of the holy Pope and Confessor Pius X, an unconquered defender of the integrity of the faith and of the liberty of the Church, and eminent for his zeal for religion; whose feast is kept on the 3rd day of September.

entries.lat: Apud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Manétii Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis; qui, eídem hymnos dicens, expiravit. Ipsíus autem ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Monte Senario, in the Diocese of Florence, the blessed Confessor Manetto one of the Seven Founders of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who died as he was reciting hymns to her.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sancti Samuélis Prophetæ, cujus sancta ossa (ut beátus Hierónymus scribit) Arcádius Augústus Constantinópolim tránstulit, et prope Séptimum collocávit.
entries.eng: In Judea, the holy Prophet Samuel, whose sacred bones, as writeth blessed Jerome, were carried to Constantinople by the Emperor Arcadius, and laid near the Hebdomon.

entries.lat: In Cypro sancti Lúcii Senatóris, qui, perspécta constántia Theodóri, Cyrenénsis Epíscopi, in martýrio pósiti, ad Christi fidem est convérsus, et ad eam étiam Digniánum Prǽsidem pertráxit; cum eóque Cyprum proféctus, ibi, cum álios Christiános pro confessióne Dómini coronári vidéret, ultro se ipsum óbtulit, et cápitis obtruncatióne eándem martýrii corónam proméruit.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Senator Lucius. He was turned to the faith of Christ by seeing the constancy with which Theodore, Bishop of Cyrene, underwent martyrdom, and drew the President Dignian to the same belief; they went together to Cyprus, and when he saw other Christians there being crowned for confessing the Lord, he thrust himself forward and gained the same crown of martyrdom by being beheaded.

entries.lat: In Thrácia sanctórum trigínta septem Mártyrum, qui sub Prǽside Apelliáno pro Christi fide, mánibus pedibúsque præcísis, in camínum ardéntem injécti sunt.
entries.eng: In Thrace, thirty-seven holy martyrs, who under the President Apellian, for Christ's faith's sake, had their hands and feet cut off, and were cast into a furnace of fire. Likewise the holy martyrs Severus and Memnon the centurion, who finished their testimony by the same kind of death, and departed to heaven as conquerors.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Sevéri, et Mémnonis Centuriónis; qui, eódem mortis génere consummáti, victóres abiérunt in cælum.
entries.eng: In the same place, the holy Martyrs Severus, and Memnon a Centurion, who, being made perfect by the same kind of death, departed victorious into heaven.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Leovigíldi et Christóphori Monachórum, qui, in Arabum persecutióne pro Christiánæ fídei defensióne in cárcerem conjécti, ac mox, cervícibus abscíssis, igni tráditi, martýrii palmam adépti sunt.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy martyrs Leovigild and Christopher. They were monks who were cast into prison for their defence of the Christian faith in the persecution under the Arabs, and were presently beheaded, and so gained the palm of martyrdom, whereafter their bodies were burnt.

entries.lat: In Hério ínsula sancti Philibérti Abbátis.
entries.eng: In the island of Noirmoutier, the holy Philibert, Abbot.

entries.lat: Romæ beáti Porphýrii, qui fuit homo Dei, qui sanctum Mártyrem Agapítum erudívit in fide et doctrína Christi.
entries.eng: At Rome, blessed Porphyry, a man of God, from whom the holy martyr Agapitus learnt the faith and teaching of Christ.

entries.lat: In castro Cainóne, in Gállia, sancti Máximi Confessóris, qui éxstitit discípulus beáti Martíni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In the castle of Chinon, the holy Confessor Maximus, a disciple of blessed Martin, Bishop.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Joánnæ-Francíscæ Frémiot de Chantal, Víduæ, quæ Ordinis Sanctimoniálium Visitatiónis sanctæ Maríæ fuit Institútrix, cujus natális dies Idibus Decémbris memorátur.
entries.eng: The holy Widow Jane Frances Fremiot de Chantal, who was the Foundress of the Order of Nuns of the Visitation of St. Mary; whose birthday is commemorated on the 13th day of December.

entries.lat: Romæ, in agro Veráno, sanctæ Cyríacæ, Víduæ et Mártyris; quæ, in persecutióne Valeriáni cum se súaque ómnia in Sanctórum ministério impendísset, demum pro Christo martýrium súbiens, vitam quoque ipsam libénter impéndit.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the Veran Field, the holy widow and martyr Cyriaca. In the Valerian persecution she spent herself, and all that she had, in ministering to the saints, and at last suffered martyrdom for Christ, and so willingly spent her life itself.

entries.lat: In território Gavalitáno sancti Priváti, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui passus est in persecutióne Valeriáni et Galliéni.
entries.eng: In the Gevaudan country, the holy martyr Privatus, Bishop who suffered in the persecution under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus.

entries.lat: Salónæ, in Dalmátia, sancti Anastásii Corniculárii, qui, cum vidéret beátum Agapítum constánter torménta perferéntem, convérsus est ad fidem, et, pro confessióne nóminis Christi, jubénte Aureliáno Imperatóre, interémptus, Martyr migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Salona, holy Anastasius, a petty officer in the army, who was converted to the faith by beholding the firmness with which the blessed martyr Agapitus bore all his torments, and who was slain by order of the Emperor Aurelian for confessing Christ's name, and so passed away as a martyr, to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: In Sardínia natális sanctórum Mártyrum Luxórii, Cisélli et Cameríni; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni sub Délphio Prǽside gládio cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Sardinia, the holy martyrs Luxorius, Cisellus, and Camerinus, who were slain with the sword under the President Delphius, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Bonósi et Maximiáni.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Bonosus and Maximian,.

entries.lat: Fundis, in Látio, sancti Patérni Martyris, qui ab Alexandría Romam venit ad Apostolórum memórias; et inde in agrum Fundánum secéssit, atque ibi, cum Mártyrum córpora sepelíret, a Tribúno comprehénsus est, et in vinculis expirávit.
entries.eng: At Fondi, in Latium, the holy martyr Paternus. He had come from Alexandria to Rome to visit the graves of the Apostles, and had gone from Rome to Fondi. He was arrested by a Tribune while he was burying the bodies of martyrs, and died in his chains.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sanctórum Mártyrum Bassæ, et filiórum, id est Thegónii, Agápii et Fidélis; quos, in persecutióne Maximiáni, pia mater exhórtans, martýrio coronátos præmísit ad palmam, et, truncáto cápite, gaudens secúta est cum victória.
entries.eng: At Edessa, the holy Bassa and her sons Theogonius, Agapius, and Faithful, all martyrs. Their loving mother by her exhortations sent them, crowned before her, to receive their palms, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, and then was herself beheaded, and thus joyfully followed them in triumph.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Euprépii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Confessor Euprepius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Item sancti Quadráti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: Likewise, the holy Bishop Quadratus.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Sidónii Epíscopi, doctrína et sanctitáte conspícui.
entries.eng: At Clermont, in France, the holy Bishop Sidonius, famous for learning and holiness.

entries.lat: Senis in Túscia beáti Bernárdi Ptolomǽi Abbátis, Congregatiónis Olivetánæ Fundatóris.
entries.eng: At Siena, in Tuscany, the holy Abbot Bernard Tolomei, Founder of the Congregation of the Olivetans.

entries.lat: Festum Immaculáti Cordis beátæ Vírginis Maríæ.
entries.eng: The Feast of the Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Ostiénsi, natális sancti Timóthei Mártyris, qui, a Præfécto Urbis Tarquínio tentus, et longa cárceris custódia macerátus, et, cum sacrificáre idólis noluísset, tértio cæsus et gravíssimis supplíciis attrectátus, ad últimum decollátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Ostian Way, the holy martyr Timothy. He was tried by Tarquinius, Prefect of the city, and suffered a long imprisonment, and forasmuch as he would not sacrifice to idols, he was then hided, put to horrid tortures, and at length beheaded.

entries.lat: In Portu Románo sancti Hippólyti Epíscopi, eruditióne claríssimi, qui, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, ob præcláram fídei confessiónem, mánibus pedibúsque ligátis in altam fóveam, aquis plenam, præcipitátus, martýrii palmam accépit; cujus corpus apud eúndem locum a Christiánis sepúltum fuit.
entries.eng: At Porto, holy Hippolytus, Bishop a man of eminent learning, who received the palm of martyrdom under the Emperor Alexander, on account of his illustrious confession of the faith, for the which he had his hands and feet tied and was cast into a deep pit full of water his body was buried by the Christians at the same place.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Symphoriáni Mártyris, qui, témpore Aureliáni Imperatóris, cum sacrificáre nollet idólis, primo verbéribus afflíctus est, deínde cárceri mancipátus; atque ad últimum, cæso cápite, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy martyr Symphorian, who finished his testimony in the time of the Emperor Aurelian, because he would not sacrifice unto idols, being first beaten, then imprisoned, and in the end beheaded.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, natális sancti Philíppi Benítii, Confessóris, Florentíni, qui Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis éxstitit propagátor et exímiæ humilitátis vir; atque a Cleménte Décimo, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum número adscríptus est. Ipsíus autem festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Todi, in Umbria, the birthday of the holy Confessor Philip Benizi, a Florentine, who was the propagator of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary and a man of singular humility; he was enrolled among the number of the Saints by Pope Clement X. His feast, however, is kept on the following day.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Antoníni Mártyris, qui, cum se Christiánum líbera voce faterétur, senténtia capitáli a Júdice Vitéllio damnátus est, et a Rufino Presbýtero via Aurélia sepúltus.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Antoninus. He openly professed himself a Christian, and therefore was sentenced to death by Vitellius the judge, and was buried upon the Aurelian Way.

entries.lat: Tarsi, in Cilícia, commemorátio sanctórum Athanásii, Epíscopi et Mártyris, Anthúsæ, nóbilis féminæ, quam ipse baptizáverat, ac simul Charísii et Neóphyti Mártyrum, ejúsdem Anthúsæ servórum, qui sub Valeriáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
