entries.eng: At Tarsus, under the Emperor Valerian, the holy martyrs Athanasius, Bishop the noble lady Anthusa, whom he had baptized, and two of her slaves,.

entries.lat: In Portu Románo sanctórum Mártyrum Martiális, Saturníni, Epictéti, Maprílis et Felícis, cum Sóciis eórum.
entries.eng: Likewise at Porto, the holy martyrs Martial, Saturninus, Epictetus, Maprilis, and Felix, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctórum Agathoníci, Zótici et Sociórum Mártyrum, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre et Eutólmio Prǽside.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, under the Emperor Maximian and the President Eutholomius, the holy martyrs Agathonicus, Zoticus, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Mauri et Sociórum.
entries.eng: At Reims, the holy martyrs Maurus and his Companions.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctórum Mártyrum Fabriciáni et Philibérti.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyrs Fabrician and Philibert.

entries.lat: Papíæ sancti Gunifórti Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy martyr Gunifort.

entries.lat: Sancti Philíppi Benítii Confessóris, qui Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis éxstitit propagátor, ac prídie hujus diéi migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Todi, the holy Confessor Philip Benizi of Florence, a man of eminent lowliness, who greatly spread the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and whose name Pope Clement X added to the list of those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Apud Ostia Tiberína sanctórum Mártyrum Quiríaci Epíscopi, Máximi Presbýteri, Archelái Diáconi, et Sociórum, qui sub Ulpiáno Præfécto, témpore Alexándri, passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Ostia, the holy martyrs Quiriacus, Bishop the Priest Maximus, the Deacon Archelaus, and their Companions, who suffered under the Prefect Ulpian, in the time of the Emperor Alexander.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Restitúti, Donáti, Valeriáni et Fructuósæ, cum áliis duódecim; qui præclaríssimo confessiónis honóre coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Restitutus, Donatus, Valerian, and Fructuosa, along with twelve others, who were crowned with the glory of an illustrious testimony.

entries.lat: Ægǽæ, in Cilícia, sanctórum Mártyrum fratrum Cláudii, Astérii et Neónis, qui, Christiánæ religiónis a novérca accusáti, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Lýsia Prǽside, post acérba torménta cruci sunt affíxi, in qua victóres cum Christo triumphárunt. Passæ sunt post eos Donvína et Theonílla.
entries.eng: At Aegaea, in Cilicia, the holy brethren Claudius, Asterius, and Neon, all martyrs. They were accused of Christianity by their step-mother, in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, and were first severely tortured, and then crucified, under the President Lysias, and so triumphed as conquerors with Christ. After them suffered Donvina and Theonilla.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, natális sanctórum Timóthei et Apollináris, qui, ibídem consummáto martýrio, cæléstia regna meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Reims, in Gaul, the holy martyrs Timothy and Apolinaris, who there finished their testimony and gained the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Minérvi, et Eleazári cum fíliis octo.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy martyrs Minervus and Eleazar, with eight children.

entries.lat: Item sancti Luppi Mártyris, qui, ex servíli conditióne, Christi libertáte donátus, martýrii quoque coróna dignátus est.
entries.eng: Likewise, the holy martyr Luppus, who was a slave, but free in Christ, and received also the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis sancti Zachǽi Epíscopi, qui, quartus a beáto Jacóbo Apóstolo, Hierosolymitánam Ecclésiam rexit.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, holy Zachaeus, the fourth Bishop from the blessed Apostle James who governed that Church.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Theónæ, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy Confessor Theonas, Pope.

entries.lat: Uticæ, in Africa, beáti Victóris Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Utica, in Africa, blessed Victor, Bishop.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Flaviáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Autun, holy Flavian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Sancti Bartholomǽi Apóstoli, qui Christi Evangélium in India prædicávit; inde in majórem Arméniam proféctus, ibi, cum plúrimos ad fidem convertísset, vivus a bárbaris decoriátus est, atque, Astýagis Regis jussu, cápitis decollatióne martýrium complévit. Ipsíus sacrum corpus, primo ad Líparam ínsulam, deínde Benevéntum, postrémo Romam ad Tiberínam translátum ínsulam, ibi pia fidélium veneratióne honorátur.
entries.eng: The holy Apostle Bartholomew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in India, whence he went into the greater Armenia, where, when he had turned many to the faith, he was flayed alive by the barbarians, and beheaded by order of King Astyages, and so finished his testimony. His sacred body was first taken to the island of Lipari, then to Benevento, and lastly to Rome, to the island in the Tiber, where it is devoutly reverenced by the veneration of the faithful.

entries.lat: Lima, in Perúvia, natális sanctæ Rosæ a sancta María, Vírginis, e tértio Ordine sancti Domínici. Ejus vero festívitas tértio Kaléndas Septémbris celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Lima, in Peru, the birthday of the holy Virgin Rose of St. Mary, of the Third Order of St. Dominic. Her feast, however, is kept on the 30th day of August.

entries.lat: Népete sancti Ptolomǽi Epíscopi, qui fuit discípulus beáti Petri Apóstoli; atque, ab eo missus in Túsciam ad prædicándum Evangélium, in eádem civitáte gloriósus Christi Martyr occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Nepi, the holy Bishop Ptolemy, who was a disciple of blessed Peter the Apostle; being sent by him into Tuscany to preach the Gospel, he died in that same city a glorious Martyr of Christ.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Eutýchii, qui fuit discípulus beáti Joánnis Evangelístæ; atque, ob Evangélii prædicatiónem in multis regiónibus cárceres, vérbera et ignes perpéssus, in pace tandem quiévit.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Eutychius, a disciple of the blessed Evangelist John. For preaching the Gospel he suffered in many countries imprisonment, stripes, and fire but at length fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Népete sancti Románi, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui, cum esset sancti Ptolomǽi discípulus, fuit étiam in passióne sócius.
entries.eng: At Nepi, the holy Bishop Ptolemy, a disciple of the blessed Apostle Peter, by whom he was sent into Tuscany to preach the Gospel, and in that city fell a glorious martyr of Christ and in the same place holy Romanus, Bishop of the same city, who, as he had been the disciple of holy Ptolemy was also his comrade in his last testimony and sufferings.

entries.lat: Carthágine sanctórum trecentórum Mártyrum, témpore Valeriáni et Galliéni. Hi Mártyres magnánimi, inter ália supplícia, cum Præses fornácem calcáriam accéndi jussísset, et, in præséntia ejus, prunas cum thure exhibéri, atque illis dixísset: « Elígite e duóbus unum, aut thura super his carbónibus offérte Jovi, aut in calcem demergímini », fide armáti, Christum Dei Fílium confiténtes, ictu rapidíssimo se injecérunt in ignem, et inter calcis vapóres in púlverem sunt redácti; ex quo candidátus ille beatórum exércitus appellári Massa cándida méruit.
entries.eng: At Carthage, three hundred holy martyrs, in the time of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, among other torments applied to them the President caused a limekiln to be lighted, and producing some hot embers and incense said to them, now choose one of two things, either offer this incense to Jupiter upon these coals, or be thrown into that lime. Then they, being armed with faith, and confessing that Christ is the Son of God, threw themselves in a twinkling into the kiln, where they were burnt to powder among the lime, whence this white-robed army of the blessed has gained the name of the White Lump.

entries.lat: In Isáuria sancti Tatiónis Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Urbáno Prǽside, gládio cæsus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: In Isauria, the holy martyr Tation, who was slain with the sword under President Urban, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Item sancti Geórgii Limniótæ Mónachi, qui, cum ímpium Leónem Imperatórem, quod sacras Imágines frángeret Sanctorúmque relíquias combúreret, reprehendísset, hanc ob causam, ejus jussu mánibus abscíssis et cápite incénso, Martyr migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: Also, the holy monk George, surnamed Limniotes. He rebuked the wicked Emperor Leo for breaking the holy images and burning the relics of the Saints, whereupon the Emperor commanded his hands to be cut off, and his head to be set on fire, and so as a martyr he passed away to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: Apud Ostia Tiberína sanctæ Aureæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, saxo ad collum ligáto, in mare demérsa est. Ipsíus autem corpus, ejéctum ad littus, beátus Nonnus sepelívit.
entries.eng: At Ostia, the holy Virgin and martyr Aurea, who was cast into the sea with a stone tied about her neck. Her body was washed up upon the shore, and was buried by blessed Nonnus.

entries.lat: Rotómagi sancti Audoéni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rouen, the holy Bishop and Confessor Ouen.

entries.lat: Nivérnis, in Gállia, sancti Patrícii Abbátis.
entries.eng: At Nevers, the holy Abbot Patrick.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sanctæ Joánnæ Antídæ Thouret, Vírginis, Institúti Sorórum a Caritáte Fundatrícis, quam Pius Papa Undécimus in album sanctárum Vírginum rétulit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy Virgin Jane Antida Thouret, Foundress of the Institute of the Sisters of Charity, whom Pope Pius XI enrolled among the holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Massíliæ, in Gállia, sanctæ Æmíliæ de Vialár, Vírginis, Fundatrícis Institúti Sorórum a sancto Joseph ab Apparitióne, fortitudine, patiéntia et caritáte insígnis, quam Pius Duodécimus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctárum númerum rétulit.
entries.eng: At Marseilles, in France, the holy Virgin Emily de Vialar, Foundress of the Institute of the Sisters of St. Joseph of the Apparition, eminent for fortitude, patience and charity, whom Pope Pius XII enrolled among the number of the Saints.

entries.lat: Valéntiæ, in Hispánia, natális sanctæ Marfæ Michaélæ, Vírginis, Fundatrícis Congregatiónis Ancillárum a Sanctíssimo Sacraménto et Caritátis, patiéndi stúdio ac desidério ánimas Deo lucrándi inflammátæ, quam Pius Papa Undécimus sanctis Virgínibus accénsuit.
entries.eng: At Valencia, in Spain, the birthday of the holy Virgin Mary Michaela, Foundress of the Congregation of the Handmaids of the Most Blessed Sacrament and of Charity, inflamed with a zeal for suffering and a desire of winning souls to God, whom Pope Pius XI numbered among the holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Apud Cartháginem sancti Ludovíci Noni, Regis Francórum et Confessóris, vitæ sanctitáte ac miraculórum glória præclári, cujus ossa póstmodum Lutétiam Parisiórum sunt reláta.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy Confessor Louis, King of France, famous for the holiness of his life and for the glory of his miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Joséphi Calasánctii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, vitæ innocéntia et miráculis illústris; qui, ad erudiéndam pietáte ac lítteris juventútem, Ordinem Clericórum Regulárium Páuperum Matris Dei Scholárum Piárum fundávit. Eum Pius Duodécimus, Póntifex Máximus, ómnium Scholárum populárium christianárum ubíque exsisténtium cæléstem apud Deum Patrónum constítuit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas sexto Kaléndas Septémbris recólitur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the birthday of the holy Priest and Confessor Joseph Calasanctius, illustrious for the innocence of his life and for miracles; who, for the instruction of youth in piety and letters, founded the Order of Poor Clerks Regular of the Mother of God of the Pious Schools. Pope Pius XII appointed him the heavenly Patron before God of all popular Christian Schools wherever they exist. His feast, however, is kept on the 27th day of August.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Eusébii, Pontiáni, Vincéntii et Peregríni; qui, sub Cómmodo Imperatóre, primum in equúleo leváti, nervis quoque disténti, ac deínde fústibus cæsi sunt, flammis circa eórum látera appósitis; et, cum in laude Christi fidelíssime permanérent, plumbátis usque ad emissiónem spíritus sunt mactáti.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Eusebius, Pontian, Vincent, and Peregrin. Under the Emperor Commodus they were first racked, then stretched with thongs, and afterwards cudgelled, their sides were burnt, and as they remained faithful in the praise of Christ they were hided to death with scourges loaded with lead.

entries.lat: Romæ prætérea natális beáti Nemésii Diáconi, et fíliæ Lucíllæ Vírginis; qui, cum de fide Christi flecti nequáquam possent, decolláti sunt, jubénte Valeriáno Imperatóre. Ipsórum córpora, a beáto Stéphano Papa sepúlta, deínde a beáto Xysto Secúndo via Appia, prídie Kaléndas Novémbris, honéstius tumuláta, Gregórius Quintus in Diaconíam sanctæ Maríæ Novæ tránstulit, una cum sanctis Symphrónio, Olýmpio Tribúno, hujúsque uxóre Exsupéria et Theodúlo fílio; qui omnes, Symphrónii ópera convérsi et ab eódem sancto Stéphano baptizáti, martýrio coronáti fúerant. Eadem Sanctórum córpora, Gregório Décimo tértio Summo Pontífice, ibídem invénta, sub altári ejúsdem Ecclésiæ honorificéntius collocáta sunt sexto Idus Decémbris.
entries.eng: At Rome also, the birthday of blessed Nemesius the Deacon, and of his daughter, the Virgin Lucilla, who, since they could in no wise be turned from the faith of Christ, were beheaded by order of the Emperor Valerian. Their bodies, buried by blessed Pope Stephen, and afterwards more honourably entombed by blessed Sixtus II on the Appian Way on the 31st day of October, were translated by Gregory V to the Deaconry of St. Mary the New, together with the holy Symphronius, Olympius the Tribune, his wife Exsuperia and his son Theodulus; all of whom, converted by the labours of Symphronius and baptized by the same holy Stephen, had been crowned with martyrdom. The same bodies of the Saints, being found in that place under the Sovereign Pontiff Gregory XIII, were placed with greater honour beneath the altar of the same Church on the 8th day of December.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Genésii Mártyris, qui, primum sub Gentilitáte mimus, cum in theátro, spectánte Diocletiáno Imperatóre, Mystériis Christianórum illudéret, repénte, inspirátus a Deo, convérsus est ad fidem et baptizátus. Mox, Imperatóris jussu, fústibus crudelíssime cæsus, deínde suspénsus in equúleo, et ungulárum diutíssima laceratióne vexátus, lampádibus étiam adústus est; ac tandem, cum in fide Christi persísteret, dicens: « Non est Rex præter Christum, pro quo si míllies occídar, ipsum mihi de ore, ipsum mihi de corde auférre non potéritis », martýrii palmam obtruncatióne cápitis proméruit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyr Genesius while he was a Gentile he was a player. One while in the theatre, in the presence of the Emperor Diocletian, he was making a mock at the mysteries of the Christians, when the spirit of God came upon him, and he was suddenly turned to the faith, and baptized. The Emperor caused him to be very cruelly beaten with cudgels, then racked, and tormented for a long time by being torn with hooks, and burned with lamps. He stood firm in Christ's faith, saying: there is no King but Christ, and if I should be slain for Him a thousand times, ye cannot take Him either out of my mouth or out of my heart. In the end he was beheaded, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Areláte, in Gállia, beáti item Genésii, qui, cum ímpia edícta, quibus Christiáni puniri jubebántur, exceptóris offício fungens, nollet excípere, et, projéctis in públicum tábulis, se Christiánum esse testarétur, comprehénsus et decollátus est, atque ita martýrii glóriam, próprio cruóre baptizátus, accépit.
entries.eng: At Arles, in Gaul, blessed Genesius. He was a registrar who refused to register the wicked edicts which commanded the punishment of Christians, but publicly cast away his tables and professed himself a Christian; for this cause he was taken and beheaded, and being so baptized in his own blood, gained the glory of martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Sýria sancti Juliáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Syria, the holy martyr Julian.

entries.lat: Tarracóne, in Hispánia, sancti Magíni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Taragona, the holy martyr Maginus.

entries.lat: Itálicæ, in Hispánia, sancti Gerúntii Epíscopi, qui, Apostolórum témpore, Evangélium in ea província prædicávit, et, post multos labóres, in cárcere quiévit.
entries.eng: At Italica, in Spain, the holy Bishop Gerontius, who in the time of the Apostles preached the Gospel in that province, and after many labours went to his rest in prison.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Mennæ Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Mennas,Bishop.

entries.lat: Trajécti sancti Gregórii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Utrecht, holy Gregory, Bishop.

entries.lat: Apud Montem Falíscum, in Etrúria, sancti Thomæ Confessóris, qui Herfordiénsis Ecclésiæ, in Anglia, Epíscopus éxstitit.
entries.eng: At Montefiascone, in Tuscany, the holy Confessor Thomas, who was Bishop of the Church of Hereford, in England.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sanctæ Patríciæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Naples, the holy Virgin Patricia,.

entries.lat: Sancti Zephyríni, Papæ et Mártyris, cujus dies natális tertiodécimo Kaléndas Januárii recensétur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope and martyr Zephyrinus.

entries.lat: Cardónæ, in Hispánia, tránsitus sancti Raymúndi Nonnáti, Cardinális et Confessóris, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, vitæ sanctitáte et miráculis clari. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur prídie Kaléndas Septémbris.
entries.eng: At Cardona, in Spain, the passing of the holy Cardinal and Confessor Raymund Nonnatus, of the Order of Blessed Mary of Mercy for the ransom of captives, famous for the holiness of his life and for miracles. His feast, however, is kept on the 31st day of August.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Irenǽi et Abúndii, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, eo quod corpus beátæ Concórdiæ, in cloácam projéctum, leváverant, in eándem cloácam demérsi fuérunt; quorum córpora, a Justíno Presbýtero inde extrácta, in crypta, juxta beátum Lauréntium, sepúlta sunt.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyrs Irenaeus and Abundius. In the persecution under the Emperor Valerian they took the body of blessed Concordia out of the sewer into which it had been thrown, and for so doing were themselves drowned in the same sewer. Justin the Priest drew their bodies thence, and buried them under the ground near blessed Lawrence.

entries.lat: Apud Albintimélium, Ligúriæ civitátem, sancti Secúndi Mártyris, viri spectábilis et Ducis ex legióne Thebæórum.
entries.eng: At Ventimiglia, a city of Liguria, the holy martyr Secundus, a man of rank and a Captain of the Theban legion.

entries.lat: Bérgomi sancti Alexándri Mártyris, qui, et ipse unus ex eádem legióne, cum nomen Dómini Jesu Christi constantíssime faterétur, cápitis abscissióne martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: At Bergamo, the holy martyr Alexander, who was also a soldier of the same legion. As he constantly confessed the name of the Lord Jesus Christ he was beheaded, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Apud Marsos sanctórum Simplícii, et ejus filiórum Constántii et Victoriáni, qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, várie primum excruciáti, tum demum, secúris ictu percússi, martýrii corónam adépti sunt.
entries.eng: Among the tribe of the Marsi, holy Simplicius and his sons, Constantius and Victorian, who were first put to diverse torments, under the Emperor Antoninus, and then beheaded, and so gained the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sancti Hadriáni, e Probo Cǽsare progéniti, qui, Licínio persecutiónem in Christiános commótam éxprobrans, ab eódem jussus est occídi. Ipsíus corpus Domítius, Byzántii Epíscopus, ejus pátruus, in ipsíus civitátis subúrbio cui nomen Argyrópolis, sepelívit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, holy Hadrian, the son of the Emperor Probus. He blamed the persecution stirred up by Licinius against the Christians, and was therefore by him ordered to be slain his body was buried at Argyropolis by his uncle Domitius, Bishop of Byzantium.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sancti Victóris Mártyris, qui pro Christi fide, a Mauris occísus, martýrii coróna donátus est.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyr Victor, who was slain by the Moors for Christ's faith's sake, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Rufíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy Confessor Rufinus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Pistórii, in Túscia, sancti Felícis, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Pistoia, the holy Priest and Confessor Felix.

entries.lat: Pódii, in diœcési Pictaviénsi, sanctæ Joánnæ-Elísabeth Bichier des Ages, Vírginis, Congregatiónis Filiárum a Cruce una cum sancto Andréa Hubérto Fournet Fundatrícis, jugi mortificatióne et vitæ innocéntia claræ, quam Pius Papa Duodécimus sanctárum Vírginum fastis accénsuit.
entries.eng: At Le Puy, in the diocese of Poitiers, the holy Virgin Jane Elizabeth Bichier des Ages, Foundress, together with holy Andrew Hubert Fournet, of the Congregation of the Daughters of the Cross, famous for her unceasing mortification and the innocence of her life, whom Pope Pius XII numbered in the calendar of the holy Virgins.

entries.lat: Sancti Joséphi Calasánctii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis Clericórum Regulárium Páuperum Matris Dei Scholárum Piárum éxstitit Fundátor, atque octávo Kaléndas Septémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Joseph, famous for the innocency of his life and for his miracles, who founded the Order of Poor Regular Clerks of the Mother of God of the Pious Schools, for the teaching of godliness and good learning unto children.

entries.lat: Poténtiæ, in Lucánia, pássio sanctórum Aróntii, Honoráti, Fortunáti et Sabiniáni; qui, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ fílii, a Valeriáno Júdice, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, jussi sunt capitálem subíre senténtiam. Eórum tamen ac reliquórum ex duódecim frátribus festum Kaléndis Septémbris celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Potenza, in Lucania, the passion of the holy Arontius, Honoratus, Fortunatus and Sabinian, who, being the sons of the holy Boniface and Thecla, were ordered by the Judge Valerian, under the Emperor Maximian, to undergo the sentence of death. Their feast, however, together with that of the rest of the twelve brothers, is kept on the 1st day of September.

entries.lat: Bérgomi sancti Narni, qui, a beáto Bárnaba baptizátus, primus ab ipso ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus est.
entries.eng: At Bergamo, holy Narnus, who was baptized by blessed Barnabas, and was ordained by him to be the first Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Cápuæ natális sancti Rufi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum esset patríciæ dignitátis, a beáto Apollináre, sancti Petri discípulo, cum univérsa família baptizátus est.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy martyr Rufus, Bishop A man of Patrician family, who was baptized along with all his house by blessed Apollinaris, the disciple of holy Peter.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Rufi et Carpóphori, qui sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno passi sunt.
entries.eng: Likewise at Capua, the holy martyrs Rufus and Carpophorus, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.

entries.lat: Tomis, in Ponto, sanctórum Mártyrum Marcellíni Tribúni, et uxóris Mannéæ, ac filiórum Joánnis, Serapiónis et Petri.
entries.eng: At Tomi, in Pontus, the holy martyrs Marcellinus the Tribune, Mannea his wife, and their sons, John, Serapion, and Peter.

entries.lat: Apud Leontínos, in Sicília, sanctæ Euthalíæ Vírginis, quæ, cum esset Christiána, ad cæléstem Sponsum, a fratre suo Sermiliáno cæsa gládio, migrávit.
entries.eng: At Lentini, in Sicily, the holy Virgin Euthalia, who was slain by her own brother Sermilian with the sword, because she was a Christian, and so passed away to Christ the Bridegroom.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sanctæ Anthúsæ junióris, quæ ob Christi fidem, in púteum mersa, martýrium sumpsit.
entries.eng: On the same day holy Anthusa the younger received martyrdom by being drowned in a well for Christ's faith's sake.

entries.lat: Areláte, in Gállia, sancti Cæsárii Epíscopi, miræ sanctitátis et pietátis viri.
entries.eng: At Arles, holy Caesarius, Bishop of that city, a man of marvellous holiness and godliness.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Syágrii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy Confessor Syagrius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Papíæ sancti Joánnis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy Bishop John.

entries.lat: Ilérdæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Licérii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Lerida, in Spain, holy Licerius, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Thebáide sancti Póemenis Anachorétæ.
entries.eng: In the Thebaid, the holy Hermit Poemon.

entries.lat: Apud Septempedános, in Picéno, sanctæ Margarítæ Víduæ.
entries.eng: At San Severino, in the March of Ancona, the holy widow Margaret.

entries.lat: Hippóne Régio, in Africa, natális sancti Augustíni Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris exímii, qui, beáti Ambrósii Epíscopi ópera ad cathólicam fidem convérsus et baptizátus, eam advérsus Manichǽos aliósque hæréticos acérrimus propugnátor deféndit, multísque áliis pro Ecclésia Dei perfúnctus labóribus, ad prǽmia migrávit in cælum. Ejus relíquiæ, primo de sua civitáte propter bárbaros in Sardíniam advéctæ, et póstea a Rege Longobardórum Luitprándo Papíam translátæ, ibi honorífice cónditæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Hippo, in Africa, the holy Augustine, Bishop of that city, the eminent Doctor of the Church. He was converted to the Catholic faith, and baptized by blessed Bishop Ambrose. He was the stalwart defender of the faith against the Manicheans and other heretics, and, after manifold toil for the Church of God, he passed away to be rewarded in heaven. His body was first brought from his own city to Sardinia, on account of the barbarians, and afterwards by Luitprand, King of the Lombards, -to Pavia, where it is honourably buried.

entries.lat: Romæ item natális sancti Hermétis, viri illústris, qui (ut in Actis beáti Alexándri Papæ légitur), prius carceráli custódiæ mancipátus, deínde, cum áliis plúrimis, gládio cædénte, martýrium complévit, sub Aureliáno Júdice.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Hermes, a man of illustrious worldly station, who, as is written in the acts of the blessed Pope Alexander, was first committed to prison, and then slain with the sword along with many others, under the judge Aurelian.

entries.lat: Venúsiæ, in Apúlia, pássio sanctórum Septimíni, Januárii et Felícis, qui, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ fílii, a Valeriáno Júdice, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, jussi sunt decollári. Ipsórum tamen ac reliquórum ex duódecim frátribus festívitas agitur Kaléndis Septémbris.
entries.eng: At Venosa, in Apulia, the passion of the holy Septiminus, Januarius and Felix, who, being the sons of the holy Boniface and Thecla, were ordered by the Judge Valerian, under the Emperor Maximian, to be beheaded. Their feast, however, together with that of the rest of the twelve brothers, is kept on the 1st day of September.

entries.lat: Briváte, apud Arvérnos, item pássio sancti Juliáni Mártyris, qui, cum esset beáti Ferréoli Tribúni comes et in hábitu militári occúlte Christo servíret, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, a milítibus tentus est, et, desécto gútture, morte horríbili necátus.
entries.eng: At Brioude, in Auvergne, the holy martyr Julian he was a comrade of the blessed Tribune Ferreolus, and secretly served Christ as a soldier but in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian he was tried by the other soldiers, who horribly murdered him by cutting his throat.

entries.lat: Constántiæ, in Germánia, sancti Pelágii Mártyris, qui sub Numeriáno Imperatóre et Evilásio Júdice, cápite amputátus, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Constance, the holy martyr Pelagius, who received his crown under the Emperor Numerian and the judge Evilasius.

entries.lat: Salérni sanctórum Mártyrum Fortunáti, Caji et Anthis; qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Leóntio Procónsule, decolláti sunt.
entries.eng: At Salerno, the holy martyrs Fortunatus, Caius, and Anthes, who were beheaded under the Emperor Diocletian and the Proconsul Leontius.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Alexándri Epíscopi, gloriósi senis; ob cujus oratiónem Arius, divíno judício damnátus, crépuit médius, et effúsa sunt víscera ejus.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Alexander, Bishop that glorious old man by the power of whose prayer the judgement of God smote Arius so that he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.

entries.lat: Apud Sántonas, in Gállia, sancti Viviáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Saintes, the holy Confessor Vivian, Bishop.

entries.lat: Item sancti Móysis Æthíopis, qui, ex insígni latróne insígnis Anachorétæ, multos latrónes convértit et secum duxit ad monastérium.
entries.eng: Likewise, the holy Moses the Ethiopian, who from a notorious robber became a famous Anchorite, converted many robbers and led them with him to the monastery.

entries.lat: Decollátio sancti Joánnis Baptístæ, quem Heródes circa festum Paschæ decollári præcépit. Ipsíus tamen memória solémniter hac die cólitur, qua venerándum ejus caput secúndo invéntum fuit; quod, póstea Romam translátum, in Ecclésia sancti Silvéstri, ad Campum Mártium, summa pópuli devotióne asservátur.
entries.eng: The Beheading of St. John the Baptist, whom Herod ordered to be beheaded about the feast of the Pasch. His memory, however, is solemnly kept on this day, on which his venerable head was found the second time; it was afterwards translated to Rome, and is preserved with the greatest devotion of the people in the Church of St. Silvester, near the Campus Martius.

entries.lat: Romæ, in monte Aventíno, natális sanctæ Sabínæ Mártyris, quæ sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, gládio percússa, martýrii palmam adépta est.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Aventine Mount, the holy martyr Sabina, who under the Emperor Hadrian was smitten with the sword, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Veliniáni, in confínibus Apúliæ, pássio sanctórum Vitális, Satóris et Repósiti; qui, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ fílii, a Valeriáno Júdice, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, capitálem senténtiam pertulérunt. Eórum tamen ac ceterórum ex duódecim frátribus memória Kaléndis Septémbris recólitur.
entries.eng: At Velleiano, on the borders of Apulia, the passion of the holy Vitalis, Sator and Repositus, who, being the sons of the holy Boniface and Thecla, suffered the sentence of death from the Judge Valerian, under the Emperor Maximian. Their memory, however, together with that of the rest of the twelve brothers, is kept on the 1st day of September.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Cándidæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; cujus corpus beátus Paschális Primus Papa in Ecclésiam sanctæ Praxédis tránstulit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Candida, whose body Pope Paschal I. brought to the Church of St. Praxedes.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Hypátii, Asiáni Epíscopi, et Andréæ Presbýteri; qui ambo, ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum, sub Leóne Isáurico, barba pice íllita atque incénsa, et cute cápitis extrácta, juguláti sunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyrs Hypatius, a Bishop of Asia, and Andrew, a Priest, who were killed, under the Emperor Leo the Isaurian, for the reverence due to the holy images, after their beards had been filled with pitch and set on fire, and their heads flayed.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Nicǽæ et Pauli.
entries.eng: At Antioch, in Syria, the holy martyrs Nicasas and Paul.

entries.lat: Metis, in Gállia, sancti Adélphi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Metz, the holy Confessor Adelphus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum deposítio sancti Mederíci Presbýteri.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy Priest Mederic.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sancti Euthýmii Románi, qui, cum uxóre et Crescéntio fílio persecutiónem Diocletiáni fúgiens, ad eam urbem secéssit, et ibi póstmodum quiévit in Dómino.
entries.eng: At Perugia, holy Euthymius, a Roman, who fled thither along with his wife and Crescentius his son, to escape the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and there fell asleep in the Lord.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Sebbi Regis.
entries.eng: In England, the holy King Sebbi.

entries.lat: Apud Sírmium natális sanctæ Basíllæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Smyrna, holy Basilla.

entries.lat: In pago Tricassíno sanctæ Sabínæ Vírginis, virtútibus et miráculis gloriósæ.
entries.eng: In the country of Troyes, the holy Virgin Sabina, glorious for her graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Rosæ a sancta María, e tértio Ordine sancti Domínici, Vírginis; cujus dies natális nono Kaléndas Septémbris recensétur.
entries.eng: The holy Virgin Rose of St. Mary, of the Third Order of St. Dominic, whose birthday is recorded on the 24th day of August.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Ostiénsi, pássio beáti Felícis Presbýteri, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Imperatóribus. Hic, post equúlei vexatiónem, data senténtia, cum ducerétur ad decollándum, óbvius ei fuit quidam Christiánus, qui, dum se Christiánum esse sponte profiterétur, mox cum eódem páriter decollátus est; cujus nomen ignorántes, Christiáni Adáuctum eum appellavérunt, eo quod sancto Felíci auctus sit ad corónam.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Ostian Way, under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the blessed Priest Felix. After being racked he was sentenced to be beheaded as he was being led to execution he was met by some man who of his own accord professed himself a Christian, and was accordingly forthwith beheaded along with him. The Christians never knew the name of this other, and they accordingly always spoke of him as him who was added, that is, added to the company of the holy martyr Felix in winning of the crown.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sanctæ Gaudéntiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, cum áliis tribus.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Gaudentia, with three others.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Suffetulánæ, in Africa, beatórum sexagínta Mártyrum, qui furóre Gentílium cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Sfaitla, in Africa, sixty blessed martyrs, who were slain by the fury of the Gentiles.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Bonónii Abbátis.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy Abbot Bononius.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Pammáchii Presbýteri, qui fuit doctrína et sanctitáte conspícuus.
entries.eng: At Rome, also the holy Priest Pammachius, who was eminent for his teaching and holiness.

entries.lat: Adruméti, in Africa, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ, qui beatórum duódecim filiórum Mártyrum paréntes fuérunt.
entries.eng: At Susa, also in Africa, holy Boniface and Thecla, who were the parents of twelve sons, all blessed martyrs.

entries.lat: Thessalonícæ sancti Fantíni Confessóris, qui, multa a Saracénis perpéssus, atque e monastério, in quo abstinéntia víxerat admirábili, expúlsus, demum, cum plúrimos ad viam salútis perduxísset, in senectúte bona quiévit.
entries.eng: At Thessalonica, the holy Confessor Fantinus. He suffered much from the Saracens, and was thrust out of the monastery wherein he had lived in marvellous austerity. He led many into the path of salvation, and at length fell asleep in a good old age.

entries.lat: In território Meldénsi sancti Fiácrii Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Meaux, the holy Confessor Fiacre,.

entries.lat: Trebis, in Látio, sancti Petri Confessóris, qui, multis clarus virtútibus et miráculis, ibídem migrávit ad Dóminum, et honorífice cólitur.
entries.eng: At Trevi, in Latium, the holy Confessor Peter, who, famous for many virtues and miracles, there departed to the Lord, and is honourably venerated.

entries.lat: Sancti Raymúndi Nonnáti, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, Cardinális et Confessóris; cujus dies natális séptimo Kaléndas Septémbris recólitur.
entries.eng: The holy Cardinal and Confessor Raymund Nonnatus, of the Order of Blessed Mary of Mercy for the ransom of captives, whose birthday is kept on the 26th day of August.

entries.lat: Apud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Bonajúnctæ Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis; qui, de Passióne Domínica ad fratres verba fáciens, in manus Dómini trádidit spíritum. Ipsíus autem ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Monte Senario, hard by Florence, the blessed Confessor Bonajuncta one of the Seven Founders of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who gave up the ghost into the Lord's hands as he was discoursing to his brethren concerning the same Lord's Passion.

entries.lat: Tréviris item natális sancti Paulíni Epíscopi, qui, témpore Ariánæ infestatiónis, ab Ariáno Imperatóre Constántio ob cathólicam fidem relegátus exsílio, et extra Christiánum nomen usque ad mortem mutándo exsília fatigátus, tandem, apud Phrýgiam defúnctus, beátæ passiónis corónam percépit a Dómino.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Paulinus, Bishop In the time of the persecution under the Arians he was exiled by Constantius the Arian Emperor on account of his Catholic belief, and when he had been wearied out by changing the places of his exile, even beyond the bounds of Christendom, he at length died in Phrygia, and received a crown from the Lord in reward of his blessed sufferings.

entries.lat: Tránsaquis, ad lacum Fúcinum, in Marsis, natális quoque sanctórum Mártyrum Cæsídii Presbýteri, et Sociórum; qui martýrio coronáti sunt in persecutióne Maximíni.
entries.eng: At Trasacco, on the Lake of Celano, the holy martyrs Caesidius the Priest and his Companions, who were crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Maximin.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Robustiáni et Marci.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Robustian and Mark.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Theódoti, Rufínæ et Ammiæ; quorum duo primi paréntes fuérunt sancti Mamántis Mártyris, quem Rufína in cárcere péperit, et Ammia educávit.
entries.eng: At Cassarea, in Cappadocia, holy Theodotus, Rufina, and Ammia. Theodotus and Rufina were the father and mother of the holy martyr Mamas. Rufina gave him birth in prison, and Ammia was his nurse.

entries.lat: Antisiodóri sancti Optáti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Auxerre, the holy Confessor Optatus, Bishop.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Aidáni, Epíscopi Lindisfarnénsis; cujus ánimam, cum sanctus Cuthbértus, cujus memória tertiodécimo Kaléndas Aprílis cólitur, tunc óvium pastor, in cælum ferri vidísset, relíctis óvibus, factus est Mónachus.
entries.eng: In England, holy Aidan, Bishop of Lindisfarne. Holy Cuthbert, who was then a shepherd lad, saw the soul of Aidan carried up into heaven, and he thereupon left his sheep and became a monk.

entries.lat: Apud Nuscum sancti Amáti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Nusco, holy Amatus, Bishop.

entries.lat: Athénis sancti Aristídis, fide et sapiéntia claríssimi, qui Hadriáno Príncipi egrégium de religióne Christiána volúmen óbtulit, nostri dogmátis cóntinens ratiónem; et quod Christus Jesus solus esset Deus, præsénte ipso Imperatóre, luculentíssime perorávit.
entries.eng: At Athens, the holy Aristides, a man illustrious for his faith and wisdom, who offered to the Emperor Hadrian a book upon the Christian religion, containing an exposition of our doctrine, and delivered a most able discourse in the presence of the said Emperor, to prove that Christ Jesus is the only God.

entries.lat: In província Narbonénsi sancti Ægídii, Abbátis et Confessóris, cujus nómine est appellátum óppidum, quod póstea crevit in loco, ubi ipse monastérium eréxerat et mortális vitæ cursum absólverat.
entries.eng: In the province of Narbonne, the holy Abbot and Confessor Giles.

entries.lat: Sentiáni, in fínibus Apúliæ, pássio sanctórum Donáti et altérius Felícis; qui, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ fílii, a Valeriáno Júdice, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, jussi sunt, post vária torménta, cápite præcídi hodiérna die, in qua et festívitas aliórum ex duódecim frátribus, quorum natális respectívis diébus ágitur, institúta est celebrári. Ipsórum vero duódecim fratrum córpora Benevéntum póstea transláta sunt, ibíque honorífice asserváta.
entries.eng: At Benevento, the Twelve Holy Brethren Martyrs.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sanctórum Jósue et Gedeónis.
entries.eng: In Palestine, holy Joshua and holy Gideon.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis beátæ Annæ Prophetíssæ, cujus sanctitátem sermo Evangélicus prodit.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the blessed Prophetess Anna, whose holiness is set forth in the words of the Gospel.

entries.lat: Cápuæ, via Aquária, sancti Prisci Mártyris, qui fuit unus de antíquis Christi discípulis.
entries.eng: At Capua, upon the Aquarian Way, the holy martyr Priscus, who was one of the original disciples of Christ.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sancti Terentiáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, Lætiáni Procónsulis jussu, equúleo et scorpiónibus cruciátus est, ac demum, abscíssa lingua, cápitis damnátus martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: At Todi, in Umbria, the holy martyr Terentian, Bishop who was racked and tormented with armed whips by command of the Pro-Consul Laetian, under the Emperor Hadrian, whereafter his tongue was cut out and he was condemned to be beheaded, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Heracléæ, in Thrácia, sancti Ammónis Diáconi, et sanctárum quadragínta Vírginum, quas ille erudívit in fide, et, sub Licínio tyránno, ad martýrii glóriam secum perdúxit.
entries.eng: At Heraclea, the holy Deacon Ammon, and the forty holy Virgins to whom he taught the faith, and whom he led with him, under the tyrant Licinius, to the glory of martyrdom.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctórum Mártyrum Vincéntii et Læti.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyrs Vincent and Laetus.

entries.lat: Populónii, in Túscia, sancti Réguli Mártyris, qui ex Africa illuc venit, ibíque, sub Tótila, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Piombino, in Tuscany, the holy martyr Regulus, who was martyred there under Totila, on his landing from Africa.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Prisci Epíscopi, qui unus fuit ex illis Sacerdótibus, qui, in persecutióne Wandalórum, ob fidem cathólicam várie afflícti et vetústæ navi impósiti, ex Africa ad Campániæ líttora pervenérunt, et Christiánam religiónem, in iis locis dispérsi diversísque Ecclésiis præfécti, mirífice propagárunt. Ipsíus autem fuérunt sócii Castrénsis, cujus dies natális tértio Idus Februárii recólitur, Támmarus, Rósius, Heráclius, Secundínus, Adjútor, Marcus, Augústus, Elpídius, Cánion et Vindónius.
entries.eng: At Capua, holy Priscus, Bishop He was one of those Priests who, in the persecution under the Vandals, were diversely afflicted for the Catholic faith's sake, and were put on board an old ship wherein they came from Africa to the shores of Campania, and being scattered about those parts, and set over diverse churches, they wonderfully spread abroad the Christian religion. His Companions were Castrensis, Tammatrus, Rosius, Heraclius, Secundinus, Adjutor, Mark, Augustus, Elpidius, Canion, and Vindonius.

entries.lat: Apud Sénonas beáti Lupi, Epíscopi et Confessóris; de quo refértur quod quadam die, præsénte Clero, dum sacris altáribus adstáret, lapsa est cǽlitus gemma in ejus cálicem sanctum.
entries.eng: At Sens, the blessed Bishop and Confessor Lupus, of whom it is related that on a certain day, in the presence of the Clergy, as he stood at the holy altar, a jewel fell from heaven into his holy chalice.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, sancti Xysti, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: At Rheims, in France, the holy Sixtus, who was the first Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Apud Cenómanos, in Gállia, sancti Victórii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Le Mans, holy Victorius, Bishop.

entries.lat: Apud Aquínum sancti Constántii Epíscopi, prophetíæ dono multísque virtútibus clari.
entries.eng: At Aquino, holy Constantius, Bishop famous for the gift of prophecy, and for many other graces.

entries.lat: Ad Aquas Duras, in Constantiénsi Germániæ território, sanctæ Verénæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Baden, in the country of Constance, the holy Virgin Verena.

entries.lat: Sancti Stéphani, Regis Hungarórum et Confessóris; qui décimo octávo Kaléndas Septémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Stephen, King of the Hungarians, who fell asleep in the Lord on the 15th day of August.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Máximæ Mártyris, quæ, simul cum sancto Ansáno Christum conféssa, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, dum fústibus cǽditur, réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Maxima, who confessed Christ along with holy Ansanus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and was beaten to death with cudgels.

entries.lat: Pámiæ, in Gállia, sancti Antoníni Mártyris, cujus relíquiæ apud Ecclésiam Palentínam, in Hispánia, magna veneratióne asservántur.
entries.eng: At Pamiers, in Gaul, (in the second century,) the holy martyr Antonine, whose relics are kept with great reverence in the church of Palencia in Spain.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Diomédis, Juliáni, Philíppi, Eutychiáni, Hesýchii, Leónidæ, Philadélphi, Menalíppi et Pantágapæ; quorum álii igne, álii aqua, ense álii et cruce martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Diomede, Julian, Philip, Eutychian, Hesychius, Leonides, Philadelphus, Menalippus, and Pantagapa, whereof some finished their testimony by fire, some by water, some by the sword, and some by the cross.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Zenónis, atque Concórdii et Theodóri, filiórum ejus.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyrs Zeno and his sons, Concordius and Theodore.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Elpídii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the March of Ancona, (in the fifth century,) at the town called by his name, which rejoices to own his sacred body, the holy Abbot Elpidius.

entries.lat: In Picéno item sancti Elpídii Abbátis, cujus nómine óppidum est appellátum, quod ejus sacrum corpus se possidére congáudet.
entries.eng: Also at Lyon, (in the fifth century,) was born into the better life the holy Confessor Elpidius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In monte Sorácte sancti Nonnósi Abbátis, qui ingéntis molis saxum oratióne sua tránstulit, aliísque miráculis coruscávit.
entries.eng: On Mount Soracte, the holy Abbot Nonnosus, who by his prayer moved a stone of great weight, and was famous.

entries.lat: Eódem die Commemorátio sanctórum Mártyrum germanórum Evódii, Hermógenis et Callístæ; de quibus, in Syracusána Sicíliæ urbe martýrium passis, ágitur étiam séptimo Kaléndas Maji.
entries.eng: On the same day, (at Syracuse,) the holy brethren Evodius and Hermogenes and their sister Callista, all martyrs.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, Translátio sanctórum Justi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, ac Viatóris, qui ejus fúerat miníster; quorum natális dies respectíve prídie Idus Octóbris et duodécimo Kaléndas Novémbris recensétur.
entries.eng: Upon the same day is commemorated at Lyon, in Gaul, (in the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Justus, Bishop (of that see,) a man of wonderful holiness of life, gifted with the spirit of prophecy he resigned his Bishopric, and withdrew himself into the desert of Egypt, along with Viator his Reader. There he led for some years a life bordering upon the life of Angels, and, when the worthy end of his labours came, departed hence to receive a crown of righteousness from the Lord. It was the 14th day of October, but it was upon the 2nd of September that his sacred body was brought to Lyon, along with the bones of his blessed servant Viator.

entries.lat: Sancti Pii Papæ Décimi, cujus natális dies tertiodécimo Kaléndas Septémbris recensétur.
entries.eng: The holy Pope Pius X, whose birthday is recorded on the 20th day of August.

entries.lat: Corínthi natális sanctæ Phœbes, cujus méminit beátus Apóstolus Paulus ad Romános scribens.
entries.eng: At Corinth, holy Phoebe, of whom the blessed Apostle Paul doth make mention in writing unto the Romans.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sanctórum Mártyrum Aristǽi Epíscopi, et Antoníni púeri.
entries.eng: At Capua, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyrs Aristaeus, Bishop (of that see,) and the little lad Antonine.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális sanctórum Mártyrum Aigúlphi, Abbátis Lirinénsis, et Sociórum ipsíus Monachórum, qui, linguis præcísis oculísque effóssis, gládio obtruncáti sunt.
entries.eng: On the same day, the birthday of the holy Martyrs Aigulphus, Abbot of Lerins, and his Companions, Monks, who, after their tongues had been cut out and their eyes plucked out, were slain with the sword.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Zenónis et Charitónis; quorum alter in lebétem liquáti plumbi conjéctus est, alter in ignis fornácem immíssus.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Zeno and Chariton, whereof the one was cast into a vessel of molten lead and the other into a fiery furnace.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sancti Sándali Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy martyr Sandalus, (who suffered in the persecution under the same Emperor Diocletian.) Upon the same day, (in the seventh century,) the holy martyrs Aigulph, Abbot of Lerins, and the monks his Companions, who had their tongues cut out and their eyes put out, and were beheaded with the sword.

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum, Euphémiæ, Dorótheæ, Theclæ et Erásmæ, quæ, sub Neróne Imperatóre et Sebásto Prǽside, post multa supplícia, gládio cæsæ sunt, et a sancto Hermágora sepúltæ.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, the holy Virgins, Euphemia, Dorothy, Thecla, and Erasma, all martyrs, who, after many torments, were slain with the sword under Nero, and were buried by holy Hermagoras.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctæ Basilíssæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, annos novem nata, cum in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, sub Alexándro Prǽside, vérbera, ignes ac béstias divína virtúte superásset, ipsum Prǽsidem ad Christi fidem convértit, ac tandem extra urbem in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy Virgin and martyr Basilissa, who, at nine years of age, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, by the power of God triumphed over stripes, fire, and wild beasts, under the President Alexander, and gave up her soul in prayer to God.

entries.lat: Tulli, in Gállia, sancti Mansuéti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Toul, in France, the holy Bishop and Confessor Mansuetus.

entries.lat: Medioláni deposítio sancti Auxáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Milan, the burial of the holy Bishop Auxanus.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Simeónis Stylítæ junióris.
entries.eng: At Toul, in Lorraine, (in the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Mansuetus, Bishop (of that see.) At Milan, (in the sixth century,) deceased holy Auxanus, Bishop (of that see.) Upon the same day, (at the end of the sixth century,) the holy Stylite Simeon the Younger.

entries.lat: Romæ Translátio sanctæ Serápiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ passa est quarto Kaléndas Augústi.
entries.eng: At Rome, the Translation of the holy Virgin and Martyr Serapia, who suffered on the 29th day of July.

entries.lat: Item Romæ Ordinátio incomparábilis viri sancti Gregórii Magni in Summum Pontíficem; qui, onus illud subíre coáctus, e sublimióri throno clarióribus sanctitátis radiis in Orbe refúlsit.
entries.eng: At Rome is commemorated the Ordination as Supreme Pontiff of that excellent man holy Gregory the Great; the compulsion which forced that burden upon him caused the rays of his holiness to shine through all the world, all the clearer in that they shone from an higher spot.

entries.lat: In monte Nebo, terræ Moab, sancti Móysis, legislatoris et Prophétæ.
entries.eng: The death of the holy Law-giver and Prophet Moses, upon Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, natális sanctæ Cándidæ, quæ sancto Petro Apóstolo, ad eam urbem veniénti, prima occúrrit, atque, ab eo baptizáta, póstea sancto fine quiévit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Candida, who was the first to meet the holy Apostle Peter when he came to that city. She was baptized by him, and in the end she fell asleep in an holy death. There also, (in the sixth century,) holy Candida, called the Younger, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Marcélli, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Trier, the holy Bishop and Martyr Marcellus.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, natális sanctórum trium puerórum Mártyrum, id est Rufíni, Silváni et Vitálici.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, in Galatia, the three holy children Rufinus, Silvanus, and Vitalicus, all martyrs.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Magni, Casti et Máximi.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Magnus, Castus, and Maximus.

entries.lat: Cabillóne, in Gálliis, sancti Marcélli Mártyris, qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, cum a Prǽside Prisco ad profanum convívium fuísset invitátus, et, hujúsmodi épulas éxsecrans, omnes qui áderant, cur idólis deservírent, líbera increpatióne corríperet, ab eódem Prǽside, inaudíto crudelitátis génere, cíngulo tenus defóssus est in terra; sicque, cum in Dei láudibus tríduo perseverásset, incontaminátum spíritum réddidit.
entries.eng: At Chalons, in Gaul, under the Emperor Antonine, the holy martyr Marcellus he was bidden by Priscus the President to a sinful banquet, and, in his horror at such a feast, he boldly rebuked all them that were there for their serving of idols wherefore the same President, with strange cruelty, caused him to be buried in the earth up to the girdle, where he remained for three days still giving praise to God, and then yielded up to Him his spirit without stain.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Thamélis, ántea idolórum sacerdótis, et Sociórum Mártyrum, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Trier, (in the third century,) the holy martyr Marcellus, Bishop (of that see.) On the same day holy Thamel, who had once been a priest of idols, and his Companions, all martyrs under the Emperor Hadrian.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Theodóri, Oceáni, Ammiáni et Juliáni; qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, disséctis pédibus in ignem conjécti, martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Theodore, Oceanus, Ammian, and Julian, who, under the Emperor Maximian, suffered martyrdom by having their feet cut off, and being then cast into a fire.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Bonifátii Primi, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope and Confessor Boniface I.

entries.lat: Arímini sancti Maríni Diáconi.
entries.eng: At Rimini, (in the fourth century,) the holy Deacon Marinus.

entries.lat: Panórmi natális sanctæ Rosáliæ, Vírginis Panormitánæ, ex régio Cároli Magni sánguine ortæ; quæ, pro Christi amóre, patérnum principátum aulámque profúgit, et, in móntibus ac spelúncis solitária, cæléstem vitam duxit.
entries.eng: At Palermo, the birthday of the holy Virgin Rosalia of Palermo, sprung from the royal blood of Charlemagne, who for the love of Christ fled from her father's principality and court, and led a heavenly life in solitude among the mountains and caves.

entries.lat: Vitérbii Translátio beátæ Rosæ Vírginis, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, témpore Alexándri Papæ Quarti.
entries.eng: At Viterbo, the Translation of the blessed Virgin Rose, of the Third Order of St. Francis, in the time of Pope Alexander IV.

entries.lat: Sancti Lauréntii Justiniáni, primi Patriárchæ Venetiárum et Confessóris, qui pontificálem Cáthedram hac die invítus ascéndit, et sexto Idus Januárii obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: The holy Confessor Laurence Justinian, first Patriarch of Venice, who on this day unwillingly ascended the pontifical Chair, and fell asleep in the Lord on the 8th day of January.

entries.lat: Romæ, in suburbáno, beáti Victoríni, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, sanctitáte et miráculis clarus, sacerdótium Amiternínæ urbis, totíus pópuli electióne, adéptus est. Póstmodum, sub Nerva Trajáno, apud Cutílias, ubi puténtes et sulphúreæ emánant aquæ, cum áliis Dei servis, relegátus, ab Aureliáno Júdice jussus est suspéndi cápite deórsum; idque cum per tríduum pro nómine Christi passus fuísset, tandem, glorióse coronátus, victor migrávit ad Dóminum. Ejus corpus rapuérunt Christiáni, et honorífica sepultúra Amitérni, in Vestínis, condidérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the suburb, the blessed martyr Victorinus, Bishop of Amiternum, (now called after him San Vittorino.) He was famous for holiness and miracles, and was chosen to the see of that city by the voice of all the people thereof. Afterwards, under Nerva-Trajan, he was sent, along with other servants of God, to Cutilia, where there is a pool of stinking sulphurous waters, and where the judge Aurelian ordered him to be hung up with his head downwards this torment he suffered for the space of three days, for Christ's name's sake, and then departed in triumph, gloriously crowned to be ever with the Lord. The Christians carried off his hody, and buried it honourably at Amiternum.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Urbáni, Theodóri, Menedémi, et Sociórum septuagínta septem ex órdine ecclesiástico; qui a Valénte Imperatóre, pro fide cathólica, in navígio impósiti, jussi sunt in mari combúri.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyrs Urban, Theodore, Menedem, and their Companions, seventy-seven in number, of the ecclesiastical state, who under the Emperor Valens, for the Catholic faith's sake, were put on board a ship and burnt at sea.

entries.lat: In Portu Románo pássio sancti Herculáni mílitis, qui, sub Gallo Imperatóre, ob Christi fidem cæsus flagris et cápite obtruncátus est.
entries.eng: At Porto, (in the second century,) the holy martyr Herculan.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sanctórum Mártyrum Quínctii, Arcóntii et Donáti.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy martyrs Quintius, Arcontius, and Donatus.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Rómuli, qui, cum esset Trajáni aulæ prefectus ac sævítiam Imperatóris in Christiános detestarétur, cæsus est virgis, et cápite truncátus.
entries.eng: Upon the same day holy Romulus, Praefect of the Palace to the Emperor Trajan he denounced the cruelty of that Emperor against the Christians, and for that cause was first beaten with rods and then beheaded.

entries.lat: Melitínæ, in Arménia, pássio sanctórum mílitum Eudóxii, Zenónis, Macárii, et Sociórum mille centum et quátuor; qui, cum abjecíssent milítiæ cíngulum, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, pro Christi confessióne necáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Melitina, in Armenia, the holy soldiers Eudoxius, Zeno, Macarius, and their Companions, one thousand one hundred and four in number, who in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian renounced their military service, and were massacred for confessing Christ.

entries.lat: In pago Tarvanénsi, monastério Sithinénsi, in Gállia, sancti Bertíni Abbátis.
entries.eng: At the monastery of Sithiu, in the country of Thérouanne, (in the eighth century,) the holy Abbot Bertin.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, sanctæ Obdúliæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Toledo, the holy Virgin Obdulia.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sancti Zacharíæ Prophétæ, qui, de Chaldǽa senex in patriam revérsus, ibíque defúnctus, juxta Aggǽum Prophétam cónditus jacet.
entries.eng: The Prophet Zachariah, who returned home from Chaldea as an old man, and is buried beside the prophet Haggai.

entries.lat: In Hellespónto sancti Onesíphori, Apostolórum discípuli, cujus méminit sanctus Paulus ad Timótheum scribens. Ipse autem Onesíphorus ibídem, una cum sancto Porphýrio, jussu Hadriáni Procónsulis ácriter verberátus et a ferócibus raptátus equis, spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, were born into the better life: At the Dardanelles, holy Onesiphorus, a disciple of the Apostles, of whom holy Paul maketh mention in writing unto Timothy. By command of the Proconsul Hadrian, holy Onesiphorus and Porphyry were heavily beaten, and drawn by wild horses, and so gave up their souls to God.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Episcopórum Donatiáni, Præsídii, Mansuéti, Germáni et Fúsculi; qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, jussu Ariáni Regis Hunneríci, pro assertióne cathólicæ veritátis, fústibus diríssime cæsi et exsílio elimináti sunt. Inter eos étiam erat Epíscopus, nómine Lætus, strénuus atque doctíssimus vir, qui, post diutúrnos cárceris squalóres, incéndio concremátus est.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy Bishops Donatian, Prassidius, Mansuetus, German, and Fusculus, who in the persecution under the Vandals were, by command of the Arian King Hunneric, because of their assertion of the Catholic truth, heavily beaten with cudgels, and banished. Among them was also a Bishop named Laetus, a man of great activity and learning, who, after suffering a long and foul imprisonment, was burnt.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Fausti Presbýteri, Macárii et Sociórum decem; qui, sub Décio Imperatóre et Valério Prǽside, pro Christi nómine, abscíssis cervícibus, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs the Priest Faustus, Macarius, and ten Companions, who finished their testimony for Christ's name's sake, under the Emperor Decius and the President Valerius, by being beheaded.

entries.lat: In Cappadócia sanctórum Mártyrum Cóttidi Diáconi, Eugénii et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In Cappadocia, the holy martyrs the Deacon Cottidus, Eugenius, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Petrónii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Petronius, Bishop (of that see.) At Rome, the holy Abbot Eleutherius, the servant of God, of whom holy Pope Gregory writeth, that by his prayer and tears he raised a man from the dead.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Eleuthérii Abbátis, qui Dei servus fuit, atque (ut sanctus Gregórius Papa scribit) oratióne et lácrimis mórtuum suscitávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Abbot Eleutherius, who was a servant of God, and (as holy Pope Gregory writes) raised a dead man to life by his prayers and tears.

entries.lat: Trecis, in Gállia, sancti Nemórii Diáconi, et Sociórum Mártyrum, quos Attíla, Rex Hunnórum, interfécit.
entries.eng: At Troyes, the holy martyrs Nemorius the Deacon, and his Companions, who were slain by Attila, King of the Huns.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ natális beáti Joánnis Mártyris, qui, cum vidéret crudélia advérsus Christiános edícta in foro pendére, hinc, fídei ardóre accénsus, injécta manu, illa detráxit atque discérpsit. Cumque hoc relátum esset Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Augústis, in eádem urbe constitútis, ómnia suppliciórum génera in eum experíri jussérunt; quæ vir nobilíssimus tanta vultus ac spíritus alacritáte pértulit, ut ne tristis quidem pro his vidéri potúerit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the blessed martyr John. When he saw the cruel edicts against the Christians hanging up in the market-place, in the heat of his faith he stretched forth his hand, pulled them down, and tore them up. When this was told to the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, who were then in that city, they ordered all the kinds of torment to be tried upon him and the man, right noble as he was, bore this with such a cheerful face and heart that he seemed not even saddened thereby.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Eupsýchii Mártyris, qui, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, accusátus quod Christiánus esset, in cárcerem conjéctus est; et, paulo post inde emíssus, patrimónium statim véndidit, et prétium partim paupéribus, partim accusatóribus, tamquam benefactóribus, distríbuit. Sed, íterum comprehénsus, atque, cum sacrificáre nollet idólis, sævíssime dilaniátus et gládio confóssus, sub Saprítio Júdice martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Eupsychius, who was cast into prison under the Emperor Hadrian on the charge of being a Christian. Being shortly liberated therefrom, he forthwith sold his inheritance, and distributed the price thereof partly unto the poor, and partly unto his accusers, as unto benefactors. He was arrested again, and finished his testimony under the judge Sapritius, being mangled, and pierced with the sword.

entries.lat: Pompejópoli, in Cilícia, sancti Sozóntis Mártyris, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, in ignem injéctus, réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Soli, in Cilicia, the holy martyr Sozon, who under the Emperor Maximian was cast into the fire, and gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ sancti Anastásii Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyr Anastasius.

entries.lat: Apud Aléxiam véterem, in território Augustodunénsi, sanctæ Regínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Procónsule Olýbrio, cárceris et equúlei ac lampadárum afflícta supplíciis, demum, cápite damnáta, migrávit ad Sponsum.
entries.eng: In the country of Autun, the holy Virgin and martyr Regina, who passed away to Christ the Bridegroom under the Proconsul Olybrius, by whose orders she was imprisoned, racked, burnt with lamps, and lastly beheaded.

entries.lat: Aureliánis, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Evórtii Epíscopi, qui, primo Románæ Ecclésiæ Subdiáconus, dehinc divíno múnere per colúmbam designátus est Póntifex præfátæ urbis.
entries.eng: At Orleans, in France, the burial of the holy Bishop Evortius, who, being first a Subdeacon of the Roman Church, was afterwards by a divine favour pointed out by a dove as Bishop of the aforesaid city.

entries.lat: In Gállia sancti Augustális, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In Gaul, the holy Confessor Bishop Augustal.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Pámphili Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Capua, holy Pamphilus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In território Parisiénsi sancti Clodoáldi, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the country of Paris, (in the sixth century,) the holy Priest and Confessor Clodoald (St. Cloud).

entries.lat: Natívitas beatissimæ semper Vírginis Genetrícis Dei Maríæ.
entries.eng: On the morrow we commemorate the birth of the Most Blessed Mary, always a Virgin, Mother of God.

entries.lat: Sancti Hadriáni Mártyris; cujus dies natális quarto Nonas Mártii recensétur, sed festívitas hac die, qua sacrum ejus corpus Romam translátum fuit, potíssime celebrátur.
entries.eng: Upon the same day are commemorated the holy martyr Adrian, and twenty-three others, who finished their testimony at Nicomedia after many sufferings, under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, by having their legs broken, upon the 4th day of March. Their relics were carried by the Christians to Byzantium, where they were buried with reverence and honour, and thence the body of holy Adrian was afterwards brought to Rome, upon the 8th of this month, upon which day the chief feast is kept in his honour.

entries.lat: Valéntiæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, natális sancti Thomæ a Villa Nova, ex Eremitárum sancti Augustíni Ordine, Epíscopi et Confessóris, insígnis propter flagrántem in páuperes caritátem; qui ab Alexándro Papa Séptimo in Sanctórum númerum adscríptus est. Ipsíus autem festum décimo Kaléndas Octóbris celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Valencia, in Spain, holy Thomas of Villanueva, Archbishop (of that city,) famous for his exceeding charity toward the poor. His name was enrolled among those of the Saints by Pope Alexander VII, and we keep his feast upon the 22nd day of this present month of September.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Ammónis, Theóphili, Neotérii et aliórum vigínti duórum.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Ammon, Theophilus, Neoterius, and twenty-two others.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Timóthei et Fausti Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Timothy and Faustus.

entries.lat: Gazæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum fratrum Eusébii, Néstabi et Zenónis; qui, témpore Juliáni Apóstatæ, irruénte in eos turba Gentílium, discérpti atque necáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Gaza, in Palestine, the holy brethren Eusebius, Nestabus, and Zeno, all martyrs, in the time of the Emperor Julian the Apostate.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Néstoris Mártyris, qui sub eódem Juliáno, ab iísdem Gentílibus furéntibus sævíssime cruciátus, emísit spíritum.
entries.eng: A multitude of the Gentiles fell upon them, rent them, and slew them.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Sérgii Primi, Papæ et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope and Confessor Sergius I.

entries.lat: Frisíngæ sancti Corbiniáni, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus. Hic, a sancto Gregório Secúndo Pontífice ordinátus et ad prædicándum Evangélium missus, úberes fructus in Gállia et Germánia rétulit, ac demum, virtútibus et miráculis clarus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: At Frisingen, holy Corbinian, first Bishop of that city. He was ordained and sent forth to preach the Gospel by Pope Gregory II. He bore much fruit in Gaul and in Germany, and at length fell asleep in peace, famous for graces and wonders.

entries.lat: Carthágine nova, in América meridionáli, sancti Petri Claver, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris; qui mira sui abnegatióne et exímia caritáte Nigrítis in servitútem abdúctis, annos ámplius quadragínta, óperam impéndens, tercénta fere eórum míllia Christo sua ipse manu regenerávit; et a Leóne Décimo tértio, Pontífice Máximo, in Sanctórum númerum relátus est, ac dein étiam cæléstis Patrónus peculiáris sacrárum ad Nigrítas Missiónum constitútus et declarátus.
entries.eng: At Cartagena, in South America, the holy Confessor Peter Claver, Priest of the Society of Jesus, who, with wonderful self-denial and singular charity, spending more than forty years in labouring for the Negroes carried away into slavery, with his own hand regenerated in Christ nearly three hundred thousand of them. He was enrolled among the number of the Saints by Pope Leo XIII, and afterwards also appointed and declared the special heavenly Patron of the sacred Missions to the Negroes.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Doróthei et Gorgónii, qui, cum essent apud Diocletiánum Augústum honóres amplíssimos consecúti, et persecutiónem, quam ille Christiánis inferébat, detestaréntur, præsénte eo, jussi sunt primo appéndi, et flagris toto córpore laniári; deínde, viscéribus pelle nudátis, acéto et sale perfúndi, sicque assári in cratícula; atque, ad últimum, láqueo necári. Interjécto autem témpore, beáti Gorgónii corpus Romam delátum fuit, ac via Latína pósitum, et inde ad Basílicam sancti Petri translátum.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Dorotheus and Gorgonius. They stood high at the Court of the Emperor Diocletian. They denounced in his presence the persecution which he was raising against the Christians, wherefore he caused them to be hung up, and their whole bodies torn with lashes, then to have the skin taken off their bowels, to be covered with vinegar and salt, and cooked upon a gridiron, and at the last strangled. In after times the body of the blessed Gorgonius was brought to Rome, and laid first upon the Latin Way, and afterwards in the Basilica of St Peter.

entries.lat: In Sabínis, trigésimo ab Urbe milliário, sanctórum Mártyrum Hyacínthi, Alexándri et Tibúrtii.
entries.eng: In the land of the Sabines, at the 30th milestone from the city of Rome, the holy martyrs Hyacinth, Alexander, and Tiburtius.

entries.lat: Sebáste, in Arménia, sancti Severiáni, qui, cum Licínii Imperatóris esset miles, et Quadragínta Mártyres, in cárcere deténtos frequens visitáret, hinc, jussu Lýsiæ Prǽsidis, saxo ad pedes ligáto suspénsus est, ac, verbéribus cæsus et flagris laniátus, in torméntis réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, under the Emperor Licinius, the holy soldier Severian. He often visited the forty martyrs while they were in prison, whereupon Lysias the President ordered him to be hung up with a stone tied to his feet, and to be beaten and torn with stripes and lashes, under the which torment he gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sancti Stratónis, qui pro Christo, ad duas árbores ligátus atque discérptus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Straton, who, for Christ's sake, was bound to two trees and torn asunder, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Rufíni et Rufiniáni fratrum.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy brethren Rufinus and Rufinian, both martyrs.

entries.lat: In território Tarvanénsi, in Gállia, sancti Audomári Epíscopi.
entries.eng: In the territory of Therouanne, in France, the holy Bishop Omer.

entries.lat: In monastério Cluanénsi, in Hibérnia, sancti Queráni, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Clonmacnoise, in Ireland, the holy Priest and Abbot Kieran.

entries.lat: Tolentíni, in Picéno, deposítio sancti Nicolái Confessóris, ex Ordine Eremitárum sancti Augustíni.
entries.eng: At Tolentino, in the March of Ancona, the holy Confessor Nicholas, of the Order of Hermits of St Augustine.

entries.lat: In Africa natális sanctórum Episcopórum Nemesiáni, Felícis, Lúcii, altérius item Felícis, Littéi, Polyáni, Victóris, Jadéris, Datívi et aliórum; qui, sub Valeriáno et Galliéno, exsurgénte persecutiónis rábie, ad primam confessiónis Christi constántiam gráviter fústibus cæsi sunt, deínde, compédibus vincti et ad fodiénda metálla deputáti, gloriósæ confessiónis agónem consummárunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy Bishops Nemesian, Felix, Lucius, another also named Felix, Litteus, Polyan, Victor, Jader, Dativus, and others, who, when the storm of persecution broke under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, at their first steadfastness in confessing Christ were heavily cudgelled, bound, and condemned to penal servitude in the mines, where they finished their glorious contending.

entries.lat: Leódii, in Bélgio, sancti Theodárdi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui ánimam suam pósuit pro óvibus suis, et miraculórum signis post mortem illúxit.
entries.eng: At Liege, in Belgium, (in the seventh century,) the holy martyr Theodard, the Bishop, who laid down his life for the sheep, and shone with the grace of miracles after his death.

entries.lat: Chalcedóne sanctórum Mártyrum Sósthenis et Victóris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Asiæ Procónsule Prisco, post víncula et béstias superátas, jussi sunt incéndi; at illi, salutántes se ínvicem in ósculo sancto, in oratióne pósiti emisérunt spíritum.
entries.eng: At Chalcedon, the holy martyrs Sosthenes and Victor, who were condemned to be burnt by Priscus the Proconsul of Asia, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, after they had overcome bonds and beasts then they saluted one another with an holy kiss, and gave up their souls in prayer to God.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Apéllii, Lucæ et Cleméntis.
entries.eng: Likewise the holy martyrs Apellius, Luke, and Clement, (who were among the first disciples of the Lord Christ.).

entries.lat: In Bithýnia sanctárum Vírginum sorórum Menodóræ, Metrodóræ et Nymphodóræ; quæ sub Maximiáno Imperatóre et Frontóne Prǽside, ob intrépidam in Christi fide constántiam martýrio coronátæ, pervenérunt ad glóriam.
entries.eng: In Bithynia, the holy sisters Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora, Virgins, who passed into glory crowned with martyrdom, under Maximian the Emperor and Fronto the President.

entries.lat: Compostéllæ sancti Petri Epíscopi, qui multis virtútibus et miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Compostella, holy Bishop Peter, famous for many graces and miracles.

entries.lat: In civitáte Albigénsi, in Gállia, sancti Sálvii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the city of Albi, in France, the holy Bishop and Confessor Salvius.

entries.lat: Nováriæ sancti Agápii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Novara, the holy Bishop Agapius.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctæ Pulchériæ Augústæ, Vírginis, religióne et pietáte insígnis.
entries.eng: In the city of Albi, (in the sixth Bishop (of that see.) At Novara, (in the sixth century,) holy Agapius, Bishop (of that see.) At Constantinople, (in the fifth century,) the holy Virgin Pulcheria, Empress of the Romans, famous for godliness.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sanctæ Cándidæ junióris, miráculis claræ.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, the holy Candida the younger, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Salária véteri, in cœmetério Basíllæ, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Proti et Hyacínthi fratrum, eunuchórum beátæ Eugéniæ. Hi, sub Galliéno Imperatóre, deprehénsi quod essent Christiáni, sacrificáre cogúntur; sed non consentiéntes, primo duríssime verberáti sunt, ac tandem páriter decolláti.
entries.eng: Under the Emperor Gallienus they were arrested on the charge that they were Christians, and, forasmuch as they could not be made to offer sacrifice, they were first grievously beaten, and then beheaded.

entries.lat: Legióne, in Hispánia, sancti Vincéntii, Abbátis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Leon, in Spain, (in the middle of the sixth century,) the holy martyr Vincent, Abbot (of the monastery of St Claudius.).

entries.lat: Laodicéæ, in Sýria, pássio sanctórum Diodóri, Diomédis et Dídymi.
entries.eng: At Laodicea, in Syria, the holy martyrs Diodorus, Diomede, and Didymus.

entries.lat: In Ægýpto sancti Paphnútii Epíscopi, qui unus fuit ex iis Confessóribus, qui, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, dextro óculo effósso et sinístro póplite excíso, ad metálla damnáti fuérunt; deínde, sub Constantíno Magno, advérsus Ariános, pro fide cathólica, strénue decertávit; et demum, multis corónis auctus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: In Egypt, holy Paphnutius, Bishop (in the Thebaid.) He was one of those Confessors who under the Emperor Galerius Maximinus had his right eye put out and his left hough cut, and was condemned to penal servitude in the mines. Under the Emperor Constantine the Great he strove stalwartly for the Catholic faith against the Arians, and at length fell asleep in peace, crowned with many crowns.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Patiéntis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Lyons, in France, the burial of the holy Bishop Patiens.

entries.lat: Vercéllis sancti Æmiliáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Vercelli, the holy Bishop Aemilian.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctæ Theodóræ, quæ, cum incáute deliquísset, inde, facti pǽnitens, mirábili abstinéntia et patiéntia in hábitu sancto perseverávit incógnita usque ad mortem.
entries.eng: At Lyons, (toward the close of the fifth century,) deceased the holy (Confessor) Patient, Bishop (of that see.) At Vercelli, (in the sixth century,) the holy (Confessor) Emilian, Bishop (of that see.) At Alexandria, (in the fifth century,) holy Theodora, who, having carelessly transgressed and deeply repented, continued unknown in the holy habit in wondrous self- denial and longsuffering, until her death.

entries.lat: Festum sanctíssimi Nóminis beátæ Maríæ, quod Innocéntius Undécimus, Póntifex Máximus, ob insígnem victóriam de Turcis, ipsíus Vírginis præsídio, Vindobónæ in Austria reportátam, celebrári jussit.
entries.eng: The Feast of the most holy Name of the Blessed Mary, which Pope Innocent XI ordered to be celebrated on account of the signal victory won over the Turks at Vienna in Austria, by the protection of the same Virgin.

entries.lat: In Bithýnia sancti Autónomi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui ex Itália, Diocletiáni Imperatóris persecutiónem declínans, illuc proféctus, ibi, cum plúrimos convertísset ad fidem, a furéntibus Gentílibus, dum sacra Mystéria perágeret, ad altáre mactátus est, et hóstia Christi efféctus.
entries.eng: In Bithynia, the holy martyr Bishop Autonomus.
