entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy Bishops Maximilian the martyr, and Valentine the Confessor.

entries.lat: Sidóne, in Phœnícia, sancti Zenóbii Presbýteri, qui, sub novíssimæ persecutiónis acerbitáte, ad martýrium álios exhórtans, martýrio et ipse dignátus est.
entries.eng: At Sidon, in Phoenicia, the holy Priest Zenobius, who, during the raging of the last of the persecutions, exhorted others unto martyrdom, and was himself found worthy of the same.

entries.lat: In Lucánia sanctórum Mártyrum Hyacínthi, Quincti, Feliciáni et Lúcii.
entries.eng: In Lucania, the holy martyrs Hyacinth, Quintus, Felician, and Lucius.

entries.lat: Bérgomi sanctæ Eusébiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Bergamo, the holy Virgin and martyr Eusebia.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis natális beáti Narcíssi Epíscopi, sanctitáte, patiéntia ac fide laudábilis, qui, centum et séxdecim annórum senex, felíciter migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the blessed Narcissus, Bishop (of that see,) praiseworthy for his holiness, his long-suffering, and his faith, who at the age of one hundred and sixteen years passed away to be ever with the Lord.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Joánnis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy Bishop and Confessor John.

entries.lat: Cassíope, in ínsula Corcýra, sancti Donáti Epíscopi, de quo scribit beátus Gregórius Papa.
entries.eng: At Cassiope, in the island of Corfu, holy Donatus, of whom writeth blessed Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, deposítio beáti Theodóri Abbátis.
entries.eng: At Vienne, (in the sixth century,) deceased the blessed Theodore, Abbot (of the monastery founded by him in honour of the Blessed Virgin, but commonly called after himself.).

entries.lat: In Sardínia natális sancti Pontiáni, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, ab Alexándro Imperatóre, una cum Hippólyto Presbýtero, in eam ínsulam deportátus, ibídem, mactátus fústibus, martýrium consummávit. Ejus corpus a beáto Fabiáno Papa Romam delátum est, atque in cœmetério Callísti sepúltum. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur tertiodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris.
entries.eng: In Sardinia, the birthday of St. Pontian, Pope and Martyr, who, being banished to that island by the Emperor Alexander together with the Priest Hippolytus, was there beaten to death with clubs and so consummated his martyrdom. His body was carried to Rome by the blessed Pope Fabian, and buried in the cemetery of Callistus. His feast, however, is kept on the 19th day of November.

entries.lat: Ægéæ, in Cilícia, pássio sanctórum Zenóbii Epíscopi, et Zenóbiæ soróris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Lýsia Prǽside.
entries.eng: At Algaea, in Cilicia, under the President Lysias and the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Zenobius, Bishop (of that see,) and Zenobia his sister.

entries.lat: Altíni, in Venetórum fínibus, sancti Theonésti, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui ab Ariánis occísus est.
entries.eng: At Altino, the holy martyr Theonestus, Bishop (of Philippi, in Macedonia,) who was slain by the Arians.

entries.lat: In Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum ducentórum vigínti.
entries.eng: In Africa, two hundred and twenty holy martyrs.

entries.lat: Tingi, in Mauritánia, pássio sancti Marcélli Centuriónis, qui, sanctórum Cláudii ac Lupérci et Victórii Mártyrum pater, cápitis abscissióne martýrium complévit sub Agricoláo, agente vices Præfécti prætório.
entries.eng: At Tangiers, in Morocco, (in the third century,) the holy centurion Marcellus, who accomplished martyrdom by being beheaded under Agricolaus, Vicar to the Prefect of the Pretorium.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum trédecim Mártyrum, qui, cum sanctis Juliáno, Euno et Macário, passi sunt sub Décio Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, thirteen holy martyrs, who suffered under the Emperor Decius, along with Julian, Eunus, and Macarius.

entries.lat: Cárali, in Sardínia, sancti Saturníni Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Bárbaro Prǽside, cápite truncátus est.
entries.eng: At Cagliari, in Sardinia, the holy martyr Saturninus, who was beheaded under the President Barbarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Apaméæ, in Phrýgia, sancti Máximi Mártyris, sub eódem Diocletiáno.
entries.eng: At Apamea, in Phrygia, under the same Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Maximus.

entries.lat: Legióne, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Lupérci et Victórii, filiórum sancti Marcélli Centuriónis; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, sub Diogeniáno Prǽside, jussi sunt decollári.
entries.eng: At Leon, in Spain, the holy martyrs Claudius, Lupercus, and Victorius, sons of the holy centurion Marcellus, who were beheaded under the President Diogenian, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum sancti Lucáni Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Paris, the holy martyr Lucan.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctæ Eutrópiæ Mártyris, quæ, Mártyres vísitans, apprehénsa est, et, cum illis sævíssime cruciáta, réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Alexandria also, the holy martyr Eutropia, who visited the martyrs, and, being most cruelly tormented along with them, gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Serapiónis Epíscopi, eruditióne claríssimi.
entries.eng: At Antioch, (in the third century,) holy Serapion, Patriarch (of that see,) eminent for his learning.

entries.lat: Cápuæ sancti Germáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, magnæ sanctitátis viri; cujus ánimam, in hora óbitus ejus, ab Angelis in cælum deférri sanctus Benedíctus aspéxit.
entries.eng: At Capua, the holy Confessor Germanus, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, whose soul, at the hour of his death, holy Benedict saw carried heavenward by Angels.

entries.lat: Poténtiæ, in Lucánia, sancti Gerárdi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Potenza, in Lucania, holy Gerard, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Ampliáti, Urbáni et Narcíssi, quorum méminit sanctus Paulus ad Romános scribens, qui, ob Evangélium Christi, a Judǽis et Gentílibus cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: The holy martyrs Ampliatus, Urban, and Narcissus, of whom mention is made by holy Paul, writing unto the Romans, and who were slain by the Jews and Gentiles for Christ's Gospel's sake.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Stachis Epíscopi, qui a beáto Andréa Apóstolo primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus est.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Archbishop Stachys, who was ordained by the blessed Apostle Andrew as the first Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Apud Augústam Veromanduórum, in Gállia, sancti Quinctíni, civis Románi et ex órdine Senatório viri, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre martýrium passus est; cujus corpus post annos quinquagínta quinque, revelánte Angelo, invéntum est incorrúptum.
entries.eng: At Saint-Quentin, in Gaul, holy Quentin, a Roman citizen of senatorial rank, who suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Maximian. His body was shown by the revelation of an Angel after fifty-five years, and was found incorrupt.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Antoníni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, (in the seventh century,) the holy Confessor Antoninus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Ratisbónæ, in Bavária, sancti Wolfgángi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Ratisbon, (in the tenth century,) holy Wolfgang, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Palmæ, in Majórca ínsula, sancti Alfónsi Rodríguez, Coadjutóris temporális formáti e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris, humilitáte ac jugi mortificatiónis stúdio insígnis; quem Leo Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Palma, in the island of Majorca, St. Alphonsus Rodriguez, formed Temporal Coadjutor of the Society of Jesus and Confessor, remarkable for his humility and his constant zeal for mortification; whom Pope Leo XIII enrolled in the calendar of the Saints.

entries.lat: Romæ Translátio beáti Nemésii Diáconi, et fíliæ Lucíllæ Vírginis, qui octávo Kaléndas Septémbris decolláti sunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the blessed Deacon Nemesius, and the Virgin Lucilla his daughter for as much as it was impossible to make them swerve from their faith in Christ, they were beheaded by order of the Emperor Valerian upon the 25th day of August.

entries.lat: Festívitas ómnium Sanctórum, quam in honórem beátæ Dei Genitrícis Vírginis Maríæ et sanctórum Mártyrum Bonifátius Papa Quartus, cum templum Pántheon tértio Idus Maji dedicásset, célebrem et generálem instítuit agi quotánnis in urbe Roma. Sed et Gregórius item Quartus póstmodum decrévit, eándem festivitátem, quæ váriis modis jam in divérsis Ecclésiis celebrabátur, in honórem ómnium Sanctórum solémniter hac die ab univérsa Ecclésia perpétuo observári.
entries.eng: The Festival of All Saints, which Pope Boniface IV, when he had dedicated the temple of the Pantheon on the 13th day of May, appointed to be celebrated solemnly and generally every year in the city of Rome, in honour of the blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God, and of the holy Martyrs. But Pope Gregory IV afterwards decreed that the same festival, which was already celebrated in divers ways in different Churches, should be observed solemnly and for ever on this day by the universal Church in honour of all the Saints.

entries.lat: In Pérside sanctórum Mártyrum Joánnis Epíscopi, et Jacóbi Presbýteri, sub Sápore Rege.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy Martyrs John, Bishop, and James, Priest, under King Sapor.

entries.lat: Tarracínæ, in Campánia, natális sancti Cæsárii Diáconi, qui, diébus multis in custódia macerátus, póstea, cum sancto Juliáno Presbýtero, in saccum missus et in mare præcipitátus est.
entries.eng: At Terracina, in Campania, (in the reign of the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy Deacon Caesarius, who suffered many days in prison, and was afterwards put into a sack, along with the holy Priest Julian, and cast into the sea.

entries.lat: In castro Divióne sancti Benígni Presbýteri, qui a beáto Polycárpo missus est in Gálliam ad prædicándum Evangélium; et, postquam, sub Marco Aurélio Imperatóre, a Teréntio Júdice gravíssimis torméntis multiplíciter est afflíctus, tandem ejus collum vecte férreo tundi et corpus láncea perforári jubétur.
entries.eng: At Dijon, the holy Priest Benignus, who was sent into Gaul to preach the Gospel by blessed Polycarp, under the Emperor Marcus Aurelius. He was put to many most grievous torments by the judge Terence, who commanded at last that his neck should be struck with an iron bar and a lance thrust through his body.

entries.lat: Damásci pássio sanctórum Cæsárii, Dácii et aliórum quinque.
entries.eng: At Damascus, suffered the holy martyrs Caesarius, Dacius, and five others.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Maríæ ancíllæ, quæ, Christiánæ religiónis nómine accusáta, hinc, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre, diris verbéribus afflícta, equúlei extensiónem et ungulárum laceratiónem passa, martýrium complévit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy handmaiden Mary, who was accused of Christianity, under the Emperor Hadrian. She was grievously lashed, racked, and torn with hooks, and so suffered martyrdom.

entries.lat: Tarsi, in Cilícia, sanctárum Cyréniæ et Juliánæ Mártyrum, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Tarsus, under the Emperor Maximian, holy Cyrenia and Juliana.

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Austremónii, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: (At Clermont,) in Auvergne, holy Austremonius, the first Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum deposítio sancti Marcélli Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Paris, (in the fifth century,) deceased the holy Marcellus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Bajócis, in Gállia, sancti Vigóris Epíscopi, témpore Childebérti, Francórum Regis.
entries.eng: At Bayeux, in the time of Childebert, King of the Franks, holy Vigor, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Andégavi, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Licínii Epíscopi, venerábilis sanctitátis viri.
entries.eng: At Angers, in France, the burial of the holy Bishop Licinius, a man of venerable holiness.

entries.lat: Tíbure sancti Severíni Mónachi.
entries.eng: At Tivoli, the holy Monk Severinus.

entries.lat: Lyricánti, in Wastinénsi Gálliæ território, sancti Maturíni Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the Gatinais, (in the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Maturin.

entries.lat: Commemorátio ómnium Fidelium Defunctorum.
entries.eng: The Commemoration of all the Faithful Departed.

entries.lat: Pœtovióne, in Pannónia superióre, natális sancti Victoríni, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui, post multa édita scripta (ut sanctus Hierónymus testátur), in persecutióne Diocletiáni, martýrio coronátus est.
entries.eng: Holy Victorinus, Bishop of Poitiers, who, after publishing many writings, as witnesseth holy Jerome, was crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Tergéste pássio beáti Justi, qui in eádem persecutióne, sub Manátio Prǽside, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Trieste, blessed Justus, who, in the same persecution, was martyred under the President Manatius.

entries.lat: Sebáste, in Arménia, sanctórum Cartérii, Styriáci, Tobíæ, Eudóxii, Agápii et Sociórum Mártyrum, sub Licínio Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, under the Emperor Licinius, the holy martyrs Carterius, Styriacus, Tobias, Eudoxius, Agapius, and their Companions.

entries.lat: In Pérside sanctórum Mártyrum Acíndyni, Pegásii, Aphthónii, Elpidíphori et Anempodísti, cum plúrimis Sóciis.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidephorus, and Anempodistus, with many others their Companions.

entries.lat: In Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum Públii, Victóris, Hermétis et Pápiæ.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Publius, Victor, Hermes, and Papias.

entries.lat: Tarsi, in Cilícia, sanctæ Eustóchii, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Juliáno Apóstata, post dira torménta, in oratióne réddidit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Tarsus, in Cilicia, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, the holy Virgin and martyr Eustochium, who, after grievous torments, gave up her soul in prayer to God.

entries.lat: Laodicéæ, in Sýria, sancti Theódoti Epíscopi, qui non solum verbis, sed rebus quoque et virtútibus fuit ornátus.
entries.eng: At Laodicea, in Syria, holy Theodotus, Bishop (of that see,) who excelled not in word only, but in deed and in power.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Geórgii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Vienne, (in the seventh century,) holy George, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In monastério Agaunénsi, in Gállia, sancti Ambrósii Abbátis.
entries.eng: In the monastery of St. Moritz, in Switzerland, (in the sixth century,) the holy Abbot Ambrose.

entries.lat: Cyri, in Sýria, sancti Marciáni Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Cyrus, in Syria, the holy Confessor Marcian, (fourth century.).

entries.lat: Medioláni natális sancti Cároli Borromǽi Cardinális, Epíscopi Mediolanénsis et Confessóris, quem, sanctitáte conspícuum et miráculis clarum, Paulus Papa Quintus in sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Milan, the birthday of St. Charles Borromeo, Cardinal, Bishop of Milan and Confessor, whom, illustrious for his holiness and famous for his miracles, Pope Paul V enrolled in the number of the Saints. His feast, however, is kept on the following day.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális quoque sancti Quarti, Apostolórum discípuli.
entries.eng: Holy Quartus, the disciple of the Apostles.

entries.lat: Vitérbii sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni Presbýteri, et Hilárii Diáconi, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, ob Christi fidem, cum saxi póndere in Tíberim præcipitáti et inde ab Angelo divínitus erépti, demum, abscíssis cervícibus, corónam martýrii percepérunt.
entries.eng: At Viterbo, the holy martyrs Valentine the Priest and Hilary the Deacon, who, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, were for Christ's faith's sake cast into the Tiber weighted with stones, but by the will of God were thence delivered by an Angel, and received the crown of martyrdom by being beheaded.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Mártyrum Germáni, Theóphili, Cæsárii et Vitális; qui, in persecutióne Deciána, óptime duxérunt martýrium.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyrs Germanus, Theophilus, Caesarius, and Vitalis, who bore a noble testimony in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: Cæsaraugústæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum innumerabílium Mártyrum, qui, sub Hispaniárum Prǽside Daciáno, mirabíliter occubuérunt pro Christo.
entries.eng: At Saragossa, countless holy martyrs, who wondrously laid down their lives for Christ's sake under Dacian, President of Spain,.

entries.lat: In Anglia sanctæ Wenefrídæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In England, the holy Virgin and Martyr Winefride.

entries.lat: In monastério Clarævallénsi, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Malachíæ, Connerthénsis in Hibérnia Epíscopi, qui multis virtútibus suo témpore cláruit; cujus vitam sanctus Bernárdus Abbas conscrípsit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Clairvaux, in France, the burial of St. Malachy, Bishop of Connor in Ireland, who was renowned in his time for many virtues; whose life was written by the holy Abbot Bernard.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Hubérti, Tungrénsis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Hubert, Bishop of Tongres.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Domni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Vienne, (in the sixth century,) holy Domnus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Item deposítio sancti Pirmíni, Meldénsis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: Likewise holy Pirmin, Bishop of Meaux.

entries.lat: Urgéllæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Hermengáudii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Urgel, in Spain, holy Hermengaudus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Sílviæ, matris sancti Gregórii Papæ.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Sylvia, the mother of holy Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: Sancti Cároli Borromǽi Cardinális, Epíscopi Mediolanénsis et Confessóris, qui migrávit in cælum prídie hujus diéi.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Charles Borromeo, Cardinal Archbishop of that city, eminent for holiness and famous for miracles, whose name Paul V enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sanctórum Mártyrum Vitális et Agrícolæ; quorum prior posterióris servus ántea fuit, póstea consors et colléga martýrii. In ipsum porro Vitálem persecutóres ómnia tormentórum génera ita exercuérunt, ut non esset in córpore ejus sine vúlnere locus, quæ ipse constánter pérferens, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit; Agrícolam vero, plúrimis clavis cruci affigéntes, interemérunt. Eórum translatióni sanctus Ambrósius cum interésset, Mártyris clavos, sánguinem triumphálem et crucis lignum se collegísse refert, ac sub sacris altáribus condidísse.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy martyrs Vitalis and Agricola. Vitalis was a slave belonging to Agricola, to whom, in suffering martyrdom, he became an equal and a companion. Upon Vitalis the persecutors exercised every kind of torment, until there was no place in his body without some wound. He bore all steadfastly, and gave up his soul in prayer to God. While they were nailing Agricola with many nails to a cross they thereby killed him. Holy Ambrose was present at the translation of their bodies, and saith that he gathered together the nails of this martyr, his victorious blood, and the wood of his cross, and buried them under the holy altar.

entries.lat: In cœnóbio Cervi Frígidi, territórii Meldénsis, natális sancti Felícis Valésii, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui Fundátor fuit Ordinis sanctíssimæ Trinitátis redemptiónis captivórum. Ipsíus autem festum, ex dispositióne Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi, celebrátur duodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Cerfroi, in the country of Meaux, holy Felix de Valois, Founder of the Order of the Most Holy Trinity for the Redemption of Captives, whose feast is kept by decree of Innocent XI upon the 20th day of this same month of November, but by us upon the 26th day of the same.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális quoque sanctórum Philólogi et Pátrobæ, sancti Pauli Apóstoli discipulórum.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Philologus and Patrobas, disciples of the holy Apostle Paul. (According to the Greek tradition Patrobas was Bishop of Pozzuoli and then of Naples, and Philologus of Sinope, in Paphlagonia.) At Autun, the holy martyr Proculus.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Próculi, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy Bishop and Martyr Proculus.

entries.lat: Myræ, in Lýcia, sanctórum Mártyrum Nicándri Epíscopi, et Hermæ Presbýteri, sub Libánio Prǽside.
entries.eng: At Myra, in Lycia, under the President Libanius, the holy martyrs Nicander, Bishop (of that see,) and Hermas, a Priest.

entries.lat: In pago Vilcassíno, in Gállia, sancti Clari, Presbýteri et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In the Vexin, the holy martyr Clarus, a Priest.

entries.lat: Ephesi sancti Porphýrii Mártyris, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Ephesus, under the Emperor Aurelian, the holy martyr Porphyry.

entries.lat: Apud Ruthénos, in Gállia, beáti Amántii Epíscopi, cujus vita éxstitit sanctitáte et miráculis gloriósa.
entries.eng: At Rodez, in Gaul, the blessed Amantius, Bishop (of that see,) whose life remains glorious on account of his holiness and miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Piérii, Presbýteri Alexandríni, qui, in divínis Scriptúris nobíliter erudítus, vita puríssimus, et ad Christiánam philosophíam nudus pénitus et expedítus, sub Caro et Diocletiáno Princípibus, regénte Alexandrínam Ecclésiam Theóna, florentíssime dócuit pópulum, et divérsos tractátus édidit; post persecutiónem vero, omne vitæ suæ tempus Romæ versátus, in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy Pierius, a Priest of Alexandria, profoundly learned in the Scriptures of God, unblemished in life, and for Christian philosophy's sake stripped nearly of all things, and unattached. He taught the people of Alexandria admirably while Theonas ruled that Church in the time of the Princes Carus and Diocletian, and published diverse treatises. After the persecution was over he spent the rest of his life at Rome, and there fell asleep in peace, (at the beginning of the fourth century.).

entries.lat: In Bithýnia sancti Joannícii Abbátis.
entries.eng: In Bithynia, the holy Abbot Joannicius.

entries.lat: Apud Albam Regálem, in Pannónia, deposítio beáti Emeríci Confessóris, qui fuit fílius sancti Stéphani, Hungarórum Regis.
entries.eng: At Albe-Royale, in Hungary, the blessed Confessor Emeric, son of holy Stephen, King of Hungary.

entries.lat: Tréviris sanctæ Modéstæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Trier, the holy Virgin Modesta.

entries.lat: Sancti Zacharíæ, Sacerdótis et Prophétæ, qui pater éxstitit beáti Joánnis Baptístæ, Præcursóris Dómini.
entries.eng: St. Zachary, Priest and Prophet, who was the father of blessed John the Baptist, the Precursor of the Lord.

entries.lat: Item sanctæ Elísabeth, ejúsdem sanctíssimi Præcursóris matris.
entries.eng: Likewise St. Elizabeth, mother of the same most holy Precursor.

entries.lat: Tarracínæ, in Campánia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Felícis Presbýteri, et Eusébii Mónachi. Ex his Eusébius, cum sepelísset sanctos Mártyres Juliánum et Cæsárium, et multos convérteret ad fidem Christi, quos sanctus Felix Présbyter baptizábat, una cum ipso Felíce tentus est; et, ad Júdicis forum ducti nec superáti, inde in cárcerem inclúsi, ambo, nocte eádem, cum sacrificáre noluíssent, decolláti sunt.
entries.eng: At Terracina, in Campania, the holy martyrs Felix, a Priest, and Eusebius, a Monk. This Eusebius buried the holy martyrs Julian and Caesarius, and turned many to believe in Christ who were baptized by the holy Priest Felix. He and Felix were therefore tried together and both led before the seat of the judge, where neither was overcome, but were committed to prison together, and the same night, since they refused to sacrifice, they were beheaded.

entries.lat: Eméssæ, in Phœnícia, sanctórum Mártyrum Galatiónis et Epistémis cónjugis, qui in Décii persecutióne, flagris cæsi, mánibus pedibúsque et lingua ínsuper mutiláti, dénique, truncáto cápite, martýrium consummárunt.
entries.eng: At Emesa, in Phoenicia, the holy martyrs Galation, and Epistemis, his wife. In the persecution under Decius they were heavily flogged, and their hands, feet, and tongues mutilated, whereafter they were beheaded, and so finished their testimony.

entries.lat: Item sanctórum Mártyrum Domníni, Theótimi, Philóthei, Silváni et Sociórum, sub Maximíno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: Also under the Emperor Maximin, the holy martyrs Domninus, Theotimus, Philotheus, Silvanus, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Magni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Magnus, Bishop (of that see, in the year 529.).

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Dominatóris Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, holy Dominator, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Fibítii, qui ex Abbáte factus est ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Fibitius, who from being Abbot was made Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Aureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Læti, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Orleans, in Gaul, the holy Confessor Laetus, a Priest,.

entries.lat: Barcinóne, in Hispánia, sancti Sevéri, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui ob fidem cathólicam, confósso per clavum cápite, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: At Barcelona, the holy martyr Severus, Bishop (of that see,) who for the Catholic faith's sake had a nail driven into his head, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Thiníssæ, in Africa, natális sancti Felícis Mártyris, qui, conféssus et ad torménta dilátus, alio die (ut refert sanctus Augustínus, Psalmum in ejus festivitáte ad pópulum expónens) invéntus est in cárcere exánimis.
entries.eng: At Thinissa, in Africa, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Felix, who had made his confession and was reserved for the torture, when on the next day he was found dead in prison, as is told by holy Augustine in his exposition of Ps. cxxvii. made to the people upon his festival.

entries.lat: Theópoli, quæ est Antiochía, sanctórum decem Mártyrum, qui a Saracénis passi legúntur.
entries.eng: At Antioch, ten holy martyrs who are recorded to have suffered at the hands of the Saracens.

entries.lat: In Phrýgia sancti Attici Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Phrygia, holy Atticus.

entries.lat: Apud Bergas, in Flándria, deposítio sancti Winóci Abbátis, qui, virtútibus et miráculis clarus, étiam frátribus sibi súbditis multo témpore ministrávit.
entries.eng: At Bergues, (before the middle of the eighth century,) holy Winoc, Abbot (of Wormhout,) famous for graces and miracles, who ministered for a long time to the brethren subject unto him.

entries.lat: Fundis, in Látio, sancti Felícis Mónachi.
entries.eng: At Fondi, in Latium, (in the sixth century,) the holy Monk Felix.

entries.lat: Lemóvicis, in Aquitánia, sancti Leonárdi Confessóris, qui fuit beáti Remígii Epíscopi discípulus. Hic, nóbili génere ortus, solitáriam vitam delégit, et sanctitáte ac miráculis cláruit; ejúsque virtus præcípue in liberándis captívis enítuit.
entries.eng: At Limoges, in Aquitaine, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Leonard, a disciple of blessed Bishop Remy. He was noble by birth, but chose the life of an hermit, and is famous for his holiness and miracles, but his power hath been most chiefly shown in the freeing of prisoners.

entries.lat: Patávii deposítio sancti Prosdócimi, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus. Hic, a beáto Petro Apóstolo Epíscopus ordinátus, ad prædicándum Dei verbum ad prædíctam civitátem missus est; ibíque, multis virtútibus et prodígiis corúscans, beáto fine quiévit.
entries.eng: At Padua, the burial of St. Prosdocimus, who was the first Bishop of that city. He was ordained Bishop by the blessed Apostle Peter, and sent to the aforesaid city to preach the word of God; and there, shining with many virtues and wonders, he rested with a blessed end.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sancti Herculáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Perugia, the holy martyr Herculanus, Bishop (of that see.) On the same day the holy martyr Amaranth, who was buried in the city of Albi when the course of his faithful contending was over, but he is alive for evermore in glory.

entries.lat: Apud Swelménsem civitátem, in Germánia, pássio sancti Engelbérti, Epíscopi Coloniénsis, qui, cum illuc ex óppido Sosátio ad templum dedicándum pérgeret, a sicáriis intercéptus in via multísque vulnéribus cæsus, gloriósum pro defensióne ecclesiásticæ libertátis et Románæ Ecclésiæ obediéntia martýrium súbiit.
entries.eng: At Cologne, holy Engelbert, Bishop (of that see), who was contented to suffer martyrdom in defence of the freedom of the Church and of the obedience due to the Church of Rome.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Amaránthi Mártyris, qui apud Albigénsem urbem, in Gállia, exácto agónis fidélis cursu, sepúltus, vivit in glória.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Amarantus, who, having finished the course of his faithful combat, was buried near the city of Albi, in France, and lives in glory.

entries.lat: Melitínæ, in Arménia, pássio sanctórum Hierónis, Nicándri, Hesýchii et aliórum trigínta; qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Lýsia Prǽside, coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Melitina, in Armenia, the holy martyrs Hiero, Nicander, Hesychius, and thirty others, who were crowned under the President Lysias, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Amphípoli, in Macedónia, sanctórum Mártyrum Aucti, Tauriónis et Thessalonícæ.
entries.eng: At Amphipolis, in Macedonia, the holy martyrs Auctus, Taurion, and Thessalonica.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, pássio sanctórum Melasíppi, Antónii et Carínæ, sub Juliáno Apóstata.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, the holy martyrs Melasippus, Anthony, and Carina.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ beáti Achíllæ Epíscopi, qui eruditióne, fide, conversatióne ac móribus fuit insígnis.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, blessed Achillas, Bishop (of that see,) eminent for his learning, faith, conversation, and life.

entries.lat: In Frísia deposítio sancti Willibrórdi, Epíscopi Trajecténsis; qui, a beáto Sérgio Papa ordinátus Epíscopus, in Frísia et Dánia Evangélium prædicávit.
entries.eng: In Frisia, the burial of St. Willibrord, Bishop of Utrecht; who, being ordained Bishop by the blessed Pope Sergius, preached the Gospel in Frisia and Denmark.

entries.lat: Metis, in Gállia, sancti Rufi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Metz, in France, the holy Bishop and Confessor Rufus.

entries.lat: Argentoráti sancti Floréntii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Strasbourg, holy Florence, Bishop (of that see, and Founder and Abbot of Haslach and of St. Thomas.).

entries.lat: Romæ, via Lavicána, tértio ab Urbe milliário, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Nicostráti, Symphoriáni, Castórii et Simplícii, qui, primo in cárcerem missi, deínde scorpiónibus gravíssime cæsi, tandem, cum ex fide Christi dimovéri non possent, a Diocletiáno jussi sunt in flúvium præcípites dari.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, upon the third milestone from the city, the holy martyrs Claudius, Nicostratus, Symphorian, Castorius, and Simplicius, they were first cast into prison, then heavily lashed with loaded scourges, and as their faith in Christ could not be shaken the Emperor Diocletian commanded that they should be cast into the river.

entries.lat: Ibídem, via Lavicána, natális sanctórum Quátuor Coronatórum fratrum, id est Sevéri, Severiáni, Carpóphori et Victoríni; qui, sub eódem Imperatóre, íctibus plumbatárum usque ad mortem cæsi sunt. Horum autem nómina, quæ póstea, interjéctis annis, Dómino revelánte, osténsa sunt, cum mínime reperíri tunc potuíssent, statútum fuit ut anniversária dies ipsórum, una cum illis quinque, sub nómine sanctórum Quátuor Coronatórum recolerétur; qui mos, étiam postquam reveláta sunt, in Ecclésia perseverávit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, upon the Lavican Way, the holy martyrs called the "Crowned" brethren, Severus, Severian, Carpophorus, and Victorinus, who under the aforesaid Emperor Diocletian were flogged to death with scourges loaded with lead. Their names were afterwards revealed by the Lord after diverse years, but as they were unknown at the time it was ordained that on the anniversary of their deaths they should be commemorated, along with the five above mentioned, under the title of the Four that were Crowned, and the said custom hath still gone on in the Church ever since their names have been known.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Deúsdedit Papæ Primi, qui tanti meriti fuit, ut leprósum ósculo a lepra sanáverit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Deusdedit, whose grace was such that by his kiss he made a leper clean.

entries.lat: In vico Blexen, ad Visúrgim flúvium, in Germánia, sancti Willehádi, qui primus éxstitit Breménsis civitátis Epíscopus; atque, una cum sancto Bonifátio, cujus discípulus fuit, in Frísia et Saxónia Evangélium propagávit.
entries.eng: At Bremen, holy Willehad, first Bishop of that see. He spread the Gospel in Friesland and Saxony along with holy Boniface, whose disciple he was.

entries.lat: Suessíone, in Gálliis, sancti Godefrídi, Ambianénsis Epíscopi, magnæ sanctitátis viri.
entries.eng: At Soissons, in France, St. Godfrey, Bishop of Amiens, a man of great holiness.

entries.lat: Apud Virodúnum, in Gállia, sancti Mauri, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verdun, the holy Confessor Maurus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Clari Presbýteri, cujus sanctus Paulínus epitáphium scripsit.
entries.eng: At Tours, (in the fourth century,) the holy priest Clarus, whose epitaph was written by holy Paulinus.

entries.lat: Romæ, in Lateráno, Dedicátio Basílicæ sanctíssimi Salvatóris, quæ ómnium Urbis et Orbis Ecclesiárum est mater et caput.
entries.eng: At Rome, in the Lateran, the Dedication of the Basilica of the most holy Saviour, which is the mother and head of all the Churches of the City and of the World.

entries.lat: Amaséæ, in Ponto, natális sancti Theodóri mílitis, qui, témpore Maximiáni Imperatóris, pro Christiánæ fídei confessióne, fórtiter cæsus et in cárcerem missus; deínde, Dómino sibi apparénte ac monénte ut constánter et viríliter ágeret, relevátus est; novíssime, postquam in equúleo suspénsus et úngulis ita excarnificátus est, ut ejus interióra apparérent nuda, ardéntibus ígnibus comburéndus tráditur. Ipsíus vero laudes sanctus Gregórius Nyssénus præcláro encómio celebrávit.
entries.eng: At Amasea, in Pontus, the holy soldier Theodore. In the time of the Emperor Maximian he was heavily flogged and cast into prison for his profession of the Christian faith, in prison the Lord appeared unto him, and bade him be steadfast and do manfully, then he was taken out and stretched upon the rack and torn with hooks until his inner parts were seen, and lastly he was thrown into the fire. Holy Gregory of Nyssa hath told his praises in a noble discourse.

entries.lat: Tyánæ, in Cappadócia, pássio sancti Oréstis, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Tyana, in Cappadocia, under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Orestes.

entries.lat: Thessalonícæ sancti Alexándri Mártyris, sub Maximiáno Príncipe.
entries.eng: At Thessalonica, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyr Alexander.

entries.lat: Apud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, sancti Ursíni Confessóris, qui, Romæ ordinátus a successóribus Apostolórum, primus eídem Bituricénsi urbi destinátur Epíscopus.
entries.eng: At Bourges, the holy Confessor Ursinus, who was ordained at Rome by the successors of the Apostles, and sent to that city as the first Bishop thereof.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Agrippíni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Agrippinus, Bishop (of that see,) famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctárum Vírginum Eustóliæ Románæ, et Sópatræ, fíliæ Maurítii Imperatóris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Virgins Eustolia of Rome, and Sopatra, daughter of the Emperor Maurice.

entries.lat: Berýti, in Sýria, commemorátio Imáginis Salvatóris, quæ, a Judǽis crucifíxa, tam copiósum emísit sánguinem, ut Orientáles et Occidentáles Ecclésiæ ex eo ubértim accéperint.
entries.eng: At Beirut, in Syria, the commemoration of the Image of the Saviour, which, being crucified by the Jews, poured forth blood so abundantly that the Churches of the East and of the West received of it in plenty.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, natális sancti Andréæ Avellíni, Clérici Reguláris et Confessóris, sanctitáte et salútis proximórum procurándæ stúdio præcélebris, quem, miráculis clarum, Clemens Undécimus, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum catálogo adscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Andrew Avellino, Clerk Regular, very eminent for his holiness and his zeal for setting forward the salvation of his neighbours. He was famous for miracles, and Clement XV enrolled his name among those of the saints.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális quoque sanctórum Mártyrum Tryphónis, et Respícii, ac Nymphæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: The holy martyrs Tryphon, Respicius, and the Virgin Nympha.

entries.lat: Romæ item natális sancti Leónis Papæ Primi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, virtútum excéllens méritis, dictus est Magnus. Ejus tempóribus celebráta fuit sancta Sýnodus Chalcedonénsis, in qua ipse per legátos damnávit Eutýchen; cujus étiam Sýnodi decréta póstmodum auctoritáte sua confirmávit. Tandem, cum sanxísset multa luculentérque scripsísset, Pastor bonus, de sancta Dei Ecclésia et univérso grege Domínico óptime méritus, quiévit in pace. Ipsíus tamen festívitas tértio Idus Aprílis celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Rome, likewise the birthday of St. Leo I, Pope, Confessor and Doctor of the Church; who, excelling in the merits of his virtues, was called the Great. In his time was celebrated the holy Council of Chalcedon, in which he condemned Eutyches by his legates; and the decrees of that Council he afterwards confirmed by his authority. At length, having enacted many things and written with great brilliance, this good Shepherd, having deserved excellently well of the holy Church of God and of the whole flock of the Lord, rested in peace. His feast, however, is kept on the 11th day of April.

entries.lat: Icónii, in Lycaónia, sanctárum mulíerum Tryphénnæ et Tryphósæ, quæ, beáti Pauli prædicatióne et exémplo Theclæ, in Christiána discíplina plúrimum profecérunt.
entries.eng: At Iconium, in Lycaonia, the holy Women Tryphenna and Tryphosa, who advanced much in Christian training by the preaching of blessed Paul and the example of Thecla.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Demétrii Epíscopi, Aniáni Diáconi, Eustósii et aliórum vigínti Mártyrum.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Demetrius, Bishop (of that see,) the Deacon Anian, Eustosius, and twenty others.

entries.lat: In território Agathénsi, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Tibérii, Modésti et Floréntiæ; qui, témpore Diocletiáni, váriis torméntis cruciáti, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: In the country of Agde, the holy martyrs Tiberius, Modestus, and Florence, who, in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, underwent diverse torments, and were crowned with martyrdom.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sancti Probi Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, holy Probus, Bishop (of that see,) famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Aureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Monitóris, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Orleans, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Monitor, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Justi Epíscopi, qui, una cum Augustíno, Mellíto et áliis a beáto Gregório Papa in eam ínsulam missus ad prædicándum Evangélium, ibídem, sanctitáte célebris, obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: In England, holy Justus, Bishop (of Rochester, afterwards translated to Canterbury,) who was sent into that island by the blessed Pope Gregory, along with Augustine, Mellitus, and others to preach the gospel, and there slept in the Lord, famous for holiness,.

entries.lat: In óppido Milléduno, in Gállia, sancti Leónis Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the town of Melun, in France, the holy Confessor Leo.

entries.lat: In Paro ínsula sanctæ Theoctístis Vírginis.
entries.eng: In the island of Paros, the holy Virgin Theoctistis.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, natális beáti Martíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus vita tantis éxstitit miráculis gloriósa, ut trium mortuórum suscitátor esse merúerit.
entries.eng: At Tours, in Gaul, the blessed Confessor Martin, Bishop of that see. His life was remarkable for extraordinary miracles he raised three persons from the dead.

entries.lat: Cotyǽi, in Phrýgia, insígnis pássio sancti Mennæ, Ægýptii mílitis, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, postquam, abjécto milítiæ cíngulo, méruit cælésti Regi secréta conversatióne in erémo militáre, procéssit in públicum, et, se Christiánum líbera voce declárans, primo diris cruciátibus examinátur; novíssime, fixis in oratióne génibus, Dómino Jesu Christo grátias agens, gládio cæsus est, ac multis post mortem miráculis cláruit.
entries.eng: At Cotyaeus, in Phrygia, the glorious passion of the holy Egyptian soldier Mennas. During the persecution under Diocletian he cast away his military belt, and served the King of Heaven in secret in the desert then he went forth, and freely declared himself to be a Christian. He was first examined with horrid tortures, then as he was kneeling in prayer, giving thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, he was beheaded, After his death he was famous for many miracles.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, Feliciáni et Victoríni; qui in Diocletiáni persecutióne coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, Felician, and Victorine, who were crowned in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: In Mesopotámia sancti Athenodóri Mártyris, qui, sub eódem Diocletiáno et Eléusio Prǽside, ígnibus cruciátus et áliis supplíciis tortus, demum cápitis damnátus est, et, cum cárnifex corruísset neque ullus álius gládio illum ferire ausus esset, orans obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: In Mesopotamia, in the persecution under the same Diocletian and Eleusius the President, the holy martyr Athenodorus. He was tormented with fire and other torments, and then condemned to be beheaded but the executioner fell to the earth, and no other dared to smite him with the sword, and as he prayed he fell asleep in the Lord.

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Veráni Epíscopi, cujus vita fuit fide et virtútum méritis illústris.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy Bishop Veran, whose life was illustrious for his faith and other graces.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Theodóri, Abbátis Studítæ, qui, pro fide cathólica advérsus Iconoclástas strénue pugnans, factus est apud univérsam Ecclésiam cathólicam célebris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Abbot Theodore the Studite, who, fighting strenuously for the Catholic faith against the Iconoclasts, became renowned throughout the whole Catholic Church.

entries.lat: In monastério Cryptæ Ferrátæ, in agro Tusculáno, sancti Bartholomǽi Abbátis, qui fuit sócius beáti Nili, ejúsque vitam conscrípsit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Grotta-Ferrata, near Frascati, the holy Abbot (of Grotta-Ferrata,) Bartholomew, a companion of blessed Nilus, and the writer of his life.

entries.lat: In província Sámnii beáti Mennæ solitárii, cujus virtútes et mirácula sanctus Gregórius Papa commémorat.
entries.eng: In the province of Samnium, the blessed hermit, Mennas, whose graces and miracles are recorded by holy Pope Gregory.

entries.lat: Sancti Martíni Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, cujus dies natális sextodécimo Kaléndas Octóbris recensétur.
entries.eng: The holy martyr, Pope Martin. He got together a synod at Rome, wherein he condemned the heretics Sergius, Paul, and Pyrrhus. Wherefore the heretic Emperor Constans caused him to be kidnapped and brought to Constantinople, whence he was banished into the Crimea, where he died, worn out by his sufferings for the Catholic faith's sake. He was famous for miracles. His body was afterward brought to Rome and buried in the Church of SS. Sylvester and Martin.

entries.lat: Vitépsci, in Polónia, pássio sancti Jósaphat, e sancti Basilíi Ordine, Epíscopi Polocénsis et Mártyris; qui a schismáticis, in ódium cathólicæ unitátis et veritátis, crudéliter interféctus est, et a Pio Papa Nono inter sanctos Mártyres adscríptus. Ejus tamen festívitas recólitur décimo octávo Kaléndas Decémbris.
entries.eng: At Vitepsk, in Poland, the holy martyr Jehosaphat, Archbishop of Polotsk, Monk of the Order of St. Basil, who was cruelly murdered by schismatics, out of their hatred for Catholic unity and truth, and whose name Pope Pius IX enrolled among those of the holy martyrs. We keep his feast upon the 28th day of this present month of November.

entries.lat: Complúti, in Hispánia, natális sancti Dídaci Confessóris, ex Ordine Minórum, humilitáte célebris; quem Xystus Quintus, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum catálogo adscrípsit. Ipsíus autem festum sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Alcala, in Spain, the holy Confessor Diego, of the Order of Friars Minor, eminent for his lowliness, whose name Sixtus V enrolled among those of the Saints, and whose feast is kept upon the morrow after.

entries.lat: In Asia pássio sanctórum Aurélii et Públii Episcopórum.
entries.eng: In Asia, the holy martyrs and Bishops Aurelius and Publius.

entries.lat: Eschæ, in Bélgio, sancti Livíni, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum plúrimos ad Christi fidem convertísset, a Pagánis necátus est. Ipsíus vero corpus ad Portum Gandæ póstea translátum fuit.
entries.eng: At Esche, in Belgium, St. Livinus, Bishop and Martyr; who, when he had converted very many to the faith of Christ, was slain by the Pagans. His body was afterwards translated to Ghent.

entries.lat: Apud Casimíriam, in Polónia, sanctórum Mártyrum Eremitárum Benedícti, Joánnis, Matthǽi, Isaac et Christiáni; qui a prædónibus, divíno inténti servítio, dire vexáti sunt et gládiis occísi.
entries.eng: In Poland, the holy martyred Hermits Benedict, John, Matthew, Isaac, and Christinus.

entries.lat: Apud óppidum Sergíniam, in território Senonénsi, sancti Patérni, Mónachi et Mártyris; qui, dum eídem occurréntes in ipsíus óppidi silva latrónes ad emendándam vitam incitáret, ab illis trucidátus est.
entries.eng: In the country of Sens, the holy martyr Paternus.

entries.lat: Avenióne sancti Rufi, qui éxstitit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: At Avignon, St. Rufus, who was the first Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ deposítio sancti Cunibérti Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Cologne, holy Cunibert, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Turiasóne, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, beáti Æmiliáni Presbýteri, qui innúmeris miráculis cláruit; cujus admirábilem vitam sanctus Bráulio, Cæsaraugustánus Epíscopus, descrípsit.
entries.eng: At Tarragona, in Spain, the blessed Priest Emilian, who was famous for countless miracles, and whose wonderful life hath been written by Braulio, the holy Bishop of Zaragoza.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Nili Abbátis, qui, sub Theodósio junióre, ex Præfécto ejúsdem civitátis factus Mónachus, doctrína et sanctitáte cláruit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Constantinople, holy Theodore, of the monastery which is called the Studium who contended mightily for the Catholic faith against the Iconoclasts, and became famous throughout the whole Catholic Church,.

entries.lat: Sancti Dídaci, ex Ordine Minórum, Confessóris; cujus dies natális recólitur prídie hujus diéi.
entries.eng: St. Didacus, of the Order of Friars Minor, Confessor; whose birthday is kept on the day before this.

entries.lat: Ravénnæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, Solutóris et Victóris; qui sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, Solutor, and Victor, who suffered in the persecution under Diocletian.

entries.lat: Aquis, in província Narbonénsi, beáti Mítrii, claríssimi Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Aix, in the province of Narbonne, blessed Mitrius, a most illustrious Martyr.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, pássio sanctórum Antoníni, Zébinæ, Germáni et Ennathæ Vírginis. Hæc, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, verbéribus cæsa, igne cremáta est; illi vero, cum intrépidi ac líbera voce Firmiliánum Prǽsidem, diis immolántem, impietátis argúerent, cápite cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, in the persecution under the Emperor Galerius Maximian, the holy martyrs Antonine, Zebinas, German, and the Virgin Ennatha. Ennatha was flogged and then burnt, and the men were beheaded because they openly rebuked the President Firmilian for his wickedness in offering sacrifice to the gods.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Hispanórum Arcádii, Paschásii, Probi et Eutychiáni; qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, cum in Ariánam perfídiam nullátenus declináre pateréntur, hinc a Genseríco, Rege Ariáno, primum proscrípti, deínde acti in exsílium atque atrocíssimis supplíciis cruciáti, postrémum divérso mortis génere interémpti sunt. Tunc et Paulílli puéruli, germáni sanctórum Paschásii et Eutychiáni, constántia enítuit; qui, cum de fide cathólica nullátenus posset avélli, fústibus diu cæsus est, atque ad ínfimam servitútem damnátus.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Arcadius, Paschasius, Probus, and Eutychian. These were all Spaniards who, during the persecution under the Vandals, could no wise be brought to turn aside unto the Arian misbelief. For this cause the Arian king Genseric first proscribed them, then banished them, afterwards tormented them with terrible sufferings, and lastly put them to death in diverse ways. Then also became glorious the faithfulness of the little lad, Paulillus, the brother of holy Paschasius and Eutychian, and as he would not give up the Catholic faith, he was cudgelled for a long time and condemned to the lowest bondage.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Nicolái Papæ Primi, vigóre apostólico præstántis.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Pope Nicholas the Great, eminent for his Apostolic vigour. (He reigned from April 28, 858 to November 13, 867. He was the 107th Pope.).

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Brítii Epíscopi, qui fuit discípulus beáti Martíni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Tours, holy Brice, Bishop of that see, a disciple of the blessed Bishop Martin.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, sancti Eugénii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Toledo, holy Eugene, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Quinctiáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Clermont, in France, the holy Bishop Quinctian.

entries.lat: Cremónæ, in Insúbria, sancti Homobóni Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Innocéntius Papa Tértius in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
entries.eng: At Cremona, the holy Confessor Homobuono, who was famous for miracles, and whose name Innocent III enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Sancti Jósaphat, e sancti Basilíi Ordine, Epíscopi Polocénsis et Mártyris, cujus dies natális recensétur prídie Idus Novémbris.
entries.eng: St. Josaphat, of the Order of St. Basil, Bishop of Polotsk and Martyr, whose birthday is recorded on the 12th day of November.

entries.lat: Gangris, in Paphlagónia, sancti Hypátii Epíscopi, qui, a magna Nicǽna Sýnodo rédiens, a Novatiánis hæréticis in via lapídibus impetítus, Martyr occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Gangra, in Paphlagonia, the holy martyr Hypatius, Bishop (of that see,) who was stoned to death by the Novatian heretics on his way back from the great Council of Nicea.

entries.lat: Heracléæ, in Thrácia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Clementíni, Theódoti et Philómeni.
entries.eng: At Heraclea, in Thrace, the holy martyrs Clementine, Theodotus, and Philomenus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Serapiónis Mártyris, quem persecutóres, sub Décio Príncipe, ita crudelíssimis affecérunt supplíciis, ut cunctas ei junctúras membrórum prius sólverent, eúmque póstea de superióribus domus suæ præcipitárent; atque ille sic gloriósus Christi Martyr efficerétur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Serapion, whom the persecutors under the Emperor Decius most cruelly tormented until they dislocated all his joints, and then cast him down headlong from the top of his own house, and so made him a martyr for Christ.

entries.lat: Trecis, in Gállia, sancti Venerándi Mártyris, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Troyes, in Gaul, under the Emperor Aurelian, the holy martyr Venerandus.

entries.lat: In Gállia sanctæ Venerándæ Vírginis, quæ, sub Antoníno Imperatóre et Asclepíade Prǽside, martýrii corónam accépit.
entries.eng: Likewise in Gaul, the holy Virgin Veneranda, who received the crown of martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine and Asclepiades the President.

entries.lat: Eméssæ, in Phœnícia, pássio plurimárum sanctárum mulíerum, quæ, sub sævíssimo Arabum duce Mady, ob Christi fidem, crudelíssime tortæ atque necátæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Emesa, many holy Women, who, for Christ's faith's sake, were most cruelly tortured and murdered under the savage Arab chief Mady.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Jucúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy Confessor Jucundus, Bishop (of that see.) In Ireland, holy Lorcan Ua Tuathail, Archbishop of Dublin.

entries.lat: Augæ, in Gállia, tránsitus sancti Lauréntii, Epíscopi Dublinénsis.
entries.eng: At Eu, in France, the passing of St. Laurence, Archbishop of Dublin.

entries.lat: Algáriæ, in Africa, beáti Serapiónis, qui, primus ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, pro captívis fidélibus rediméndis et Christiánæ fídei prædicatióne actus in crucem et membrátim disséctus, martýrii palmam méruit obtinére.
entries.eng: At Algiers, in Africa, the blessed Serapion, the first martyr of the Order of Blessed Mary of Ransom for the Redemption of the Captive Faithful and the Preaching of the Christian Faith. He won his crown by being fastened to a cross and cut limb from limb.

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ sancti Albérti Epíscopi et Confessóris, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, cognoménto Magni, sanctitáte et doctrína célebris, quem Pius Papa Undécimus Doctórem universális Ecclésiæ declarávit, et Pius Duodécimus cultórum scientiárum naturálium cæléstem apud Deum Patrónum constítuit.
entries.eng: At Cologne, St. Albert, Bishop and Confessor, of the Order of Preachers, surnamed the Great, renowned for holiness and learning, whom Pope Pius XI declared a Doctor of the universal Church, and Pope Pius XII appointed heavenly Patron before God of those who cultivate the natural sciences.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális sancti Eugénii, Epíscopi Toletáni et Mártyris; qui fuit beáti Dionýsii Areopagítæ discípulus, et in território Parisiénsi, consummáto martýrii cursu, beátæ passiónis corónam percépit a Dómino. Ipsíus autem corpus Tolétum, in Hispánia, póstea fuit translátum.
entries.eng: The holy martyr Eugene, Archbishop of Toledo, a disciple of blessed Denys, the Areopagite. He finished his testimony in the country of Paris, and received from the Lord a blessed crown of suffering, His body was afterwards brought to Toledo.

entries.lat: Nolæ, in Campánia, beáti Felícis, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, a quintodécimo ætátis suæ anno, miráculis cláruit, et, sub Marciáno Prǽside, cum áliis trigínta Sóciis, agónem martýrii complévit.
entries.eng: At Nola, in Campania, the holy martyr Felix, Bishop (of that see,) who was famous for miracles from the fifteenth year of his age upward and gained the battle of martyrdom under the President Marcian, along with thirty others.

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Mesopotámia, pássio sancti Abibi Diáconi, qui sub Licínio Imperatóre et Lysánia Prǽside, únguibus lacerátus, in ignem conjéctus est.
entries.eng: There likewise, under the Emperor Licinius and the President Lysanias, the holy Deacon Abibus, who was torn with hooks and cast into the fire.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Guríæ et Samónæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Antoníno Prǽside.
entries.eng: At Edessa, in Syria, under the Emperor Diocletian and Antonine the President, the holy martyrs Gurias and Samonas.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Secúndi, Fidentiáni et Várici.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Secundus, Fidentian, and Varicus.

entries.lat: Apud Arcum, in território Santonénsi, natális sancti Machúti, Aleténsis in Gállia Epíscopi; qui, in Anglia natus, a primǽvo ætátis suæ tirocínio miráculis emícuit.
entries.eng: In Brittany, (in the sixth century,) holy Machutus, (St. Maclou or St. Malo, first) Bishop (of the ancient See of Aleth, in Brittany,) who was marked by miracles even from his youth upward.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Lupérii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Confessor Luperius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Kahlembérgæ, prope Vindobónam, in Austria, sancti Leopóldi, ejúsdem provínciæ Austriæ Marchiónis, quem Innocéntius Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum adscrípsit.
entries.eng: In Austria, holy Leopold, (Margrave of Austria,) Marquess of that country, whose name Innocent VIII enrolled with those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Gertrúdis Vírginis, cujus natális sequénti die recensétur.
entries.eng: The holy Virgin Gertrude, whose birthday is recorded on the following day.

entries.lat: Edimbúrgi, in Scótia, natális sanctæ Margarítæ Víduæ, Scotórum Regínæ, amóre in páuperes et voluntária paupertáte célebris. Ipsíus tamen festívitas quarto Idus Júnii celebrátur.
entries.eng: At Edinburgh, in Scotland, the birthday of St. Margaret, Widow, Queen of Scots, renowned for her love of the poor and her voluntary poverty. Her feast, however, is kept on the 10th day of June.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Rufíni, Marci, Valérii et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Rufinus, Mark, Valerius, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Elpídii, Marcélli, Eustóchii et Sociórum; ex quibus Elpídius, cum esset órdinis Senatórii et coram Juliáno Apóstata Christiánam fidem constantíssime profiterétur, ídeo, primum equis indómitis, una cum Sóciis, alligátus atque pertráctus, deínde, in ignem conjéctus, gloriósum martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Elpidius, Marcellus, Eustochius, and their Companions. Elpidius was of the Senatorial Order, and steadfastly confessed the Christian faith in the presence of the Emperor Julian the Apostate. He and his Companions were first tied to unbroken horses, and so dragged about, but afterwards cast into the fire, and so achieved a glorious martyrdom, (in the fourth century.).

entries.lat: Lugdúni, in Gállia, natális sancti Euchérii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, viri admirándæ fídei et doctrínæ. Hic, ex nobilíssimo Senatórum órdine ad religiósam vitam habitúmque convérsus, diu, intra septa spelúncæ sponte conclúsus, in oratiónibus et jejúniis Christo servívit; deínde apud præfátam urbem in pontificáli Cáthedra, revelánte Angelo, solémniter collocátus est.
entries.eng: At Lyon, the holy Confessor Eucherius, Bishop of that see, a man of wonderful faith and teaching. He was of the noblest of the Senatorial Order, and adopted the life and dress of a monk. For a long while he shut himself up in a cave, where he served Christ in fastings and prayers. He was called through the revelation of an angel to occupy the See of Lyons, and was therein solemnly placed. (He died about the year 450.).

entries.lat: Patávii sancti Fidéntii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Padua, holy Fidentius, Bishop (of that see, in the year 168.).

entries.lat: Cantuáriæ, in Anglia, sancti Edmúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, pro Ecclésiæ suæ júribus tuéndis in exsílium actus, apud Provínum, Sénonum óppidum, sanctíssime óbiit; et Sanctórum cánoni ab Innocéntio Papa Quarto adscríptus est.
entries.eng: At Canterbury, in England, the holy Confessor Edmund Rich, Archbishop of that see, who was driven into exile (at Pontigny) for his defense of the rights of his Church, and died a holy death near Provins, (in Champagne, in the year 1242,) and whose name Innocent IV enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Eódem die deposítio sancti Othmári Abbátis.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy Othmar, Abbot (of St. Gall, in Switzerland.).

entries.lat: Neocæsaréæ, in Ponto, natális sancti Gregórii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte illústris, qui propter signa atque mirácula, quæ cum multa Ecclesiárum glória perpetrávit, Thaumatúrgus est appellátus.
entries.eng: At Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, holy Gregory, Archbishop of that see, who was famous for teaching and holiness, and who came to be called the Wonder-worker, on account of the great signs and wonders which he worked to the great glory of the churches, whose feast we keep upon the 27th day of this present month of November.

entries.lat: Helpíthi, in Saxónia, item natális sanctæ Gertrúdis, Vírginis, ex Ordine sancti Benedícti, quæ dono revelatiónum clara éxstitit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas prídie hujus diéi celebrátur.
entries.eng: In Germany, the holy Virgin Gertrude, of the Order of St. Benedict, eminent for her gift of revelations, whose feast we have kept upon the 15th day of this present month.

entries.lat: In Palæstína sanctórum Mártyrum Alphǽi et Zachǽi, qui primo anno persecutiónis Diocletiáni, post multa torménta, capitálem senténtiam subiére.
entries.eng: In Palestine, the holy martyrs Alphaeus and Zacchaeus, who were put to death after suffering many torments, in the first year of the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Acíscli et Victóriæ germanórum, qui, in eádem persecutióne, Diónis Prǽsidis jussu sævíssime cruciáti sunt, et illústri passióne corónas a Dómino meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy brother and sister Acisclus and Victoria, both martyrs, who in the same persecution by Diocletian aforesaid, were most cruelly tortured by command of the President Dion, and earned crowns of glory from the hand of the Lord.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Dionýsii Epíscopi, summæ eruditiónis viri, qui, multis confessiónibus clarus et pro passiónum tormentorúmque diversitáte magníficus, plenus diérum Conféssor quiévit, Valeriáni et Galliéni Imperatórum tempóribus.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, holy Denys, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great learning, and glorious on account of his many confessions and his diverse sufferings and torments, who at length fell asleep in the Lord, full of days but still a Confessor, in the time of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus,.

entries.lat: Aureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Aniáni Epíscopi, cujus mortem in conspéctu Dómini pretiósam mirácula crebra testántur.
entries.eng: At Orleans, holy Anian, Bishop (of that see,) the preciousness of whose death, in the sight of the Lord, is attested by many miracles.

entries.lat: In Británnia sancti Hugónis Epíscopi, qui, ex Mónacho Carthusiáno ad Ecclésiam Lincolniénsem regéndam vocátus, multis cláruit miráculis, et sancto fine quiévit.
entries.eng: In Britain, the holy Bishop Hugh, who, being called from a Carthusian Monk to rule the Church of Lincoln, was renowned for many miracles, and rested with a holy end.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Gregórii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Tours, holy Gregory, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Floréntiæ sancti Eugénii Confessóris, qui fuit Diáconus beáti Zenóbii, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Florence, the holy Confessor Eugene, a Deacon of blessed Zenobius, Bishop of that see.

entries.lat: Romæ Dedicátio Basilicárum sanctórum Petri et Pauli Apostolórum. Eárum primam, restitútam in ampliórem formam, Summus Póntifex Urbánus Octávus consecrávit hac ipsa recurrénte die; álteram vero, miserándo incéndio pénitus consúmptam, ac magnificéntius reædificátam, Pius Nonus die décima Decémbris solémni ritu consecrávit, ejúsque ánnuam commemoratiónem hodiérna die agéndam indíxit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the Dedication of the Basilicas of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul. The first of these, restored in an ampler form, the Sovereign Pontiff Urban VIII consecrated on this very day; the other, wholly consumed by a lamentable fire and rebuilt more magnificently, Pope Pius IX consecrated with solemn rite on the 10th day of December, and ordered its annual commemoration to be kept on this day.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sancti Románi Mártyris, qui, témpore Galérii Imperatóris, cum Asclepíades Præféctus in Ecclésiam irrúmperet eámque fúnditus conarétur evértere, céteros Christiános hortátus est ut ei contradícerent, ideóque, post dira torménta et abscissiónem linguæ (sine qua tamen Dei præcónia loquebátur), in cárcere strangulátus láqueo, célebri martýrio coronátur. Passus est étiam ante ipsum puérulus, nómine Bárula, qui, cum fuísset ab eódem interrogátus Præfécto utrum mélius esset unum Deum cólere an plures deos, atque in unum Deum, quem Christiáni colunt, credéndum esse respondísset, proptérea, verbéribus cæsus, jussus est decollári.
entries.eng: Before him there suffered also the little lad Barula, who was asked by Romanus whether it were better to worship one God or many gods, and answered that we ought to believe in the one God whom the Christians worship for the saying of the which thing he was first flogged and then beheaded.

entries.lat: Item Antiochíæ sancti Hesýchii Mártyris, qui, cum esset miles, et præcéptum audísset ut quisquis non sacrificáret idólis, cíngulum milítiæ depóneret, repénte cíngulum solvit; ob quam causam, ingénti saxo in déxtera ejus ligáto, in flúvium præcipitári jussus est.
entries.eng: Likewise at Antioch, the holy martyr Hesychius. He was a soldier, but when he heard the command that whosoever would not sacrifice to idols should cast away his military belt, he straightway took off his belt, for which cause a large stone was tied to his right hand, and he was thrown into the river.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Orículi et Sociórum, qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, pro fide cathólica passi sunt.
entries.eng: On the same day, (in the fifth century,) the holy martyrs Oriculus and his Companions, who suffered for the Catholic faith in the persecution under the Vandals.

entries.lat: Mogúntiæ sancti Máximi Epíscopi, qui, témpore Constántii multa passus ab Ariánis, Conféssor occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Mainz, holy Maximus, Bishop of that see, who suffered many things from the Arians in the time of the Emperor Constantius, and died a Confessor.

entries.lat: Turónis, in Gállia, tránsitus beáti Odónis, Abbátis Cluniacénsis.
entries.eng: At Tours, blessed Odo, Abbot of Cluny.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Thomæ Mónachi, quem Antiochéni, ob sedátam ejus précibus pestem, solemnitáte annua coluérunt.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy monk Thomas, in whose honour the Antiochenes keep a solemn feast-day every year on account of a plague which was stayed by his prayers.

entries.lat: Lucæ, in Túscia, Translátio sancti Frigdiáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Lucca, in Tuscany, the Translation of St. Frigidian, Bishop and Confessor.

entries.lat: In óppido Marpúrgi, in Germánia, deposítio sanctæ Elísabeth Víduæ, Regis Hungarórum Andréæ fíliæ, ex tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, quæ, pietátis opéribus assídue inténta, miráculis clara migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Marburg, in Germany, the holy Widow Elizabeth, (Landgravine of Hesse and Thuringia,) of the third Order of St Francis, daughter of Andrew II, King of Hungary, busied without ceasing in works of mercy and famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Sancti Pontiáni, Papæ et Mártyris; cujus dies natális tértio Kaléndas Novémbris recensétur.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr, Pope Pontian, who was exiled to Sardinia along with the Priest Hippolytus, under the Emperor Alexander, and was there cudgelled to death. His body was brought to Rome by blessed Pope Fabian, and buried in the cemetery of Kallistus.

entries.lat: Samaríæ, in Palæstína, sancti Abdíæ Prophétæ.
entries.eng: At Samaria, the holy Prophet Obadiah.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Appia, natális sancti Máximi, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni passus, pósitus est ad sanctum Xystum.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, the holy martyr Maximus, a Priest, who suffered in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, and was buried hard by holy Pope Xystus.

entries.lat: In civitáte Astiagénsi, in Hispánia, beáti Crispíni Epíscopi, qui, cápite amputáto, martýrii glóriam adéptus est.
entries.eng: In the city of Ecija, blessed Crispin, Bishop (of that see,) who was beheaded, and so won the glory of martyrdom.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Fausti, Diáconi Alexandríni, qui primum, in persecutióne Valeriáni, cum sancto Dionýsio, in exsílium missus est; deínde, ætáte longǽvus, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, animadvérsus gládio martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, holy Faustus, a Deacon of Alexandria, who was first sent into exile along with holy Denys in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, and afterwards in his old age was beheaded in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sancti Bárlaam Mártyris, qui, agréstis licet et rudis, Christi sapiéntia munítus tyránnum vicit, et ignem ipsum per invíctam fídei constántiam superávit; in cujus die natáli sanctus Basilíus Magnus célebrem hábuit oratiónem.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Barlaam. He was an unlettered peasant, but filled with the wisdom of Christ, and by the steadfastness of his faith conquered the tyrant (Diocletian) and his fire. Holy Basil the Great preached a famous sermon upon his feast-day.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Severíni, Exsupérii et Feliciáni; quorum córpora, post multa annórum currícula, ipsis revelántibus, invénta, et a Pontífice, clero et pópulo illíus urbis honorífice subláta, condígno honóre cóndita sunt.
entries.eng: At Vienne, in Gaul, (in the second century,) the holy martyrs Severinus, Exuperius, and Felician after many years had passed they themselves revealed where their bodies were lying the which, being so found, were honourably taken up by the Bishop, clergy, and people of that city, and buried again with due reverence.

entries.lat: In Isáuria pássio sanctórum Azæ et Sociórum centum quinquagínta mílitum, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Aquilíno Tribúno.
entries.eng: In Isauria, under the Emperor Diocletian and the Tribune Aquilinus, the holy martyrs Azas and a hundred and fifty Companions, all soldiers.

entries.lat: Sancti Felícis Valésii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis sanctíssimæ Trinitátis redemptiónis captivórum éxstitit Fundátor, ac prídie Nonas Novémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
entries.eng: St. Felix of Valois, Priest and Confessor, who was the Founder of the Order of the most holy Trinity for the redemption of captives, and fell asleep in the Lord on the 4th day of November.

entries.lat: In Pérside pássio sanctórum Nersæ Epíscopi, et Sociórum.
entries.eng: In Persia, the passion of the holy Bishop Nerses and his Companions.

entries.lat: Messánæ, in Sicília, sanctórum Mártyrum Ampéli et Caji.
entries.eng: At Messina, in Sicily, the holy martyrs Ampelus and Caius.

entries.lat: Tauríni sanctórum Mártyrum Octávii, Solutóris et Adventóris, Thebánæ legiónis mílitum; qui, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, egrégie decertántes, martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: At Turin, the holy martyrs Octavius, Solutor, and Adventor, soldiers of the Theban legion, who contended gloriously under the Emperor Maximian, and were crowned with martyrdom.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Agápii Mártyris, qui, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, damnátus ad béstias et ab iis nil læsus, tandem, lapídibus ad pedes appénsis, in mare demérgitur.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyr Agapius, who was condemned to the wild beasts under the Emperor Galerius Maximian but as they did not hurt him, he was sunk in the sea with stones tied to his feet.

entries.lat: Doróstori, in Mýsia inferióre, sancti Dásii Mártyris, qui, cum in festo Satúrni nollet impudicítiis ejus consentíre, sub Basso Prǽside cæsus est.
entries.eng: At Dorostorum, in Mysia, holy Dasius, Bishop (of that see,) who was beheaded under the President Bassus, because he would not join in the uncleanliness of the Feast of Saturn.

entries.lat: Nicǽæ, in Bithýnia, sanctórum Mártyrum Eustáchii, Thespésii et Anatólii, in persecutióne Maximiáni.
entries.eng: At Nice, in Bithynia, in the persecution under Maximinus, the holy martyrs Eustace, Thespesius, and Anatolius.

entries.lat: Heracléæ, in Thrácia, sanctórum Mártyrum Bassi, Dionýsii, Agapíti et aliórum quadragínta.
entries.eng: At Heraclea, in Thrace, the holy martyrs Bassus, Denys, Agapitus, and forty others.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Eadmúndi, Regis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: In England, St. Edmund, King and Martyr.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Gregórii Decapolítæ, qui ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum multa passus est.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Gregory of Decapolis, who suffered many things for honouring the holy images.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Benígni Epíscopi, qui, in magna barbarórum perturbatióne, commíssam sibi Ecclésiam summa constántia et religióne administrávit.
entries.eng: At Milan, (in the fifth century,) holy Benignus, Bishop (of that see,) who, in the midst of all the troubles caused by the incoming of the barbarians, ministered in all steadfastness and godliness unto the Church committed to his care.

entries.lat: Cabillóne, in Gálliis, sancti Silvéstri Epíscopi, qui quadragésimo secúndo sui sacerdótii anno, plenus diérum atque virtútum, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Chalons, (in the sixth century,) holy Sylvester, Bishop (of that see,) who passed away to be ever with the Lord, full of days and graces, in the forty-second year of his priesthood.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Simplícii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, (likewise in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Simplicius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Hildeshémii, in Saxónia, sancti Bernwárdi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui a Cælestíno Papa Tértio in Sanctórum númerum adscríptus est.
entries.eng: At Hildesheim, in Saxony, St. Bernward, Bishop and Confessor, who was enrolled in the number of the Saints by Pope Celestine III.

entries.lat: Hierosólymis Præsentátio beátæ Dei Genitrícis Vírginis Maríæ in Templo.
entries.eng: At Jerusalem, the Presentation of the blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God, in the Temple.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális beáti Rufi, de quo sanctus Paulus Apóstolus ad Romános scribit.
entries.eng: Holy Rufus, touching whom the holy Apostle Paul writeth unto the Romans.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctórum Celsi et Cleméntis.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Celsus and Clement.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, sancti Albérti, Epíscopi Leodiénsis et Mártyris; qui pro tuénda ecclesiástica libertáte necátus est.
entries.eng: At Rheims, the holy martyr Albert, Bishop of Liege, who was slain for defending the freedom of the Church.

entries.lat: Apud Ostia Tiberína natális sanctórum Mártyrum Demétrii et Honórii.
entries.eng: At Ostia, the holy martyrs Demetrius and Honorius.

entries.lat: In Hispánia sanctórum Mártyrum Honórii, Eutýchii et Stéphani.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy Martyrs Honorius, Eutychius and Stephen.

entries.lat: In Pamphýlia sancti Heliodóri Mártyris, in persecutióne Aureliáni, sub Aétio Prǽside. Post eum vero ipsi tortóres, convérsi ad fidem, in mare demérsi sunt.
entries.eng: In Pamphylia, under the President Aetius, in the persecution under the Emperor Aurelian, the holy martyr Heliodorus, by whom his very torturers were converted to the faith for the which cause they were drowned in the sea.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Gelásii Papæ Primi, doctrína et sanctitáte conspícui.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy Pope Gelasius, famous for his teaching and holiness.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Mauri, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, the holy Confessor Maurus, Bishop (of that see.) At the monastery of Bobbio, deceased the holy Abbot Columbanus, the founder of many monasteries, and the Father of many monks, who fell asleep in a good old age, bright with many graces.

entries.lat: In monastério Bobiénsi deposítio sancti Columbáni Abbátis, qui, multórum cœnóbiorum fundátor, plurimórum Monachórum éxstitit Pater, multísque virtútibus clarus, in senectúte bona quiévit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Bobbio, the burial of the holy Abbot Columbanus, who, the founder of many monasteries, was the Father of very many Monks, and being renowned for many virtues, rested in a good old age.

entries.lat: Sanctæ Cæcíliæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ ad cæléstem Sponsum, próprio sánguine purpuráta, transívit sextodécimo Kaléndas Octóbris.
entries.eng: St. Cecilia, Virgin and Martyr, who, empurpled with her own blood, passed to her heavenly Spouse on the 16th day of September.

entries.lat: Colóssis, in Phrýgia, sanctórum Philémonis et Apphíæ, sancti Pauli discipulórum; qui, sub Neróne Imperatóre, cum Gentíles, in die festo Diánæ, invasíssent Ecclésiam, ambo, céteris fugiéntibus, tenti, jussu Artoclis Prǽsidis verbéribus cæsi sunt, et, usque ad renes in fóveam inclúsi, lapídibus opprimúntur.
entries.eng: At Colossae, in Phrygia, the holy martyrs Philemon and Apphia, the disciples of the holy Apostle Paul, (unto whom he addressed an Epistle.) During the reign of the Emperor Nero, the Gentiles broke into the Church upon the feast day of Diana. The rest of the faithful escaped, but these were taken, and by command of the President Artocles they were flogged, buried up to the middle, and stoned to death.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Mauri Mártyris, qui, cum ex Africa venísset ad sepúlcra Apostolórum, sub Imperatóre Numeriáno et Urbis Præfécto Celeríno agonizávit.
entries.eng: Likewise, at Rome, the holy martyr Maurus, who came from Africa to visit the graves of the Apostles, and suffered under the Emperor Numerian, and the Prefect of the city, Celerinus.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ Pisídiæ pássio sanctórum Marci et Stéphani, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Antioch, in Pisidia, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Mark and Stephen.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Pragmátii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Autun, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Pragmatius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Natális sancti Cleméntis Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, tértius post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Pontificátum ténuit, et, in persecutióne Trajáni, apud Chersonésum relegátus, ibi, alligáta ad ejus collum ánchora, præcipitátus in mare, martýrio coronátur. Ipsíus autem corpus, Hadriáno Secúndo Summo Pontífice, a sanctis Cyríllo et Methódio frátribus Romam translátum, in Ecclésia quæ ejus nómine ántea fúerat exstrúcta, honorífice recónditum est.
entries.eng: The holy Pope Clement, he was the third, after the blessed Apostle Peter, who held the Papacy. In the persecution under the Emperor Trajan he was sent to the Crimea, where he was sunk in the sea with an anchor tied to his neck, and so received the crown of martyrdom. In the time of Pope Nicholas I his body was brought to Rome and honourably buried in the church which had already been built in his name.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Felicitátis Mártyris, septem filiórum Mártyrum matris; quæ, post eos, jubénte Marco Antoníno Imperatóre, decolláta est pro Christo.
entries.eng: Likewise, at Rome, the holy martyr Felicity, mother of seven sons, who were all likewise martyrs. After they had suffered, the Emperor Mark Antonine commanded her also to be beheaded for Christ's sake.

entries.lat: Cýzici, in Hellespónto, sancti Sisínii Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, post multa torménta, gládio cæsus est.
