entries.eng: At Cyzicus, on the Hellespont, the holy martyr Sisinius, who was slain with the sword, after suffering many torments, during the same persecution.

entries.lat: Eméritæ, in Hispánia, sanctæ Lucrétiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ in eádem persecutióne, sub Daciáno Prǽside, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Merida, in Spain, the holy Virgin and martyr Lucretia, who suffered martyrdom under the President Dacian, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

entries.lat: Icónii, in Lycaónia, sancti Amphilóchii Epíscopi, qui, sanctórum Basilíi et Gregórii Nazianzéni in erémo sócius et in Episcopátu colléga, tandem, post multa quæ suscépit pro cathólica fide certámina, sanctitáte et doctrína clarus, quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Iconium, in Lycaonia, holy Amphilochius, Bishop (of that see,) the fellow of holy Basil and Gregory of Nazianzus, in the desert and in the Episcopate. He went through many contendings for the Catholic faith's sake, but fell asleep at length in peace, famous for holiness and teaching.

entries.lat: Agrigénti deposítio sancti Gregórii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Girgenti, in Sicily, (at the end of the sixth century,) deceased holy Gregory, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In óppido Hasbániæ, in Bélgio, sancti Trudónis, Presbýteri et Confessóris, cujus nómine póstmodum insignítum fuit tum monastérium illic ab eódem Sancto in suis prǽdiis eréctum, tum ipsum óppidum in eo loco paulátim exstrúctum.
entries.eng: In the town of Hesbaye, in Belgium, St. Trudo, Priest and Confessor, whose name was afterwards given both to the monastery there erected by the same Saint on his own estates, and to the town itself which was gradually built up in that place.

entries.lat: Sancti Joánnis a Cruce Presbýteri, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, sanctæ Terésiæ in Carmelitárum reformatióne sócii, cujus dies natális décimo nono Kaléndas Januárii recensétur.
entries.eng: St. John of the Cross, Priest, Confessor and Doctor of the Church, the companion of St. Teresa in the reform of the Carmelites, whose birthday is recorded on the 14th day of December.

entries.lat: Eódem die natális sancti Chrysógoni Mártyris, qui, post longa víncula et cárceres pro constantíssima Christi confessióne tolerátos, Aquiléjam, jubénte Diocletiáno, perdúctus, tandem, cæsus cápite et in mare projéctus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: The holy martyr Chrysogonus, who long endured bonds and imprisonment for his steadfast confession of Christ, but was at length brought to Aquileia by command of Diocletian, and was there beheaded, whereafter his body was cast into the sea, and so he finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Crescentiáni Mártyris, qui in passióne beáti Marcélli Papæ memorátur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Crescentian, of whom record is made in the history of the last sufferings of the blessed Pope Marcellus.

entries.lat: Apud Corínthum sancti Alexándri Mártyris, qui, sub Juliáno Apóstata et Sallústio Prǽside, pro Christi fide certávit usque ad mortem.
entries.eng: At Corinth, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate and the President Sallust, the holy martyr Alexander, who fought for Christ's faith even unto death.

entries.lat: Perúsiæ sancti Felicíssimi Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Perugia, the holy martyr Felicissimus.

entries.lat: Amériæ, in Umbria, sanctæ Firmínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, várie cruciáta est, ac demum, suspénsa et lampádibus ardéntibus adústa, immaculátum spíritum Deo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Amelia, in Umbria, the holy Virgin and martyr Firmina in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian she was put to diverse torments, but was at length hung up and burnt with lamps, until she gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum Floræ et Maríæ; quæ, post diutúrnos cárceres, in persecutióne Arábica, gládio interémptæ sunt.
entries.eng: At Cordova, the holy Virgins and martyrs Flora and Mary, who were long imprisoned, and then slain with the sword, in the persecution under the Arabs.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Protásii Epíscopi, qui apud Constántem Imperatórem in Concílio Sardicénsi causam Athanásii deféndit, ac demum, pro Ecclésia sibi commíssa et pro religióne multis perfúnctus labóribus, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Protasius, Bishop (of that see,) who defended the cause of Athanasius before the Emperor Constans in the Council of Sardica, and passed away to be ever with the Lord, worn out by many toils for the sake of religion and of the Church committed to his care.

entries.lat: In território Arvernénsi sancti Portiáni Abbátis, qui, sub Theodoríco Rege, miráculis cláruit; cujus étiam nomen índitum mansit tam monastério cui Sanctus ipse prǽfuit, quam óppido quod in eódem loco póstea constrúctum fuit.
entries.eng: In Auvergne, (in the sixth century,) holy Portian, Abbot (of Mirande,) who was famous for miracles, under King Theodoric.

entries.lat: In castro Blávio, in Gállia, sancti Románi Presbýteri, cujus sanctitátis præcónium glória miraculórum declárat.
entries.eng: At Blaye, (in the fourth century,) the holy Priest Romanus, the praise of whose holiness is proclaimed by the glory of his miracles.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctæ Catharínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, ob fídei Christiánæ confessiónem, sub Maximíno Imperatóre, in cárcerem trusa, et póstmodum scorpiónibus diutíssime cæsa, tandem cápitis obtruncatióne martýrium complévit. Ipsíus corpus, in montem Sínai mirabíliter ab Angelis delátum, ibídem, frequénti Christianórum concúrsu, pia veneratióne cólitur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy Virgin and martyr Katharine. On account of her confession of the Christian faith, she was cast into prison under the Emperor Maximinus. She was long flogged with loaded scourges, and at length beheaded. Her body was in wondrous wise carried by angels to Mount Sinai, where it is devoutly honoured by the pilgrimages of multitudes of Christians.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Móysis, Presbýteris et Mártyris; quem, cum áliis deténtum in cárcere, sanctus Cypriánus per lítteras sæpe est consolátus. Ipse autem Móyses, cum non tantum advérsus Gentíles, sed étiam advérsus schismáticos et hæréticos Novatiános infrácto ánimo stetísset, demum (ut sanctus Cornélius Papa testátur), in persecutióne Décii, exímio et admirábili martýrio decorátus est.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Moses, a Priest, who was among those whom holy Cyprian oftentimes comforted by his letters while they were kept in prison. He contended manfully not only against the Gentiles, but also against the schismatics and Novatian heretics. At length, as is attested by holy Pope Cornelius, he was crowned with an eminent martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sancti Erásmi Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyr Erasmus.

entries.lat: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, pássio sancti Mercúrii mílitis, qui custodiéntis se Angeli patrocínio et bárbaros vicit, et Décii sævítiam superávit; multísque auctus tormentórum trophǽis, martýrio coronátus migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Mercury. He was a soldier, who, by the help of his Guardian Angel, overcame the barbarians and the cruelty of the Emperor Decius, and passed away to heaven crowned with a martyrdom adorned by victory over many torments.

entries.lat: In Æmília, Itáliæ província, sanctæ Jucúndæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: In the province of Aemilia, the holy Virgin Jucunda.

entries.lat: Apud Fabriánum, in Picéno, beáti Silvéstri Abbátis, Institutóris Congregatiónis Monachórum Silvestrinórum.
entries.eng: At Fabriano, in the March of Ancona, the blessed Abbot Silvester, founder of the Congregation of Monks of the Order of St Benedict, who are called Silvestrians.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ natális sancti Petri, ejúsdem urbis Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum esset ómnibus virtútibus exornátus, ibídem, Galérii Maximiáni præcépto, cápite obtruncátus est.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Peter, Pope of that city, a man enriched with all graces, who was beheaded by order of the Emperor Galerius Maximian.

entries.lat: Passi sunt étiam Alexandríæ, in eádem persecutióne, sancti Mártyres Faustus Présbyter, Dídius et Ammónius, itémque Epíscopi quátuor Ægýptii, idest Philéas, Hesýchius, Pachómius et Theodórus, cum áliis sexcéntis sexagínta, quos persecutiónis gládius evéxit ad cælos.
entries.eng: Likewise at Alexandria, in the same persecution, the holy martyrs Faustus a Priest, Didius, and Ammonius, along with whom are commemorated the Egyptian Bishops Phileas, Hesychius, Pachomius, and Theodore, and six hundred and sixty Others, who were raised to heaven by the sword of the persecutor.

entries.lat: Apud villam cui nomen Fracta, in território Rhodigiénsi, sancti Bellíni, Epíscopi Patavíni et Mártyris; qui a sicáriis, cum esset Ecclésiæ jurium defénsor exímius, crudéliter impetítus ac multis illátis vulnéribus occísus est.
entries.eng: At the village called Fratta, in the territory of Rovigo, St. Bellinus, Bishop of Padua and Martyr; who, being a most eminent defender of the rights of the Church, was cruelly set upon by assassins and killed with many wounds.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ sancti Marcélli Presbýteri, qui, Constántii témpore, ab Ariánis e rupe præcipitátus, Martyr occúbuit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy Priest Marcellus, who in the time of the Emperor Constantius was thrown over a cliff by the Arians, and so died a martyr.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Sirícii, Papæ et Confessóris, doctrína, pietáte et religiónis zelo præclári, qui vários damnávit hæréticos, et discíplinam ecclesiásticam salubérrimis decrétis instaurávit.
entries.eng: At Padua, the holy martyr Bellinus, Bishop (of that see.) At Rome, (at the end of the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Pope Siricius, very famous for his teaching, godliness, and zeal for the faith. He condemned diverse heretics and restored the discipline of the Church by healthy enactments.

entries.lat: Augustodúni sancti Amatóris Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Autun, the holy Bishop Amator.

entries.lat: Constántiæ, in Germánia, sancti Conrádi Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Autun, (in the third century,) holy Amator, Bishop (of that see.) At Constance, (in the tenth century,) holy Conrad, Bishop (of that see.) In the country of Rheims, (in the seventh century,) the holy Confessor Basolus.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Leonárdi a Portu Maurítio, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Confessóris, zelo animárum et sacris per Itáliam expeditiónibus conspícui; quem Pius Nonus, Póntifex Máximus, in Sanctórum cánonem rétulit, ac Pius Papa Undécimus cæléstem Patrónum Sacerdótum qui ad sacras populáres Missiónes in regiónibus cathólicis ubíque terrárum incúmbunt, elégit et constítuit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Leonard of Port Maurice, of the Order of Friars Minor of the stricter observance, who was famous for his zeal for the salvation of souls and his holy journeys throughout Italy, and whose name the Supreme Pontiff Pius IX enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: In território Rheménsi natális sancti Básoli Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the territory of Rheims, the birthday of the holy Confessor Basolus.

entries.lat: Hadrianópoli, in Paphlagónia, sancti Styliáni Anachorétæ, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Adrianople, in Paphlagonia, the holy hermit Stylian, who was famous for miracles.

entries.lat: In Arménia sancti Nicónis Mónachi.
entries.eng: In Armenia, (in the tenth century,) the holy monk Nicon.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Basiléi Epíscopi, Auxílii et Saturníni.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Basileus, Patriarch (of that see,) Auxilius, and Saturninus.

entries.lat: Sebáste, in Arménia, sanctórum Mártyrum Hirenárchi, Acácii Presbýteri, ac septem mulíerum. Harum porro constántia Hirenárchus commótus, ad Christum convérsus, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Máximo Prǽside, una cum Acácio, secúri percútitur.
entries.eng: At Sebaste, in Armenia, the holy martyrs Hirenarchus, the Priest Acacius, and seven women. It was the constancy of these women which moved Hirenarchus to turn to Christ, and he was beheaded along with Acacius, under Diocletian the Emperor and Maximus the President.

entries.lat: Apud Cæam flúvium, in Gallǽcia, sanctórum Facúndi et Primitívi, qui sub Attico Prǽside passi sunt.
entries.eng: At the river Cea, in Galicia, the holy martyrs Facundus and Primitivus, who suffered under the President Atticus.

entries.lat: In Pérside sancti Jacóbi intercísi, Mártyris conspícui, qui, témpore Theodósii junióris, cum in Isdegérdis Regis grátiam Christum negásset, et proptérea mater ejus et uxor ab ipsíus se consuetúdine subtraxíssent, hinc, in se revérsus, intrépide coram Vararáne, Isdegérdis fílio ac successóre, se Christiánum esse conféssus est; ideóque ab iráto Rege, lata in eum mortis senténtia, membrátim jussus est concídi et cápite obtruncári. Quo étiam témpore innúmeri álii Mártyres ibídem passi sunt.
entries.eng: In Persia, the holy martyr James, styled the Dismembered, a famous martyr. In the time of the Emperor Theodosius the younger, to please King Isdegerd, he denied Christ, wherefore his mother and his wife held aloof from him. Then he bethought himself, and went to the King and confessed Christ, and the King in wrath commanded him to be cut limb from limb, and his head to be cut off. At that time countless other martyrs suffered there also.

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ sancti Valeriáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, (in the fourth century,) holy Valerian, Bishop (of that see).

entries.lat: Apud Régium, in Gállia, sancti Máximi, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, usque a primǽvæ ætátis annis omni virtútum grátia prǽditus, primum Lirinénsis cœnóbii Pater, deínde Regiénsis Ecclésiæ Epíscopus, signis et prodígiis ínclytus éxstitit.
entries.eng: At Riez, in France, the holy Bishop and Confessor Maximus; who, endowed from the years of his earliest age with the grace of every virtue, was first Father of the monastery of Lerins, and then Bishop of the Church of Riez, and was renowned for signs and wonders.

entries.lat: Salisbúrgi, in Nórico, sancti Virgílii, Epíscopi et Carinthiórum Apóstoli, qui a Gregório Nono, Pontífice Máximo, in Sanctórum númerum adscríptus est.
entries.eng: At Salzburg, (in the eighth century,) the holy Confessor Farrell, an Irishman, Bishop (of that see,) and Apostle of Carinthia, whose name the Supreme Pontiff Gregory IX enrolled among those of the Saints.

entries.lat: Apud Indos, Persis finítimos, sanctórum Bárlaam et Jósaphat, quorum actus mirándos sanctus Joánnes Damascénus conscrípsit.
entries.eng: In India, toward the borders of Persia, holy Barlaam and Josaphat, whose wonderful acts were written by holy John of Damascus.

entries.lat: Lutétiæ Parisiórum deposítio sancti Severíni, Mónachi et Solitarii.
entries.eng: At Paris, (in the sixth century,) deceased the holy Monk and Solitary Severinus.

entries.lat: Apud Corínthum natális sancti Sósthenis, ex beáti Pauli Apóstoli discípulis; cujus mentiónem facit idem Apóstolus Corínthiis scribens. Ipse autem Sósthenes, ex príncipe Synagógæ convérsus ad Christum, fídei suæ primórdia, ante Galliónem Procónsulem ácriter verberátus, præcláro inítio consecrávit.
entries.eng: At Corinth, holy Sosthenes, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul, of whom the same Apostle doth make mention in writing unto the Corinthians. He was the chief man of the synagogue when he turned to Christ, and eminently hallowed the first-fruits of his faith by being sharply beaten in the presence of Gallio the Proconsul.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Rufi, quem, cum omni família sua, Christi Mártyrem Diocletiánus fecit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Rufus, with all his house, whom Diocletian made martyrs unto Christ.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Papiniáni et Mansuéti Episcopórum, qui, témpore Wandálicæ persecutiónis, sub Rege Ariáno Genseríco, pro fídei cathólicæ defensióne, candéntibus ferri láminis toto córpore adústi, gloriósum agónem consummárunt. Quo étiam témpore álii novem sancti Epíscopi, scílicet Valeriánus, Urbánus, Crescens, Eustáchius, Crescónius, Crescentiánus, Felix, Hortulánus et Florentiánus, damnáti exsílio, cursum vitæ suæ implevérunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs the Bishops Papinian and Mansuetus.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Stéphani junióris, Basilíi, Petri, Andréæ, et Sociórum trecentórum et trigínta novem Monachórum; qui, sub Constantíno Coprónymo, pro sanctárum Imáginum cultu váriis excruciáti supplíciis, veritátem cathólicam effúso sánguine confirmárunt.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy martyrs Stephen the younger, Basil, Peter, Andrew, and their Companions, even three hundred and thirty-nine monks, who for the honouring of holy images under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus were put to diverse cruel torments, and sealed their confession of the Catholic truth by the outpouring of their blood.

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, deposítio sancti Jacóbi Picéni, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Confessóris, vitæ asperitáte, apostólica prædicatióne ac plúribus pro re Christiána óbitis legatiónibus præclári; quem Benedíctus Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum fastis adjúnxit.
entries.eng: At Naples, the holy Confessor James of Picenum, of the Order of Friars Minor, famous for the sharp self-denial of his life, for his Apostolic preaching, and for the embassages which he undertook for Christendom's sake, whose name the Supreme Pontiff Benedict XIII enrolled among those of the saints.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Salária, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Saturníni senis, et Sisínii Diáconi, sub Maximiáno Príncipe; quos, diu in cárcere macerátos, jussit Urbis Præféctus in equúleum levári et áttrahi nervis, fústibus ac scorpiónibus cædi, deínde eis flammas appóni, et, depósitos de equúleo, cápite truncári.
entries.eng: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Saturninus the Elder, and Sisinius the Deacon. They suffered long in prison, and the Prefect of the city then commanded them to be stretched upon the rack, and drawn with thongs, to be flogged with cudgels and loaded scourges, then tormented with fire, and at last to be taken down from the rack and beheaded.

entries.lat: Tolósæ sancti Saturníni Epíscopi, qui, tempóribus Décii, in Capitólio ejúsdem urbis a Pagánis tentus atque de summa Capitólii arce per omnes gradus præcipitátus est, atque ita, cápite collíso, excussóque cérebro, et toto córpore dilaniáto, dignam Christo ánimam réddidit.
entries.eng: At Toulouse, the holy martyr Saturninus, Bishop (of that see,) who, in the time of the Emperor Decius, was tried by the pagans in the capitol of the same city, and cast down the steps from the summit thereof, so that his head was broken, and his brain scattered, and his whole body mangled, and he gave up his worthy soul to Christ.

entries.lat: Item pássio sanctórum Parámonis et Sociórum trecentórum septuagínta quinque, sub Décio Imperatóre et Aquilíno Prǽside.
entries.eng: Likewise, under Decius the Emperor and Aquilinus the President, the holy martyrs Paramon and three hundred and seventy-five others, his Companions.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, sancti Philómeni Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Aureliáni Imperatóris, sub Felíce Prǽside, igne probátus, mánibus pedibúsque ac demum cápite clavis confíxo, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, the holy martyr Philomen, who, under the President Felix, in the persecution under the Emperor Aurelian, was tried with fire, and then had nails driven into his hands and feet, and at last into his head, and so finished his testimony.

entries.lat: Vérulis, in Hérnicis, sanctórum Mártyrum Blásii et Demétrii.
entries.eng: At Veroli, the holy martyrs Blaise and Demetrius.

entries.lat: Tudérti, in Umbria, sanctæ Illuminátæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: At Todi, (in the fourth century,) the holy Virgin Illuminata.

entries.lat: Apud Patras, in Achája, natális sancti Andréæ Apóstoli, qui in Thrácia et Scýthia sacrum Christi Evangélium prædicávit. Is, ab Ægéa Procónsule comprehénsus, primum in cárcere clausus est, deínde gravíssime cæsus, ad últimum suspénsus in cruce, in ea pópulum docens bíduo supervíxit; et, rogáto Dómino ne eum síneret de cruce depóni, circúmdatus est magno splendóre de cælo, et, abscedénte póstmodum lúmine, emísit spíritum.
entries.eng: At Patrae, in the Peloponnesus, the holy Apostle Andrew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in Thrace and Scythia. He was arrested by the Proconsul Aegeas, and first imprisoned, then heavily flogged, and, lastly, crucified. He remained alive upon the cross through the second day, and taught the people. He besought the Lord not to suffer him to be taken down from the cross, and then a great light from heaven shone round about him, and when it faded away he gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctórum Cástuli et Euprépitis.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs Castulus and Euprepis.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctæ Mauræ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Virgin and martyr Maura.

entries.lat: Item sanctæ Justínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: Likewise, the holy Virgin and martyr Justina.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Constántii Confessóris, qui, fórtiter Pelagiánis resistens, ab eórum factióne pértulit multa, quæ illum sanctis Confessóribus sociárunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Constantius, who manfully withstood the Pelagians, and bore much at their hands, the which contendings have gained him a place among the holy Confessors.

entries.lat: Apud Sántonas, in Gállia, sancti Trojáni Epíscopi, magnæ sanctitátis viri, qui, sepúltus in terris, se in cælis vívere multis virtútibus maniféstat.
entries.eng: At Saintes, (in the sixth century,) holy Trojan, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, who, albeit he be buried in the earth, yet showeth by many works of power that he is alive in heaven.

entries.lat: In Palæstína beáti Zósimi Confessóris, qui, sub Justíno Imperatóre, sanctitáte et miráculis fuit insígnis.
entries.eng: In Palestine, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Zosimus, who was eminent for holiness and miracles in the time of the Emperor Justin.

entries.lat: Sancti Nahum Prophétæ, in Bégabar quiescéntis.
entries.eng: The Prophet Nahum, who sleepeth in Begabar.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Diodóri Presbýteri, et Mariáni Diáconi, cum áliis plúribus, qui, sub Numeriáno Príncipe, cum in Arenário natalítia Mártyrum ágerent, illic, obstrúcta a persecutóribus jánua cryptæ ac díruta désuper mole, martýrii glóriam meruérunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs the Priest Diodorus, and the Deacon Marianus with many others, who gained the glory of martyrdom by command of the Emperor Numerian.

entries.lat: Item Romæ pássio sanctórum Lúcii, Rogáti, Cassiáni et Cándidæ.
entries.eng: There likewise the holy martyrs Lucius, Rogatus, Cassian, and Candida.

entries.lat: Nárniæ sancti Próculi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, post multa egrégia ópera, a Rege Gothórum Tótila jussus est decollári.
entries.eng: At Narni, the holy martyr Proculus, Bishop (of that see,) who, after many good works, was beheaded by order of Totila, King of the Goths.

entries.lat: In civitáte Casalénsi sancti Evásii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At the city of Casala, the holy martyr Evasius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Ansáni Mártyris, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, Romæ conféssus Christum et in cárcerem trusus, deínde Senas, in Túscia, perdúctus, ibídem cápitis obtruncatióne cursum martýrii perfécit.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyr Ansanus, who confessed Christ at Rome, under the Emperor Diocletian, and was cast into prison then was brought to Sienna, in Tuscany, where he was beheaded, and so finished the course of his testimony,.

entries.lat: Amériæ, in Umbria, sancti Olympíadis, viri Consuláris, qui a beáta Firmína ad fidem est convérsus, et sub Diocletiáno, in equúleo tortus, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Ameria, in Umbria, under the same Diocletian, the holy martyr Olympias. He was a man of consular rank, who had been converted by blessed Firmina, and died upon the rack,.

entries.lat: Arbéle, in Pérside, sancti Ananíæ Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Arbela, in Persia, the holy martyr Ananias.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Castritiáni Epíscopi, qui, in máxima Ecclésiæ perturbatióne, virtútum méritis ac rerum pie religioséque gestárum laude enítuit.
entries.eng: At Milan, holy Castritian, Bishop (of that see,) who gained great praise for his worthy acts and his godly and pious conduct of affairs during the most troublous times of the Church.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Ursicíni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, holy Ursicinus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Noviómi, in Bélgio, sancti Elígii Epíscopi, cujus vitam admirándam múltiplex signórum númerus comméndat.
entries.eng: At Noyon, in Belgium, the holy Bishop Eligius, whose admirable life is commended by the manifold number of his miracles.

entries.lat: Apud Virodúnum, in Gállia, sancti Ageríci Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verdun, holy Ageric, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctæ Natáliæ, uxóris beáti Hadriáni Mártyris, quæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, sanctis Martýribus, Nicomedíæ in cárcere deténtis, multo témpore ministrávit; impletóque eórum certámine, Constantinópolim est profécta, et ibídem in pace quiévit.
entries.eng: On the same day, holy Natalia, the wife of the blessed martyr Hadrian. She ministered for a long time to the holy martyrs who were kept in prison at Nicomedia under the Emperor Diocletian, and after their battle was over went to Constantinople, where she fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Romæ pássio sanctæ Bibiánæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, sub Juliáno Imperatóre sacrílego, ob Christum támdiu plumbátis cæsa est, donec rédderet spíritum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Bibiana, who under, the profane Emperor Julian was for Christ's sake flogged to death with scourges loaded with lead.

entries.lat: Apud Forum Cornélii, in Æmília, natális sancti Petri, Epíscopi Ravennátis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cognoménto Chrysólogi, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus tamen festum prídie Nonas hujus mensis recólitur.
entries.eng: At Imola, holy Peter, Bishop of Ravenna, styled Chrysologus, (or him of the golden words,) famous for his teaching and holiness, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of this present month.

entries.lat: In Sanciáno, Sinárum ínsula, item natális sancti Francísci Xavérii, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris, Indiárum Apóstoli, géntium conversióne, donis et miráculis clari; qui plenus méritis et labóribus obdormívit in Dómino. Ipsum beátum virum Pius Décimus, Póntifex Máximus, cæléstem sodalitáti et óperi Propagándæ Fídei Protectórem elégit atque constítuit; Pius vero Papa Undécimus peculiárem ómnibus Missiónibus Patrónum dedit et confirmávit. Ejus autem festívitas, jussu Alexándri Papæ Séptimi, sequénti die celebrátur.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, (at the end of the 2nd century,) the holy martyr Pontian and four others.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Eusébii Presbýteri, Marcélli Diáconi, Hippólyti, Máximi, Adriæ, Paulínæ, Neónis, Maríæ, Martánæ et Auréliæ; qui omnes in persecutióne Valeriáni, sub Secundiáno Júdice, martýrium complevérunt.
entries.eng: There likewise, the holy martyrs the Priest Eusebius, the Deacon Marcellus, Hippolytus, Maximus, Adria, Paulina, Neo, Mary, Martana, and Aurelia, who suffered martyrdom under the judge Secundian, in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian,.

entries.lat: Item Romæ sancti Pontiáni Mártyris, cum áliis quátuor.
entries.eng: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyr Pontian, with four others.

entries.lat: In Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sevéri, Secúri, Januárii et Victoríni; qui ibídem martýrio coronáti sunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Severus, Securus, Januarius, and Victorinus, who were there crowned with martyrdom, At Aquileia, the holy Confessor Chromatius, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Aquiléjæ sancti Chromátii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Aquileia, the holy Bishop and Confessor Chromatius.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Lupi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Verona, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Lupus, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Edéssæ, in Sýria, sancti Nonni Epíscopi, cujus précibus Pelágia pǽnitens ad Christum convérsa est.
entries.eng: At Edessa, holy Nonnus, Bishop (first of that see, and afterwards of Heliopolis in Syria,) through whose prayers Pelagia the penitent was converted to Christ.

entries.lat: Tróade, in Phrýgia, sancti Silváni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Troas, in Phrygia, holy Bishop Silvanus, famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Evásii Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, the holy Bishop Evasius.

entries.lat: Sancti Francísci Xavérii, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris, Indiárum Apóstoli, sodalitátis et óperis Propagándæ Fídei atque Missiónum ómnium Patróni cæléstis; qui prídie hujus diéi quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: In the island of San-Chan, in the Canton River, in China, holy Francis Xavier of the Society of Jesus, Apostle of the Indies, illustrious for the conversion of the Gentiles, for gifts and miracles, who died, full of good works and labours, upon this present 2nd day of December, but his feast is kept upon the morrow by order of Alexander VII.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sancti Sophoníæ Prophétæ.
entries.eng: In Judea, the holy Prophet Sophonias.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii Tribúni, et uxóris Hiláriæ, filiórum Jásonis et Mauri, cum septuagínta milítibus. Ex eis Cláudium jussit Numeriánus Imperátor, ingénti saxo alligátum, in flumen præcípitem dari; mílites vero et ipsíus Cláudii fílios capitáli senténtia puníri. Beáta autem Hilária, cum filiórum córpora sepelísset, paulo post, orans ad eórum sepúlcrum, tenta est a Pagánis, et, in cárcerem trusa, migrávit ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyrs the Tribune Claudius, his wife Hilaria, their sons Jason and Marus, and seventy soldiers. The Emperor Numerian commanded a great stone to be tied to Claudius and that he should be cast into the river the soldiers and the sons of Claudius he also caused to be put to death. The blessed Hilaria buried the bodies of her sons, and was praying at their grave soon after, when she was seized by the heathen, and departed hence to be ever with the Lord,.

entries.lat: Tingi, in Mauritánia, pássio sancti Cassiáni Mártyris, qui, cum exceptóris diu gessísset offícium, tandem, admirátus intrépida beáti Marcélli Centuriónis respónsa et immóbilem in Christi fide constántiam, atque cǽlitus inspirátus, exsecrábile duxit Christianórum neci deservíre; ideóque, cum renuntiásset eídem offício, et ipse, sub Christiána professióne, cápite abscíssus, triúmphum méruit obtinére martýrii.
entries.eng: At Tangier, in Morocco, the holy martyr Cassian. He had of a long time discharged the office of a public clerk when the thought came to him from heaven that it was an accursed thing to serve for the slaughter of Christians he resigned his office therefore, and under the public profession of a Christian he earned the victory of martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Item in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Crispíni, Magínæ, Joánnis et Stéphani.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyrs Claudius, Crispin, Magina, John, and Stephen.

entries.lat: In Pannónia sancti Agrícolæ Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Hungary, the holy martyr Agricola.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctórum Ambici, Victóris et Júlii.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Ambicus, Victor, and Julius.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Miroclétis, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cujus aliquándo sanctus Ambrósius méminit.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Confessor Mirocles, Bishop (of that see,) of whom mention is made by holy Ambrose.

entries.lat: Dorcéstriæ, in Anglia, sancti Biríni, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: In England, holy Brian, first Bishop of Dorchester, (he was a Priest of Rome about the year 650, whose feast we keep upon the 5th day of this present month of December.).

entries.lat: Curiæ, in Germánia, sancti Lúcii, Britannórum Regis, qui primus ex iis Régibus fidem Christi suscépit, témpore sancti Eleuthérii Papæ.
entries.eng: At Chur, in Switzerland, holy Lucius, King of the Britons (of Morganweg,) who was the first British prince to receive the faith of Christ, in the time of Pope Eleutherius,.

entries.lat: Senis, in Túscia, sancti Galgáni Eremítæ.
entries.eng: At Sienna, in Tuscany, the holy Hermit Galgan, (of the order of St. Benedict. He lived on a mountain called Siepi, and died in the year 1181.).

entries.lat: Sancti Petri Chrysólogi, Epíscopi Ravennátis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cujus memória quarto Nonas hujus mensis recensétur.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Peter Chrysologus, Archbishop of Ravenna, of whom mention is made upon the 2nd day of this present month of December.

entries.lat: Nicomedíæ pássio sanctæ Bárbaræ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, in persecutióne Maximíni, post diram cárceris maceratiónem, lampadárum adustiónem, mamillárum præcisiónem atque ália torménta, gládio martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, the passion of St. Barbara, Virgin and Martyr; who, in the persecution of Maximinus, after a cruel wasting in prison, burning with torches, the cutting off of her breasts and other torments, consummated her martyrdom by the sword.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctórum Theóphanis et Sociórum.
entries.eng: At Nicomedia, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximin, the holy Virgin and martyr Barbara. After a cruel and wasting imprisonment she endured burning with torches, the cutting off of her breasts, and other torments, and finished her testimony by the sword, At Constantinople, the holy martyr Theophanes and his Companions.

entries.lat: In Ponto beáti Melétii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, cum esset ob eruditiónis prærogatívam præcípuus, ob virtútem tamen animi et vitæ sinceritátem longe magnificéntior éxstitit.
entries.eng: In Pontus, the blessed Confessor Meletius, Bishop (of Sebastopol.) He was a man of extraordinary learning, but this gift was outshone in him by the mightiness of his soul and the straightforwardness of his life.

entries.lat: Bonóniæ sancti Felícis Epíscopi, qui ántea Mediolanénsis Ecclésiæ, sub sancto Ambrósio, Diáconus fúerat.
entries.eng: At Bologna, the holy Bishop Felix, who had formerly been a Deacon of the Church of Milan under St. Ambrose.

entries.lat: In Anglia sancti Osmúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: In England, holy Osmund, Bishop, whose feast we keep upon the 17th day of July, which is the day of the translation of his sacred body. (He was Count of Seez in Normandy, and, following William the Conqueror, was made Count of Dorset and Lord High Chancellor of England. He died in 1099, and was canonised by Pope Calixtus III, in the year 1458.).

entries.lat: Colóniæ Agrippínæ sancti Annónis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Cologne, holy Annon, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: In Mesopotámia sancti Marúthæ Epíscopi, qui Dei Ecclésias, ob persecutiónem Isdegérdis Regis collápsas, in Pérside reparávit, multísque miráculis clarus, apud hostes étiam méruit honorári.
entries.eng: In Mesopotamia, holy Maruthas, Bishop of Tagrit, who raised up again the churches of God in Persia which had been cast down in the persecution under King Isdegerd he was famous for many miracles, and achieved honour even among his enemies. (Several of his works are extant. Tagrit is now Miafarakin.).

entries.lat: Parmæ sancti Bernárdi, Cardinális et ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, ex Ordine Vallis Umbrósæ.
entries.eng: At Parma, holy Bernard, Cardinal-bishop of that city, of the Congregation of the Order of St Benedict, called that of Vallombrosa.

entries.lat: In Judǽa sancti Sabbæ Abbátis, in óppido Cappadóciæ Mútala orti, qui miro sanctitátis exémplo refúlsit, et pro fide cathólica, advérsus impugnántes sanctam Sýnodum Chalcedonénsem, strénue laborávit, ac tandem in ea diœcésis Hierosolymitánæ laura, quæ ipsíus sancti Sabbæ nómine póstmodum est insigníta, requiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Mutalasque, in Cappadocia, the holy Saba, Abbot (in Palestine in the year 531,) who shone in Palestine as a marvellous example of holiness, and toiled manfully for the Catholic faith against those that impugned the holy Council of Chalcedon, (held in the year 451.).

entries.lat: Níciæ, apud Varum flúvium, sancti Bassi Epíscopi, qui, in persecutióne Décii et Valeriáni, a Perénnio Prǽside, ob Christi fidem, equúleo tortus, láminis candéntibus ustus, fústibus et scorpiónibus cæsus, in ignem missus, et, cum inde evasísset illǽsus, duóbus clavis confíxus, illústre martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Nice, upon the river Var, holy Bassus, Bishop (of that see, in the third century.) In the persecution under the Emperors Decius and Valerian the President Perennius caused him for Christ's faith's sake to be racked, burnt with plates of white-hot metal, beaten with cudgels and loaded scourges, cast into the fire, and when he came out therefrom unharmed, to be pierced with two nails, and so he achieved an illustrious martyrdom.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Dalmátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui in persecutióne Maximiáni passus est.
entries.eng: At Pavia, the holy martyr Dalmatius, Bishop (of that see,) who suffered in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian,.

entries.lat: Corfínii, in Pelígnis, sancti Pelíni, Epíscopi Brundusíni, qui, cum ob ejus oratiónem, sub Juliáno Apóstata, templum Martis corruísset, a templórum Pontifícibus diríssime cæsus est, atque, octogínta et quinque vulnéribus confóssus, martýrii corónam proméruit.
entries.eng: In the days of the Emperor Julian the Apostate a temple of Mars fell down in answer to his prayer, wherefore the heathen priests beat him direfully, and he earned the crown of martyrdom by eighty-five wounds,.

entries.lat: Item sancti Anastásii Mártyris, qui, præ ardóre martýrii, sponte se persecutóribus óbtulit.
entries.eng: Likewise, (in the sixth century,) the holy martyr Anastasius, whose desire for martyrdom caused him to show himself of his own will to the persecutors.

entries.lat: Thagúræ, in Africa, sanctórum Mártyrum Júlii, Potámiæ, Crispíni, Felícis, Grati et aliórum septem.
entries.eng: At Thagara, in Africa, the holy martyrs Julius, Potamia, Crispin, Felix, Gratus, and seven others.

entries.lat: Thebéste, in Numídia, sanctæ Crispínæ, nobilíssimæ féminæ, quæ, tempóribus Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, cum sacrificáre nollet, jussu Anolíni Procónsulis decolláta est; quam sanctus Augustínus sæpe láudibus celébrat.
entries.eng: At Thebeste, in Africa, holy Crispina, (of Thagara,) a woman of very high rank, who refused to sacrifice to idols, in the days of the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, and was therefore beheaded by command of the Pro-consul Anolinus, Holy Augustin doth oftentimes speak in her praise.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Nicétii Epíscopi, miræ sanctitátis viri.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Nicetius, Bishop (of that see,) a man of wonderful holiness. (Two of his works are still extant.).

entries.lat: Polýboti, in Asia, sancti Joánnis Epíscopi, cognoménto Thaumatúrgi.
entries.eng: At Polybotus, in Asia, holy John, called the Wonder-worker, Bishop (of that see in the time of the Emperor Leo the Isaurian.).

entries.lat: Myræ, quæ est metrópolis Lýciæ, natális sancti Nicolái, Epíscopi et Confessóris, de quo, inter plura miraculórum insígnia, illud memorábile fertur, quod Imperatórem Constantínum ab intéritu quorúmdam se invocántium, longe constitútus, ad misericórdiam per visum mónitis defléxit et minis.
entries.eng: At Myra, which is the chief city of Lycia, the holy Confessor Nicolas, Bishop (of that see,) of whom among many other signs and wonders it is recorded that when the Emperor Constantine had condemned certain persons to death and these called upon Nicolas, who was alive, and afar off, he appeared unto the Emperor, and bent him to mercy by exhortation and threats.

entries.lat: Eódem die sancti Polychrónii Presbýteri, qui, témpore Constántii Imperatóris, cum ad altáre Missas ágeret, invásus est ab Ariánis et jugulátus.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy priest Polychronius, who was saying Mass in the time of the Emperor Constantius, when the Arians attacked him and slew him, (fourth century.).

entries.lat: In Africa sancti Majórici, fílii sanctæ Dionýsiæ, qui, cum esset adolescéntulus ac torménta pavésceret, matris obtútibus verbísque corroborátus est, et, céteris fórtior factus, in torméntis ánimam réddidit; quem amplexáta mater domi sepelívit, et ad ejus sepúlcrum assídue orare consuévit.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy women Dionysia, Dativa, and Leontia, and the monk Tertius, the physician Aemilian, Boniface, and three others, who in the Vandal persecution under the Arian King Hunneric were tormented in most grievous and manifold ways for their defence of the Catholic faith, and so earned a place among Confessors of Christ,.

entries.lat: Ibídem sanctárum mulíerum Dionýsiæ, quæ sancti Majórici Mártyris éxstitit mater, Datívæ ac Leóntiæ; itémque religiósi viri, nómine Tértii, Æmiliáni médici, et Bonifátii, cum áliis tribus. Hi omnes, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, gravíssimis et innúmeris supplíciis pro cathólicæ fídei defensióne cruciáti, sanctórum Christi Confessórum número sociári meruérunt.
entries.eng: At the same time and place, the holy martyr Majoricus, the son of holy Dionysia. He was but a little lad and was in fear of the torments, but by the looks and words of his mother, he was so strengthened that he became mightier than them all, and died under the torture his mother took his body to her heart, and buried it in their home, and was used to pray instantly at his grave.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctæ Aséllæ Vírginis, quæ (ut beátus Hierónymus scribit), ex útero matris benedícta, vitam in jejúniis et oratiónibus usque ad senéctam prodúxit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Virgin Asella, who, as writeth blessed Jerome, was blessed from her mother's womb, and passed her life in fastings and prayers unto a good old age. (Born about 334 and died about 410.).

entries.lat: Granátæ, in Hispánia, pássio beáti Petri Paschásii, Epíscopi Giennénsis et Mártyris, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum.
entries.eng: At Granada, in Spain, the blessed martyr Peter Paschasius, Bishop of Jaen, of the order of blessed Mary of Ransom for the redemption of captives,.

entries.lat: Sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, qui prídie Nonas Aprílis obdormívit in Dómino, sed hac die potíssimum cólitur, qua Mediolanénsem Ecclésiam gubernándam suscépit.
entries.eng: St. Ambrose, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church, who fell asleep in the Lord on the 4th day of April, but is chiefly honoured on this day, on which he undertook the government of the Church of Milan.

entries.lat: Romæ beáti Eutychiáni Papæ, qui per divérsa loca trecéntos quadragínta duos Mártyres manu sua sepelívit; quibus et ipse deínde sociátus, sub Numeriáno Imperatóre, martýrio coronátus est, et in cœmetério Callísti sepúltus.
entries.eng: At Rome, the blessed Pope Eutychian, who with his own hand buried three hundred and forty-two Martyrs in divers places; and being afterwards himself joined to their company, was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Numerian, and buried in the cemetery of Callistus.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ natális beáti Agathónis militáris, qui, in persecutióne Décii, cum prohíberet quosdam voléntes illúdere cadavéribus Mártyrum, clamor repénte totíus vulgi advérsus eum extóllitur; oblátus autem Júdici, et in Christi confessióne persístens, cápite pro pietáte damnátus est.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the blessed soldier Agatho. During the persecution under the Emperor Decius, there were some that would make mock of the bodies of the martyrs, and Agatho forbade them, whereupon straightway a cry of the whole mob was got up against him, he was brought before the judge, and as he stood firm in the confession of Christ he was beheaded,.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Polycárpi et Theodóri.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Polycarp and Theodore.

entries.lat: Tubúrbi, in Africa, sancti Servi Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, fústibus diutíssime cæsus, tróchleis frequénter in sublíme elevátus atque ictu céleri super sílices póndere córporis dimíssus, et lapídibus acutíssimis perfricátus, martýrii palmam adéptus est.
entries.eng: At Tebourba, in Africa, the holy martyr Servus, who in the Vandal persecution under the Arian king Hunneric, was long cudgelled, repeatedly jerked up with pulleys and dropped upon flints, and scraped with sharp stones, and by this torment gained the palm of martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Theáni, in Campánia, sancti Urbáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Chieti, in the kingdom of Naples, (in the ninth century,) the holy Confessor Urban, Bishop of (that see.).

entries.lat: Apud Sántonas, in Gállia, sancti Martíni Abbátis, ad cujus túmulum crebérrima divínitus fiunt mirácula.
entries.eng: At Saintes, in Gaul, the holy Abbot Martin, at whose grave by the power of God famous miracles are oftentimes wrought. (He was the founder and first Abbot of the Monastery of Sanjon.).

entries.lat: Eboriáci, in território Meldénsi, commemorátio sanctæ Faræ, étiam Burgundofáræ nómine appellátæ, Abbatíssæ et Vírginis, cujus dies natális tértio Nonas Aprílis recensétur.
entries.eng: At Faremoutiers, in the territory of Meaux, the commemoration of St. Fara, also called by the name of Burgundofara, Abbess and Virgin, whose birthday is recorded on the 3rd day of April.

entries.lat: Concéptio Immaculáta gloriósæ semper Vírginis Genitrícis Dei Maríæ, quam fuísse præservátam, singulári Dei privilégio, ab omni originális culpæ labe immúnem, Pius Nonus, Póntifex Máximus, hac ipsa recurrénte die, solémniter definívit.
entries.eng: On the morrow we keep the feast of the glorious Mary, Mother of God, and always a Virgin, whom the supreme Pontiff Pius IX. did upon this day solemnly define to have been by a singular gift of God preserved unstained by original sin.

entries.lat: Tréviris sancti Euchárii, qui fuit discípulus beáti Petri Apóstoli et primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
entries.eng: At Trier, holy Eucharius, a disciple of the blessed Apostle Peter, and the first Bishop of that city.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sancti Macárii Mártyris, qui, témpore Décii, cum a Júdice multis verbis ad negándum Christum suaderétur, et eo majóri constántia suam profiterétur fidem, vivus ad últimum exúri jubétur.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Macarius. Under the Emperor Decius the judge dealt with him in many words to persuade him to deny Christ, but as he only professed his faith the more constantly he was burnt alive,.

entries.lat: In Cypro sancti Sophrónii Epíscopi, qui pupillórum, orphanórum ac viduárum defénsor miríficus, et páuperum atque oppressórum ómnium adjútor fuit.
entries.eng: In Cyprus, the holy Bishop Sophronius, who was a wonderful protector of little children, orphans, and widows, and an helper of all the poor and depressed.

entries.lat: In monastério Luxoviénsi, in Gállia, sancti Romárici Abbátis, qui, cum in aula Theodobérti Regis primus esset, renuntiávit sǽculo, et monásticæ étiam observántiæ laude céteris antecélluit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Lisieux, the holy Abbot Romaric, who was the first man in the court of King Theodobert, but gave up the world, and became the first in monastic observance. (He was a monk of Luxeuil. He founded the Abbey of Remiremont, of which he became second Abbot in the year 627, and died on Dec. 8, 653.).

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Patápii Solitárii, virtútibus et miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy Hermit Patapius, famous for his graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Romæ Invéntio sanctórum Mártyrum Nemésii Diáconi, ejúsque fíliæ Lucíllæ Vírginis, Symphrónii, Olýmpii Tribúni, hujúsque uxóris Exsupériæ et Theodúli fílii; quorum memória octávo Kaléndas Septémbris recensétur.
entries.eng: At Rome, the Finding of the holy Martyrs Nemesius the Deacon, and his daughter the Virgin Lucilla, Symphronius, Olympius the Tribune, and his wife Exuperia and his son Theodulus; whose memory is recorded on the 25th day of August.

entries.lat: Verónæ Ordinátio sancti Zenónis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Verona, is commemorated the ordination of holy Zeno, Bishop (of that see in the fourth century.).

entries.lat: Carthágine sancti Restitúti, Epíscopi et Mártyris, in cujus solemnitáte sanctus Augustínus de ipso ad pópulum sermónem hábuit.
entries.eng: At Carthage, the holy martyr Restitutus, Bishop (of that see,) concerning whom on whose solemn feastday holy Augustine preached a discourse to the people.

entries.lat: Item in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Petri, Succéssi, Bassiáni, Primitívi et aliórum vigínti.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, the holy martyrs Peter, Successus, Bassian, Primitivus, and twenty others.

entries.lat: Toléti, in Hispánia, natális sanctæ Leocádiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni Imperatóris, a Præfécto Hispaniárum Daciáno inclúsa cárcere ac dire maceráta, in eo tandem, cum gravíssimos beátæ Euláliæ et reliquórum Mártyrum cruciátus audísset, impollútum spíritum, génibus in oratióne pósitis, Christo réddidit.
entries.eng: At Toledo, in Spain, the holy Virgin and martyr Leocadia. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian she suffered a terrible imprisonment under Dacian, Prefect of Spain, and when she heard of the grievous torments of blessed Eulalia and the other martyrs, she knelt down in prayer and gave up her unstained spirit to Christ (,in the year 303).

entries.lat: Lemóvicis, in Aquitánia, sanctæ Valériæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
entries.eng: At Limoges, in France, the holy Virgin and martyr Valeria.

entries.lat: Verónæ sancti Próculi Epíscopi, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cólaphis ac fústibus cæsus, e civitáte pulsus est, ac tandem, in Ecclésiam suam restitútus, quiévit in pace.
entries.eng: At Verona, holy Proculus, Bishop (of that see, in the fourth century.) In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian he was buffeted and cudgelled and thrust out of the city, but was at length restored to his own church and fell asleep in peace.

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Syri, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, atque apostólicis signis et virtútibus cláruit.
entries.eng: At Pavia, St. Syrus, who was the first Bishop of that city, and was renowned for apostolic signs and virtues.

entries.lat: Apaméæ, in Sýria, beáti Juliáni Epíscopi, qui, témpore Sevéri, sanctitáte refúlsit.
entries.eng: At Apamea, in Syria, blessed Julian, Bishop, who shone with holiness in the time of the Emperor Severus.

entries.lat: Graji, in Burgúndia, sancti Petri Fourier, qui Canónicus Reguláris fuit Salvatóris Nostri, et Canonissárum Regulárium Dóminæ Nostræ edocéndis puéllis Institútor; atque, virtútibus ac miráculis clarus, a Leóne Décimo tértio, Pontífice Máximo, Sanctórum catálogo adjúnctus est.
entries.eng: At Grai, in Burgundy, holy Peter Fourier, Canon Regular of Our Saviour, founder of the Canonesses Regular of Our Lady for the education of girls whom, illustrious for his virtues and miracles, Leo XIII added him to the roll of the Saints.

entries.lat: Petragóricis, in Gállia, sancti Cypriáni Abbátis, magnæ sanctitátis viri.
entries.eng: At Perigueux, in France, the holy Abbot Cyprian, a man of great holiness. (He lived as a hermit in the latter part of his life near Dordogne, at a place now called after him.).

entries.lat: Naziánzi, in Cappadócia, sanctæ Gorgóniæ, quæ fuit beátæ Nonnæ fília, atque beatórum Gregórii Theológi et Cæsárii soror, cujus ipse Gregórius virtútes et mirácula conscrípsit.
entries.eng: At Nazianzus, holy Gorgonia, sister of blessed Gregory the theologian, who hath written of her graces and miracles.

entries.lat: Sancti Melchíadis, Papæ et Mártyris, cujus dies natális recensétur tértio Idus Januárii.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Pope Melchiades, (who reigned three years, 7 months, and 62 days, from the year 310 till January 10, 314,) who suffered much in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, but fell asleep in the Lord after peace had been restored to the church.

entries.lat: Romæ, via Ostiénsi, Dedicátio Basílicæ sancti Pauli Apóstoli; quæ, simul cum Dedicatióne Basílicæ sancti Petri, Apostolórum Príncipis, annua celebritate recólitur quartodécimo Kaléndas Januárii.
entries.eng: At Rome, on the Ostian Way, the Dedication of the Basilica of St. Paul the Apostle; which is celebrated every year, together with the Dedication of the Basilica of St. Peter, Prince of the Apostles, on the 19th day of December.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Carpóphori Presbýteri, et Abúndii Diáconi; qui, in Diocletiáni persecutióne, primo fústibus crudelíssime cæsi, deínde in cárcerem, negáto cibo et potu, retrúsi, et rursum in equúleo torti, et post hæc diu in cárcere maceráti, novíssime gládio percússi sunt.
entries.eng: Upon the same day the holy martyrs Carpophorus the Priest, and Abundius the Deacon. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian they were first most cruelly cudgelled and recommitted to prison, where they were denied food and drink, then they were racked, and suffered long imprisonment, and lastly were beheaded,.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Mennæ, Hermógenis et Eugraphi; qui sub Galério Maximiáno passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, under the Emperor Gallerius Maximian, the holy martyrs Mennas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus.

entries.lat: Apud Leontínos, in Sicília, sanctórum Mártyrum Mercúrii et Sociórum mílitum; qui, sub Tertýllo Prǽside, témpore Licínii Imperatóris, gládio cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Lentini, in Sicily, the holy soldiers, Mercury and his Companions, all martyrs, who were slain with the sword in the time of the Emperor Licinius, under the President Tertyllus.

entries.lat: Ancýræ, in Galátia, sancti Gemélli Mártyris, qui, post dira torménta, sub Juliáno Apóstata, crucis supplício martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Ancyra, in Galatia, the holy martyr Gemellus, who, after most grievous torments under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, achieved martyrdom by the death of the cross.

entries.lat: Eméritæ, in Hispánia, pássio sanctæ Euláliæ Vírginis, quæ, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, cum esset annórum duódecim, ibi, jussu Daciáni Prǽsidis, pro confessióne Christi, plúrima torménta est perpéssa; novíssime, in equúleo suspénsa et exunguláta, fáculis ardéntibus ex utróque látere appósitis, hausto igne, spíritum réddidit.
entries.eng: At Merida, (in Estramadura,) in Spain, (in the same year,) under the Emperor Maximian, the holy Virgin and martyr Eulalia, at the age of twelve years. The President Dacian commanded her to be put to many tortures for confessing Christ at last she was hung upon the rack, and lacerated with hooks and, burning torches being put to her sides, some of the flame and smoke went down her throat and she gave up the ghost.

entries.lat: Item ibídem sanctæ Júliæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ beátæ Euláliæ sócia fuit, et illi ad passiónem properánti indivídua comes adhǽsit.
entries.eng: Likewise at Merida, the holy Virgin and martyr Julia, who was a Companion of the blessed Eulalia, and the only one who clave unto her as she went to suffer.

entries.lat: Romæ beáti Gregórii Papæ Tértii, qui sanctitáte meritísque præclárus migrávit in cælum.
entries.eng: At Rome, the blessed Pope Gregory III, who, illustrious for holiness and merits, departed to heaven.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Sindúlphi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Vienne, the holy Confessor Sindulph, Bishop (of that see).

entries.lat: Bríxiæ sancti Deúsdedit Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Brescia, holy Deusdedit, Bishop (of that see).

entries.lat: Lauréti, in Picéno, Translátio sacræ Domus Genitrícis Dei Maríæ, qua in domo Verbum caro factum est. Ipsam vero beatíssimam Vírginem, Lauretánæ título nuncupátam, Benedíctus Papa Décimus quintus ómnibus aëreonáutis præcípuam apud Deum Patrónam attríbuit.
entries.eng: At Loreto, in Picenum, is commemorated the translation, of the holy house of Mary the Mother of God, wherein the Word was made flesh.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Dámasi Primi, Papæ et Confessóris; qui Apollinárem hæresiárcham damnávit, et Petrum, Epíscopum Alexandrínum, fugátum restítuit; multa étiam sanctórum Mártyrum córpora invénit, eorúmque memórias vérsibus exornávit.
entries.eng: At Rome, St. Damasus I, Pope and Confessor; who condemned the heresiarch Apollinaris, and restored Peter, Bishop of Alexandria, who had been driven out; he also found many bodies of the holy Martyrs, and adorned their memorials with verses.

entries.lat: Item Romæ pássio sancti Trasónis, qui, cum Christiános laborántes in thermis, aliísque opéribus públicis fatigátos, et in cárcere pósitos, de suis facultátibus áleret, jussu Maximiáni tentus est, et cum áliis duóbus, id est Pontiáno et Prætextáto, martýrio coronátus.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy Confessor Pope Damasus (of Spain), who condemned the arch-heretic Apollinaris, and restored to his papacy Peter, Pope of Alexandria, who had been driven into exile moreover, he found the bodies of many holy martyrs, and caused to be engraved upon their tombstones verses composed by himself. (He died in the year 384.) Likewise at Rome, the holy martyr Thrason, who fed at his own expense Christians who were in prison or sent to work in the baths, or at other public works. He was arrested by order of the Emperor Maximian, and crowned with martyrdom along with two others named Pontian and Pretextatus,.

entries.lat: Ambiáni, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Victórici et Fusciáni, sub eódem Imperatóre, in quorum náribus et áuribus jussit Rictiovárus Præses immítti tarínchas, et clavis ardéntibus témpora transfígi, deínde óculos evélli, ac póstmodum eórum córpora jaculári; sicque, una cum sancto Gentiáno, eórum hóspite, capítibus amputátis, migravérunt ad Dóminum.
entries.eng: At Amiens, under the same Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Victoricus and Fuscian. Rictiovarus the President had iron spikes driven into their nostrils and ears, and redhot nails hammered into their temples after which their eyes were torn out, their bodies pierced with darts, and their heads cut off, and so they and holy Gentian, their host, passed away to be for ever with the Lord,.

entries.lat: In Pérside sancti Bársabæ Mártyris.
entries.eng: (At Astrahara, near Persepolis,) in Persia, the holy martyr Barsabas, (with ten monks, whose Abbot he was, in the year 342, at the beginning of the great persecution under Sapor II.).

entries.lat: In Hispánia sancti Eutýchii Mártyris.
entries.eng: In Spain, the holy martyr Eutychius.

entries.lat: Placéntiæ sancti Sabíni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
entries.eng: At Piacenza, holy Sabinus, Bishop of that see, (in the fourth century,) famous for miracles.

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sancti Daniélis Stylítæ.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, holy Daniel the Stylite.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Epímachi et Alexándri, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre, cum fuíssent multo témpore in vínculis, atque, divérsis supplíciis affécti, perdurássent in fide, ígnibus tandem consúmpti sunt. Sanctus vero Epímachus, simul cum sancto Gordiáno Mártyre, festíva celebritáte cólitur sexto Idus Maji.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, under the Emperor Decius, the holy martyrs Epimachus and Alexander; they were long kept in chains and put to diverse torments, but they persevered in the faith, and at the last were burnt,.

entries.lat: Romæ sancti Synésii Mártyris, qui, beáti Xysti Papæ Secúndi témpore ordinátus Lector, et, cum multos convertísset ad Christum, apud Aureliánum Imperatórem accusátus, martýrii corónam gládio percússus accépit.
entries.eng: At Rome, the holy martyr Synesius, who was ordained a Reader in the time of the blessed Pope Xystus, and converted many to Christ he was accused before the Emperor Aurelian, and received the crown of martyrdom by being beheaded,.

entries.lat: Eódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Hermógenis, Donáti et aliórum vigínti duórum.
entries.eng: On the same day, the holy martyrs Hermogenes, Donatus, and twenty-two others.

entries.lat: Tréviris sanctórum Mártyrum Maxéntii, Constántii, Crescéntii, Justíni et Sociórum; qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Rictiováro Prǽside, passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Trier, (in the fourth century,) under the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, suffered the holy martyrs Maxentius, Constantius, Crescentius, Justinus, and their Companions.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctárum Ammonáriæ Vírginis, Mercúriæ, Dionýsiæ et altérius Ammonáriæ. Harum prima, in persecutióne Décii, inaudítis tormentórum genéribus superátis, beátum vitæ finem, ferro cædénte, percépit; tres vero áliæ, cum Judex a féminis superári erubésceret, ac dubitáret, ne, eádem in illas exércens cruciaménta, viríli eárum étiam constántia vincerétur, statim jussæ sunt decollári.
entries.eng: Likewise at Alexandria, the holy women Ammonaria the Virgin, Mercuria, Dionysia, and another called also Ammonaria. In the aforesaid persecution under the Emperor Decius, the first of these died a blessed death by the sword, after overcoming torments unheard of. The judge was ashamed to be conquered by women, and shrank from causing the application to them of the same tortures as to the first, and so conquered by their steadfastness, ordered them to be beheaded,.

entries.lat: Syracúsis, in Sicília, natális sanctæ Lúciæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, in persecutióne Diocletiáni. Hæc nóbilis Virgo, cum eam lenónes, quibus, jubénte Paschásio Consulári, trádita erat ut a pópulo castitáti ejus illuderétur, dúcere vellent, nullátenus per illos movéri pótuit, nec fúnibus ádditis, nec boum jugis plúrimis; deínde vero, picem, resínam ac fervens óleum nil læsa súperans, tandem, gládio in gútture percússa, martýrium consummávit.
entries.eng: At Syracuse, in Sicily, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy Virgin and martyr Lucy. By command of Paschasius the Consular she was handed over to panders to make a public mock of her chastity, but when they would have led her away they could not move her even with ropes, and not even when these were drawn by many yoke of oxen then they poured upon her boiling pitch, rosin, and oil but these did not hurt her, and at length she was smitten in the neck with a sword, and so finished her testimony,.

entries.lat: Molíni, in Gállia, item natális sanctæ Joánnæ-Francíscæ Frémiot de Chantal Víduæ, quæ Ordinis Sanctimoniálium Visitatiónis sanctæ Maríæ fuit Institútrix; ac, nobilitáte géneris, vitæ sanctimónia, quam in quadrúplici statu constánter duxit, et miraculórum dono illústris, a Cleménte Décimo tértio, Pontífice Máximo, in Sanctárum númerum reláta est. Sacrum ejus corpus Annésium, in Sabáudia, translátum fuit, et solémni pompa in prima sui Ordinis Ecclésia tumulátum. Ipsíus autem festum duodécimo Kaléndas Septémbris ab univérsa Ecclésia Clemens Papa Décimus quartus celebrári mandávit.
entries.eng: At Moulins, in Gaul, the holy widow Jeane Frances Fremiot de Chantal, (1572-1641,) foundress of the Congregation of Nuns of the Visitation of St. Mary. She was eminent by her noble birth, by the holiness of her life, which she sanctified unceasingly in the four different states of maiden, wife, widow, and nun, and by the grace of working miracles, and Clement XIII enrolled her name among those of the Saints. Her sacred body was translated to Annecy, in Savoy, and there entombed with solemn pomp in the first church of their order. Clement XIV ordered her feast to be kept by the Universal Church upon the 21st day of August.

entries.lat: In Arménia pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Eustrátii, Auxéntii, Eugénii, Mardárii et Oréstis, in persecutióne Diocletiáni. Ex ipsis Eustrátius, primum sub Lýsia, deínde Sebáste, sub Agricoláo Prǽside, una cum Oréste exquisítis torméntis cruciátus, in fornácem missus réddidit spíritum; Oréstes autem, in stratum férreum ignítum pósitus, migrávit ad Dóminum; céteri apud Arábracos, sævíssimis agitáti supplíciis, sub Lýsia Prǽside, diversímode martýrium consummárunt. Eórum córpora, póstea Romam transláta, in Ecclésia sancti Apollináris honorífice collocáta sunt.
entries.eng: In Armenia, in the same persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius, and Orestes. Eustratius was first put to dreadful torments under Lysias, and afterwards to the like at Sebaste, along with Orestes, under the President Agricolaus, and was then cast into a furnace, wherein he gave up the ghost. Orestes was laid upon an iron bed heated with fire, and so passed away to be ever with the Lord. The others finished their testimony in diverse ways in the country of the Arabraci, after enduring most cruel sufferings under the President Lysias. Their bodies were afterwards brought to Rome and honourably buried in the church of St. Apollinaris.

entries.lat: In Sulcitána ínsula, apud Sardíniam, pássio sancti Antíochi, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre.
entries.eng: In the island of Sulcis, off the coast of Sardinia, (in the second century,) under the Emperor Hadrian, the holy martyr Antiochus.

entries.lat: Cameráci, in Gállia, sancti Authbérti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Cambrai, in France, the holy Bishop and Confessor Autbert.

entries.lat: In pago Pontívo, in Gállia, sancti Judóci, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Ponthieu, (in Gaul, in the year 669,) the holy Confessor Josse, (King of Brittany and hermit at Ponthieu.).

entries.lat: In território Argentoraténsi sanctæ Othíliæ Vírginis.
entries.eng: In the territory of Strasburg, the holy Virgin Odilia.

entries.lat: Ubédæ, in Hispánia, natális sancti Joánnis a Cruce, Presbýteri et Confessóris, sanctæ Terésiæ in Carmelitárum reformatióne sócii; quem, a Summo Pontífice Benedícto Décimo tértio Sanctis adscríptum, Pius Papa Undécimus Doctórem universális Ecclésiæ declarávit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas ágitur octávo Kaléndas Decémbris.
entries.eng: At Ubeda, in Spain, the holy Confessor John of the Cross (died in 1591) a companion of holy Teresa in reforming the Carmelites, whose feast is kept upon the 24th day of November.

entries.lat: Rhemis, in Gállia, pássio sanctórum Nicásii Epíscopi, ac soróris Eutrópiæ Vírginis, et Sociórum Mártyrum; qui a bárbaris Ecclésiæ hóstibus cæsi sunt.
entries.eng: At Reims, the holy martyrs Nicasius, Bishop, of that see the Virgin Eutropia, his sister, and their Companions, who were slain by the savage enemies of the Church.

entries.lat: Alexandríæ sanctórum Mártyrum Herónis, Arsénii, Isidóri, et Dióscori púeri. Horum tres primos Judex, in persecutióne Deciána, cum eos, váriis torméntis dilánians, pari armátos constántia vidéret, tradi ígnibus jubet; Dióscorus vero, multiplíciter flagellátus, divíno nutu ad consolatiónem fidélium dimíssus est.
entries.eng: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Heron, Arsenius, and Isidore, and a lad Dioscorus. In the persecution under the Emperor Decius the judge caused Heron, Arsenius, and Isidore to be lacerated with diverse torments, and, when he saw them to be all equally steadfast, to be burnt. Dioscorus was heavily whipped, but God was pleased that, for the comfort of the faithful, he should then be set at liberty.

entries.lat: Antiochíæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Drusi, Zósimi et Theodóri.
entries.eng: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Drusus, Zosimus, and Theodore.

entries.lat: Eódem die pássio sanctórum Justi et Abúndii, qui, sub Numeriáno Imperatóre et Olýbrio Prǽside, conjécti in ignem, et, cum inde evasíssent illǽsi, gládio percússi sunt.
entries.eng: Upon the same day, the holy martyrs Justus and Abundius. Under Olybrius the President, in the persecution under the Emperor Numerian, they were cast into the fire, and when they appeared thence unburnt, they were beheaded.

entries.lat: In Cypro natális beáti Spiridiónis Epíscopi, qui unus fuit ex illis Confessóribus, quos Galérius Maximiánus, dextro oculo effósso et sinístro póplite succíso, ad metálla damnáverat. Hic prophetíæ dono et signórum glória ínclitus fuit, et in Nicǽno Concílio philósophum éthnicum, Christiánæ religióni insultántem, devícit et ad fidem perdúxit.
entries.eng: In the island of Cyprus the blessed Spiridion, Bishop (of Tremithos) he was one of those Confessors whose right eyes were put out and their left thighs hamstrung, and were condemned to penal servitude in the mines by the Emperor Galerius Maximian. He was illustrious for the gift of prophecy, and the fame of miracles, and at the Council of Nicea, (held in 325,) he confuted and converted to the faith a heathen philosopher who attacked the Christian religion, (and died after the year 347.).

entries.lat: Bérgomi sancti Viatóris, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Bergamo, the holy Confessor Viator, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Pápiæ sancti Pompéji Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Pavia, holy Pompey, Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Neápoli, in Campánia, sancti Agnélli Abbátis, virtúte miraculórum illústris, qui obséssam urbem sæpe visus est Crucis vexíllo ab hóstibus liberáre.
entries.eng: At Naples, in Campania, holy Agnello, Abbot (at Naples,) famous for the grace of miracles, who, when the city had been beleaguered, had often been seen with a flag marked with a cross, delivering it from the enemy.

entries.lat: Medioláni sancti Matroniáni Eremítæ.
entries.eng: At Milan, the holy Hermit Matronian.

entries.lat: Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Irenǽi, Antónii, Theodóri, Saturníni, Victóris, et aliórum decem et septem, qui, in persecutióne Valeriáni, pro Christo passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Rome, (in the third century,) the holy martyrs Irenaeus, Antony, Theodore, Saturninus, Victor, and seventeen others who suffered for Christ's sake in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian.

entries.lat: In Africa pássio sanctórum Faustíni, Lúcii, Cándidi, Cæliáni, Marci, Januárii et Fortunáti.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Faustinus, Lucius, Candidus, Caelian, Mark, Januarius, and Fortunatus.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Valeriáni Epíscopi, qui, cum esset annórum plus octogínta, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Rege Ariáno Genseríco, convéntus ab eo ut tráderet Ecclésiæ utensília, idque constánter renuísset, extra civitátem singuláris jussus est pelli; cumque præcéptum esset ut nullus eum neque in domo neque in agro dimítteret habitáre, multo témpore in strata pública nudo sub áere jácuit, et, in confessióne et defensióne cathólicæ veritátis, cursum beátæ vitæ complévit.
entries.eng: Likewise in Africa, holy Valerian, Bishop (of Abbenze.) When he was more than eighty years of age the Arian king Genseric, during the Vandal persecution, sought to make him consent to give up the vessels of the church, and because he steadfastly refused so to do, he caused him to be thrust out of the city alone, and since it was forbidden to any man to allow him to come into his house or to dwell in his field, he lay a long time in the open air on the public highway, and finished the course of his blessed life, in the profession and defense of Catholic truth.

entries.lat: In território Aurelianénsi sancti Maximíni Confessóris.
entries.eng: In the country of Orleans, the holy Confessor Maximin, (2nd Abbot of Michy, in the Diocese of Orleans about the year 520.).

entries.lat: Apud Ibéros, trans Pontum Euxínum, sanctæ Christiánæ ancíllæ, quæ miraculórum virtúte gentem illam, témpore Constantíni, ad Christi fidem perdúxit.
entries.eng: In the country of the Iberians, beyond the Black Sea, (in the third century,) the holy handmaiden Christiana, (the Apostle of the Iberians of the Caucasus,) who in the time of the Emperor Constantine, by the power of her miracles, brought that people to believe in Christ.

entries.lat: Vercéllis Ordinátio sancti Eusébii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
entries.eng: Commemorated the ordination (on December 15, about the year 340,) of holy Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, (he was a Reader of the Church of Rome,) who was born into the better life: upon the 1st day of August, but whose feast is kept upon the 16th day of this present month of December by command of Pope Benedict XIII. (He was born about the year 315 and died about the year 371 or 375.).

entries.lat: Sancti Eusébii, Epíscopi Vercellénsis et Mártyris; cujus dies natális Kaléndis Augústi, et Ordinátio décimo octávo Kaléndas Januárii refértur.
entries.eng: The feast of the holy martyr Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, of whom mention is made also upon the 1st day of August, (when he died between the years 370 and 375,) and yesterday as for this day.

entries.lat: Sanctórum Trium Puerórum, id est Ananíæ, Azaríæ et Misaélis; quorum córpora apud Babylóniam, sub quodam specu, sunt pósita.
entries.eng: The three children Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, whose bodies are laid in a certain cave at Babylon (in the sixth century before Christ.).

entries.lat: Ravénnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, magístri mílitum, ejúsque fílii Concórdii, atque Navális et Agrícolæ; qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, pro Christo passi sunt.
entries.eng: At Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, a military instructor, Concordius his son, Navalis, and Agricola, who suffered for Christ's sake, (in the fourth century,) in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian.

entries.lat: Fórmiis, in Campánia, sanctæ Albínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, sub Décio Imperatóre.
entries.eng: At Formiae, in Campania, the holy Virgin and Martyr Albina, under the Emperor Decius.

entries.lat: In Africa pássio plurimárum sanctárum Vírginum, quæ, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, suspéndia, póndera laminásque ignítas perpéssæ, martýrii agónem felíciter consummárunt.
entries.eng: At Nola, in Campania, in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, the holy Virgin and martyr Albina, In Africa, many holy Virgins and martyrs, who in the Vandal persecution under the Arian king Hunneric suffered hanging, pressing, and redhot plates, and happily brought to a close the conflict of martyrdom,.

entries.lat: Viénnæ, in Gállia, beáti Adónis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
entries.eng: At Vienne, the blessed Confessor Ado, (monk of the Order of St Benedict,) Bishop (of Vienne.).

entries.lat: In Hibérnia sancti Beáni Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Aberdeen, in Scotland, holy Bean, (called first) Bishop (of that see.).

entries.lat: Gazæ, in Palæstína, sancti Ireniónis Epíscopi.
entries.eng: At Gaza, in Palestine, holy Bishop Irenion.

entries.lat: Romæ natális sancti Joánnis de Matha, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis sanctíssimæ Trinitátis redemptiónis captivórum Fundátor éxstitit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas, ex dispositióne Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi, ágitur sexto Idus Februárii.
entries.eng: At Rome, holy John de la Matha, founder of the Order of the most Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives. (He died in the year 1213.) His feast is kept upon the 8th day of February by order of Innocent XI.

entries.lat: Massíliæ, in Gállia, beáti Lázari Epíscopi, sanctárum Maríæ Magdalénæ ac Marthæ fratris, quem Dóminus in Evangélio appellásse amícum et a mórtuis excitásse légitur.
entries.eng: At Marseilles, in France, the blessed Bishop Lazarus, brother of the holy Mary Magdalen and Martha, whom we read in the Gospel that the Lord called His friend and raised from the dead.

entries.lat: Eleutherópoli, in Palæstína, sanctórum Mártyrum Floriáni, Calaníci, et Sociórum quinquagínta et octo; qui, témpore Heráclii Imperatóris, a Saracénis ob Christi fidem occísi sunt.
entries.eng: At Eleutheropolis, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Florian, Calanicus, and fifty-eight others, their Companions, who were slain by the Saracens for Christ's faith's sake in the time of the Emperor Heraclius.

entries.lat: In monastério Fuldénsi sancti Stúrmii, Abbátis et Saxóniæ Apóstoli; quem Innocéntius Papa Secúndus, in Concílio secúndo Lateranénsi, in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
entries.eng: In the monastery of Fulda, the holy Abbot Sturmius, (of the Order of St Benedict, and first Abbot of Fulda,) Apostle of Saxony, whose name Innocent II enrolled with those of the saints at the second Council of Lateran.

entries.lat: Bigárdis, prope Bruxéllas, in Brabántia, sanctæ Wivínæ Vírginis, cujus egrégiam sanctitátem mirácula crebra testántur.
entries.eng: At Groot-Bijgaarden, near Brussels, in the Brabant, the holy Virgin Wivina, whose eminent holiness is oftentimes attested by miracles. (Foundress of the Abbey of Bijgaarden, in the Archdiocese of Mechelen, of the Order of St. Benedict.).

entries.lat: Constantinópoli sanctæ Olympíadis Víduæ.
entries.eng: At Constantinople, the holy widow Olympias,.

entries.lat: Andániæ, apud Septem Ecclésias, in Bélgio, beátæ Beggæ Víduæ, quæ fuit soror sanctæ Gertrúdis.
entries.eng: In the Ardennes, the blessed Widow Begga, sister of holy Gertrude. (She married Ansegise, son of St. Arnoult, Bishop of Metz. She was born about 368, became a widow in 386, and died about 410.).

entries.lat: Eódem die Translátio sancti Ignátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, tértius post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Antiochénam rexit Ecclésiam. Ejus corpus ab urbe Roma, ubi ipse, sub Trajáno, glorióse martýrium tertiodécimo Kaléndas Januárii consummáverat, Antiochíam delátum, ibídem, in cœmetério Ecclésiæ, extra portam Daphníticam, pósitum fuit; in qua celebritáte sanctus Joánnes Chrysóstomus conciónem ad pópulum hábuit. Póstmodum vero ejus relíquiæ rursus Romam translátæ sunt, et in Ecclésia sancti Cleméntis, una cum córpore ejúsdem beatíssimi Papæ et Mártyris, summa veneratióne recónditæ.
entries.eng: Upon the same day is commemorated the translation of the body of the holy martyr Ignatius, Patriarch of Antioch, who was the third to govern that church after the blessed Apostle Peter he suffered at Rome under Trajan, but his body was brought thence to Antioch and laid in the cemetery of the church outside the gate which leadeth unto Daphne, upon the anniversary of the which ceremony holy John Chrysostom preached unto the people. In after-times the body was again brought back to Rome, where it is buried, and highly honoured in the church of St. Clement along with the body of that most blessed Pope and martyr.

entries.lat: Philíppis, in Macedónia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Rufi et Zósimi, qui ex illórum número discipulórum fuérunt, per quos primitíva Ecclésia in Judǽis et Græcis fundáta est; de quorum étiam felíci agóne scribit sanctus Polycárpus in epístola ad Philippénses.
entries.eng: At Philippi, in Macedonia, the holy martyrs Rufus and Zozimus, who were of the number of the disciples by whom the early Church was founded among the Jews and Greeks of whose happy contending holy Polycarp writeth in his Epistle unto the Philippians.

entries.lat: Laodicéæ, in Sýria, pássio sanctórum Theotími et Basiliáni.
entries.eng: At Laodicea, in Syria, the holy martyrs Theotimus and Basilian.

entries.lat: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Quincti, Simplícii et aliórum; qui sub Décii et Valeriáni persecutióne passi sunt.
entries.eng: In Africa, the holy martyrs Quintus, Simplicius and others, who suffered in the persecution under the Emperors Decius and Valerian.

entries.lat: Ibídem sancti Moysétis Mártyris.
entries.eng: There also the holy martyr Moysetes.

entries.lat: Item in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Victúri, Victóris, Victoríni, Adjutóris, Quarti et aliórum trigínta.
